The shrine has a long connection to sake rice wine and sake dealers across Japan often hang a wooden cedar ball made at Ōmiwa Shrine as a talisman. The 32-meter torii gate in front of the shrine is the 2nd largest in Japan.

spots.name: Uwajima Castle
spots.desc: Uwajima Castle occupies a strategic location at the heart of the city. Unlike most Japanese castles, it's actually an original (dating to 1665), not just a ferroconcrete shell. That said, the castle is comparatively small and modest.

spots.name: Tōjinbō
spots.desc: A group of cliffy rocks facing the Sea of Japan. Aside from its unique shape of rocks, the Sea of Japan's horizon is also a must-see point when visiting.

spots.name: Yoshida Shrine
spots.desc: Most famous as the site of the Setsubun Festival held in February, this small shrine was very highly revered during the Heian Period, and the court made offerings here.

spots.name: Great Boiling Valley
spots.desc: Volcanic hot spot full of sulphurous springs.

spots.name: Murder Stone
spots.desc: A large boulder that has been belching out noxious fumes for centuries, killing small critters who venture nearby. (Humans seem to manage.) According to legend, when Lady Tamamo, the lover of Emperor Konoe (c. 1150), was executed for being a fox in disguise, her soul turned into the stone. Haiku poet Matsuo Basho also paid his respects here on his Narrow Road to the Deep North. In March 2022, the…

spots.name: Yambaru National Park
spots.desc: Subtropical forest home to the Okinawa rail (ヤンバルクイナ), an endangered flightless bird found nowhere else on earth.

spots.name: Nintendo Museum
spots.local: ニンテンドーミュージアム
spots.desc: This video game giant converted their old plant into a museum for the company. Has many historical items in their collection, and interactive experiences for Nintendo products.
spots.price: ¥3300 for adult(18+), ¥2200 for youth(12-17),¥1100 for children(6-11),free for preschooler(0-5)

spots.name: Chiba Marine Stadium
spots.local: 千葉マリンスタジアム
spots.desc: Home to the Chiba Lotte Marines baseball team. Its 30,000 seats also host events and converts, including the annual Summer Sonic Festival in August, drawing big-name musical acts from around the globe.

spots.name: Rikugien
spots.desc: A classical Japanese park with ponds, hills and teahouses, that was built in 1695 by Yanagisawa Yoshiyasu, a Tokugawa daimyo. It's a popular cherry blossom spot in spring and is lit up at night at this time.

spots.name: Koishikawa Botanical Garden of the University of Tokyo
spots.local: 東京大学大学院理学系研究科附属植物園
spots.desc: Not one of the great gardens of Japan and sometimes a bit shabby, but a pleasant stroll with interesting trees, a medicinal herb garden and several ponds. Not to be confused with Koishikawa Korakuen.

spots.name: Sengaku-ji
spots.desc: A temple most famous as the resting place of the 47 Rōnin, a famous group of samurai who banded together to avenge their unfairly slain master. Having obtained the head of the offender, they brought it to this very temple and then were condemned to commit ritual suicide, like their master. The story is told in Chūshingura, the best-known of all Kabuki plays. History aside, the temple isn't much…

spots.name: Meiji Jingu Stadium
spots.desc: Known as Jingu Stadium. Can see university and professional baseball games. It is also famous for being a stadium for the Tokyo qualifying round of the National High School Baseball Tournament.

spots.name: Tsurumaru Castle
spots.desc: Once the castle of the Shimazu clan who governed the Satsuma domain till the Meiji Restoration, it was destroyed during the Satsuma Rebellion. The only parts remaining today are the wall and the moat. Reconstruction of the castle's gate was completed in April 2020. The Reimeikan is located inside the gate on the former castle grounds.

spots.name: Huis ten Bosch
spots.desc: Dutch-themed amusement park, Sasebo's most famous tourist attraction. Be sure to see the fireworks every evening at 20:48.
spots.price: A one-day passport to the park costs ¥6,100

spots.name: Kakuzan Park
spots.desc: This park contains the ruins of Tsuyama Castle (津山城), once considered to be the most spectacular Japanese castle. Since the castle was decommissioned during the Meiji Period, all that remains₨ are the castle walls however, they are truly well-preserved, and a walk around the castle grounds offers many great views of the city and a feel for the castle's former grandeur. The small turret, the only…

spots.name: Akiyoshidai Quasi-National Park
spots.desc: includes the Akiyoshidai (秋吉台, Akiyoshi plateau) and Japan’s longest cave, the Akiyoshido (秋芳洞), the latter of which is designated a Special Natural Monument. Akiyoshidai is served by a natural history museum, visitor center, rest house, youth hostel and park headquarters building, and is traversed by a scenic roadway and several walking trails. Events include a fireworks festival in July, a…

spots.name: Kenninji Temple
spots.desc: Japan's oldest Zen temple, has handsome halls and sand and moss gardens, and is of particular interest to art lovers. Sōtatsu's famed Edo-period screens of the Wind and Thunder Gods are on display. And on the high ceiling of the Hatto Dharma Hall writhe Koizumi Junsaku's splendid Twin Dragons, painted and installed in 2002.

spots.name: Higashi Honganji
spots.desc: Higashi Honganji was established in 1602 by the Shogun Tokugawa Ieyasu when he split the Shin sect in two (Nishi Honganji being the other) in order to diminish its power. Today it is the headquarters of the Ōtani branch of Jōdo Shin-shū. The Founder’s Hall (Goei-dō) is said to be the second-largest wooden structure in Japan. With a capacity for 5,000 people, it's majestic. Check out the massive…

spots.name: Toyosu Market
spots.desc: Toyosu is new home of the world's largest wholesale market for seafood and produce after its relocation from Tsukiji. Unlike the old facility where tourists could almost walk up to the fish, Toyosu's market has large enclosed observation decks and dedicated paths for tourists to view the action, including the famous tuna auctions. However, early morning fish sales start before public transit…
spots.hours: Mon-Sat 05:00-17:00; closed holidays and most Wednesdays

spots.name: Ozu Castle
spots.desc: Reconstructed keep with excellent views over the town and river.

spots.name: Hiroshima City Museum of Contemporary Art
spots.desc: Probably the most deserving of a visit among Hiroshima's art museums. There are a few famous Western names in its collection, including Andy Warhol and Frank Stella, but the real focus is on interesting modern Japanese artists working in their own styles, and the exhibition designers make creative use of the museum space. Special exhibitions cost extra. There is a sculpture garden outside that…
spots.price: ¥360 adults, ¥270 college students, and ¥170 for other students

spots.name: Shukkeien
spots.desc: While it's not one of Japan's Top 3, this compact and beautifully landscaped Japanese garden is well worth a visit, and an ideal place to decompress from the atomic bomb sites. Despite high-rises peeping over the trees, Shukkeien can feel like an entirely different world, with little paths crossing ponds on bridges and winding their way around graceful teahouses and waterfalls. Visitors can feed…

spots.name: Iwakuni Castle
spots.desc: Although the original castle only stood for seven years, that was excuse enough for a reconstruction during the 1960s. The foundations of the original lie a short distance behind the new one; the builders apparently decided to move it closer to the cliff for scenic purposes. Inside the castle is a small historical museum.

spots.name: Hitachinaka Seaside Park
spots.desc: World-famous for its flower installations. It was developed as a theme park after the site narrowly missed out on being Japan's location to construct Disneyland. Has a small section of theme park rides, carnival games, a human maze, mini-golf, BMX course, and disc golf. The park is split to be about one-third amusement park, one-third sports park, and one-third nature park. Good for families…
spots.price: Different admission options and prices; ¥510 for parking

spots.name: Seibu Dome stadium (aka Belluna Dome)
spots.desc: The baseball stadium of the Saitama Seibu Lions professional baseball team.

spots.name: Tokyo Racecourse
spots.desc: Japan's largest horse racing facility. Home to several prestigious Grade 1 events including the Yasuda Kinen and Japan Cup races. Racing on weekends only, generally late January-February, May-June and October-November, though you may bet on video races on other weekends. There is also a Horseracing Museum near the grandstand (no additional fees required). Has many eateries inside which are a bit…

spots.name: The Tōyō Bunko
spots.desc: The Toyo Bunko is a special library and a research institute of Oriental studies. The research focuses on Asian history and cultures. The Toyo Bunko collects and saves historical records of Asia. The collection of books exceeds 950,000 items. People can read the books free of charge. Library materials cannot leave the building. Photocopiers are available for use at a minimal charge.

spots.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Teien Art Museum
spots.desc: Art museum housed in a classic Art Deco style structure, connected to a small park with Japanese and Western gardens and outdoor sculptures.

spots.name: Fukuoka Art Museum
spots.desc: This art gallery has an excellent permanent collection, and hosts temporary exhibitions.

spots.name: Miyazaki Prefectural Art Museum
spots.desc: Has a permanent collection but is best visited for its special exhibitions, so it's best to check what will be featured during your visit.

spots.name: Zuihoden
spots.desc: Mausoleum of Date Maasamune, first lord of Sendai Domain. Zuihoden was designed in the ornate style of the Momoyama Period. The original complex was destroyed during World War II, but has been rebuilt and is in a dense forest (which survived the war; many of the trees are over 300 years old). It features intricate woodwork and a rich variety of vivid colors. Massive cedar trees surround the paths…

spots.name: Shōfuku-ji
spots.desc: Japan's first Zen temple.

spots.name: Bitchu Matsuyama Castle
spots.desc: One of the few remaining original Japanese castles, dating back to the 17th century, it is the only original mountain castle in the nation. It is also the highest castle, built atop Mount Gagyu. Although you can take a taxi up most of the mountain, there is a point at which you must walk up (as no vehicles are allowed on the path leading to the castle). The ascent to the castle will take you…

spots.name: Takeda Castle Ruins
spots.desc: Only the stone walls remain, but nevertheless the ruins are impressive. It is located above the clouds, so if you view the ruins from a nearby mountain on a day that is cloudy, you can see the castle standing over the clouds. This view has given rise to its nickname "Castle in the Sky".

spots.name: Komine Castle
spots.desc: A reconstruction of a 17th-century castle.

spots.name: Shōwashinzan
spots.desc: This mountain, literally "Showa New Mountain", popped out in a local farmer's field in December 1943 and, two years later, had reached a height of 402 m. It is next to the cable car valley station on the east side of Mt. Usu.

spots.name: Chichu Art Museum
spots.desc: Designed by the architect Tadao Ando and entirely underground, this museum integrates art and architecture. The museum only has a few exhibits: 5 paintings by Claude Monet, a room with a giant sphere and 27 wooden sculptures designed by Walter de Maria, and 3 works by James Turrell, including one where you walk into a room with variable lighting that changes your perception. The James Turrell…
spots.hours: Oct—Feb: Tue-Sun 10:00—17:00, Mar—Sep: Tue-Sun 10:00—18:00; closed on the day following a public holiday

spots.name: Sentō Imperial Palace
spots.desc: This palace is one of the most competitive for reservations, because this is the palace where the Imperial family stays when in Kyoto.

spots.name: Nagoya TV Tower
spots.desc: Standing 180 meters tall, the Nagoya TV Tower is Japan's oldest - predating even the Tokyo Tower. Take an elevator to the 100-m-high sky balcony for great views of Hisaya-odori park and Sakae. Under the tower is a small terrace with tables and a number of small food stands.

spots.name: Tomonoura
spots.desc: An ancient port town on the Seto Inland Sea with scenic views of outlying islands. It is famous for Homeishu, a sweet liqueur, made in the Tomo area for over a thousand years. Four distilleries offer free tastes. Tomonoura is also known for its red sea bream fishing display using traditional methods each May. Enjoy a drink or lazy lunch at one of two harbor-side cafes next to the lighthouse.

spots.name: Hiroshima Museum of Art
spots.desc: Established by the Hiroshima Bank in 1978. The permanent collection covers European art from late Romanticism to early Picasso, including a couple of Japanese painters who painted in Western styles. There's at least one painting by every famous artist of the period, but no major works by any of them.

spots.name: Jinpukaku Mansion
spots.desc: This French-style mansion was home to the remnants of the Edo-era feudal clan, Ikeda.

spots.name: Engyō-ji Temple
spots.desc: The beautiful temple complex founded in 966 is in the northern area of Himeji. This temple is best known among the locals as the setting for part of Tom Cruise's The Last Samurai. Mount Shosha, where the temple complex is located, is particularly beautiful in the fall, when the Japanese maples change colors.

spots.name: The Tale of Genji Museum
spots.local: 宇治市源氏物語ミュージアム
spots.desc: It's across the river from Byōdō-in, near Ujigami Shrine and the Keihan Uji station. The latter third of the Japanese classic The Tale of Genji took place in Uji, and there are statues sprinkled throughout the city to commemorate that. It all reaches a crescendo at the Tale of Genji Museum. There are English audio guides available to use for a self-guided tour to help you better understand the…

spots.name: Utsunomiya Castle
spots.desc: The castle is Utsunomiya's claim to Japanese Royalty, where the emperor or other royal members would rest and/or change horses before their last leg to Nikko. The castle is reconstructed from previous excavations and is an excellent place to picnic, but little else. Historical significance and exhibits are limited.

spots.name: Jindai Botanical Gardens
spots.desc: Something is always blooming in this large, all-season botanical garden. The park is divided into areas which feature specific plants such as plum and cherry blossom trees; the Japanese azalea garden and English-style rose garden are good. The main gate is on the west side is near the bus stop; you can also enter from the gate adjacent to Jindaiji Temple on the south side.
spots.price: Adults ¥500, seniors ¥250, junior high schoolers ¥200, children free

spots.name: Koishikawa Kōrakuen
spots.desc: Laid out in the 17th century, this splendid traditional garden boasts a large collection of trees and flowering plants that provide touches of beauty all year round. Winding paths, wooded hills, ponds teeming with ducks and fish. The place can be a little crowded at certain times of year (such as during the cherry blossom season in late March-mid April), but there's plenty of room for everyone.

spots.name: Tsukiji Hongwanji
spots.desc: A Jōdo Shinshū temple just a few blocks away from the fish market, worth seeing because of its unique, South Asian-inspired architecture. Buddhist services are held in English on Saturday evenings.

spots.name: Nezu Museum
spots.desc: Showcases the private art collection of Nezu Kaichirō with many pieces from the Edo period.

spots.name: Gotokuji Temple
spots.desc: The origin of the maneki-neko or beckoning-cat statuettes that bring good fortune to Japanese merchants the world over.

spots.name: Fukuoka Castle ruins
spots.desc: The foundations of Fukuoka Castle and part of its moat are all that remains of the original complex. Work is underway to rebuild part of the castle to show what it looked like. The ruins give a good feel for the scale of the original castle though, and form an attractive park. Additionally, you may drop by the Fukuoka Castle Ruins Visitor Center to rent a tablet PC providing an augmented reality…

spots.name: Mount Ōyama
spots.desc: An easy day hike.

spots.name: Fukui Prefectural Dinosaur Museum
spots.desc: The third largest dinosaur museum in the world. Don't miss the displays about the Fukuiraptor and Fukuisaurus, the two dinosaurs discovered in Katsuyama. You can also dig for your own fossils in a small area on the grounds. The surrounding park has picnic areas, a playground, and cross-country skiing in the winter.
spots.price: ¥720 for adults, free every third Sunday of the month

spots.name: Ogaki Castle
spots.desc: Ogaki Castle is an important historic site. The Battle of Sekigahara actually began here before moving west to Sekigahara, where the battle ended. The original castle was destroyed in World War II, so the current castle was reconstructed in 1959. Inside it is a museum with information about the castle and the Battle of Sekigahara.

spots.name: Kakegawa Castle
spots.desc: Kakegawa castle is the main attraction in Kakegawa. It was built in 1513 by Yasuhiro Asahina and lost to Ieyasu Tokugawa in 1569. The castle was torn down in the Meiji Era, so like the majority of such castles within Japan, it is not the original, but the remaining grounds are well-preserved and original, and the main keep was rebuilt in 1993 with the original techniques, materials, and…
spots.price: Adults ¥300, children ¥150; combined ticket with Ninomaru Art museum: adults ¥400, children ¥200

spots.name: Fukuchiyama Castle
spots.desc: The original castle was built by the Yokoyama family but was ordered to be dismantled during the Meiji Period. This castle was rebuilt in 1986 and houses exhibits of the original castle and artifacts from around the area.

spots.name: Hase-dera
spots.desc: Dating to 686, this temple is the headquarters of the Buzan sect of Shingon Buddhism and contains numerous National Treasures including the main hall and a wooden statue of Eleven-Faced Kannon nearly 10 meters tall. Particularly popular in spring, when the 700 peony trees are in bloom, and in fall, when the maples turn red.

spots.name: Kujukuri-hama
spots.desc: This beach is, for many travelers, their first glimpse of Japan: it's the long coastline you see from the plane coming in over the Pacific into Narita. The name means "99-ri coast", where a "ri" is an old unit of length equal to about 654 m. The coast is in fact around 60 km in length. There are numerous small towns along the coast, from Iioka on the north to Ichinomiya on the south.

spots.name: Katori Jingu Shrine
spots.desc: Long considered an important shrine by the Imperial household, the present main shrine and tower gate were built in 1700 by orders from the fifth Tokugawa Shogunate. It houses the god of war/peace (depending on whether or not Japan is at war or peace). The shrine is surrounded by an impressive forest with huge trees, some of which have been given particular names.

spots.name: Hakone Jinja Shrine
spots.desc: Nestled on the south shore of the lake, close to Moto-Hakone, is a picturesque Shinto shrine with torii gates in water.

spots.name: Mori Art Museum
spots.desc: This impressive art gallery hosts special exhibitions. The museum ticket includes admission to Tokyo City View. The Mori Arts Center Gallery adjacent to the Mori Art Museum requires separate admission (prices vary), not included with the Tokyo City View / Mori Art Museum ticket.

spots.name: Kurama-dera Temple
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple overlooking the valley from the hills. There is a short cable car from the village to the hills (¥200/100 adult/child), but in order to see all the temples you have to walk either up or down. If you have been doing temple-hopping in Kyoto, Kurama-dera will be a pleasant surprise - even during the peak season, it doesn't get crowded here.

spots.name: Tennoji Zoo
spots.desc: The zoo has animals from African Savanna, Asian tropical rainforest, aviary, polar bears, penguins and sea lions.

spots.name: Tokyo Midtown
spots.desc: Opened in April 2007, this competitor to Roppongi Hills boasts Tokyo's second tallest office building, a Ritz-Carlton and yet more endless acres of shopping and eating. Still, Midtown favors wood paneling and greenery over raw concrete and feels a little more human than Hills do. The main gallery (and the floor under) always have open Japanese art exhibits.

spots.name: Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts
spots.desc: The museum focuses on Japanese and east Asian art.
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 09:30-17:00 (temporarily closed for renovation until spring 2025)
spots.price: Adults ¥300, high school and university students ¥200, elementary school students and under free

spots.name: Mount Daibosatsu
spots.desc: One of the 100 Famous Mountains of Japan.

spots.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Museum of Photography
spots.desc: A must for fans of photography, with multiple floors of constantly changing exhibitions of the best photography from around Japan and the world.
spots.price: Entrance fees depend on the exhibits you wish to visit but there are often some free ones

spots.name: National Bunraku Theater
spots.desc: One of the last places in the world where bunraku, a form of intricate puppet theater from the Edo period, can be seen live. The large puppets, which require three operators each, are accompanied by traditional music and narration, and act out great Japanese plays of the 1600s and 1700s. Transcripts in Japanese and synopses in English are provided.

spots.name: Kiyosumi Garden
spots.desc: Not the most famous of Tokyo's gardens, but is quite lovely and uncrowded. It was created in the Edo period, and took its present form during the Meiji Era, under the ownership of the founder of Mitsubishi. The ancient-looking pavilion was built in 1909 to host Lord Kitchener on his visit to Japan.

spots.name: Nagoya City Art Museum
spots.desc: Collection of 2,000 works including pieces by Modigliani, Laurencin, and Utrillo, as well as those of local artists, such as Takanori Ogisu and Tamiji Kitagawa.
spots.hours: Tue-Thu Sat Sun 09:30-17:00, Fri 09:30-20:00 (last admission 30 min before closing), closed Mon (Tue when Mon is a…
spots.price: Permanent collection: adults ¥300, students over 16 ¥200, under 15 free

spots.name: Fukui Castle
spots.desc: The castle was built in 1606 by Yuki Hideyasu after he was given control of the province as thanks for siding with the victors in the Battle of Sekigahara. The castle name (as well as the city and prefecture) comes from a lucky well (福の井) which you can still visit today on the castle grounds. The castle has some well-preserved walls and moat but none of the buildings remain. The prefectural…

spots.name: Oyama Shrine
spots.desc: Built in the early Meiji period to honor the founding father of the Kaga Domain, Maeda Toshiie. It is notable for a unique gate with stained-glass windows that is a fusion of Japanese and Western architecture. The back gate to the shrine is also one of the few remaining parts of the original castle: a gate from the palace compound that escaped destruction when it was moved to the shrine. "Oyama"…

spots.name: Fukuyama Castle
spots.desc: The original castle which dated back to 1619 was destroyed in the bombing of Fukuyama in WWII. The current structure was rebuilt in 1966. The castle grounds are pleasant and the keep looks attractive. It is literally right outside Fukuyama Station, which can be convenient for travelers who want to make a quick stop between Hiroshima and Okayama but unfortunate that the station's presence stymies…

spots.name: Hiroshima Prefectural Museum of Art
spots.desc: Has a good permanent collection of modern European art, including major works by Dali and Magritte, and a few modern Japanese artists as well. Special exhibitions are of a generally high quality, ranging from Persian carpets to The Legend of Ultraman. It's located in front of Shukkeien.
spots.price: ¥500 adults, ¥300 for college students, children free

spots.name: Kasuga-yama Primeval Forest
spots.desc: A gorgeous hill of wild, undeveloped forest leading to Kasuga Taisha and some of the other sights in Nara Koen. The path is clearly marked, though, so don't worry about getting lost. It's a quiet walk at any time of day. If you're determined to feed some deer, save your biscuits for the ones out here instead of the loafers by Todai-ji.

spots.name: Naritasan Shinshō-ji Temple
spots.desc: Said to date back to 800 AD, the large temple has a wide assortment of classical Japanese pagodas and halls and a pleasant quasi-European park. Half the fun is getting there: the kilometer-long Omote-sandō from Narita station is a giant shopping arcade filled with restaurants and souvenir shops. Directions are available from the airport's Tourist Information Desk. The largest of its many annual…

spots.name: Minowa Castle
spots.desc: There isn't much left to see, but with the help of a good imagination and artist impression, you can get an impression of what was once an important castle. Except for the well and a few rock walls, there are almost no parts of the buildings left, but the earthworks and moats are all visible. All signs are in Japanese and there are some photos from excavation work showing many details that have…

spots.name: Inamuragasaki
spots.desc: This is also a famous beach. The Inamuragasaki Park (稲村ガ崎公園 Inamuragasaki Kōen) is there and is well known for its sunsets. The film "Inamura Jane" (稲村ジェーン), directed by Keisuke Kuwata, was set there. The remains of the Hojo, Kamakura's government, was destroyed there in 1333. It follows along National Road 134.

spots.name: Shichirigahama
spots.desc: This is also a famous beach in Kamakura. Unfortunately, swimming is prohibited. But it's still a good beach to relax and have an enjoyable time. Many surfers enjoy surfing there.

spots.name: Kawagoe Castle
spots.desc: Kawagoe's castle dates back to the 15th century, unfortunately the castle was disassembled in the 1870s and only the "Yagura" (tower) and primary hall (Honmaru Goten) still remain. These days the main hall serves as a small museum.

spots.name: Yūshūkan War Memorial Museum
spots.desc: An odd collection of military paraphernalia (including human torpedoes and letters from kamikaze pilots) and one-sided (allegedly revisionist according to the Chinese, Koreans and other Asian countries except Taiwan) descriptions of Imperial Japan and World War II, but it can be pretty confronting at times. The museum includes a small military history book and model shop.
spots.price: Adult ¥1000, post-secondary student ¥500, high school student ¥300, child free

spots.name: Mitsui Memorial Museum
spots.desc: Art museum, the collection includes items used in the Japanese tea ceremony as well as Eastern antiques. Housed in an historic building dating back to 1926.

spots.name: Ikegami Honmon-ji
spots.desc: A large temple with a five-story pagoda. It hosts a lantern festival called O-Eshiki every year from 11 to 13 October.

spots.name: Fukuoka City Museum
spots.desc: Permanent exhibition of city history and changing temporary exhibitions.
spots.price: ¥200 adults / 150 high schoolers / free for children

spots.name: Ishinomori Manga Museum
spots.desc: It commemorates the works of manga artist and author Shotaro Ishinomori, who created several immensely popular long-running series such as Cyborg 009, the Super Sentai series (adapted into the Power Rangers series), and the Kamen Rider series.

spots.name: Ōsaki Hachiman Shrine
spots.desc: Completed in 1607, and is designated a national treasure. The metal ornaments and colorful designs displayed against the black lacquer woodwork is an especially attractive feature.

spots.name: Sendai City Museum
spots.desc: Houses a range of items relating to the city's history. Note that it is closed for renovations until approximately April 2024.

spots.name: Sagami Lake
spots.desc: A popular spot to see summer fireworks.

spots.name: Yokohama Museum of Art
spots.hours: Fri–Wed 10:00–18:00 (last entry 17:30), closed Thu and New Year holidays

spots.name: Sunomata Castle
spots.desc: Nicknamed "Sunomata Ichiya Castle" (墨俣一夜城), the castle is famous for the tale that it was built in just one night (ichiya). It was indeed built very quickly, but took a couple days rather than a single night. It was not actually a castle with a donjon like you see today. The original site was built as a fortress with wall and towers by Toyotomi Hideyoshi as part of the campaign to overtake Gifu…

spots.name: Toba Aquarium
spots.desc: Visitors can see African manatees, dolphins, a walrus, and a wide variety of shellfish, among other things. Although the manatees are quite popular, as they are the largest animals in the aquarium, the real gem is the dugong, listed as the "mermaid" in the pamphlet. Toba aquarium is one of only 4 aquariums in the world to display dugong, the others being in Sydney, Singapore, and Jakarta. English…

spots.name: Cupnoodles Museum Osaka Ikeda
spots.local: 安藤百福発明記念館 大阪池田
spots.desc: Retells the story of the cup noodles brand and its founder Momofuku Ando.
spots.price: Free, ¥500 if you want to make your own cup noodles

spots.name: Nagahama Castle
spots.desc: Nagahama Castle was built in 1575-1576 by Hashiba Hideyoshi (later known as Toyotomi Hideyoshi) in the village then called Kunitomo, renaming the area Nagahama. In 1615, the castle was demolished, though parts of it were utilized in the construction of Hikone Castle. The castle as it was rebuilt in 1983 and houses a museum (in Japanese only) about the history of Nagahama. Nagahama Castle is in…

spots.name: Watarase Keikoku Railway Line
spots.local: わたらせ渓谷鐵道わたらせ渓谷線
spots.desc: Buy a one-day pass on the Keikoku Railway that runs up the Watarase River valley, get off at one of the larger stops, hike around a bit, and hop back on the next train. Trains run at less than hourly intervals, so check the schedule at each station before setting out. Stop off at Mizunuma Station to enjoy the refreshing public baths at the only "in-Station" spa in all of Japan! In Autumn, many…

spots.name: Bannaji Temple
spots.desc: Founded by Ashikaga Yoshikane during the early Kamakura period (1192-1333), Bannaji Temple maintains the style of a samurai residence of that era. It was designated a National Historic Site in 1922. In addition to the main temple, the spacious grounds include a bell tower, library, and other buildings, as well as a fine assortment of trees, including cherry trees and a huge, old gingko tree.

spots.name: Kabira Bay
spots.desc: At the northwest corner of the island is this stunning emerald blue bay with a perfect yellow-white beach, dotted by craggy islands — but no swimming allowed, so the closest you can get is a glass-bottom boat tour (¥1000, 30 min). You can walk along the coast from bay to bay, but beware of the fast-moving tides that may trap you if you dally too much in the evening. The best free…

spots.name: Ono Castle
spots.desc: A 'Castle in the Sky'. A castle was built here by Kanamori Nagachika in around 1580, but the current structure dates from 1968.
spots.hours: Apr-Sep: 06:00-17:00, Oct-Nov: 06:00-16:00, last admission 30 minutes before closing. Closed December-March

spots.name: Yoshida-Koriyama Castle
spots.desc: It is listed as one of Japan's Top 100 Castles. Adapted by warlord Mōri Motonari as Mōri clan’s main castle and demolished during early Edo period after the Shimabara Rebellion (1637-1638), the site contains ruins of Mōri Clan's former mountain castle.

spots.name: Rokuharamitsu-ji
spots.desc: While the temple may not seem so special, the trip is made worthwhile by the amazing Kamakura Period artwork housed in its museum. In particular, the statue of Kuya is quite a unique piece of artwork depicting Kuya Shonin reciting the nenbutsu. To depict the words, the artist Taira Kiyomori, sculpted six miniature figures of Kuya Shonin walking out of his open mouth. Each figure represents one…

spots.name: Kyoto Municipal Museum of Art
spots.desc: This museum houses a wide variety of art with the permanent collections featuring artists that are from Kyoto. Special exhibits may feature Japanese art from other areas or foreign artwork.

spots.name: Maruyama Park
spots.desc: One of the most popular spot for cherry blossom viewing in Kyoto, and can get extremely crowded at that time of year. The park's star attraction is a weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura), which offers an ethereal vision lit up in the night. Outside of the season, a nice spot to rest yourself during travelling around the Higashiyama area. Main entrance to the park is through Yasaka Shrine.

spots.name: Zentsuji temple
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple of the Shingon sect in Zentsūji. It was established in 807 by Kūkai, founder of Shingon Buddhism, who was born where the temple now stands. The oldest structure, the Shakadō Hall, dates to around 1677.

spots.name: Tōji-in
spots.desc: Dedicated to the Ashikaga family, the statues inside represent each Ashikaga ruler. The temple also features a lovely garden.

spots.name: Hirano Shrine
spots.desc: A small shrine, which is an especially popular destination during the cherry blossom season, setting up amusement and food stalls. A small park of cherry trees next to the shrine is hung with lanterns and drawings by local schoolchildren.

spots.name: Niukanshōfu Shrine
spots.desc: It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range".

spots.name: Minna Island (Minnajima)
spots.desc: A small but picturesque croissant-shaped island just 15 min from Toguchi Harbor, with good snorkeling and beaches.

spots.name: Suntory Museum of Art
spots.desc: Hosts changing art exhibitions.

spots.name: Kajū-ji
spots.desc: A temple with a peaceful lily pond and a variety of cherry trees.

spots.name: Yoshida Castle
spots.desc: Feudal lord Kohaku Makino built the castle in 1505 and originally called it Imahashi Castle. After the Warring States period, the castle was renamed Yoshida Castle and became the residence of Terumasa Ikeda.

spots.name: Kaze no Bon
spots.desc: Attracts large crowds. Lanterns line the streets of this picturesque town and dancers and musicians parade through the streets demonstrating this traditional dance style. There are also many food and souvenir stalls. Rumor has it the best time to enjoy the atmosphere is after midnight.
spots.hours: three days at the beginning of September

spots.name: Shin-Yakushi-ji
spots.desc: It's a single hall with twelve ferocious warrior statues (each with his own collection plate) standing guard by a Buddha of healing. The statues are quite impressive — this is as well-protected a Buddha as you're likely to find.

spots.name: Ishiyama-dera
spots.desc: This temple was founded in 749 and the hondō (main hall) is the oldest building in Shiga Prefecture built 850 years ago. Inside the hondo, in the room on the right, is the "Genji Room" where it is believed Murasaki Shikibu wrote her famous book "Tale of Genji", considered to be the world's first novel. The temple precincts are quite large, with a 750 year old pagoda and Muyū-en Garden (無憂園) among…

spots.name: Tōkeiji
spots.desc: (東慶寺). It was established as a nunnery, and was famous during the feudal era for sheltering abused women fleeing their families. It thus earned the nickname "Kakekomidera" (the fugitive temple). Those who remained at the temple for three years could then obtain a divorce. Tōkeiji's large atmospheric graveyard and blooming ume (Japanese plum) are also major attractions.

spots.name: Hōkokuji
spots.desc: Notable for its lovely bamboo grove. Tour agencies have added this onto their itineraries, so if you're looking for tranquility, arrive in the first hour of opening or towards closing.

spots.name: Yuigahama
spots.desc: This is a representative beach in Kamakura, so many people visit in summer to enjoy the sea-bathing there. It is also a spot for a good view of the firework display held in summer. Kamakura is famous for aquatic fireworks. (Just remember when walking along this beach that it was not so long ago that a lot of severed heads buried in and near the sand were found. The heads were very old, from an…

spots.name: Yamashita Park
spots.desc: You can see the whole port of Yokohama and there's a lot of greenery. A short walk from Motomachi-Chinatown Stn (元町・中華街駅), JR Ishikawachō station (JR石川駅), JR Kannai station (JR関内駅).

spots.name: Kitain temple
spots.desc: This temple is notable for its main hall, part of the original the Edo Castle in downtown Tokyo, which was moved here by the Shogun to rebuild the temple after a fire. Also of note are the statues of 540 Rakan, disciples of the Buddha.

spots.name: Saitama Wild Knights 埼玉パナソニックワイルドナイツ
spots.desc: A Japanese rugby union team that plays in the Top League. The street from Kumagaya Station to its home stadium is named the "Rugby Road". Kumagaya was one of the host towns for the World Cup 2019.

spots.name: Showa Kinen Park
spots.desc: The largest park in Tokyo. Spanning over 160 hectares, this huge park boasts a variety of natural spaces, seasonal flowers, water features, museums and sports facilities. The park was opened in 1983 to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Emperor Showa's reign, on land reclaimed from a US air base.

spots.name: Hachioji Castle Ruins
spots.desc: Ruins of a castle destroyed during the Warring States Period by Toyotama Hideyoshi. You can see Sagami Bay from the lookout at the mountaintop.

spots.name: Tokyo Dome City
spots.desc: An attractions complex featuring a large indoor stadium, an amusement park, bowling alley, off-track betting center, and the LaQua shopping mall/spa (see Buy). Tokyo Dome is one of several Tokyo stadiums. It is home to the Yomiuri Giants baseball team and also hosts concerts, trade show events, and professional sports. Attached by a walkway is Korakuen Hall, a hub for Japanese martial arts and…

spots.name: Idemitsu Museum of Arts
spots.desc: Has a noteworthy collection centering on Japanese traditional arts.
spots.addr: On the 9th floor of the Imperial Theatre building

spots.name: Machiko Hasegawa Museum
spots.desc: Art museum dedicated to the works of Machiko Hasegawa, creator of Sazae-san, one of Japan's longest running comic strips and cartoons. Showcases include original drawings, clay dolls, and paintings.
spots.price: Adults ¥600, college and high school students ¥500, junior high and elementary school students ¥400

spots.name: Mount Sarakura
spots.desc: Accessible by Hobashira cable car, provides superb views of the city, especially at night.

spots.name: Akiu Great Falls
spots.desc: A 55-m-high waterfall in a forested valley southwest of Sendai, considered one of Japan's most impressive waterfalls.

spots.name: Yamanashi Chuo Bank Stadium
spots.local: 山梨県小瀬スポーツ公園陸上競技場
spots.desc: Home of the local football team, Ventforet Kofu.

spots.name: Yushima Seido
spots.desc: A temple of Confucius.

spots.name: Komazawa Olympic Park
spots.local: 駒沢オリンピック公園
spots.desc: A large public park, built for the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.

spots.name: Nanao Castle Ruins
spots.desc: Contrary to the name, this area contains very little in the way of castle ruins, offering just a small section of stone wall that was once used to fortify the small castle. The reason to go is not for the (non-existent) castle, but for the best view of Nanao and its bay. The small park at the top is peaceful, and the view is gorgeous. The best time to go is in spring on a clear day.

spots.name: Sakura Castle
spots.desc: Very dilapidated ruins with nice view of the city and in a very nice park.

spots.name: Sony Building
spots.desc: The Sony Showroom has four floors of the latest Sony products, with a small shop on the 3rd floor. The building also houses a BMW showroom.

spots.name: Wako
spots.desc: Japan's most expensive luxury department store, the clock tower of this grand art deco building is a Ginza landmark. Founded in 1881 as a watch and jewellery shop, these still make up the core of their offerings but they've expanded to cover high end houseware to a discerning clientele. If you're itching to drop ¥50,000 on a handkerchief or ¥770,000 on a miniature brass replica of a Victorian…

spots.name: Toyota Automobile Museum
spots.desc: A large collection of cars from many countries and manufacturers, from a delicate replica of Benz Patent-Motorwagen in 1886 to the modern Toyota Mirai in 2014. About 1/4 of the collection is dedicated to post-war Japanese cars. Restaurant on-site.

spots.name: Shōren-in
spots.desc: Once associated with the head Tendai Buddhist sect temple, Enryaku-ji on Mount Hiei, Shōren-in is considered to be one of the top five Tendai sect temples. During the Tokugawa period, it served as temporary lodging for a retired emperor after the Imperial Palace burned down. Those who come during November may be able to practice a tea ceremony (See "Do" section of the guide).

spots.name: Pola Museum of Art
spots.desc: The Pola Museum of Art's permanent collection is centered on works gathered over a 40-year period by Suzuki Tsuneshi, the son of the founder of Pola, a Japanese health and beauty company. The collection of around 10,000 items spans a wide range of genres including Western painting, Japanese Western-style painting, Japanese-style painting, prints, sculpture, Oriental ceramics, Japanese modern and…

spots.name: Nippo Coast Quasi National Park
spots.desc: Nippo Coast Quasi National Park is a Quasi National Park characterized by ria (sawtooth) coastline interspersed with occasional sandy beaches. Cape Hyuga is a perfect example of this dramatic coastline.

spots.name: Udo Jingu
spots.desc: A unique shrine in a cave on a cliff face. This brightly colored shrine has become a popular tourist attraction. You can buy small clay pellets that you can attempt to throw into a hole at the top of one of the nearby boulders, women with their right hand and men with their left hand. If you get the pellet into the hole, they say your wish will be granted.

spots.name: Kirigamine Highland
spots.desc: Look at flowers at this volcano.

spots.name: Jingo-ji
spots.desc: An overlooked gem among Kyoto temples, it is an ideal place to visit for those wanting to escape the tourist hordes. It is located in Mt. Takao in the north-western corner of Kyoto. Jingoji Temple was established by Priest Kukai as the head of the Shingon Sect during the Heian Period. Make sure you walk all the way to the back of the temple ground to a commanding view of the Kiyotaki River below…

spots.name: Kifune Shrine
spots.desc: Small shrine in the quiet village of Kibune. Draws crowds of influencers around dusk for its picturesque lantern-lit stairway.

spots.name: 21_21 Design Sight
spots.desc: Changing exhibitions devoted to the latest and greatest in Japanese design.

spots.name: Kyushu Ceramic Museum
spots.local: 佐賀県立九州陶磁文化館
spots.desc: It is famous throughout Japan for its research on ceramics. There are large exhibits of old and modern style ceramics.

spots.name: Konpira Grand Theatre
spots.desc: Built in 1835, this kabuki playhouse is the oldest remaining in Japan. It was designated an Important Cultural National Property in 1970. You can get a surprising amount of access to almost the entire theater, including the elevated walkway, trapdoor, revolving stage, and actors' changing rooms. English pamphlets are available.

spots.name: Osaka Science Museum
spots.desc: Big interactive activity center on several floors. Great for kids. Planetarium and cinema (with science films) downstairs.
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 09:30-17:00, closed Dec 28-Jan 4, closed on public holidays
spots.price: Adults ¥400, university and high school students ¥300, children free, additional charges for planetarium

spots.name: Tobu World Square
spots.local: 東武ワールドスクウェア
spots.desc: A miniature 1:25 model of the world's most famous sites, covering everything from the Pyramids to the Statue of Liberty and, oddly enough, Narita Airport.

spots.name: Tomioka Hachiman Shrine
spots.desc: The largest Shintō hachiman shrine in Tokyo.

spots.name: Port of Nagoya Aquarium
spots.desc: (site in Japanese) Large aquarium featuring a number of different marine environments, including killer whales.

spots.name: Ishikawa Prefectural Museum of Art
spots.desc: This is a pleasant museum showcasing works by local artists hailing from Isihikawa prefecture. There are six galleries showing parts of the collection, which is rotated through the year. Many of the pieces come from the collection of the Maeda lords. The building provides nice views on the surrounding woods.

spots.name: Japan Ukiyo-e Museum
spots.desc: Featuring over 10,000 pieces of ukiyo-e (traditional woodblock prints), it is the largest private museum of its kind in the world. Though the building housing the museum is imposing, a rather small selection of the pieces is shown at any time (2 rooms, about 40 prints). Also reprints of famous Ukiyo-e are on display. The collection was begun over 200 years ago by Yoshiaki Sakai and was…

spots.name: Old Battlefield of Kawanakajima
spots.desc: Togakushi Shrine is a complex of five Shinto shrines in the forested mountains northwest of Nagano, associated with Japanese mythology and the legend of the sun goddess Amaterasu. The shrines are spread across the area, with the Okusha (Upper Shrine) reached by a roughly 2-km approach through an avenue of towering Japanese cedars, many several centuries old. The complex also includes the Chūsha…

spots.name: Miho no Matsubara
spots.desc: A spot on the Miho peninsula with pine trees and views of Mount Fuji on a clear day. One of Japan's New Three Views.

spots.name: Okayama Prefectural Museum of Art
spots.desc: A large museum housing approximately 2,000 works by famous artists throughout Okayama Prefecture. The museum's permanent exhibition features art dating back as far as the Muromachi Period (1336-1573), such as work by the priest Sesshu and the swordsman Musashi Miyamoto, as well as Bizen pottery and works by more contemporary artists.

spots.name: Shimane Art Museum
spots.desc: Works by artists from Shimane prefecture as well as from other parts of Japan are on display. The museum also has a nice selection of ukiyo-e woodblock prints. There are often special exhibitions featuring Japanese and international artists. The museum has a lakeside sculpture park. When you encounter the statues of a line of hopping rabbits be sure to rub the head of the foremost rabbit as it is…
spots.price: Permanent exhibition ¥300, special exhibitions ¥1000. Foreigners get a 50% discount on special exhibitions

spots.name: Kitano Ijinkan
spots.desc: Kōbe's main attractions are the Ijinkan (foreign houses). These are 19th-century residences of Kobe's foreign traders, clustered in the Kitano area.

spots.name: Kobe Maritime Museum
spots.desc: Exhibits rich history of the port city with many photos, artifacts, models and some actual ships. Also houses Kawasaki World, a corporation museum for the Kawasaki Heavy Industries (no additional fees).
spots.price: Adult ¥900, High School student or lower ¥400

spots.name: Osaka Museum of History
spots.desc: An ideal place to learn all-abouts of Osaka's history. Enjoyable view over Osaka Castle and the OBP skyscrapers.
spots.hours: Mon-Thu 09:30-17:00, Fri 09:30-20:00, closed Tue, or Wed if Tue is a holiday

spots.name: Lake Biwa Museum
spots.local: 滋賀県立琵琶湖博物館
spots.desc: It was founded in 1996. The Lake Biwa Museum was established in order to introduce the nature and culture of this valuable lake to everyone, under the theme of “Lakes and People". The Lake Biwa Museum’s aquarium is one of the largest freshwater aquarium in Japan.The giant Lake Biwa catfish (Silurus biwaensis) is the symbol of the Lake Biwa Museum.

spots.name: Omi Jingu
spots.desc: An attractive shrine dedicated to Emperor Tenji as an imperial shrine. It has strong associations with the origins of the karuta game and it hosts the National Karuta Championships every year.

spots.name: Nokogiriyama
spots.desc: Meaning "sawtooth mountain", Nokogiriyama is a group of Buddhist temples cut into sheer cliffs. A rope-way gondola will take you up to the top, and on a clear day you'll have a spectacular 180-degree panorama spanning Chiba, Tokyo, and Yokohama to the north, Mount Fuji to the west, and Izu Oshima and Niijima to the south. Even on a so-so day, Yokosuka should be visible across Tokyo Bay. The most…

spots.name: Nakayama Horse Race Course
spots.desc: One of the four major JRA racecourses. Famous for Arima Kinen, the highest betting horserace in the world and the Nakayama Grand Jump, Japan's premier steeplechase races.

spots.name: Jōmyōji
spots.desc: Not visited often by foreign tourists. Sample tea ceremony in the gardens available with a cup of matcha tea, though tea hall hours are inconsistent.
spots.price: ¥100 admittance; ¥600 for matcha tea (sample tea ceremony)

spots.name: Sugimotodera
spots.desc: Oldest temple in Kamakura, founded in 734. Contains an eleven-faced statue of Kannon. The summit is closed as of April 2025, limiting views to surrounding rooftops.
spots.price: ¥300 for adults, ¥200 for junior high school students, ¥100 for elementary school students

spots.name: Ōsanbashi Pier
spots.desc: Ōsanbashi Pier is the main international pier at the Port of Yokohama where cruise ships dock. Architecturally renovated with an abstract modern style in 2002, it provides a view of the Minato Mirai skyline. The rooftop garden is open to public and is very beautiful, especially during sunset.

spots.name: Yokohama Cosmo World
spots.local: よこはまコスモワールド
spots.desc: Across the water from Minato Mirai 21, is a small amusement park which boasts the Cosmo Clock 21, a 112.5-m Ferris wheel which doubles as "the world's largest clock" (the 60 arms double as second hands). The park also has two roller coasters, a log flume ride and several other attractions. Free but rides ¥500-700 each.

spots.name: Bunkyo Civic Center
spots.desc: The lavish government building for the Bunkyo ward of Tokyo, once described in the Japan Times as "a colossal Pez candy dispenser." A free observation deck on the 25th floor, jutting out of the top like the Starship Enterprise, commands a fine view of much of Tokyo.

spots.name: Yamatane Museum of Art
spots.desc: Specializes in modern Japanese-style paintings and has a notable collection, though only a handful are on display at one time due to preservation issues.

spots.name: Hara Museum of Contemporary Art
spots.desc: This small museum hosts a variety of interesting exhibitions in a 1930s house which is a great example of modern architecture in pre-war Japan. There is a very nice indoor/outdoor cafe. (2026: closed/moved to Gunma prefecture, see Wikipedia)

spots.name: Hanazono Shrine
spots.desc: More remarkable for its location than its appearance, but it's a nice place to take a breather. There's often a flea market in the surrounding park on weekends.
spots.addr: near the intersection of Meiji-dori and Yasukuni-dori

spots.name: Japanese Sword Museum
spots.desc: Display of all types of Japanese art swords and fittings, some of them centuries old. Beautiful view from balcony on 3rd floor over Kyū Yasuda Garden. Quite hefty entrance fee, but a must see for anyone interested in Japanese swords.

spots.name: Hakata Port Tower
spots.desc: It has an observatory 70 m above the ground, allowing for a great view of the port and the streets of Fukuoka.

spots.name: Ohori Park
spots.desc: Tourists visiting Fukuoka should not miss this beautiful park located 2 stops west of Tenjin on the subway. The park has a 2 km jogging track that is popular with locals throughout the year. Also, next to Ohori Park is Maizuru park, featuring the ruins of Fukuoka Castle and a good view of the city.

spots.name: Miyazaki-jingū
spots.desc: A shrine in the city's center, sacred to Japan's first emperor, Jinmu. There are two shrines in the place: one is the main shrine on the east side, and the other one is the Miyazaki Gokoku Shrine (宮崎縣護國神社) on the west side. The Miyazaki Gokoku Shrine, sacred soldiers who died in World War II, is much smaller than the main one. A path between the two shrines can lead visitors to the Miyazaki…

spots.name: Miyazaki Prefectural Museum of Nature and History
spots.desc: Features dynamic exhibits about the prefecture's flora and fauna, along with historic and cultural exhibits. Behind the museum are a handful of preserved buildings moved here from villages in Miyazaki Prefecture's interior. The buildings called minka-en (民家園) by locals.

spots.name: Heiwadai Park
spots.desc: A park said to be the site where the capital of legendary Emperor Jimmu used to stand. The park is known for Heiwadai Tower (平和の塔) or Peace Tower (also known as the Hakkō ichiu monument) built as a symbol of world peace. It's also home to the famous Haniwa Garden with hundreds of haniwa, which were once placed around ancient burial mounds, scattered around.

spots.name: Nagasaki Prefectural Art Museum
spots.desc: Beautiful new building (featured in Architecture Week) that often has touring exhibits from around the world. Fees are required for temporary exhibits.
spots.hours: Daily 10:00-20:00, closed 2nd and 4th Mon of each month and Dec 29-Jan 2
spots.price: Free; exhibitiins: adult ¥420, senior or student ¥310, child ¥210

spots.name: Tokorozawa Aviation Museum
spots.desc: Japan's first airfield.
spots.price: Exhibition hall: Adult ¥520, child ¥100. Movie theatre: Adult ¥630, child ¥260. Combination ticket: Adult ¥840, child…

spots.name: Obama Castle Ruins (Obama Shrine)
spots.desc: Only the walls remain of the ruined 17th century castle, but it does have some nice views over Obama Bay.

spots.name: Itsuo Art Museum
spots.desc: This museum features works collected by Kobayashi Ichizo, the founder of both Hankyu Railway and the Takarazuka Revue, in his former home.

spots.name: Aso Shrine
spots.desc: An old shrine dedicated to the god of transportation and traffic safety.

spots.name: Mount Ishikawa
spots.desc: 204m high hill, the highest point in the city, with hiking trails to the summit.

spots.name: Cape Irizaki
spots.desc: Yonaguni's main aboveground sight of any interest is the marker for the westernmost point of Japan (日本最西端の碑) at the westernmost tip of the island, about a kilometer from Kubura (15 minutes on foot). Despite the marker being located on the island, the official westernmost point of Japan and the closest point to Taiwan is Tuishi (トゥイシ), a rocky reef about 120 m northwest of the shoreline that…

spots.name: Hottai Waterfall
spots.desc: A large waterfall with picnic and camping area and restaurant in Momoyake, Hitane, Chokai. There is also a 2-km hiking trail. The facilities are closed in winter, and the road is not plowed. However, the road is plowed in Momoyake until the last 2 km, so one can easily walk in on snowshoes.

spots.name: Kyoto City Zoo
spots.desc: Like most zoos, visitors will see lions, tigers, and monkeys. There is an aviary and reptile exhibit, as well. The zoo has some native Japanese animals, but there isn't much to set it apart from most other zoos in the world.

spots.name: Enoshima Shrine
spots.desc: Best known for its rather unusual naked statue of Benzaiten (裸弁財天 hadaka Benzaiten), a Shinto deity rarely found in such a state. The shrines at the top of Enoshima 2 chome have an all seeing turtle painted on the ceiling.

spots.name: Hanayashiki
spots.desc: The oldest amusement park in Japan. Next to the Sensō-ji temple grounds is this small and somewhat lackluster carnival complex with rides, booths, and games. The neighborhood theatre specializes in showing classic Japanese films, as many of the tourists are elderly Japanese.

spots.name: Shitamachi Museum
spots.local: したまちミュージアム
spots.desc: A small museum that offers a glimpse into life in the area in the early 20th century, with re-created houses and stores, and cultural artifacts. Closed for renovation until March 2025.

spots.name: Former Iwasaki Family House and garden
spots.desc: Not a major tourist attraction, but an interesting bit of history. The house was built in the Meiji era in the style of an American or British mansion. In WWII the fire raids consumed most of the houses behind the mansion, which was used by GHQ during the occupation. A few attached Japanese-style rooms remain. Sit and sip green tea. The garden--mostly lawn and trees--is of no great interest.

spots.name: Obi Castle
spots.desc: While a fort stood here during the 14th century, it was not until the 15th century that the Shimazu clan built an actual castle on the site in order to defend against the Itoh clan. The castle was eventually decommissioned. Today there are some refurbished walls and gates and a history museum on the site.

spots.name: Kushima Castle
spots.desc: Founded on a peninsula extending into Ōmura Bay in the Kamakura period (1185–1333), the remains and reconstructed parts of the castle are set in beautiful gardens.

spots.name: Jūraku-ji
spots.desc: Temple 7 on the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage.

spots.name: Shisen-dō
spots.desc: Built in 1641, this temple once housed the poet Jōzan Ishikawa. Inside the temple there are portraits of 36 influential Chinese poets. Outside there is a garden filled with many azaleas.

spots.name: Sanzen-in
spots.desc: As the top attraction in the Ohara area, this temple is well worth the visit. Housed within the temple are three ancient Buddha statues. Outside, there is a lovely moss garden and a variety of Buddhist statues ranging from the typical spiritual statues to adorable, animated statues.

spots.name: Oka-dera Temple
spots.desc: Oka-dera Temple, also known as Ryūgaiji, is a Buddhist temple founded in 663 on a hillside overlooking the Asuka plain. The temple is particularly noted for its gardens, autumn colours and the large Nyoirin Kannon, a clay statue dating from the Nara period and regarded as the largest clay Buddhist statue in Japan. The temple's name means “Temple on the Hill”, while its traditional name, Ryūgaiji…

spots.name: Ishibutai Tumulus
spots.desc: Ishibutai Tumulus (Ishibutai kofun) is one of Asuka's most famous archaeological sites. The enormous stone chamber is exposed because its original earthen burial mound has disappeared. Built in the late 6th or early 7th century, the tomb is traditionally associated with Soga no Umako, one of the most powerful figures of the Asuka period. The massive stones forming the chamber are particularly…

spots.name: Kitora Tomb
spots.desc: Kitora Tumulus (Kitora kofun) is a small 7th-century burial mound famous for its exceptionally preserved wall paintings. The original tomb is closed to visitors to protect the paintings, but the nearby Shijin-no-Yakata exhibition hall displays a full-scale reproduction of the burial chamber, allowing visitors to see the paintings and their arrangement. The murals include the Four Guardian Gods…

spots.name: Dainenbutsu-ji Temple
spots.desc: The head templesōhonzan of the Yūzū-Nembutsu sect (融通念佛宗). Its massive wooden main hall (hondō) is the largest wooden building in Osaka Prefecture and a registered tangible cultural property.It is famous for the spectacular Manbu Onenri (万部おねり) festival (early May 1–5), featuring a grand procession of 25 bodhisattvas, music, and dance — designated an Osaka City Intangible Folk Cultural Property.
spots.hours: Temple grounds/gate: 06:00–17:00; main hall viewing: 09:30–16:30 (closes 17:00). Free admission.

spots.name: Oharano Shrine
spots.desc: The shrine is believed to have been moved to Nagaokakyo at the bidding of Empress Kammu, who made it the shrine of the Fujiwara family's guardian god. The Imperial Court made annual offerings at this shrine. The pond within the shrine precincts was once a popular place for writing poetry. The Sengan-zakura tree in the precincts is nicknamed "phantom cherry blossom", because it only blooms for…

spots.name: Yoshimine-dera
spots.desc: In 1034 Emperor Go-Ichijo gave Yoshimine-dera imperial rank, so the head priest was a member of the imperial family for many years, although it is no longer so today. The 20th temple on the Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage.

spots.name: Tobita Shinchi
spots.desc: This is Japan's largest red-light district outside Tokyo, where ladies pose at genkan entrances Amsterdam-style to attract clientele, accompanied by an older woman (called a yarite-baba or mama-san) who serves as the pimp and collects money from customers. However, this place is arguably more interesting to walk through than its Amsterdam counterpart, and most of the brothels operate out historic…

spots.name: Fukagawa Edo Museum
spots.desc: This intimate museum features a wonderfully recreated Tempo-period (1830-1843) neighbourhood - complete with homes, shops, narrow alleyways, and even the local rubbish dump. Wander about, peering in windows and entering buildings furnished with household goods and Edo-period bric-a-brac. Light and sound effects create the illusion of a whole day passing from day to night in the space of a few…

spots.name: Tokyo Sea Life Park
spots.desc: In the huge 2,200-ton tank, you can enjoy watching bluefin tuna darting swiftly around. The aquarium also exhibits sea birds including penguins, and giant kelp from California, US. The facility sits on the beach of Tokyo Bay and could be reached in half an hour by train from Tokyo station.
spots.hours: Thu-Tue 09:30-17:00; tickets sold until 16:00; closed Wed if Thu is a public holiday

spots.name: Masumida Shrine
spots.desc: Ichinomiya means 'first shrine' (in the sense of most important) and Masumida was the principal shrine of Owari Province (now Aichi). The ornate shrine is surrounded by pleasant grounds, including a pool with carp and turtles, which are a pleasant place to stroll on a summer day. The main gate has been refurbished, to restore the carving and gilding. Masumida plays host to most of the town's…

spots.name: Nittai-ji Temple
spots.desc: Among the 165,000 m² of temple grounds is the 15 meter Gandhara-style Taian Pagoda, which houses relics of the Buddha that were presented to Japan by the king of Thailand. Unlike any other temple in Japan, Nittai-ji does not belong to a particular sect, and is instead managed by a different sect every 3 years.

spots.name: SCMAGLEV and Railway Park
spots.desc: Train museum highlighting the evolution of Japan's high-speed rail.
spots.hours: 10:00-17:30 (last entry 17:00), closed Tue (next day if holiday) & Dec 28-Jan 1

spots.name: Matsushiro Underground Imperial Headquarters
spots.desc: Large underground bunker complex built during the Second World War, it was meant to protect the Emperor and the central organs of government, but Japan surrendered before its completion.

spots.name: Hypocenter
spots.local: 広島市への原子爆弾投下
spots.desc: One block east of the A-Bomb Dome (outside Shima Clinic) is a plaque which marks the exact point above which the bomb exploded.

spots.name: Gokoku Shrine
spots.desc: Located on the castle grounds, this concrete shrine has great significance to locals, having been rebuilt after the atomic blast and now the center for most annual Shinto traditions in the city. But other than a historical marker, there's not much to see for travelers, other than festivals (especially New Year's Eve).

spots.name: Mitaki-dera
spots.desc: It was founded in 809 AD. Mitaki-dera is a tranquil, lovely temple to the west of Hiroshima, known for its three waterfalls, which supply the water for the annual Peace Memorial Ceremony (see Festivals), as well as its gorgeous autumn colors and fascinating statues. The tahoto (treasure pagoda) was moved here from Wakayama in 1951 and consecrated in memory of the victims of the atomic bomb. From…

spots.name: Flower Festival
spots.local: ひろしまフラワーフェスティバル
spots.desc: This is Hiroshima's biggest festival, begun in 1975 to celebrate the Carp's first baseball championship. There are food vendors and things for sale, but live performances now dominate the program, with comedians and J-pop bands on stages along Heiwa-o-dori. It's the smaller performances that make the Flower Festival worthwhile, though, particularly in the stalls near Jizo-dori, where you might…

spots.name: Okayama Prefectural Museum
spots.desc: An excellent museum with a variety of artifacts excavated from various areas throughout Okayama Prefecture from prehistoric artifacts to the Edo and Meiji Periods. Some highlights of the museum are the famous Bizen swords and Bizen pottery. It's just outside the main entrance to Korakuen, so it's well worth a stop.

spots.name: Nunobiki Falls
spots.desc: Four waterfalls that empty into the Ikuta River. The largest is 43m high.

spots.name: Takarazuka Grand Theater
spots.desc: The most famous and popular attraction in the city, this theater is home to the all-female Takarazuka Revue. The most famous actresses are the women who play male roles (男役 otoko-yaku), and it is for them that the theater is so popular. They make it quite easy to get lost in the story, forgetting that none of the men on stage are actually men. It is generally easy to get tickets at the door, but…

spots.name: Uji Shrine
spots.desc: The Uji shrine and the Ujigami shrine next door used to be part of the same complex, then known as Rikyukamisha. An interesting feature is the rabbit sculpture, which is said to have prevented the deity from getting lost.

spots.name: Kamakurakōkōmae Station
spots.desc: Fans of Japanese anime, TV shows and movies will instantly recognize the surroundings of this station as the location is frequently featured. The railway crossing on the east side of the station is prominently featured in the theme song of Slam Dunk anime.

spots.name: Meigetsuin
spots.desc: The temple is nicknamed the "Hydrangea Temple" with the surrounding grounds amply planted with the flowers. It is also renowned for the grave of Hojo Tokiyori, approached by a tunnel, the largest of its type in Japan.

spots.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Museum of Natural History
spots.local: 神奈川県立生命の星・地球博物館
spots.desc: A large natural history museum, two stops from Odawara Station on the Hakone Tozan Line. The museum focuses primarily on the natural history of Kanagawa Prefecture, including sea life found in Sagami Bay. It includes an extensive geology section discussing the formation of the Japanese isles, as well as large displays of volcanic rock from Australia and northern Canada.
spots.hours: 09:00 to 16:30. Closed Mondays (except National Holidays) and 2nd Tuesdays

spots.name: Yokohama History Museum
spots.desc: This museum introduces Yokohama's history from Primary period to Modern period. Next to the museum, there are excavations of Yayoi period.
spots.price: Adults ¥400, high school and university students ¥200, seniors and elementary school students ¥100

spots.name: Toki no Kane
spots.desc: This bell tower (litt. "Bell of Time") is a famous landmark.

spots.name: Railway Museum
spots.desc: A must of rail buffs and great for kids, the museum features 36 engines on display (including Japan's first steam locomotive), train cab simulators, Japan's largest HO-gauge miniature railway and more. You can even eat your lunch in a restored dining car. English language signage is sparse.

spots.name: Ohkunitama Shrine
spots.desc: One of the oldest shrines in Tokyo. Kurayami Matsuri (night festival) is famous. Six large drums. Eight omikoshi (small shrines).

spots.name: Azabu-Jūban
spots.desc: A quieter commercial district to the southeast of Roppongi Hills, and a good place to spend a lazier afternoon browsing through shops and enjoying the local cafés. The surrounding residential area is popular among professional expats, so expect to see many international families as you walk through.

spots.name: Nakano Broadway and the Broadway Arcade
spots.desc: On the 2nd and 3rd floor of this otherwise typical suburban shopping complex is the Broadway Arcade. Renowned throughout Tokyo and beyond for its jam-packed stores catering to the "otaku" culture of comics, anime, collectible toys, and the like. If you're looking for two-meter-high Godzilla figure, this is where you'll find it. There are also some used and specialty audio and video equipment…
spots.hours: Many of the shops are not open until late morning or early afternoon, especially on weekends. Most shops are open at…

spots.name: Carrot Tower
spots.desc: This is the tallest building in Setagaya and contains a free observation deck on the 26th floor and Gamefreak Co. on the 22nd floor.

spots.name: Zōshigaya Cemetery
spots.desc: The final resting place of Lafcadio Hearn is about the most exciting attraction in this neck of the woods.

spots.name: Kushida Shrine
spots.desc: The 8th-century Kushida Shrine is starting point for the annual Gion-Yamakasa Festival.

spots.name: Sengan-en Garden
spots.desc: Former residence of the powerful Shimazu clan. Features a Neko (cat) Shrine, industrial heritage buildings of the Meiji restoration and stately gardens. Known for prominently making use of Sakurajima Volcano as borrowed scenery.

spots.name: Iwakiyama Shrine
spots.desc: A shrine with over 1200 years of history, built at the base of Mount Iwaki for mountain worship.

spots.name: Abukumado Cave
spots.desc: An 80 million-year-old, 3,000-meter-long limestone cave discovered in 1969. Traversing the 600 meters open to the public will take about an hour. This is a developed cave for tourism, so there are footpaths, lighting, handrails, and information signs. At the same time, the mix of small passages to huge grand hall cavern, and large variety of rock formations not found elsewhere in Japan, will…

spots.name: Fukushima Prefectural Museum of Art
spots.desc: Small museum mostly with local art, though it does have some national and international exhibits as well (including a handful of prized Impressionist and Pointillist paintings). Phones and cameras are not permitted, except with an armband for hand-written translation (camera translation is not permitted). The attached curry restaurant and cafe, and library, are both popular with locals.

spots.name: Mount Shinobu Park
spots.desc: Hilly park with three observation decks overlooking the city, as well as the Neko Inari Shrine, Fukushima-ken Gokoku Shrine and Henshoin Temple

spots.name: Miyagi Museum of Art
spots.desc: A reasonable collection of modern art. Special room for Juryo Sato, a local (but nationally famous) sculptor. Beautiful garden and a nice view of the river. The museum has been closed for renovations since June 2023.

spots.name: Kamogawa Sea World
spots.desc: Marine park.

spots.name: Gunma Prefectural Museum of Modern Art
Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum
spots.hours: Mar-Sep: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, Oct-Feb: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00, closed Dec 29-Jan 1
spots.price: Adults ¥500, seniors ¥300, children ¥200; discounts for groups of 20 or more

spots.name: Fukushima Prefectural Museum
spots.desc: Prefectural museum of natural history, history and culture.

spots.name: Takayama Jinya
spots.desc: This is a beautifully preserved government building from the time of the shogun and still used as local government building until 1969. Many rooms at the beginning of the visit are basically empty tatami rooms with some indication of what the original use was. In the rice storage area there are interesting displays and information (mostly in Japanese) about how local government worked in the Edo…

spots.name: Noboribetsu Onsen
spots.desc: One of Japan's best-known hot-spring resorts, centred on the volcanic springs of Jigokudani. The compact town has numerous ryokan, hotels, restaurants and souvenir shops, and is particularly atmospheric in the evening when staying overnight.

spots.name: Mikimoto Pearl Island
spots.desc: A museum celebrating the local inventor of the cultured pearl, and demonstrations by Ama (海女 woman pearl divers). English guidance available.

spots.name: Ashikaga School
spots.desc: Known as Japan's oldest university, Ashikaga School was established during the 1400s by deputy shogun Uesugi Norizane (although some credit Lord Ashikaga Yoshikane during the Kamakura period, and still others claim it dates from either the Nara or the Heian period). In any case, by the 1500s, St. Francis Xavier and other foreign missionaries recognized Ashikaga School as the most famous…
spots.hours: Daily 09:00-16:30 (16:00 October–March). Closed 3rd Mon October–March, 3rd Tue April–September

spots.name: Hōfu Tenman-gū
spots.desc: A Shinto shrine.

spots.name: Okubo-ji Temple
spots.desc: 88th site. A temple of the Shingon sect Daikakuji sect.

spots.name: Onbashira-sai
spots.desc: Every six years, Suwa is home to Onbashira-sai, one of the "three dangerous festivals" in Japan. Onbashira is a symbolic reconstruction of the four shrines of the Suwa Taisha with gigantic logs harvested from the forests at the base of Mt. Yatsugatake. The highlight of the festival is the kiotoshi portion, where brave and foolhardy young men ride on these giant logs as they slide down a steep…

spots.name: Daisho-in
spots.desc: Because it's nestled into the hills, this Buddhist temple is easily missed by tourists, but it features several interesting sights and a welcome respite from the crowds. Look for the Dai-hannyakyo Sutra (大般若経), the golden prayer wheels that are said to bring enormous fortune to anyone who touches them, and the Henjokutsu Cave (遍照窟), a fascinating and eerie collection of Buddhist icons related to…

spots.name: Hōnen-in
spots.desc: A quiet temple with some interesting raised sand designs. It was built in honor of Hōnen, the founder of the Jōdo sect.

spots.name: Taku Seibyō
spots.desc: A Confucian temple built in 1708 by Lord Shigefumi. This is one of the oldest Confucian temples in Japan and has been designated as an Important Cultural Asset. It is also the oldest original surviving Confucian temple. Free tours are provided by volunteer student guides in Japanese. The temple is host to festivals throughout the year. Usually students from the local schools participate in dances…

spots.name: Hōrai Bridge
spots.desc: It was constructed in 1879 with a length of 900 m.

spots.name: Muroji Temple
spots.desc: Five-storied pagoda

spots.name: Hōrin-ji
spots.desc: Temple 9 on the Shikoku 88 temple pilgrimage.

spots.name: Takizakura in Miharu
spots.desc: An Ancient Sakura (cherry tree)

spots.name: Tachibana-dera Temple
spots.desc: Tachibana-dera is a Buddhist temple traditionally regarded as the birthplace of Prince Shōtoku, one of the most important figures in the early development of Buddhism in Japan. Founded in the Asuka period, the temple occupies a peaceful site surrounded by rice fields and hills. The main hall contains a number of Buddhist images, including the unusual **Taishō Kannon**, while the temple grounds…

spots.name: Jison-in
spots.desc: This Shingon Buddhist temple functions as the start for pilgrims planning to pilgrimage to Mount Koya, it is inscribed as part of the Mount Koya due to this religious significance. The temple is also a destination for women struggling with motherly issues such as child birth, this is because the temple served as the residence Kukai's mother.

spots.name: Sunosaki Lighthouse
spots.desc: A lighthouse with a great view on the sea and neighboring mountain. Sweets are sold in the small store at the bottom. Sunset spot just beside on the same hill.

spots.name: Takachiho Gorge
spots.desc: Carved by the Gokase River, one of the main highlights is the 17-m Minai Waterfall, best viewed by the sightseeing railway above or renting a boat (¥5,000/30 min for up to 3 people) and going for a paddle, since the current is gentle and easy to navigate. But there is also a 300-m hiking path beside the river, which passes several striking rock formations, and terminates at a small rest area…

spots.name: Cape Tappi
spots.desc: The scenic northernmost point of the peninsula. Panoramic views of the Tsugaru Strait, Sea of Japan, and mountains of Hokkaido and Shimokita. There are some souvenir shops and restaurants near the lookout point, along with some monuments and an interesting dragon bridge. Route 339 briefly turns into a pedestrian path here. The hydrangeas, which are abundant, usually bloom in July.

spots.name: Nishiki Market
spots.desc: An enclosed traditional shopping street, expensive but full of interesting shops and products, including great souvenirs and snacks. It runs east-west, a block north of Shijo-dori, and at its eastern end it connects to Teramachi-dori, another, newer shopping street that runs north-south.

spots.name: Kyū-Furukawa Teien
spots.desc: Probably Tokyo's best-preserved early Edo-era Western-style mansion, designed by English architect Josiah Condor. The rose garden here is also well-known and blooms twice a year in May–June and Oct-Nov, and there's a Japanese garden to round out the set.

spots.name: Tsūjunkyō
spots.desc: The biggest of the stone bridges, built by Nunoda in 1854.

spots.name: Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology
spots.local: トヨタ産業技術記念館
spots.desc: Built on the site of one of Toyota's original loom factories, this museum tells the story of the Toyota corporation, from its beginnings as an industrial loom manufacturer to its transformation into one of the world's largest car manufacturers. Includes large loom machinery and car display halls as well as a hands-on "Technoland" with interactive science exhibits. Museum also includes a library…
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 09:30-17:00 (last admission 16:30), (restaurant open until 21:00), closed Mon (Tue if Mon is a holiday), New…
spots.price: Adults ¥1000, Jr. & Sr. high school students: ¥300, Elem. School Students: ¥200

spots.name: Fukui Prefecture Fine Arts Museum
spots.desc: The prefectural art museum with special exhibits throughout the year.

spots.name: Ninja Temple
spots.desc: The tour guides insist there is no connection between the 'Ninja Temple' and actual ninja assassins. But with 23 rooms and 29 staircases, an impressive array of trapdoors and hidden rooms, and a sepukku (ritual suicide) chamber, it is easy to see why people would make that assumption. Visitors cannot enter the temple except through the tours, so call ahead to book a tour. The tour is conducted in…

spots.name: D.T. Suzuki Museum
spots.desc: This small museum commemorates the life and works of Suzuki Daisetz Teitaro, a prominent Buddhist philosopher whose books were instrumental in spreading interest in Zen Buddhism in the West. The museum is organized around three areas: a first room exhibiting the writings and calligraphy of D.T. Suzuki, as well as pictures and explanations about his work and life; a second room where his books can…

spots.name: Nagano Prefectural Art Museum
spots.desc: Reopened in a new building in 2021. The prefecture's premier art museum. The Higashiyama Kaii Gallery showcases the tranquil landscapes (depicting Northern Europe as well as Japan) of one of the masters of nihon-ga (traditional "Japanese-style painting").

spots.name: Tanaka Castle
spots.desc: Built in 1537 by the Imagawa clan, and demolished in 1871. The current structures include remnants of the moats and stonework, as well as a large yagura, reconstructed in 1992 to serve as a local history museum.

spots.name: Yamanashi Prefectural Museum of Art
spots.desc: This museum has some interesting paintings including several by well known artists.

spots.name: Numaji Transportation Museum
