spots.desc: Changed names from Hiroshima City Transportation Museum by a naming rights deal. Located on the outskirts of the city, the Transportation Museum has exhibits and interactive games about planes, trains, ships, and cars of the past, present, and future — and a transit nerd's treasure trove of details about the history and model numbers of Hiroshima's streetcars. (Tram #654, which remained in…
spots.price: Free on the first floor, elsewhere ¥500 adults, ¥250 children

spots.name: Ube Shrine
spots.desc: The first shrine to be built in the Inaba area, which consists of the entire eastern half of modern Tottori Prefecture. Praying at this shrine is believed to bestow fertility, long life, and wealth.

spots.name: Watanabe Museum
spots.desc: Opened in 1978 by the late Hajime Watanabe, a local doctor who began his collection when he was working in Taiwan in the 1940s. This museum houses a wild display of samurai armor and artifacts, as well as a selection of other things such as musical instruments and ukiyo-e woodblock prints.
spots.price: ¥900 adults, ¥500 high school and college students, ¥300 younger

spots.name: Museum of Northern Peoples
spots.local: 北海道立北方民族博物館
spots.desc: A modern and moderately interesting museum documenting the lives of northern peoples around the world, not just Japan's own Ainu, but Canadian Inuit, Scandinavian Saami and many more. Most of the material is also in English and there are some fairly bizarre exhibits involving, among other things, seal intestines.

spots.name: Toei Kyoto Studio Park
spots.desc: Toei Kyoto Studio Park is an active film studio which continues to be used for the filming of period dramas. Visitors may visit the outdoor sets used in many samurai movies, and if they are lucky, could potentially observe the filming of a period drama.

spots.name: Peace Osaka
spots.local: 大阪国際平和センター
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the promotion of peace through displays of war. Because it is an Osaka museum, it largely focuses on the effects of the bombings on Osaka in World War II. In the past, the museum also had exhibitions depicting the atrocities committed by Japan against China, Korea, and Southeast Asia. Sadly, however, those exhibitions were permanently removed in 2015 in response to pressure…

spots.name: Museum of Aeronautical Science
spots.desc: Main building has aircraft exhibit including engines, cockpits, Boeing 747 cross-sectional dissect and an observation deck on the fifth floor. It also has an outdoor exhibit with about 15 planes on static display.
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00, closed on year end and new years holidays

spots.name: Gunma Prefecture Governmental Building
spots.desc: A beautiful building with two restaurants on the second highest floor and a mechanized car park. The top floor is enclosed in window allowing a 360 degree view of Maebashi, awesome at night, and beautiful during the day.

spots.name: Green Dome Maebashi
spots.desc: A beautifully-designed domed stadium situated in Maebashi Park. With a seating capacity of 8,000, it hosts indoor sports events and exhibitions. It is most popular for hosting Keirin races (pari-mutuel bicycle races) throughout the year. Local buses connect JR Maebashi station to the park and the Green Dome in 10 minutes (¥190).

spots.name: Yokosuka Museum of Art
spots.desc: Glass-clad museum with views over Tokyo Bay, housing modern & contemporary paintings & sculpture.

spots.name: Saitama Museum of Modern Art
spots.desc: A museum of modern art featuring works by famous painters, such as Monet, Picasso, and Chagall.

spots.name: Shinkyō Bridge
spots.desc: This much-photographed red bridge separates the shrines from the town of Nikko. In feudal times, only the shogun was permitted to cross the bridge, and even today it's barred from pedestrian traffic — although there's a 4-lane highway rumbling right past. You can get a nice view from the sidewalk, but to set foot on the bridge and look down into the gorge below, you'll have to buy a…

spots.name: Jindaiji Temple
spots.desc: This temple of the Tendai sect, constructed in 733, is nearly the oldest in the Tokyo area, second only to Sensoji in Asakusa. Although the temple building itself is modest, the surrounding village of food stands, soba restaurants and waterwheels evokes an image of Edo-period Japan, and makes Jindaiji Temple a hidden gem in suburban Tokyo. The temple complex houses a bronze statue of Shaka…

spots.name: Tobu Museum
spots.desc: A museum of railways and buses, operated by Tobu Railway. At the museum, visitors can also see trains running through Higashi Mukojima Station, which is located directly above the museum.

spots.name: Jōkan-ji
spots.desc: Arguably the most visible reminder of the tragedy of the lives of the prostitutes who lived and worked in Yoshiwara. This is where many of the prostitutes were buried when they died, as the brothels would just unceremoniously dump their corpses at the back entrance to the temple.

spots.name: Kabuki theatre
spots.desc: An experience worth checking out. Check times and prices at the Hakata-za near Nakasu. If you don't want to stay for the whole show, or don't have so much money to spend, you can watch part of a show for about ¥800; see here for details. Half price student/young (~25) adult tickets may be available day of performance to be released 20 minutes prior to the show; see here for details.

spots.name: Canal City
spots.desc: This uniquely designed mall houses a wide range of stores, but is somewhat faded with the main action having moved to the new malls attached to Hakata Station. Nevertheless, it includes clothing stores, restaurants, rare character shops - including a Studio Ghibli goods shop - and even a well-appointed theatre. If you have time, be sure to catch one of the hourly fountain shows held in the centre…

spots.name: Museum of the Meiji Restoration
spots.desc: A museum about the Meiji restoration and its relationship with the local history. An excellent audio-guide in English is available for free. In the basement, projections (25 min) and robot animations (20 min) relating this period are presented hourly, with English translation though the audio-guide. Allow between 1.5 and 2 hours.

spots.name: Kagoshima City Aquarium
spots.local: いおワールドかごしま水族館
spots.desc: 1500¥ for adults (September 2025) 5 floors of exhibits. Of note, has 7 dolphins, 2 seals, and a whale shark. Closes 6pm.

spots.name: Grass-covered tram lines
spots.desc: The city core of Kagoshima has sections of tramways laid with grass. The city's tram network has its main claim to fame as the world's first lawn-mowing train.

spots.name: Kofuku-ji
spots.desc: This was the first Obaku Zen temple in Japan, established around 1620, and Nagasaki residents often call it the "red temple". It was used by many Chinese for over 3 centuries, and is one of the few historical places to escape damage from the atomic bombing.

spots.name: Japan Folk Crafts Museum
spots.desc: Founded in 1936. Must see for Japanese handicraft lovers.

spots.name: Tahara Castle Ruins
spots.desc: The castle was built around 1480; the grounds now house a small municipal museum.

spots.name: Hida Folk Village
spots.desc: An attractive open-air museum assembled from real buildings that effectively recreates an entire traditional mountain village. Artisans continue to work in many buildings; you can buy their crafts and even try your own hand at a number of activities. The architectural highlights are the traditional thatched-roof gasshō-zukuri houses, built with roofs like hands in prayer to withstand the heavy…
spots.price: ¥700 entry, or ¥930 for entry with bus ticket from and to JR Takayama Station

spots.name: Nanao Art Museum
spots.desc: Nanao was the birthplace of Tohaku Hasegawa (長谷川等伯), who was a well known Japanese master painter. They have annual exhibitions related to his works. You can also see many local artists' works there. Worth checking out if you have some free time.
spots.price: Tickets range from free to ¥800, depending on the event

spots.name: Kurobe Gorge Railway
spots.desc: This sightseeing railway runs through the steep, forested valleys of the Kurobe Gorge in the Northern Japanese Alps. The open-sided trolley trains cross more than 20 bridges and pass through over 40 tunnels, offering views of the Kurobe River, cliffs and mountain forests. The full 20-km journey from Unazuki to Keyakidaira takes about 80 minutes each way. The railway normally operates from late…

spots.name: Seihakuji
spots.desc: A temple first constructed in 1333, the butsudan has been designated as one of Japan's National Treasures.

spots.name: Ashikajima Station
spots.desc: Easternmost train station in the Kanto region. Also has a tiny, one-room art museum (open Sa, Su and holidays 09:00-17:00).

spots.name: Sekiyado Castle
spots.desc: a Japanese castle built in 1590 by Matsudaira Yasumoto. It was demolished in 1875 and again reconstructed in 1995 to boost local tourism and to function as an annex to the local Sekiyado Castle Museum. However, the reconstructed buildings are not on the original foundations, nor are the buildings historically accurate.

spots.name: Okawa Museum of Art
spots.desc: The Okawa Museum of Art opened in April 1989 overlooking the city of Kiryu, a textile center. About 1,600 works of art have been collected over a period of 40 years by the museum's founder, Eiji Okawa. The museum, deceptively small on first notice, is built in stages on the hillside and provides its visitors with an amazing number of rooms to peruse its incredibly rich collection. Largest…
spots.price: adults:¥1,000, university/high school students: ¥600, jr high / elementary school students:¥300

spots.name: Chichibu Night Festival
spots.desc: Held every year on December 2nd and 3rd, with the main parade of floats on the 3rd.

spots.name: Jyakoten
spots.desc: Uwajima is well-known for this flat, oval fish cake made by processing fish (with bones and all). It is tasty, but has a gritty texture to it.

spots.name: Jōdogahama Beach
spots.desc: Jōdogahama beach is the only real attraction around Miyako, but it alone is worth planning a stopover in the city. Jōdo in Buddhism is equivalent to "Heaven" in Christianity. There are also some nice hiking trails around the same area. The beach Visitor Center is about a 15-minute ride from the Miyako train station; the local Kenpoku Bus runs 1-2 times an hour. The last bus goes back soon after…

spots.name: Hakushu Distillery
spots.desc: A Japanese whisky distillery.

spots.name: Suwahara Castle ruins
spots.desc: The ruins of this Sengoku period yamashiro-style Japanese castle in the Kanaya neighborhood are a protected national historic site. The original plan of this 300 m by 200 m castle clearly remains. The site is about a 30-minute walk from Kanaya Station on the JR East Tokaido Main Line.

spots.name: Oshino Hakkai
spots.desc: Oshino Hakkai is a group of eight clear spring-fed ponds in Oshino village, between Lake Yamanaka and Lake Kawaguchi at the foot of Mount Fuji. The ponds are fed by snowmelt filtered through the mountain's volcanic rock, a process that can take decades. Considered sacred in traditional Fuji worship, they were once used by pilgrims for ritual purification before climbing the mountain. The village…

spots.name: Daizen-ji Temple
spots.desc: Daizen-ji is a Buddhist temple best known for its Main Hall (Kondō), a National Treasure built in 1286 during the Kamakura period. The hall is one of the oldest surviving wooden temple buildings in Yamanashi Prefecture and is an unusually well-preserved example of medieval Japanese architecture. The temple is also known for its association with grape cultivation and is sometimes called the "Grape…

spots.name: Erin-ji Temple
spots.desc: Erin-ji Temple is a Zen Buddhist temple associated with the warlord Takeda Shingen, who made it his family temple. Founded in the 14th century, it is known for its traditional gardens, historic buildings and connection to the Takeda clan. After Shingen's death, the temple became a place of commemoration for the famous warrior. In 1582, it was burned by forces of Oda Nobunaga, and its abbot…

spots.name: Miyao Castle
spots.desc: A hill fort built in the early 16th century, it was a key focus of the 1555 Battle of Miyajima as part of the Mōri army’s offensive against Sue Harukata. It appears to have declined after that, and the site is now marked by a small park with an explanatory signboard, a small shrine and a pavilion.

spots.name: Hōrinji Temple
spots.desc: One of the five head Shingon temples in Kyoto. The Boddhisatva Akasagarbha is enshrined in this temple. The complex offers a nice view of Kyoto City. The lights here are quite beautiful during the autumn Kyoto Light-Up.

spots.name: Enoshima Sea Candle
spots.desc: The observation lighthouse that serves as a modern symbol of the Shonan area. From its observation floor, you can enjoy a 360-degree panoramic view of the sea, the surrounding cityscape, and Mt. Fuji (on a clear day).
spots.addr: At the top of Enoshima Island, in Samuel Cocking Garden

spots.name: Hakone Museum Of Art
spots.desc: Museum with a collection of ancient Japanese earthenware. There is also a moss garden with a tearoom.

spots.name: Shinobazu Pond
spots.desc: Full of lotus flowers and waterfowl and has the picturesque little Bentendō Hall shrine, dedicated to the goddess Benzaiten, in the middle. Outside the main entrance of the temple is a statue of Ugajin, a Japanese folk god of harvests, fertility, and wealth who is represented as a coiled serpent with a bearded man’s head.

spots.name: Kirihata-ji Temple
spots.desc: the 10th temple of the Shikoku Pilgrimage. The daitō pagoda dates from 1618.

spots.name: Kumadani-ji Temple
spots.desc: Temple 8 on the Shikoku 88 temple pilgrimage.

spots.name: Ryōzen Shrine
spots.desc: founded in 1881

spots.name: Imamiya Shrine
spots.desc: Although the current structure dates back to 1902, the original was built during the Heian Period. At the time, the city was being plagued by illness and disease, so Imamiya Shrine was built to appease the gods. Even today, many visitors come to pray for good health and to ward off illness.

spots.name: Asuka Historical Museum
spots.desc: The Asuka Historical Museum presents archaeological discoveries from the Asuka region, including stone carvings, architectural remains and artefacts from the area's ancient temples and burial sites. Exhibits explain the development of Asuka as an early political and cultural centre of Japan and help put the many scattered archaeological sites around the countryside into context. The museum is…

spots.name: Tozan Shrine
spots.desc: Famous for its porcelain archway and other items of porcelain, which are usually made of stone at other shrines. This shrine is and was particularly revered by Arita’s ceramists.

spots.name: Hotokegaura
spots.desc: Hotokegaura is the main attraction to Sai. It is a collection of odd rock formations that have sparked people's imaginations. People claim to see shapes and faces in the rocks that resemble Buddhas. The azure sea reflects off their surface creating a surrealistic atmosphere. One can easily spend an afternoon exploring them and watching the magnificent Japanese sunset. Hotokegaura can be accessed…

spots.name: Senkō-ji Temple
spots.desc: A temple of the Koyasan Shingon sect, traditionally said to have been founded by Prince Shotoku in the early 7th century. It is widely renowned for its interactive "Jigoku-do" (Hell Hall), which provides a vivid, visual depiction of Buddhist purgatory and judgment to teach the consequences of bad actions. The temple grounds also feature a small museum dedicated to retro snacks and toys from the…
spots.price: Free for the main temple grounds (¥100 entry fee for the Hell Hall)

spots.name: Kōsan-ji Temple
spots.desc: Built by an eccentric businessman to mourn the loss of his mother, this sprawling temple complex has concrete replicas of various famous Japanese buildings, earning it the nickname Nishi-no-Nikko (Nikko of the Western Japan). Other attractions include a grim replica of Buddhist hell and the dazzling white marble Miraishin no Oka (Hill of Eternal Hope).

spots.name: The Museum of Kyoto
spots.desc: The museum features many ancient artifacts relating to Kyoto life and history. It has an expansive ancient ceramics collection.
spots.price: Adults: ¥500; students: ¥400; children: free. For special exhibits: adults: ¥1,400; students: ¥1,000; children: ¥500

spots.name: KidZania Tokyo
spots.desc: "A land of kids, by kids, for kids" - where children can experience their favorite job and learn about the social system while having fun.
spots.addr: Urban Dock LaLaport Toyosu, North Port 3rd floor 33200 2-4-9 Toyosu Kōtō-ku

spots.name: Kōshō-ji Temple
spots.desc: Koshoji Temple was established in the 17th century by the Tokugawa family. The temple hosts the annual "1,000 Lantern Festival." There are numerous restaurants and universities surrounding the Koshoji Temple area.

spots.name: Daijōji Temple
spots.desc: Daijōji Temple is an old and active Zen Buddhist Temple set away from traffic on a hillside. The temple in its current location dates from 1697. Old trees shade dense moss. There is a large bell hanging under the gate along the path which visitors may ring. Strikingly loud at first, the sound fades to accentuate the tranquillity. There are free early-early-morning pray-with-the-Zen-monks sessions…

spots.name: Ishikawa Prefectural Museum
spots.desc: Entry ¥250 (more when special exhibitions are held). 09:00-17:00 (last entry at 16:30). Housed in three long brick buildings, restored armouries from the time when the area was used by the Imperial Japanese Army, it features a chronological display of local history in a modern and well-laid-out setting. There is also an area for hands-on history, where you can try on various outfits, including…

spots.name: Bandai Bridge
spots.desc: Built in 1929 at the site of the first bridge to cross the Shinano River, this bridge is a nationally Important Cultural Property.

spots.name: Atami Castle
spots.desc: While the Atami Castle was built in 1959 (the castle is, therefore, not a real historical site, but rather a tourist spot), it is still an interesting place to visit - there's a small museum collecting information about samurai, ukiyo-e (adult only), and castles in Japan. There's also a panoramic view on top, and a trick art museum there.

spots.name: Nihondaira
spots.desc: A 308-meter hill in central Shizuoka, with good views of Mt. Fuji, the Izu Peninsula, Shimizu Bay and more.

spots.name: Takeda Shingen Festival
spots.desc: A big festival to celebrate the 16th century warlord. Usually a famous Japanese TV actor plays the part of Takeda Shingen himself.

spots.name: Hiroshima National Peace Memorial Hall for the Atomic Bomb Victims
spots.local: 国立広島原爆死没者追悼平和祈念館
spots.desc: The Peace Memorial Hall is dedicated to collecting names and photographs of people who died in the blast. The entrance of the memorial hall leads downward to a quiet hall for contemplation, and then back up again to a set of kiosks with compelling stories and recollections from survivors (in English and Japanese). Like the Cenotaph and the Peace Memorial Museum, it was designed by architect Kenzo…

spots.name: Fudoin
spots.desc: Only a short trip east of the city, this 14th century temple is another of the few structures in the area to have survived the atomic blast. The Main Hall is an impressive sight, and both the bell tower and the two-story gate are regarded as cultural treasures.

spots.name: Okayama Orient Museum
spots.local: 岡山市立オリエント美術館
spots.desc: An interesting museum of Middle Eastern art. The special exhibit details art and trade between China and Persia. If you can speak conversational Japanese, talk with the friendly docents; they will present some highly interesting explanations and background. However, the dates and areas are clearly marked, and the artifacts themselves are interesting enough that you don't need to have a guide to…

spots.name: Shimane Museum of Ancient Izumo
spots.local: 島根県立古代出雲歴史博物館
spots.desc: This elegantly designed complex is near the shrine. Exhibitions feature speculative designs of the original Izumo Taisha, displays on the history and development of nearby Iwami Ginzan, and a dramatic collection of ceremonial bronze bells and swords.
spots.hours: Mar-Oct: 09:00-18:00, Nov-Feb: 09:00-17:00; closed the third Tue of each month

spots.name: Shikano Castle Ruins
spots.desc: Although none of the original castle remains, the inner and outer moats and stone columns can still be seen. It's most popular during cherry blossom season with approximately 500 trees scattered throughout the castle grounds.

spots.name: Kōkoen Garden
spots.desc: This magnificent collection of 9 Edo-period-style walled gardens was laid out in 1992 on a site where samurai houses once stood. The street plan and gated partitions preserve the appearance of the old residential quarter, except that within the various enclosures visitors find beautifully landscaped gardens and water features instead of noble residences. There is a tea arbour and a restaurant…
spots.hours: Open from 09:00 daily and closes at either 17:00 or 18:00 (last admission at 16:30 or 17:30) depending on the time of…
spots.price: ¥400 adults and ¥0 children. A ¥2,600 combination ticket gets you into both Kōkoen and Himeji Castle

spots.name: Hyogo Prefectural Museum of History
spots.desc: Unlike most prefectural museums, this one actually has very little information about Hyogo prefecture's history, and historical artifacts also tend to be lacking, so if you really want to learn more about Hyogo, you may be disappointed however, if you are interested in Japanese history as a whole, this museum is well worth visiting. It contains replicas of all twelve original castles remaining in…
spots.price: Entrance fee ¥200 (adult), ¥150 college and high school students. During special exhibitions admission changes…

spots.name: Himeji Central Park
spots.local: 姫路セントラルパーク
spots.desc: A drive-in safari park, amusement park and car racing tracks. It is possible to rent a campsite in summer months.

spots.name: Kōshō-ji Temple
spots.desc: A Zen temple that features a long, justly-famous tree-covered approach from the river. It's a lovely walk in the autumn. Kosho-ji is a working temple, so while visitors can walk the grounds, the temple buildings themselves are frequently in use. Keep quiet while you're there; zen chants hang in the air in the late afternoon.

spots.name: Mimuroto-ji Temple
spots.desc: One of the settings of the Tale of Genji, as well as the 10th temple along the Saigoku 33 Kannon Temple Pilgrimage Route. This temple will be of high interest to those who love flowers and gardens. Around the temple, lotus flowers have been planted in pots. Within the entire temple complex however, there are thousands of hydrangea, rhododendron, and azaleas all over the mountainside, and there…

spots.name: Amagase Dam
spots.desc: This dam is south of the city. A scenic walkway leads there from Uji either shore of the river and the dam itself offers nice views.

spots.name: Ruins of Kudara-dera
spots.desc: In 660 AD, the Korean kingdom of Baekje was conquered by the Silla-Tang Alliance and their last king, Uija, was taken to China as a prisoner. However, his son Buyeo Seon'gwang (Zenkō) managed to escape to Japan, where the Japanese emperor recognized him as the King of Baekje (Kudara no Konikishi). The king in exile settled around Hirakata and in 750 AD his grandson founded this temple, whose name…

spots.name: Hattori Ryokuchi Park
spots.desc: A large park, partly within the city grounds, with a number of worthwhile sights. The pretty Hattori Ryokuchi Arboretum (1-13 Terauchi) holds bamboo gardens and some 2,500 cherry trees. The Open-Air Museum of Old Japanese Farmhouses is another favourite, displaying replicas of traditional farmhouses from different parts of Japan.

spots.name: Tokyo German Village
spots.desc: Reconstructed half-timbered houses and bratwurst meals. Because why not.

spots.name: Chiba Port Tower
spots.desc: 10 minutes on foot from monorail and Keiyo line Chiba Minato station. Towers like this are a fixture of any self-respecting Japanese city, and here the observation deck (112m) offers views of the surrounding docks, at least for a kilometer or two until they fade off in the smog. Sunset is the most popular time to visit, and you can cap off your visit with all-you-can-eat BBQ at a number of…

spots.name: Aqua World Oarai
spots.local: アクアワールド・大洗
spots.desc: One of the top aquariums in the country right on the ocean, and famous among aquariums for its sunfish. Dolphin show attendance is included in admission (you may get wet). There is a gift shop, a food stand including fresh sushi (perhaps the fate of unpopular attractions?) and free parking. Bus accessible from the nearest station. On site is a nice beach popular with swimmers and surfers but the…

spots.name: Myohonji Temple
spots.desc: The cemetery contains the grave of the creator of Ultraman, a popular 1960s TV show. Fans who visit the grave place toy Ultraman action figures on his grave.

spots.name: Tenkaisan Ōya Temple
spots.desc: Home to 10 stone Buddhas carved in Central Asian style, thought to have been created by Afghan monks as part of a Japanese "silk road".

spots.name: Chidoriga-fuchi Moat
spots.desc: One of, if not the most prominent cherry blossom site in Tokyo, and attracts throngs of people in its March-to-April peak season. It is located just across the street from Yasukuni-shrine. Rowboats are also available for one to row along a limited portion of the moat at ¥500 for 30 minutes, ¥1000 for an hour and at a slightly more expensive rate during cherry blossom periods.
spots.addr: on the northwest side of the Imperial gardens grounds

spots.name: Institute for Nature Study
spots.local: 国立科学博物館附属自然教育園
spots.desc: A 200,000 sq m nature preserve in the heart of the city, with birds and waterfowl, insects and marine life.
spots.hours: Sep 1-Apr 30: 09:00-16:30, May 1-Aug 31: 09:00-17:00; closed Mondays, closed Dec 28-Jan 4
spots.price: Adults ¥300, senior citizens and children free

spots.name: Aquapark shinagawa
spots.desc: A popular aquarium with exhibits that combine dolphin shows and technology. The tunnel tank includes manta rays, green sawfish, and the only dwarf sawfish on display in the world.

spots.name: Tokyo Anime Center
spots.desc: Offers information, showings, demonstrations, and events centered around animation and gaming. In the recording studio, visitors can experience a post-recording on certain days.

spots.name: Tobacco and Salt Museum
spots.desc: This peculiar institution owes its existence to Japan's government monopoly on these two substances. The website advises that "dangerous substances are not permitted within the museum". They have map-guides of the museum in English and most exhibits have English translations. There is a free mobile-app based auto tour as well.

spots.name: Asakura Museum of Sculpture
spots.desc: Sculptor Asakura Fumio (Artist name Kōso 1883-1964) designed this atmospheric house himself. It combined his original Japanese home and garden with a large studio that incorporated vaulted ceilings, a 'sunrise room' and a rooftop garden with wonderful neighbourhood views. It's now a reverential museum with many artist's signature realist works, mostly of people and cats, on display. This is a…

spots.name: Kōgan-ji Temple
spots.desc: This small temple in Sugamo is known for two statues: Togenuki Jizō, who heals sick children, and the boddhisattva Kannon, who will cure your pains if you wash themagical appropriate part of the statue. More morbidly, you can also pray to Kannon for a swift and painless death, so you will not be a burden to your relatives in your old age. Visitors pray Enmei Jizōson for their health too. The way…

spots.name: Hiraodai
spots.desc: A rare karst plateau in Kokura Minami ward, 30-40 minutes by car from Kokura station. The grassy mountains are covered with large gray round rocks which the locals will tell you look like sheep grazing. Great for walks, hiking and camping. Caves can also be visited and the Shonyudo cave is not to be missed - wade through ice cold water in midsummer. There is no direct public transportation to…

spots.name: Aoshima Shrine
spots.desc: The shrine is on an island accessible by bridge. It was once considered so sacred that people were forbidden to even step foot on the island. It was not open to the public until 1737. Aoshima Shrine is dedicated to wedded gods so is unsurprisingly a shrine for marriage. The rock layers pointing dramatically up from the sea along the island by the shrine's torii gate are unique and interesting…

spots.name: Sadowara Castle
spots.desc: It is not known when or who built the original castle, but it was expanded by Yoshisuke Ito and used as his residence. One of the palace buildings has been rebuilt as the Sadowara History and Folk Museum (also free). The rest of the former castle can be seen via walking trails on and around the hill.

spots.name: Oita Prefectural Art Museum
spots.desc: Built by renowned architect Shigeru Ban, the building is as much of an attraction as the art inside. The museum's permanent collection contains over 3,000 works from artists from around Oita Prefecture. There are also special exhibits, including international exhibits, that change throughout the year.
spots.price: ¥300 for permanent collection, additional costs for special exhibits

spots.name: Iyo Kokubun-ji
spots.desc: This is the former head temple of Iyo Province. It's now the 59th temple of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage.

spots.name: Oyakuen Garden
spots.desc: Built in 1670 as a garden for a teahouse for the lords of Aizu. The garden is well known for growing medicinal herbs - around 400 kinds of herbs are still grown.

spots.name: Tohoku University Museum of Natural History
spots.local: 東北大学総合学術博物館
spots.desc: Showcases a wide array of specimens from the university's research in earth sciences, featuring complete skeletons of a Stegosaurus, Fukuiraptor, and a Sei whale, alongside a comprehensive collection of fossils and minerals that illustrate 2 billion years of evolution and Earth's changes.

spots.name: Takebe Shrine
spots.desc: This was once the head shrine of Omi Province.

spots.name: Jion-ji
spots.desc: The 12th temple of the Bandō 33 Temple Pilgrimage.

spots.name: Tōchō-ji
spots.desc: It has a 10.8-m wooden Great Buddha.
spots.price: Free entry; ¥100 to see the Buddha

spots.name: Senyū-ji
spots.desc: The 58th temple of the Shikoku Pilgrimage.

spots.name: Motorcar Museum of Japan
spots.desc: This large red brick building has an area of and displays in the region of 500 vehicles all in working condition. Collected from both inside and outside of Japan including a Ford Model T. The museum has a restaurant, a shop and an amazing collection of toilets from all over the world that can be used if the need arises!

spots.name: Hirayama Ikuo Silk Road Museum
spots.local: 平山郁夫シルクロード美術館
spots.desc: Features the famous Silk Road paintings by Hirayama Ikuo along with artifacts from various places along the Silk Road.
spots.hours: 10:00-17:00; closed in winter (late December to early March)

spots.name: Kanjōsan Castle Ruins
spots.desc: Remains of a Muromachi period castle built in the 13th century.

spots.name: Ikoma Shrine
spots.local: 往馬坐伊古麻都比古神社
spots.desc: A shrine set beneath a forest with wooden structures and brass lanterns, this shrine was built in the 5th century and is dedicated to seven gods. It also hosts an annual fire festival, registered as one of Japan's intangible cultural assets.

spots.name: Fukiware Falls
spots.desc: Fukiware Falls is a broad, 7-m-high waterfall where the Katashina River plunges into a narrow fissure in the rock, creating the impression of a giant split in the riverbed. Often called the “Niagara of Japan”, the falls were formed by erosion of soft volcanic rock and stretch approximately 30 m across. Walking trails follow the river through a forested gorge, with several viewing points…

spots.name: Ashikaga Flower Park
spots.local: あしかがフラワーパーク
spots.desc: A 20-acre park most famous for its four huge wisteria arbors, in bloom from mid April to mid May, the park contains such a wide variety of flowers and trees that it is worth seeing in any season: plum blossoms in February–March, hydrangeas in June–July, lotus flowers in May–October, purple sage in October–November, and roses in May–June and September–November Lights adorn the trees in midwinter.…
spots.hours: The opening time will change according to the season.
spots.price: The admission fee changes according to the season

spots.name: Kurita Museum
spots.desc: A beautifully landscaped 24-acre park whose carefully designed buildings house one of the finest and largest collections of Imari and Nabeshima porcelain in the world. Other exhibits include historical and archaeological information. There is also a small atelier and a climbing kiln near the base of the hill, and a working (but off-limits) potters' village behind the sprawling complex. The gift…
spots.hours: Daily except at New Year's 10:00-17:00 (18:00 on Sundays and holidays)

spots.name: Kanyoa Air Base Museum
spots.desc: Imperial Japanese Navy exhibition of the history of the era to the present day of the Maritime Self-Defense Force. There are also aircraft on display and many exhibits related to the kamikaze corps.

spots.name: Uwajima City Historical Museum
spots.local: 宇和島市立歴史資料館
spots.desc: One of the first Western-style buildings in Ehime Prefecture, it serves as a museum dedicated to the history of Uwajima. It is designated as a Registered Tangible Cultural Property.

spots.name: Yokote Castle
spots.desc: The original castle was burned down in the Boshin War. Although the reconstructed castle has a keep, the original castle had a palace but not a keep.

spots.name: Kunohe Castle
spots.desc: The site was believed to have been the site of the final battle in Toyotomi Hideyoshi's campaign to unify Japan. Nobunao Nanbu was chosen by Toyotomi to take Ninohe Castle, but Masazane Kunohe whose family built the castle in 1501 would not relinquish the territory. Nanbu sent 65,000 troops to force Kunohe out.

spots.name: Agena Park and Castle
spots.desc: Park with some remains of 14th century castle.

spots.name: Hōkyōji
spots.desc: Founded by the 13th-century Chinese Zen monk Jiyuan (better known as Jakuen) after he left Eiheiji, this beautiful Sōtō Zen temple in the hills on the outskirts of the town displays an original self-portrait of Zen Master Dogen.

spots.name: Kozenji Temple
spots.desc: The old Buddhist temple is hidden in lush, green forest. The atmosphere is very calm and relaxing.

spots.name: Miyajima Public Aquarium
spots.desc: A collection of more than 380 sea creatures and daily animal events such as sea lion shows and photo opportunities with penguins. It's worth a stop if you have restless kids in tow — about a 20-minute walk from the pier.

spots.name: Akiyoshi Cave
spots.desc: Towards the southern end of Akiyoshidai is the Akiyoshido cave, named by Emperor Hirohito in 1926 when he was crown prince. This cave is up to 100 m wide and has almost 9 km of passages, making it the longest in Japan and one of the longest in Asia. An approximately 1 km-long section of the cave is open to the public as a sightseeing course, with a walkway and bridge system, entering at the…

spots.name: Hosomi Art Museum
spots.desc: A museum that showcases Japanese religious art from all periods of history. Exhibits change each season but typically feature famous artwork from local temples and shrines.
spots.price: Prices vary depending on the exhibit

spots.name: Ryōzen Kannon Statue
spots.desc: A memorial to the unknown Japanese soldiers who died in World War II, with a 24-meter-tall statue of Kannon.
spots.price: Admission is ¥200, including a lit incense stick to place in front of the temple

spots.name: Ryozen History Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to displaying artifacts and information about the Meiji Period.

spots.name: Tempozan Ferris Wheel
spots.desc: One of the largest Ferris wheels, overlooking Osaka Bay and surrounding areas such as Mount Ikoma to the east, Akashi Kaikyō Bridge to the west, Kansai International Airport to the south, and the Rokko Mountains to the north. 17-minute ride. There is an option of a gondola with a see-through floor for no additional cost, but lines for these gondolas tend to be dramatically longer as they are…

spots.name: Suigo Sawara Aquatic Botanical Garden
spots.local: 水郷佐原あやめパーク
spots.desc: Around 1.5 million irises of 400 different breeds bloom in late May to early June. There are also many other plants such as lotuses and water lilies. It is open daily except on Monday.

spots.name: Shirakawa no seki
spots.desc: Believed to be the site of the ancient barrier between the unconquered north and the capital region of Kanto to the south. The poet Basho is said to have visited here.
spots.addr: in a park to the south of the city

spots.name: Enoshima Samuel Cocking Garden
spots.local: 江の島サムエル・コッキング苑
spots.desc: A botanical garden and park facility at the summit of Enoshima, which houses the Enoshima Sea Candle. The garden features seasonal plants, plazas inspired by Fujisawa's sister cities, several cafes and shops, and the historic ruins of a large greenhouse built in the Meiji era. It is particularly famous for its spectacular seasonal light-up events held at night.
spots.hours: 9:00–20:00 (Last admission 19:30). Hours may be extended for special events.
spots.price: Free. During events after 17:00: Adults 500, children 250.
spots.addr: At the top of Enoshima Island

spots.name: Asago Art Village
spots.desc: A large sculpture park and museum.

spots.name: Hōsen-in
spots.desc: Like Yogen-in in Higashiyama, the ceiling of Hosen-in was built using the floorboards of Fushimi Castle, where a bloody historic battle took place. As a result, you'll notice blood stains on the ceiling. Outside, there is a charming garden containing a famous 700-year-old pine tree.

spots.name: Chiriku Hachiman Shrine
spots.desc: A Hachiman shrine, dedicated to the kami Hachiman. It was established in 724.

spots.name: Ōjima island
spots.desc: Where is located Tatami Ishi (畳石), an arrangement of stones in pentagonal and hexagonal shapes, resembling a carapace.

spots.name: Lee Ufan Museum
spots.desc: Also designed by Tadao Ando, this museum displays only the works of Lee Ufan 李禹煥.
spots.hours: Oct—Feb: Tue-Sun 10:00—17:00, Mar—Sep: Tue-Sun 10:00—18:00; closed on the following day of a public holiday

spots.name: Entsū-in
spots.desc: Entsū-in is a Buddhist temple that was founded in 1647 as a mausoleum for Mitsumune, the grandson of the powerful feudal lord Date Masamune. The temple is known for its traditional gardens and a small mausoleum decorated with intricate paintings.

spots.name: Midono-juku
spots.desc: The 41st post town on the Nakasendo.

spots.name: Tokyo Budokan
spots.desc: A very distinctive architecture by the famous Japanese architect Kijō Rokkaku.

spots.name: Shibamata
spots.desc: In Katsushika-ku, it features Taishakuten Temple (帝釈天) with its cozy shopping street that rivals Asakusa in liveliness while being much more authentic, lacking the overseas-tourist kitsch. The district's biggest claim to fame is being the setting for "Otoko wa tsurai yo", Japan's longest-running movie series, and the hero of the series, Tora-san, can be seen every block of the way from the…

spots.name: Diamond and Flower Ferris Wheel
spots.local: ダイヤと花の大観覧車
spots.desc: The park's most visible landmark is the Diamond and Flowers Ferris Wheel, so named due to its light shows that give it the appearance of a sparkling diamond or flower. At 117 meter tall it is the second tallest Ferris wheel in Japan. The top offers views of Tokyo Bay, Tokyo Disney Resorts, Chiba and as far away as Mt. Fuji.
spots.hours: Mon-Fri 10:00-20:00, Sat Sun 10:00-21:00, closed one or two days per month

spots.name: small worlds
spots.local: ミニチュアミュージアムスモールワールズ
spots.desc: Indoor miniature world, including futuristic scenes.

spots.name: Shiroyama Hakusan Shrine
spots.desc: Formerly the Suemori Castle, the present day Shrine hosts festivals that feature Japanese dance and music.

spots.name: Danpusan Kofun
spots.desc: The Dampusan Kofun is a large keyhole-shaped kofun burial mound located within the grounds of the Atsuta Shrine.

spots.name: Higashi-Chayagai
spots.desc: Across the Asano River, Kanazawa's most famous geisha district. Many of the tall narrow houses are still used as high-class entertainment, but the Shima House (¥400) is open for all to see, and is well worth the entry fee for a chance to experience its refined and elegant atmosphere. Quite a few of the buildings have been converted into speciality shops and teahouses (of the non-geisha variety)…

spots.name: Ishikawa Prefectural Museum of Traditional Arts and Crafts
spots.local: 石川県立伝統産業工芸館
spots.desc: A craft museum that displays 36 types of traditional arts and crafts cultivated by the people who lived in Ishikawa. The exhibits are grouped by type and well-displayed.
spots.hours: Daily 09:00-17:00 (last entry at 16:30); closed Apr-Nov: 3rd Thu of the month; Dec-Mar: Thu, Year-end and New Year
spots.price: ¥250, ¥200 for seniors, and ¥100 for children under 17. Group rates are available

spots.name: Northern Culture Museum
spots.desc: Built as a wealthy family's home in 1885-1887. The museum comprises several buildings, and a few restaurants/cafes. Documents and art collections including paintings and sculptures from former households are on display. It is worth at least a half day visit.

spots.name: Shosenkyo Gorge
spots.desc: This is considered to be the most beautiful gorge in Japan. It is part of the Chichibu-Tama-Kai National Park.

spots.name: International Conference Center
spots.desc: At the south end of the Peace Park, this complex of buildings has an International Exchange Lounge with English-language publications and city information; it also has the Restaurant Serenade (10:00-19:00).

spots.name: Hiroshima Children's Museum
spots.local: 広島市こども文化科学館
spots.desc: Great fun for kids, with hand-on science exhibits and a planetarium on the top floor. There's also a library with a few shelves of English language books.

spots.name: Sake Festival
spots.desc: The suburb of Saijo is famous for its sake breweries and this annual boozy blow-out. For the price of entry, attendees can drink their fill of sake from local breweries. In short order, the festival area turns into a wild (yet reasonably well-behaved) display of public drunkenness involving people of all ages. Outside the festival area, tours of sake breweries are also available, with wood sake…
spots.price: Tickets ¥1000 in advance, ¥1500 at the festival

spots.name: Okonomi-mura
spots.desc: Three floors packed with no less than 27 okonomiyaki shops. This, indeed, is Hiroshima culinary nirvana. They all serve beer and okonomiyaki with some variations (kimchi, oysters, etc.), and they'll all start clamoring for your business as soon as you walk through the door. It's right behind PARCO, with a distinctive 'Okonomi-mura' arch out front.
spots.hours: The shops keep their own hours, but most will be open around 11:00, and a few stay open until 02:00-03:00

spots.name: Hayashibara Museum of Art
spots.desc: A small museum which houses the private collection of the Ikeda Family, the former Lords of Okayama. The collection features Japanese and Chinese works, primarily calligraphy and scrolls. Pottery, beautiful textiles, samurai armor, and other works may also be on display; however, because the museum is not large enough to display the entire collection at once, the exhibits are rotated often.

spots.name: Yumeji Art Museum
spots.desc: A museum featuring the works of Okayama-born artist Yumeji Takehisa, a well-known artist throughout Japan. He is best known for producing paintings and sketches of beautiful women, and many such works are on display in the museum.

spots.name: Okhotsk Ryūhyō Museum
spots.desc: A museum devoted to pack ice, a common phenomenon in the Okhotsk Sea but for some reason a subject of fascination among the Japanese. Here you will learn all you ever wanted to know and more about pack ice, and even get a chance to touch some in a room kept at -15 °C (5 °F) (coats provided).

spots.name: Kushiro City Museum
spots.desc: The museum is on a hill overlooking Lake Harutori and its architecture is said to represent a Japanese crane spreading its wings. The museum has many excellent exhibits representing the natural history of the area and there are both Japanese and English explanations. One can garner a greater appreciation of the area by spending just an hour in this excellent museum..

spots.name: Nusamai Bridge
spots.desc: Nusamai Bridge is located near Kushiro Fisherman's Wharf MOO. It is said to be one of the most beautiful bridges in Hokkaido. The atmosphere around Nusamai Bridge is very romantic with street lamps and bronze statues symbolizing the four seasons. It is especially lovely at dusk and as the sunsets the views around Nusamai Bridge are simply beautiful. It takes about 10 minutes to walk from Kushiro…

spots.name: Himeji City Museum of Art
spots.desc: Features artwork from local artists and European art, along with special exhibitions.

spots.name: Yoshikien Garden
spots.desc: Really nice garden that is worth a visit because it is free. Can be coupled with the Isui-en Garden as the entrances are right beside each other.

spots.name: Asahi Group Oyamazaki Villa Art Museum
spots.local: アサヒグループ大山崎山荘美術館
spots.desc: The elaborate Gothic-Tudor villa of wealthy businessman Shotaro Kaga, now turned into an elegant art museum showcasing mostly Taisho-era art from the 1920s. Has a rather jarring modern annex by Tadao Ando bolted on, with three works by Monet. The coffee shop serves Taisho era delicacies like hot Calpis and azuki bean chiffon cake.

spots.name: Gichu-ji Temple
spots.desc: The burial place of famed haiku poet Matsuo Bashō, of Narrow Road to the Deep North fame. The temple is 300 m away from JR Zeze Station (膳所駅), one stop from Otsu on the JR Tokaido Line.

spots.name: Shōrinzan Daruma Temple
spots.desc: Famous for being the place where daruma dolls originated. The temple itself is nice, although nothing too special. The small museum of old daruma dolls beside the main temple is interesting.

spots.name: Yokohama Port Opening Memorial Hall
spots.desc: Historic red-brick building near the waterfront in Yokohama, completed in 1917 to commemorate the opening of the port. Nicknamed the “Jack Tower,” it features an elegant clock tower and distinctive early 20th-century Western-style architecture. Today it serves as a cultural venue and event space, with parts of the interior occasionally open to visitors.

spots.name: Kishine Park
spots.desc: A large park 9 min away from Yokohama Stn, this is strictly for the locals most of the year, but very popular during cherry blossom season.

spots.name: Motomachi
spots.desc: (元町) is a small but fashionable shopping district located near Chinatown. Get off at Minato Mirai line "Motomachi-Chinatown" station or JR line "Ishikawacho" station.

spots.name: Kashiya-yokocho
spots.desc: It was prospering as temple town of Youjyuin and one of the places which started to make dagashi (cheap sweets). In the beginning of Showa period, in its peak, there were about 70 shops. It is still mirthful and selling cheap sweets, and including those made from sweet potato, one of the well-known products of Kawagoe.

spots.name: Saitama Prefectural Museum of History and Folklore
spots.local: 埼玉県立歴史と民俗の博物館
spots.desc: Exhibits artifacts from around Saitama Prefecture with information about its history and culture.

spots.name: Ōmiya kōen
spots.desc: The first prefectural park in Saitama, later expanded twice to become a very big park. There is a small zoo, swimming pool, amusement park, soccer field, museum and archery ground in the park, making it enjoyable for all ages. In the spring, many people enjoy cherry-blossom viewing there.

spots.name: Seibuen Yuenchi
spots.desc: Seibuen Yuenchi is a long-standing amusement and water park since 1950. A water park opens in the summer. Winter activities include outdoor ice skating and a trout fishing pond.
spots.price: One day pass ¥4900 for adults, ¥3600 for children (free for under 3)

spots.name: Tamozawa Imperial Villa Memorial Park
spots.local: 日光田母沢御用邸記念公園
spots.desc: Built for the Emperor Taisho in 1899, the former imperial villa also served as a hide-out for Hirohito during World War II.

spots.name: Nikko Botanical Garden
spots.desc: Has plenty of the local flora and gardens that were said to be favorites of the Emperor Taisho. It's now an adjunct to Tokyo University.

spots.name: Futaarayama Shrine
spots.desc: This is probably the most popular shrine in Utsunomiya. The front is lined by a massive stairway several stories in height before ending at a large temple. Excellent for pictures and very convenient.

spots.name: Suginami Animation Museum
spots.local: 杉並アニメーションミュージアム
spots.desc: Suginami Animation Museum is for general animation. It shows animation and also gives people hands-on experience of making their own animation.

spots.name: Sumo Museum
spots.desc: A small, quirky museum tucked inside the arena's first floor, dedicated to the history of sumo, particularly artifacts and ceremonial clothing, almost entirely in Japanese only. The collection rotates several times a year. During sumo tournaments, it is open daily, but only to tournament ticket holders.
spots.addr: first floor of the Ryogoku Kokugikan

spots.name: Namja Town
spots.desc: The Namja Town has many attractions. For example there are some Japanese style haunted houses, interactive 1964 shooting games, egg-raising game (the whole process is quite similar to raising a child, where you will need to take the egg to toilets, restaurants, and hospitals, until after a certain point. Then you can take the eggs to play games. This is quite a 'couply' game to do). And there are…

spots.name: Itazuke Ruins Yayoi-kan Museum
spots.desc: Itazuke Ruins and Yayoi-kan Museum is an important archaeological site associated with the Yayoi period, when wet-rice agriculture and new technologies transformed Japanese society. The site contains the remains of an early rice-farming settlement, including reconstructed houses, a moat and rice paddies. Archaeological discoveries include pottery, stone tools and evidence of rice cultivation. The…

spots.name: Nagashima Museum
spots.desc: Art museum that contains works of Marc Chagall, Auguste Rodin, and Kuroda Seiki.

spots.name: Nankobo
spots.desc: In spite of its small size, it is a must-visit for Shikoku Pilgrims, as it is temple number 55 of the pilgrimage.

spots.name: Isaniwa Shrine
spots.desc: Sitting upon Dōgo Hill and accessible by car or climbing 135 stone steps, this important cultural asset is one of three great examples of Shinto Hachiman-zukuri (God of War) architecture in Japan. It was promised by the lord of Matsuyama Castle, Matsudaira Sadanaga (松平定長), if the gods awarded him victory in the 1667 Edo Castle Yabusame (horseback archery) competition. The outer walls are modeled…

spots.name: Takamatsu Art Museum
spots.desc: The permanent exhibit is rather small, although it does contain a smattering of works by famous artists, such as Andy Warhol. The main draw and what most of the museum is dedicated to, are the special exhibits which change every few months.
spots.price: Permanent exhibit ¥200, special exhibits are priced separately

spots.name: Zuirakuen Garden
spots.desc: A study garden created by the Toma Family, a wealthy farming family that served the local lord of Tsugaru during the feudal period.

spots.name: Nisshinkan
spots.desc: A former school of the Aizu Clan built in 1803. Known as a "samurai school", the boys who attended had lessons in academics, martial arts, and culture in order to make them proper moral citizens and soldiers. Some of the byakkotai boys who fought in the Boshin War were students here. It has been converted into a museum where you can learn about daily life at the school. Visitors can participate…

spots.name: Tohoku University Botanical Gardens
spots.local: 東北大学学術資源研究公開センター植物園
spots.desc: Botanical garden with 800+ species, with a focus on willows and alpine plants.

spots.name: Miyakoh Botanic Garden Aoshima
spots.desc: Also known as Aoshima Subtropical Botanical Garden (青島亜熱帯植物園), it's a pleasant and surprisingly free garden that is nice for strolling around and relaxing. There is a greenhouse within the garden that visitors may also enter.

spots.name: Tsuruga Castle
spots.desc: Built in 1384, this was the site of one of the last battles of the Boshin War between samurai fighting for the shogunate and new government forces formed during the Meiji Restoration of 1868. While the castle is a concrete reconstruction (there are very few original castles left in Japan), it remains an impressive attraction thanks to its large scale, unique red roof, and natural and historical…

spots.name: Taiseishōgun-ji
spots.desc: Buddhist temple founded in 587

spots.name: Funabashi Racecourse
spots.desc: NAR racecourse run by Chiba Prefecture. Meet on weekdays.

spots.name: Hachikokuyama Nature Park
spots.desc: Best known for being the inspiration for Totoro.

spots.name: Taki-no-jo (Waterfall Castle) Ruins
spots.desc: Ruins of a 16c (Sengoku era) castle.

spots.name: Jonanjima Seaside Park
spots.desc: Reservations requested by phone, can BBQ, and camping.

spots.name: Tamagawa Modern Art Museum
spots.local: 今治市玉川近代美術館

spots.name: Enmei-ji
spots.desc: The 54th temple of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage.

spots.name: Taisan-ji
spots.desc: The 56th temple of the Shikoku Pilgrimage.

spots.name: Eifuku-ji
spots.desc: The 57th temple of the Shikoku Pilgrimage.

spots.name: Ruins of Komaru Castle
spots.desc: Komaru Castle was built by Oda Nobunaga’s follower, Sassa Narimasa, from 1575 to 1581. Here you can still see the foundations, part of the gate, and some roof tiles on which stories about the Buddhist revolts against Oda’s repression were written.

spots.name: Heisenji Hakusan Shrine
spots.desc: A 1300-year-old complex of multiple religious buildings and ruins, surrounded by tall trees. Renowned for beautiful stone pavement. Quiet and sacred atmosphere. Once an influential head temple to worshippers of Mount Hakusan, the temple-shrine complex was a gate into the worshippers' road to the sacred mountain.

spots.name: Katsuyama Castle
spots.desc: Built in 1992, supposedly the tallest castle in Japan. Similar to Echizen Daibutsu, it has little historical significance, but it's still an impressive structure to look at.

spots.name: Ishikawa Aviation Plaza
spots.desc: If time permits, there is an interesting and free aircraft museum just opposite the airport, a short walk from the arrivals hall. It houses several exhibits on the history of Japanese aviation, and about a dozen actual (small) aircraft. The souvenir shop sells some unique souvenirs, largely based on the Sixth Air Group that occupies Komatsu Air Base (Komatsu Kichi), which shares the runway with…

spots.name: Kurobe Gorge
spots.desc: Notable for having a unique truck train that goes about half way up the gorge, but also for great hiking and hot springs.

spots.name: Reverberating Furnace
spots.desc: This massive furnace was built in 1858 for the production of modern weapons, but rarely used. It's partially in ruins today, but still an impressive sight.

spots.name: Mōri Museum
spots.desc: Formerly the residence of the Mōri Clan, this museum houses four of Japan's National Treasures.

spots.name: Hell Valley
spots.desc: Sulphurous volcanic pits and geysers. Included in the Japanese Ministry of Environment`s top 100 areas of fragrance and scenery!

spots.name: Yatsu-higata tidal flat
spots.desc: A Ramsar Site and protected wetlands for migratory birds. The spring and summer months see an increase of jellyfish and small crabs to the wetlands.

spots.name: Kawamura Memorial DIC Museum of Art
spots.desc: World-class museum with more than 1000 works collected by the Japanese resin and ink manufacturer DIC Corporation.

spots.name: Ōita Prefectural Museum of History
spots.desc: Collection organised around themes including life and ancient Buddhism in Toyo no kuni and the Kunisaki peninsula, and the culture of Usa Hachiman-gū and Fuki-ji.

spots.name: Cape Agarizaki
spots.desc: The kanji mean East Cape, but the reading of the name refers to the rising sun. You can observe it from a cliff. On a clear day, if you're lucky, you can see the coast of Iriomote. Also a grazing area, many Yonaguni horses can be found here.
spots.addr: at the east tip of the island

spots.name: Omaezaki Lighthouse
spots.desc: Built in 1874.

spots.name: Inubōsaki Lighthouse
spots.desc: The most visited lighthouse in Japan, completed in 1874.
spots.hours: Mar-Sep Daily 08:30-17:00, Oct-Feb Daily 08:30-16:00 (closed in inclement weather)
spots.price: Adults ¥300, elementary school and younger free

spots.name: Byōbugaura
spots.desc: See the steep cliff caused by wave erosion.

spots.name: Nishishiiya Falls
spots.desc: Waterfall

spots.name: African Safari
spots.local: 九州自然動物公園アフリカンサファリ

spots.name: Naegi Castle Ruins
spots.desc: Ruins of a castle built in the 1500s with nice views of the surrounding area and Kiso River

spots.name: Momijidani Park
spots.desc: The ropeway station is in the middle of Momijidani Park, but the park is worth a stroll even if you're not headed up. Known for its autumn colors, there are quite a few quiet little temples to explore along the way, and many of the island's hotels are tucked away here.

spots.name: Unzen Onsen
spots.desc: A highly acidic sulfuric hot spring. In addition to sulfur, the mineral content includes aluminum, iron, and sulfate. The water temperature is 98 °C, and the hot carbonate and hydrogen sulfide gasses that erupt from the springs can be as high as 120 °C.

spots.name: Obama Onsen
spots.desc: The hot spring system known for having the hottest and most active springs in Japan, with some of them reaching 80-105 °C and producing over 15,000 tons of hot water daily. The hot spring system consists of 30 individual springs.

spots.name: Takeo Onsen
spots.desc: The ancient hot springs are within walking distance of the station and the nightclubs, and you can sleep here if you like. There are three hot springs to choose from.

spots.name: Shinjō Festival
spots.desc: This annual 3-day festival, held since 1755, has a parade and traditional dancing.

spots.name: Ena Gorge
spots.desc: River and rock formations.

spots.name: Tarui-juku
spots.desc: Tarui was the 57th station of the Nakasendo trail that connected Kyoto with Edo and the first station of the Minoji Trail that connected the Nakasendo to the Tokaido trail. During its heyday, there were 315 hotels. The building marked as the Tarui-juku you see today is the Nagahamaya. When the princess traveled through on the Nakasendo, the men who carried her mikoshi stayed here (she of course…

spots.name: Chiune Sugihara Memorial Hall
spots.desc: The Chiune Sugihara Memorial Hall tells the story of Chiune Sugihara, who saved thousands of Jews while working at the Japanese consulate in Kaunas, Lithuania during World War II. As anti-semitism rose in Europe due to Hitler's rise in power, many Jews wanted to escape the continent but were denied visas by most countries, when Sugihara asked if he could grant visas to Jews, the Japanese…

spots.name: Myoman-ji
spots.desc: For anyone looking to see something slightly different from the standard Japanese temple, Myōman-ji offers a replica of Bodh Gaya's Mahabodhi Temple, where the Buddha obtained Enlightenment. The rest of the complex is quite Japanese, but still very beautiful, with artwork and a garden.
spots.price: Temple grounds are free, entrance to the main hall and garden ¥300

spots.name: Jakko-in
spots.desc: Built in honor of Prince Shōtoku's father, the temple's Jizo contains 6000 tiny Buddha statues inside. The temple is also significant as the final resting place of Empress Kenreimonin, the only member of the Taira clan to survive in the Tales of Heike.

spots.name: Shima Onsen
spots.desc: The main draw of tourists to Nakanojō are the onsen (natural hot spring) resorts. There are two major hot spring resort areas within the town. The larger and more famous one is Shima Onsen, in the mountains to the north of town. The name means "forty thousand", and represents the 40,000 ailments the water is supposed to cure.

spots.name: Ama-no-Iwato Shrine
spots.desc: The cave where Amaterasu hid and the shrine protecting it. This being a Shinto site, the cave is much too holy to let mere mortals inside, but there's an observation deck across the river and pilgrims have stacked countless stones on the paths around the shrine.

spots.name: Southeast Botanical Gardens
spots.desc: Divided into a water garden and botanical garden, it showcases a variety of tropical flora found on the islands of Okinawa. They have night illuminations and other events throughout the year.

spots.name: Nago Castle Ruins
spots.desc: Don't expect to find the castle as it was in the 14th century, but enjoy the nice walk to the top of the hill. The park of the Nago castle is on the Top 100 list of cherry tree flower viewing (hanami) spots of Japan, and the only place in the Okinawa prefecture on the list.

spots.name: Junglia
spots.desc: Opened in 2025, this is a jungle-themed theme park with a twist: no rollercoasters here, more extreme sports type activities (ziplines, treetop walks) and a few immersive rides, including the showpiece Jurassic Park style "Dinosaur Safari". Expect long waits at many attractions unless you fork out extra for a Premium Pass. There is also a hot spring/spa (separate charges apply). The park is…
spots.price: Theme park ¥8800/5940, spa ¥3080/1870, combined ticket ¥11800/7810 for non-resident adult/child

spots.name: Kazurabashi Vine Bridge
spots.desc: The most popular vine bridge is in Nishi-Iya and known simply as "Kazurabashi", fairly close to the main village, and sole destination for 90% of visitors to the valley. There is a rather large operation going on here due to the number of visitors, and the bridge itself is not particularly scary or atmospheric. Entrance costs ¥550 adult, ¥350 child, and the bridge's operating hours are sunrise to…

spots.name: Tōson Memorial Museum
spots.desc: Once the honjin of Magome, this former large inn serves as a memorial to the author Shimazaki Tosin and tells stories about his various works.
spots.hours: Apr-Nov: 09:00-17:00, Dec-Mar: 09:00-16:00, closed on Wed from December–February

spots.name: Shinhotaka Ropeway
spots.desc: The ropeway, from its lower terminal in Shin-Hotaka Onsen, the ropeway climbs 1,033 m, the greatest altitude change of any ropeway in Asia, in two stages to its upper terminal at Nishihihodaka-guchi. The trip takes 20 minutes, during which you’ll travel over 3 km before being deposited at the top. From here, stunning views of the Japanese Alps open in every direction, with hiking paths leading on…

spots.name: Zuishin-in
spots.desc: According to legend, this is where Ono no Komachi, one of Japan's famous femme fatales, resided. She made Prince Fukakusa agree to court her for 100 days before she would agree to marry him, but on the 99th day, he died, leaving her single and her beauty to fade.

spots.name: Hikarigaoka Park
spots.desc: One of the larger parks in Tokyo. It was left over land from a U.S. military base. The park has extensive open, grassy areas for picnics, frisbee and the like. There is also a large public pool, and a gym, a bird-watching center, a small water play area, tennis courts, archery, a baseball diamond and other facilities. A number of festivals and flea markets and special events are often held in the…

spots.name: Chiran Special Attack Peace Museum
spots.desc: During World War II, Chiran was a base for kamikaze pilots and this museum displays photos and letters of the pilots. The museum was founded in 1975. In Japanese, English headsets available.

spots.name: Shirotori Garden
spots.desc: In this Japanese garden you can see and feed koi fish in large ponds, take a look at the tea ceremony house, and also view the beautiful waterfall. On spring the plum trees bloom beautifully and on autumn you can enjoy the night illumination.

spots.name: Nagamachi Samurai District
spots.desc: Towards the coast from Oyama Shrine, this is an area of a few streets where considerable effort has been expended in order to recreate the feel of the samurai housing areas. The fact that almost none of the actual samurai houses remain does little to daunt the enthusiasm of the tourists. While historically dubious, it is a pleasant area to stroll, and one of the best of the remaining samurai…

spots.name: Kazuemachi
spots.desc: A small but very nice area of geisha houses along the riverbank across from Higashiyama.

spots.name: Matsumoto City Museum of Art
spots.desc: This art museum has a large exhibit on Yayoi Kusama, who came from Matsumoto before moving to the United States for many years. It also has a photograph collection of mountains in Nagano.

spots.name: Minatopia - Niigata City History Museum
spots.desc: A museum where you can learn about the history and culture of Niigata. Audio guides available in English, Korean, and Russian.
spots.price: ¥300 adults, ¥200 college or vocational school students, ¥100 elementary, junior high, and high school students

spots.name: Honkawa Elementary School Peace Museum
spots.local: 本川小学校平和資料館
spots.desc: Of the more than 400 students and teachers who were in the school when the bomb exploded, only one student and one teacher survived. After a new school was built, this section of the original structure was kept as a museum, housing a small collection of photos and artifacts.

spots.name: Fukuro-machi Elementary School Museum
spots.desc: Like Honkawa, part of the original school building that remained standing after the atomic bomb has been converted into a museum. In the days after the explosion, survivors used the school's chalk to leave messages for lost friends and family members on its blackened walls.

spots.name: Hiroshima City Manga Library
spots.desc: Around the corner from the Museum of Contemporary Art (below). The vast majority of the manga are in Japanese, of course, but they do have a selection of Western superhero comics.

spots.name: Mazda Museum
spots.desc: Mazda's corporate headquarters are a short distance outside of Hiroshima. The tour is a must for any automobile fan, but if you have any serious technical questions, then you should go on the Japanese tour and bring along your own interpreter, as there's less detail on the English tour. Highlights include the Mazda Cosmos (the world's first car with a rotary engine) and the 4-Rotor Mazda 787B…
spots.hours: Tours weekdays 09:30 and 13:00 in Japanese, 10:00 in English, lasting around 90 minutes. Space is limited, and they ask…

spots.name: Hinomisaki Lighthouse
spots.desc: Supposedly, it's the tallest lighthouse in Asia. The lighthouse appears like any other lighthouse, but the bus ride out there and the chance to see a fishing village makes it worth the 1/2 hour trip.

spots.name: Inasa Beach
spots.desc: Beach with a rock where gods are said to gather. Enjoy the beach and the beautiful sunset.

spots.name: Abashiri Prison Museum
spots.desc: The original buildings of the infamous prison, but moved halfway up Mt. Tento to free up some real estate. Inside are wax dolls of prisoners and a hair-raising array of shackles and other prison paraphernalia.

spots.name: Fisherman's Wharf MOO and EGG
spots.local: 釧路フィッシャーマンズワーフMOO
spots.desc: Kushiro Fisherman's Wharf MOO is a worthwhile stop with its bustling marketplace located on the waterfront, close to Nusamai Bridge. Its unique architecture and location near the ocean make it an excellent photo opportunity. Beyond this the building houses a multitude of restaurants, shops, and recreational facilities. Tourists and locals alike enjoy sightseeing, eating, shopping, and relaxing at…

spots.name: Himeji City Zoo
spots.desc: This zoo has a pretty comprehensive array of animals, but usually only one of each and all in very small cages or enclosures.

spots.name: Naramachi
spots.desc: The neighborhood, founded in the 8th century when Heijōkyō was the capital of Japan, today contains several small museums, machiya (町家) (traditional Japanese merchant houses from Edo Period), unique cafes and restaurants. (David Bowie is rumored to have owned a house here.) It's well worth the time to stop and do a tasting at Harushika (春鹿), Naramachi's fabulous Nihon-shu (sake) brewery.

spots.name: Mother Farm
spots.desc: A farm where kids can pet cows, alpacas and other animals. At the pig race, kids direct their pig to the finish line as fast as possible. Also. Free on rainy days, but not everything is free inside.
spots.price: ticket purchased locally/in advance in a combini: adults ¥1500/¥1350; kids: ¥800/¥700

spots.name: Narita Airport and Community Historical Museum
spots.local: 成田空港 空と大地の歴史館
spots.desc: Opened in June 2011, this museum explains the history of Narita and complicated relationship between its residents and the airport due to land expropriation.

spots.name: Kozuke Kokubunji
spots.desc: A park featuring the ruins of the head temple of the former Kozuke Province (modern Gunma Prefecture).

spots.name: Mt. Kannonyama
spots.desc: This mountain and the enormous statue on top of it are the most obvious attractions. You can enter the statue for ¥200 to get a good view of the city from the top. Halfway down the mountain there is a cave with Kannon sculptures carved from the stone inside, along with a Japanese garden. Entrance ¥800. To get there, you can catch a bus from Takasaki Station, although they're infrequent, and it…

spots.name: Kamakura Museum of History and Culture
spots.desc: Local history museum covering the history of Kamakura. The modern exhibits are complemented by English-speaking volunteer docents. Includes access to the ruins of a mostly forgotten cliffside Shinto shrine, now used as a scenic lookout point.

spots.name: Kanagawa Museum of Modern Literature
spots.desc: Located in Harbor View Park, this museum specializes in modern Japanese literature. The museum holds large-scale exhibitions several times a year and collects materials on various authors. The museum also has a reading room where visitors can obtain a variety of materials.

spots.name: River Karasuyama
spots.desc: This is a narrow river, but cherry trees are along both sides of the river. In spring, the cherry trees are in full bloom and very beautiful. Also, there are lawn and benches here, so you can relax on the benches in a good weather.

spots.name: Shōmyō Temple
spots.desc: It is a temple built by Hojo Sanetoki in 1258. It has developed into Kamakura Period. It is specified for the historic site in Japan. There is a beautiful garden. A lot of cherry blossoms bloom in spring. Moreover, precincts are illuminated at fireworks of summer and the New Year and it is very beautiful.

spots.name: Yokohama Bay Quarter
spots.desc: 7-min walk from East Exit, across the river from Sogo, steps away from Sea Bus stop Up-market stores set in a pet-friendly, open-air and often breezy atmosphere with great views of the waterfront! Food options are on the gourmet side.

spots.name: Tsukayama Park
spots.desc: The scenic hilltop park where William Adams (called in Japanese Miura anjin and the inspiration for the Richard Chamberlain character in Shogun) and wife Oyuki are buried. The park's 10,000 cherry trees make this the best blossom viewing in April in Yokosuka. Locals find it a nice place to walk dogs! Park also has a scenic overlooking north.

spots.name: Kawagoe Festival Museum
spots.desc: If you don't happen to be in Kawagoe during the yearly festival held in October, you can get a feel for it in this museum, which exhibits the great floats used in the procession and screens a 5 minute movie about the festival. Naturally the museum also details the history of the festival in Japanese.

spots.name: Aeon Lake Town
spots.desc: The largest shopping complex in Japan and one of the largest in Asia with 700+ shops. It has three premises:"kaze", "mori" and newer "outlet". Opened in 2008.

spots.name: Kangi-in Temple
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple with architecture designated as a National Treasure

spots.name: Nikko Kirifuri Ice Arena
spots.local: 栃木県立日光霧降アイスアリーナ
spots.desc: Home arena of Nikkō Ice Bucks of the Asia League Ice Hockey. No competition day, play ice skating.

spots.name: Matsugamine Church
spots.desc: The church, built in 1932, is full-dress Romanesque cathedral. Almost all the building is composed of Ōya Stone including exterior and interior walls.

spots.name: Oya History Museum
spots.desc: A former Oya stone mine which is now open to tourists, located a half-hour bus ride away from Utsunomiya. Mining took place almost entirely underground, leaving behind straight-walled caverns of awe-inspiring, Biblical proportions.

spots.name: Orion Dori
spots.desc: A pedestrian mall, this is the main site for the yearly festivals Utsunomiya holds during the start of August. Connects with many of the above mentioned locations, such as Tobu Department Store. Mostly clothing stores with bars opening at nighttime.

spots.name: Hijiri-bashi Bridge
spots.desc: On the Kanda river (神田川), on the border between Bunkyō and Chiyoda wards. It offers one of the best spots in Tokyo to see trains, three lines crossing each other (on the west, so better seen in the afternoon). Akihabara district in 500 m/10 min away to the east. Its name means Saints bridge. One side at Temple of Confucius Yushima Seido (湯島聖堂), the other side at cathedral of the Japanese Orthodox…

spots.name: Taro Okamoto Memorial Museum
spots.desc: Former studio and house of Okamoto Taro. Unfinished works and paintings are shown. He made numerous masterpieces such as "Tower of the Sun" at the Expo 1970 and "Myth of the Future" mural now exhibited in Shibuya.

spots.name: Hanegi Park
spots.desc: A public park, where kids can play freely with the Play Park facility.

spots.name: Fire Museum
spots.desc: Three fire-fighting helicopters, ten trucks, and 3 floors of exhibitions. Very popular with kids, who can wear fire-fighting clothes and ride some of the helicopters and trucks.

spots.name: Amuran
spots.desc: A large Ferris wheel atop AMU Plaza attached the Kagoshimachuo station. Enter from 6F near cinema and game arcade. You’ll also find a rubbish bin (rare!) and public toilets on 6F, so it could be an inexpensive and quick way to take in the view of Kagoshima if just passing through.

spots.name: Amu Plaza Kagoshima
spots.desc: attached to Kagoshimachuo station, can enter from 1F or 2F of the station or go outside and head east a few steps. Contains a grocery, Sanrio shop, music store, stationary store, craft shop, kitchenware, cinema, game arcade, restaurants 5F, and Ferris wheel on the roof. In general, expensive shops are closer to the station entrances and on the lower floors. Youth clothing, cool-casual are more…

spots.name: Former Hongkong and Shanghai Bank
spots.local: 旧香港上海銀行長崎支店
spots.desc: A stately Western-style building near Nagasaki’s waterfront, this former branch of the Hongkong and Shanghai Bank dates from the early 20th century and reflects the city’s role as a major international trading port. Restored and now open as a museum, it offers exhibits on Nagasaki’s global commerce and foreign settlements during the Meiji era.

spots.name: Naha Tug-of-war
spots.desc: Naha hosts a rope pulling event. Two 100-metre long ropes are laid down in the street. The ropes represents opposing armies or rival kingdoms in a battle between East and West. It is preceded by a parade, karate demonstrations, drums, and firecrackers. People dress like Ryukyu kings with naginata swords. Each team tries to pull the rope their way for 30 minutes, or until the rope is moved by a…

spots.name: Tobe Zoo
spots.desc: It's south of Matsuyama. Tobe Dobutsuen is the destination for viewing over 190 species of animals, particularly "Peace" the polar bear. Though more spacious than its previous grounds and the silhouette animal footprints leading to the entrance are endearing, the zoo may leave much to be desired for those not used to Japanese zoological standards.

spots.name: Saishō-in Monastery
spots.desc: Known for its five-storied pagoda, completed in 1667, which stands 31.2 meters tall and took ten years to build on the order of Tsugaru clan leader Nobuyoshi.

spots.name: Tanamukaihara Ruins
spots.desc: Dates back 20,000 years. These are the oldest ruins in Japan. There is an historical museum nearby where you can learn about the area's history and culture. An old residence has been restored in the outdoor exhibition.

spots.name: Kawachi Reservoir
spots.desc: Reservoir in Yahata Higashi Ward with an onsen (hot spring) with a rotenburo (outdoor bath). Courtesy bus from Yahata station. You can walk round the reservoir in about an hour, or rent a bicycle.

spots.name: Shirakawa Park
spots.desc: Beautiful trees, Nagoya Science and Modern Art Museums.

spots.name: Yokokan Garden
spots.desc: A small but scenic strolling garden.

spots.name: Narita Wholesale Market
spots.local: 成田市公設地方卸売市場
spots.desc: A public wholesale fish, fruit, and vegetable market.

spots.name: Oshio Hachiman Shrine
spots.desc: In 887 this shrine was built by Kino Tomonaka, who was exiled to Echizen area because of a false charge against the government. He continuously prayed to clear his name of the charges for some years, and eventually was allowed to return to the capital, Nara. To display his gratitude, he built this shrine, which is now a National Important Cultural Property.

spots.name: Hikaru Museum
spots.desc: A beautiful, sprawling building completed in 1999 inspired by the Nayan complex at Tikal in Guatemala. The collection is good, but sparse. There is a good exhibition of Japanese art, a small collection of European art (a Renoir, a Van Gogh, a Monet, etc.), and a smattering of artifacts from the world's ancient cultures.
spots.hours: Late Feb to mid-Dec: Thu-Tue 10:00-17:00, last admission 16:00
spots.price: ¥900; combination ticket with Hida Takayama Museum of Art ¥1300

spots.name: Nata-dera Temple
spots.desc: Popular on the Japanese tourist circuit, this temple is noted for its extensive grounds, beautiful garden and natural caves. One of the best times to visit is in late autumn when the colorful red foliage is truly spectacular. Nata-dera's history can be traced back to 717 AD.

spots.name: Kiyotsu Gorge
spots.desc: Kiyotsu Gorge is a spectacular gorge known for its steep cliffs of columnar rock formations and the clear waters of the Kiyotsu River. A 750-metre-long pedestrian tunnel provides several viewing points, culminating in the Panorama Station, where a reflective pool creates striking views of the gorge. The tunnel's artistic design makes it a popular destination for photographers, especially during…
spots.hours: 8:30 to 17:00 from March to November, and 09:00 to 16:00 in winter

spots.name: Iyama Hofukuji Temple
spots.desc: Priest Sesshu, one of Japan's most famous painters, studied here as a child. There is a legend that he painted a mouse using only his tears, and it is here that this event is said to have taken place. Very nice leaves colors in autumn.
