Worth the detour if you are cycling the Kibiji cycling trail.

spots.name: Ebisugahana Shipyard
spots.desc: The shogunate had banned shipbuilding in the provinces to avoid uprisings however, as outsiders took more interest in Japan, the ban was lifted in 1853 and within a few years the Choshu Domain began building warships with new Western technology from Russia and the Netherlands. The ruins of the shipyard were registered as part of Hagi's World Heritage listing.

spots.name: Tōkō-ji
spots.desc: This is the family shrine of the Mori clan. The beautiful gate, belfry, and temple buildings show Chinese influence; behind the temple are the graves of several Mori warlords — and 500 stone lanterns to mark their power. It's a short walk east of Shoin Shrine.

spots.name: Bear Farm
spots.desc: The small, crowded enclosures in which the bears are kept may be disturbing to Western visitors.

spots.name: Marine Park Nixe
spots.local: 登別マリンパークニクス
spots.desc: Aquarium built like a Danish castle, with a small amusement park bolted on.

spots.name: Ikomasanjo Amusement Park
spots.desc: Old amusement park on the hilltop. Closed in winter: December to mid March.

spots.name: Ryujin Onsen
spots.desc: Riverside Onsen town with many open air onsens, the hotspring's water is said to result in smooth skin.

spots.name: Kimisarazu Tower
spots.desc: There is a mountain park called "Odayama", also called "love forest". The main tower, called “Kimisarazu Tower”, is on the top of the mountain park. You can see the big statue of a couple on a ship, based on a tragic love story. Once, there was a man named Yamato-takeru-no-mikoto and his wife Oto-tachibana-hime. One day, Yamato-takeru-no-mikoto was trying to cross the sea to go to Kazusa-no-kuni…

spots.name: Ōnomatsu stable
spots.desc: ​A stable of sumo wrestlers, one of the Nishonoseki ichimon or group of stables.

spots.name: Sakuragi Jinja
spots.desc: is a Shinto shrine. The shrine was founded in 851 CE by a member of the Fujiwara clan and is the oldest shrine in Noda city. The shrine is a famous spot for cherry blossom viewing.

spots.name: Nagatoro
spots.desc: Sail down the Ara River (荒川) on a traditional Japanese wooden boat, taking in the beautiful nature of Nagatoro.

spots.name: Orihime Shrine
spots.desc: A shrine was built here in 1879 to enshrine the deities Yachichihime no mikoto (八千々姫命) and Amenomihoko no mikoto (天御鉾命), and to protect the textile industry of Ashikaga. In 1880, it was reduced to ashes in a fire and the current shrine building was built in 1937. It stands in the midst of Orihime Park and is also the departure and arrival point for the hiking course in the Ashikaga Prefectural…

spots.name: Matsushita Museum of Art
spots.desc: Works from Japanese artists associated with Kagoshima Prefecture.

spots.name: Nobeoka Castle Ruins
spots.desc: The ruins of Nobeoka Castle stand atop Mt. Shiroyama. The main castle walls and some foundations are all that remain, along with a recreated main castle gate. The main wall at the entrance is known as the "killer of a thousand men," because it is said that if a certain stone is removed, the wall will collapse and kill one thousand enemies. Much of the old castle grounds are now a park covered…

spots.name: Kawamura Art Museum
spots.desc: The museums houses a collection of paintings from the 19th to early 20th centuries.

spots.name: Tindabana
spots.desc: Tindabana is a natural rock formation with a nice view. About 70 m tall. From Tindabana, you can see the entire village of Sonai, and Nandahama. According to tradition, the great empress of Yonaguni, Sanai Isoba, resided here.

spots.name: Noshiro City General Gymnasium
spots.desc: This large gymnasium hosts a variety of sporting events, for both participants and spectators. In the past, it has held professional basketball games.

spots.name: Yokote Masuda Manga Museum
spots.local: 横手市増田まんが美術館
spots.desc: A museum about Japanese comics with original works by famous manga artists.

spots.name: Chido Museum
spots.desc: Chidō Museum is an open-air museum in the former Shōnai domain, featuring historic buildings including a traditional samurai residence, a Meiji-era police station and a Western-style building.

spots.name: Tomita Chausan Tomb
spots.desc: The largest tumulus in the Shikoku region. It is estimated to have been built around the first half of the 5th century CE.

spots.name: Hikage Onsen
spots.desc: Remote mountain hot spring. Day trip and hotel stay packages available.

spots.name: Ōishi Shrine
spots.desc: Shrine dedicated to the 47 ronin.

spots.name: Misaka Pass
spots.desc: A National Historic Site. It is a mountain pass through the southern end of the Kiso Mountains, connecting the city of Nakatsugawa with the village of Achi, Nagano. The highest point on the pass is 1,569 m (5,148 ft). The pass is accessible by car via a forestry road from the Gifu side; however, due to the danger of falling rocks, the road on the Nagano side of the pass is closed to vehicular…

spots.name: Yamanashi Prefectural Maglev Exhibition Center
spots.local: 山梨県立リニア見学センター
spots.desc: This exhibition center showcases the technology that is used in the Linear Chuo Shinkansen that is being built between Tokyo and Osaka. In addition, visitors can also witness the new train in action, as the center is built alongside the track, where the train can be seen speeding by at 504 km/h.

spots.name: Senjokaku
spots.desc: This huge wooden pavilion is called the 'Sentamikaku' because it is the size of 857 tatami mats. There is actually nothing but empty space in this huge wooden building. It was started by Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1587, but left incomplete after his death. There's also a picturesque 5-story pagoda (五重塔 Gojuto) next door, though as of May 2025 this is entirely covered by scaffolding for restoration…

spots.name: Yogen-in
spots.desc: The original temple was built by one of Hideyoshi Toyotomi's concubines in honor of her father, but the temple was destroyed by a fire. When rebuilding the temple, the floorboards of Fushimi Castle in Southern Kyoto were used to construct the ceiling. Since Fushimi Castle was the site of quite a bloody battle, when you look at the ceiling, you can still see blood stains and body outlines from…

spots.name: Enoshima Aquarium
spots.desc: Fairly large aquarium most notable for its occasional use as a Jellyfish research facility for the current emperor. Features a dolphin show, and notably, unique exhibits on jellyfish, the marine biology research of the Imperial family, and its whitebait breeding program.

spots.name: Hakone Kowakien Yunessun
spots.desc: Indoor complex featuring rapids, Dead Sea-style salt baths and jacuzzis, while the outdoor area offers waterfalls, rocks and a water slide. The popular outdoor relaxation section includes a renowned sake bath, as well as coffee, green tea and wine baths. Mori No Yu is a traditional Onsen style Japanese spring in the same complex.

spots.name: Fukiagehama Beach
spots.desc: Fukiagehama is a sand dune coastline in western Kagoshima Prefecture , stretching from Ichikikushikino City to Hioki City and Minamisatsuma City. It is one of Japan's three largest sand dunes, and has also been selected as one of Japan's 100 best beaches. It is located on the west coast of the Satsuma Peninsula, facing the East China Sea.

spots.name: Izumi Crane Habitat
spots.desc: A National Special Natural Monument known for the wintering of about 10,000 cranes from mid-October to March each year. It is breeding grounds of the cranes that migrate to the Izumi Plain are the wetlands from Lake Baikal to the middle Amur River basin for the hooded cranes, and the wetlands for the white-naped cranes from the middle to upper Amur river basins.

spots.name: Mifuneyama Rakuen Garden
spots.desc: An expansive garden constructed by the local lord Shigeyoshi Nabeshima in 1845 below Mount Mifune.

spots.name: Takeo City Library
spots.local: 武雄市図書館・歴史資料館
spots.desc: Do some reading or update your blog at the first library in the world to have a public-private partnership with a large music store chain. When tired, enjoy a Starbucks coffee inside the library. If you have a child, the kids' library (こども図書館) can also satisfy your child.
spots.addr: 5304-1 Tekeocho Oaza Takeo (武雄町大字武雄5304番地1)

spots.name: Nanko Park
spots.desc: Claimed to be one of the first officially named parks in Japan, with a traditional garden and teahouse.
spots.price: Access to Nanko park is free, but a small fee is charged for entry to the garden and teahouse (Kyorakutei)

spots.name: Kashikuri Shrine
spots.desc: A Shinto shrine rebuilt in 1989.
spots.addr: 鹿児島県出水市下鯖町1272

spots.name: Saimyōji Temple
spots.desc: A former sub-temple of Jingoji. While it is not worth making a special trip to see this temple, those touring the Takao area might as well visit, as it is located on the path connecting Jingo-ji to Kōzan-ji. The bridge leading to the temple and the lanterns outside the entrance are quite nice.

spots.name: Entsū-ji
spots.desc: A temple famous for its gardens. A particularly unique feature of this garden is incorporation of Mount Hiei, of which there is a great view from the temple, into the layout of the garden.

spots.name: Abeno Q's Mall
spots.local: あべのキューズタウン
spots.desc: Enormous mid-range shopping mall integrated into the Abeno Harukas complex. Clothes, electronics, restaurants, supermarket, the works.

spots.name: Nogi's house and shrine
spots.desc: General Nogi's house is a great example of Western architecture constructed during the Meiji period (19th century), mixing Japanese and Western elements. The general killed himself here after the Meiji Emperor's death. Descend the stairs to reach the shrine that was dedicated to him in 1917. Lonely place, very photogenic.

spots.name: Uegusuku Castle
spots.desc: The castle ruins are located on the top the highest point in Okinawa, offering great views of the entire island, adjacent Hatenohama sandbar, and neighboring islands.

spots.name: Omoro Botanical Garden
spots.desc: This garden collects plants that are described in the Omoro Sōshi (おもろそうし), a collection of Okinawan poems and songs. The garden contains about 400 species of salt-resistant plants, including large trees, small trees, shade trees, various garden plants, and herbs. The garden also contains more than 110 wild orchid species, many of them endangered, native to the Ryukyu Islands.

spots.name: Benesse House Museum
spots.desc: The first contemporary art museum on the island remains one of the best. A superb fusion of nature, art and architecture that displays the works of Andy Warhol, Richard Long, Bruce Nauman, and others. The Museum building, now one of 4 buildings in the complex, was designed by world famous Japanese architect Tadao Ando. There are also numerous outdoor exhibits nearby.

spots.name: Kaerikumo Castle
spots.desc: The castle disappeared into the ground, along with the town surrounding it, when a big earthquake struck one night in 1586. A goldmine near the castle was also swallowed by the earth that night, leaving people to speculate to this day that as much as ¥10 billion may still be buried there. Nowadays there is nothing left but a monument and some greenery.

spots.name: Tochibaraiwakage ruins
spots.desc: The village's main attraction is an archaeological site designated as a National Historic Site with a Jomon-era cave dwelling.

spots.name: Takayama Inari Shrine
spots.desc: Hundreds of red torii gates snake through a garden at this picturesque shrine near the Sea of Japan.

spots.name: Shiramizu Falls
spots.desc: A scenic waterfall near Shiramizu Lake.

spots.name: Shōbō-ji
spots.desc: A Shingon sect temple featuring an impressive statue of the 3-faced thousand armed Kannon and a beautiful, well-kept Zen rock garden. Many of the rocks within the garden were chosen to resemble animals, like a rabbit and frog.

spots.name: Edo Wonderland Nikko Edomura
spots.desc: A cultural theme park that resurrects and showcases the life and culture of the Edo period. The park hosts Edo period architecture from rural lodgings to urban samurai residences and government buildings. Also features 7 theatres featuring various traditionally themed shows including Ninja action, Oiran shows, Ninja workshops, Japanese traditional archery, shuriken throwing, and costume hire.
spots.hours: 9AM-5PM; Closed on Wednesdays and holidays, shorter hours in the winter

spots.name: Izena Castle
spots.desc: Ruins of a 14th-century Okinawan gusuku castle.

spots.name: 138 Tower Park
spots.desc: 'Ichino-mi-ya' can be read as the number '138', and so the number crops up regularly in the local area. Ichinomiya Twin Arch 138 is the tallest arch-style tower in Asia, at (you guessed it) 138 m tall. An observation platform at 100 m (admission ¥500 for adults) gives a panoramic view of the Kiso Valley. One sight of note is the nearby village which is constructed entirely on an island in the…

spots.name: Ichinomiya Tanabata Festival
spots.desc: Held from Thursday to Sunday of the last weekend in July, this is reputed to be one of the three biggest Tanabata festivals in Japan, and attracts up to 1.3 million visitors annually. The streets are strikingly decorated and bustling with festival-goers in yukata, centering around Masumida Shrine, and the festivities include a parade to dedicate local products to the shrine, bon-dancing - which…

spots.name: Toyota Kaikan Museum
spots.desc: Fortunately, this Toyota museum is here. You can see some cars made by Toyota, and try some small vehicles here. You may still want to visit some other facilities related to Toyota, anyways.
spots.addr: 愛知県豊田市トヨタ町１

spots.name: Fukui City History Museum
spots.local: 福井市立郷土歴史博物館
spots.desc: Contains interesting displays on the history of the local area from early civilizations to its days as a castle town to the bombings in WWII.

spots.name: Nishi-Chayagai
spots.desc: The "west" to Higashi's "east", this is another district of restored geisha houses. This is considerably smaller (and quieter) than Higashi, with effectively just a single street, and aside from the (free) information center it's not possible to formally visit any of the houses. One can however enter the several shops that dot the street and appreciate the inside of these beautiful houses.

spots.name: Tentoku-in
spots.desc: The largest temple in Kanazawa during the Edo period, it stood at the eastern end of the city. It was built to house the spirit of Tama-hime (珠姫: the Princess Tama), the wife of Maeda Toshitsune (the third Maeda lord). She was born in 1599 as the granddaughter of Tokugawa Ieyasu, the founder of the Tokugawa Shogunate, and the daughter of the second Shogun, Hidetada. It was a political marriage…

spots.name: Kaga Honda Museum
spots.desc: Near Kenrokuen is this pleasant green park-like area which houses the very interesting Prefectural Museum (housed in three long narrow pre-war army storehouses of brick), the Art Gallery, and a few other smaller museums, as well as the Prefectural Noh Hall and the National Defence Shrine (護国神社 Gokoku Jinja), a smaller regional version of the main Yasukuni Shrine in Tokyo. Just outside the shrine…

spots.name: Uchibuse River French Waterfall
spots.local: 牛伏川フランス式階段工
spots.desc: These tiered waterfalls are located in a large scenic park. The falls themselves can be seen in ten minutes, though there are several kilometers of trails for more adventurous souls. There are dozens of picnic spots along the road to the falls. The parking lot closest to the falls has a restroom, though there is no tap water.

spots.name: Sea View Forest Museum
spots.desc: The majority of the collection consists of Japanese art from the Middle Ages to the modern era. Representative holdings include modern Japanese paintings from Kyoto, mainly by Takeuchi Seiho. The foundation of the collection is several thousand pieces of powdered wood, sketches, photographs, etc. In the field of ukiyo-e, the museum excels in Utagawa Hiroshige's flower and bird prints, and has a…

spots.name: Chuo Park
spots.desc: A big, sprawling green space in the middle of the city. Broadly defined, the park grounds include many of the attractions below, including the castle and the Carp's old baseball stadium (scheduled for demolition). But Chuo Park is worthy of note in its own right, with nice, long walking paths and athletic fields — there are quite a lot of open-invitation soccer, football, and ultimate…

spots.name: Tachikue Gorge
spots.desc: A pleasant hike that ends with hundreds of stone figures with red hats on them. There's an onsen/youth hostel.

spots.name: Kōunkaku
spots.desc: A sort of colonial house with Japanese architectural elements.

spots.name: Shiomi Nawate
spots.desc: This old samurai residential street runs along the north east side of Matsue Castle, across the moat. Many of Matsue's musea and other historical attractions can be found in this area.

spots.name: Matsue History Museum
spots.desc: The Matsue History Museum offers a glimpse into the past of Matsue and the surrounding area. The museum also houses the Matsue International Tourist Information Office. The staff speaks English and can help with booking a hotel.
spots.price: ¥500 for adults, ¥250 for children, 50% discount for foreigners

spots.name: Lake Harutori
spots.desc: Lake Harutori has the distinction of being the largest lake in Japan within a city. It has been designated a National Natural Monument as a habitat for the Red Crucian Carp. This lake is popular as a place for relaxing and for taking walks. It has a circumference of 4.7 km, an area of 36.1 ha, and the deepest part is 5.7 m.

spots.name: Akashi Municipal Planetarium
spots.desc: A great stop for science fans. It is known as the place where Japan Standard Time is measured, because it is located at exactly 135 degrees east longitude, the Japan Standard Time Meridian. The planetarium is the longest running planetarium in Japan. It also features a time and space museum.

spots.name: Senhime Shrine
spots.desc: This is the only shrine in Japan associated with a castle. While the shrine is rather small and not very interesting, travelling up the stairs to the next lookout reveals a spectacular view of Himeji Castle.

spots.name: Tegarayama
spots.desc: A district with a large park with a small WWII museum, aquarium, amusement park, botanic garden, and a monorail museum..

spots.name: Japan Toy Museum
spots.desc: A small museum based in the home of the toy collector and founder Mr Shigeyoshi Inoue. The toys may have aged over the decades but they are still fun for anyone with an inner child. Inoue-san has collected toys and dolls from several prefectures and several countries since the 1970s.

spots.name: Sawa-no-Tsuru Museum
spots.desc: This museum is probably the best of the bunch, with an informative multi-level exhibit partly labelled in English, and a well-stocked gift shop

spots.name: Hakutsuru Sake Brewery Museum
spots.desc: This museum is inside a former brewery, and features traditional tools, dioramas and English-language videos to explain the sake-making processes. At the end, you can sample some sake, which is non-pasteurized, presumably because it doesn't have to travel far from the factory. Write your name on a piece of paper provided by the guard and return that at the end.

spots.name: Settsu-kyō Gorge
spots.desc: Gorge of the Akuta River on the north side of Takatsuki, with pathways, hikes and hot springs (see Sleep). Cherry blossoms in spring, fireflies in summer, autumn colors in the fall.

spots.name: Mitsui Outlet Park Makuhari
spots.local: 三井アウトレットパーク 幕張
spots.desc: There are lots of shops including such major brands as Coach, Edwin, Nike, and so on. During special events or holiday seasons like Christmas the sales draw large crowds. For people who want to enjoy shopping with their pets, some shops have special areas that pets can enjoy.

spots.name: LaLaport Tokyo-Bay
spots.desc: One of Japan's largest shopping malls, it features 2 department stores and 440 shops.

spots.name: Ichikawa City Zoo
spots.desc: Ichikawa's best-known attraction is this modest zoo with listless animals in cramped concrete cages. It's frankly rather depressing and best avoided.

spots.name: Hondoji Temple
spots.desc: Approximately 10,000 Japanese hydrangeas and 5,000 Japanese iris called 'Ajisai' and 'Shoubu' are in this temple. In June, a lot of people visit it and enjoy watching them. In autumn, the leaves turn red like fire. Red leaves are called 'Momiji' in Japan. A tour called the 'Ajisai tour' and 'Momiji tour' is available. It is open on New Year's Eve and you can ring a bell. It is called "Joya no…

spots.name: Sakura-no-Yama
spots.desc: Is located near the northern end of the main runway of Narita International Airport. Unfortunately there is no bus service to this location. There is nice little park with beautiful cherry trees and a good view of airplanes landing and taking off from the main runway.

spots.name: Boso No Mura
spots.desc: A living museum of traditional Japanese culture. Enjoy the exciting activities on the reproduction Japanese town street. The superb burial mound and the samurai residence are a must-see for anyone interested in Japanese history. Exotic traditional festivals are held every now and then. Film-location for historical dramas. Next to Doramu No Sato (drum village) and Komorebi Restaurant

spots.name: AEON Mall Narita
spots.desc: A very large shopping mall within spitting distance of Narita Airport. Over 150 stores can be found here, including anchor Aeon Style supermarket and foreign outlets like Starbucks and Sports Authority. Popular with foreigners due to its proximity to the airport.

spots.name: Moro-oka Kumano Shrine
spots.desc: Okurayama area. Take Tokyu-Toyoko Line from Yokohama Stn, about 10 min. Then, 7 min walk from Okurayama Stn. This is a famous shrine in Yokohama. Its god is a bird which has three legs. This bird seems like the symbol of the soccer teams of Japan. Therefore, as well as many soccer fans, even Japanese soccer players visit here and pray for the victory of their team. Of course, many other people…

spots.name: Yodobashi Yokohama
spots.desc: West Exit Forget Akihabara, this gigantic "denki-ya-san" branch is more than suffice for all your electronics needs. Also has a selection of duty free items. Be sure to sign up for a point card; you'll receive a percentage in points depending on the purchase (usually 13%), which can then be applied same as cash on future purchases at any Yodobashi nationwide.

spots.name: Yokohama Vivre
spots.desc: Japanese fashion at its best (or worst, depending on your take) for 20- and 30-somethings. Think Shibuya 109 and Parco. Beer garden on the top.

spots.name: LaLaport Yokohama
spots.desc: The largest shopping mall in Kanagawa, located in Kamoi. You get off at Yokohama line "Kamoi". There are about 370 shops, cinemas and restaurants.

spots.name: Shiba Fishing Port
spots.desc: Fishing port where the catch from Tokyo Bay and nearby is landed, with local specialities including conger (anago), lobster (ise-ebi) and sea bass (tai). 1:30PM onwards on Sundays and public holidays only.

spots.name: Museum of Kurazukuri
spots.desc: Built after the great fire, in 1893, this old wholesale Tobacco warehouse of the Koyama family, gives you a chance to look inside the warehouses, and learn about the history of Kurazukuri construction.

spots.name: City Museum
spots.desc: Useful after visiting the warehouse district as it contains information on how the warehouses were built. Otherwise your average local museum detailing local history with artifacts and models. Next door is a small art museum with a collection of local art.

spots.name: Omiya Bonsai Art Museum
spots.local: さいたま市大宮盆栽美術館
spots.desc: An informative museum with exhibits about the various types of bonsai, themes they represent, and how they are trained. The museum includes English explanations and brochures, so you can learn a lot about this traditional Japanese art form without knowing Japanese.

spots.name: Omiya Park Zoo
spots.desc: A small children's zoo, home to a variety of birds, monkeys, squirrels, reptiles, and other small animals.

spots.name: Saitama Arts Theater
spots.local: 彩の国さいたま芸術劇場
spots.desc: The city's primary performing arts theater. Throughout the year, they hold orchestral concerts, piano concerts, plays, musicals, and other events. It has even been used to film dramas. There is also a cafeteria and restaurant on site.

spots.name: Taiyuin-byō
spots.desc: Iemitsu, the 3rd Tokugawa Shogun and grandson of Ieyasu, is buried here. Smaller, although much more beautiful than Tōshōgū. The main hall and mausoleum can only be viewed from outside. Unlike Tōshōgū, the tomb is not accessible to the public.

spots.name: Takino-o Shrine
spots.desc: This often overlooked mountain shrine is situated slightly up the mountain behind Toshogu and provides a welcome relief from the more crowded areas of Sannai. It takes its name from the picturesque waterfall that greets you at the base of the entrance. You can get there by walking for about 15-20 minutes along an ancient and atmospheric stone path that begins behind the Toshogu Shamusho (office).…

spots.name: Kanmangafuchi Abyss
spots.desc: A long series of jizo protector statues on the side of a hill, some adorned with hats and bibs, some crumbling with age, with a river, small waterfalls and rapids below. Legend says that the statues change places from time to time, and a visitor will never see them in the same order twice. It can be tricky to find - at Shinkyō, instead of heading up the steps to the temple area, follow the road…

spots.name: Hachimanyama Park
spots.desc: A popular spot for cherry blossom viewing (hanami). The park is quiet, relaxed, and usually pretty empty except for certain summer celebrations. It contains a tower-viewing area, a large foot-bridge, and a play areas for families. It is a worth a picnic if you have extra time. Within the park grounds is Utsunomiya's velodrome. For ¥100 entry you can watch keirin bicycle races on race days, or bet…

spots.name: Akishimaensis
spots.desc: Educational facility that contains a local heritage museum and a public library. Has a massive life-size replica of the Akishima whale fossil.

spots.name: Kumano Shrine
spots.desc: Built 800 years ago. Surrounded by trees, people visit to pray or just for the peace and quiet. Some come for specific the worship practice of Yakuyoke, a purification ritual to drive out evil spirits. Like all shrines, they sell protective amulets for health, good studies, or traffic safety, but these are distinctively cute. For a traditional shrine, they have a particularly flashy website that…

spots.name: TEPIA
spots.desc: Science museum showcasing new technologies, robots, home automation. Explanations are in Japanese but playing with the objects is still fun for kids and adults.

spots.name: Nakano Sunmall
spots.local: 中野サンモール商店街
spots.desc: The center of Nakano's commercial area is an over 200-m-long covered shopping street (arcade) featuring a wide variety of shops, cafes and restaurants. Branching off to the east are several side-streets with various additional restaurants, including many Izakaya.
spots.hours: Many of the shops are not open until late morning or early afternoon, especially on weekends. Most shops are open at…

spots.name: Haneda Innovation City
spots.local: 羽田イノベーションシティ
spots.desc: Several restaurants are located in this commercial and research complex. There is a rooftop where you can watch planes or enjoy a foot bath.

spots.name: Tollywood
spots.desc: This small theater (46 seats) specializes in independent short films, mostly Japanese. The films aren't dubbed or subtitled of course, but they're so offbeat and often bizarre that you're sure to have a good time anyway.

spots.name: Hōmyōji
spots.desc: Famous Japanese temple built in 810. Features the statue of Kishimojin (鬼子母神像) who is a Japanese God of fertility. Visitors go to Hōmyōji to pray for their children's birth, growth and security. The Kishimojin figure typically take the form of the devil, but this statue holds a baby, and the figure is beautiful. In this temple the Oeshiki-Taisai festival (御会式大祭) is held from October 16 to October…

spots.name: Maizuru Park
spots.desc: Maizuru park includes the ruins of Fukuoka Castle (福岡城, Fukuoka-jō). Also inside the park, you will find the ruins of the Korokan (鴻臚館), a reception hall built around 1,200 years ago.

spots.name: Toto Museum
spots.desc: The museum is on the second floor of the company's headquarters, in a building with a modern architectural style. The building resembles a bathtub. The museum exhibits old toilets and toilet seats, urinals, bathtubs, and the company's most famous product, the toilet bowl.

spots.name: Miyazaki Science Center
spots.desc: Has a variety of interactive science exhibits and a planetarium.

spots.name: Neputa Village
spots.desc: Located at the park's northerneastern corner, this is where the festival's floats and memorabilia are held outside the Neputa festival season (see Do). The Village showcases a particularly large 8x10m specimen, and sheepishly notes that it's now too big to fit under the electric wires that crisscross Japanese streets. There are also several workshops preparing traditional Hirosaki handicrafts…

spots.name: Chōshō-ji Temple
spots.desc: Known for the Sanmon Gate (1629) and a hall filled with wooden statues of the 500 Disciples of Buddha.

spots.name: Hirosaki Museum of Contemporary Art
spots.local: 弘前れんが倉庫美術館
spots.desc: This brick building was built as a brewery that operated under various owners from 1923 to 1965. It was then used for rice storage by the government until it was bought by Hirosaki City and converted into a museum in 2015. The museum has no permanent gallery, so check what the feature is during your visit to determine if it interests you.

spots.name: Hanamiyama Park
spots.desc: This park is the place to go in spring for cherry blossom viewing. It is quickly becoming a place famous throughout Japan, be prepared for crowds. You can take a short trail up a hill and see some amazing panoramas as well as enjoy walking underneath gorgeous light-pink canopies. There are regular buses leaving for Hanamiyama from the train station. Ask the people at the tourist office for more…

spots.name: Shioyazaki Lighthouse
spots.desc: The Shioyazaki Lighthouse, a famous symbol of Iwaki City, stands tall on a cliff top overlooking the Pacific Ocean. The beacon stands 80 m above sea level and its beam reaches a distance of 40 km out to sea. This lighthouse has guided ships to safety since 1890. In front of the lighthouse are two stones, one of which appears to be playing the same song over and over again. This stone is a…

spots.name: Hamamatsu Plaza
spots.desc: Another large shopping mall complex consisted of five buildings: Xebio, Costco, Frespo, FitnessRelaxation ZEN, and Hamamatsu Plaza West. A tourist may be interested in Frespo and Hamamatsu Plaza West the most. The former is itself a shopping mall that consists of daily goods stores, restaurants, and a supermarket, while the latter are retail chains such as Mont-Bell, Uniqlo, GU and ABC. Xebio…
spots.addr: 静岡県浜松市東区上西町1020-1

spots.name: Kanmon Straits Fireworks Festival
spots.desc: One of Japan's largest fireworks festivals is held over the Kanmon Straits every year on August 13th, with over a million people in attendance and 13,000 hanabi to enjoy.

spots.name: Kanuma Park
spots.desc: Contains a duck pond also frequented by swans. The park also contains a mock road where children can learn the rules of the road while riding their bicycles or go-carts. The park is a popular spot for picnicking during the cherry blossom season in early April; flower aficionados will also enjoy the park's hydrangea bushes during the rainy season.

spots.name: Mitsui Outlet Park Yokohama Bayside
spots.local: 三井アウトレットパーク 横浜ベイサイド
spots.desc: An outlet shopping mall located in Kanazawahakkei bay area. You get off at Sea side line "Torihama" Stn. It looks like small bay side town. There are about 220 shops. For example, Adidas, Nike, Coach, Edwin and many other popular brands.

spots.name: Cubic Plaza Shin-yokohama
spots.local: キュービックプラザ新横浜
spots.desc: This is a station building at Shin-yokohama Station. There are many types of shops in it. There are 25 restaurants and 9 cafes, and other shops. For example, many shops for clothes, shoes, accessories and bags. Also, a bookstore, some household goods stores, even a bearty-treatment clinic are here. Of course, you can just go shopping or having meals anytime, but it is convenient for passengers…

spots.name: Seikeien Garden
spots.desc: It is a strolling garden designated as a scenic spot of the city.

spots.name: Tokyo Regional Immigration Bureau
spots.local: 東京出入国在留管理局
spots.desc: This center serves foreign residents and long-term visitors. Also houses immigration detention. If going in the morning, get there early because a line forms outside long before opening hours.

spots.name: Miyazaki Prefectural Office
spots.desc: A local icon built prior to World War II in a European style. It's lit up at night.

spots.name: Amaga Castle
spots.desc: The keep has been rebuilt and there is also a museum around the site about the castle and local history.

spots.name: Human Rights and Peace Museum
spots.local: 福山市人権平和資料館

spots.name: Rinkokaku
spots.desc: A guesthouse dating back to 1905 with a nice garden.

spots.name: Former Residence of Marquis Kachō Hironobu
spots.desc: Reiwa-era home of interest to architecture lovers.

spots.name: Kumagaya Sports Park 熊谷運動公園
Aeon Mall Yono
spots.desc: Large shopping complex.

spots.name: Sayama Ski Slope
spots.desc: An indoor ski slope.

spots.name: Utsunomiya Zoo
spots.desc: You can feed many of the animals here.

spots.name: Fusaiji Temple
spots.desc: Buddhist temple.

spots.name: Suwa Jinja Shrine
spots.desc: Shinto shrine.

spots.name: Kanda Yabu soba
spots.desc: Yabu Soba opened its doors for business in 1880.

spots.name: Rihga Royal Hotel
spots.local: リーガロイヤルホテル小倉
spots.desc: This hotel has several high-priced restaurants.

spots.name: Aeon Mall Tokoname
spots.desc: A big mall in the city. You can even take a day of shopping if you want. It is also very close to Chubu Airport, so time management can be easier. Another point worth visiting is the big maneki-neko in the mall called "Otafuku" (おたふく).
spots.addr: 愛知県常滑市りんくう町2丁目20番3

spots.name: Murasaki Shikibu Park
spots.desc: This park was built in honor of Murasaki Shikibu, the author of "The Tale of Genji" who lived for a year in Echizen with her father, Tametoki Fukuwara, governor of this area. The park was modeled after a nobleman's residence in the Heian period, and looks like a very old, rich, and elegant garden. A statue of Murasaki Shikibu stands in the park, gazing in the direction of Kyoto.

spots.name: Nishiyama Park
spots.desc: This small park is particularly beautiful in springtime, when hundreds of azaleas trees bloom on the slopes. There is also a small zoo there, complete with red pandas.

spots.name: Gassho Village
spots.desc: A traditional village with thatched-roof gasshō-zukuri (shaped like hands in prayer) houses. At least one house is authentic, having been constructed in Shirakawa-go in the mid-1800s, and later relocated here to escape being submerged behind a dam. Paint pottery and make paper yourself, and they will mail your handiwork back to you for a fee. There are displays of traditional festivals, and a…
spots.price: Admission ¥800 adults, ¥400 children; ceramics ¥900-1,300; pottery session (1.5 hours, reservations required) ¥2,800…

spots.name: Oku no Hosomichi Haiku Journey Museum
spots.local: 奥の細道むすびの地記念館
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the famous poet Matsuo Basho's journey from Edo (Tokyo) to the Tohoku Region, known as The Narrow Road to the Deep North (Oku no Hosomichi). While Ogaki is obviously not in Tohoku, the museum is here because his journey ended here. There is a 3-D video theater that shows a few different videos throughout the day, and the rest of the museum features exhibits on Basho's…

spots.name: Hida Takayama Museum of History and Art
spots.local: 飛騨高山まちの博物館
spots.desc: The museum is in 17th-century warehouses once owned by the Yajima family who ran a timber business and the Nagata family who owned the best sake breweries in Takayama. There are 14 exhibition rooms dedicated to individual themes ranging from the Takayama Festival and traditional houses to the city’s history and local artists.

spots.name: Sanmachi
spots.desc: It is a very pretty section of Takayama's old city. Consisting of three narrow lanes packed with wooden buildings housing sake breweries and little boutiques, some of the larger merchant houses are now open as museums. The area, though it is definitely worth a visit, is quite touristy now and you will find many tourists around browsing the lanes flanked by tourist-oriented shops. The area is a…

spots.name: Miyagawa Morning Market
spots.desc: Local vendors set up stands along the Miyagawa River each morning to sell their wares, ranging from crafts and handmade items to produce, flowers, and snacks.

spots.name: Kutaniyaki Art Museum
spots.desc: Nestled inside Daishoji's Ko-Kutani-no-Mori Park, the museum artfully displays of a variety of Kutaniyaki Porcela. Visit the second floor tea shop where Japanese tea and sweets are served while you enjoy the beauty of the surrounding gardens.
spots.price: Adult ¥500; 75 or above ¥250; free entry for those under 18 years of age

spots.name: Nakaya Ukichiro Museum of Snow and Ice
spots.local: 中谷宇吉郎雪の科学館
spots.desc: Born in Katayamazu, Dr.Ukichiro Nakaya (1900-1962) was a specialist in snow and the first person to create an artificial snowflake. Museum exhibits highlight the works of Dr. Nakaya and give detail explanations of developments in the study of snow and ice.

spots.name: Yunokuni no Mori
spots.local: 加賀 伝統工芸村 ゆのくにの森
spots.desc: A resort in the Kaga onsen district which has a village of multiple buildings of traditional construction, each showcasing a particular handicraft of the Hokuriku area such as lacquer, gold leaf, fabric dying, paper making, pottery, wood carving, etc. Numerous activities exist for children to try their hands at making their own souvenir, as well as ample high-end products. Multiple restaurants…
spots.price: Adults ¥530, middle and high school students ¥420, children over 4 ¥320

spots.name: Rojo Park
spots.desc: Near city hall, this public park was once the grounds of a castle belonging to Maeda Toshitsune. Though the castle was torn down during the Meiji Era to make way for what is now Komatsu High School, the park remains. It is a very traditional Japanese garden with a tea house, waterfall, and series of ponds. While there are some nods to the design of Kenrokuen — the statue on the hill, the plum…

spots.name: Notojima Glass Art Museum
spots.local: 石川県能登島ガラス美術館
spots.desc: This museum is the only public specialized glass art museum in Japan. It displays some unique glass sculptures based on original ideas from artists such as Picasso and Chagall. It also has some interesting sculptures and a section devoted to old liquor bottles once used in Japan. If that wasn't quirky enough, the building looks like a ship straight out of Star Wars.

spots.name: Nezu Memorial Museum
spots.desc: Located in the former home of Kaichiro Nezu, an entrepreneur who owned over 136 different businesses. Twenty-four of those were railway companies, including Tobu Railway which still operates in the Kanto Region.

spots.name: Shojoji
spots.desc: Mildly famous for a nursery rhyme called "Shojoji no Tanukibayashi", about a raccoon dog (tanuki) whose statue can be found in the temple.

spots.name: Yatsu Rose Garden
spots.desc: A rose garden which displays over 6,000 individual blossoms in May and October. The garden was founded with Yatsu Yūen (谷津遊園), an amusement park which was managed by Keisei Electric Railway and closed in 1982. When the park was closed, the city bought the garden, and has managed it since that time.

spots.name: Mogi Honke Museum of Art
spots.desc: is an art museum opened in January 2006 and displays artworks collected by Shichizaemon Mogi, the 12th head of the Takanashi-Moki family, one of the eight families of the Mogi family that founded Kikkoman.
spots.hours: Wed through Sun from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM (entry until 4:00 PM)

spots.name: Former Residence of Lord Hotta
spots.desc: Residence of Hotta Masatomo, the last lord of the Sakura Domain. Very well preserved.

spots.name: Kiryu Meijikan
spots.desc: Built as the Gunma Prefecture Public Health Centre in 1878, it is a classic example of pseudo-Western architecture. Inside there are exhibition rooms and a coffee/tea shop featuring a nostalgic gramophone and music of the era.
spots.price: Adults: ¥150; elementary and jr high school students: ¥50

spots.name: Kennen Kinenkan
spots.desc: One of the oldest buildings in Western-style architecture in the prefecture. Inside, local antiquities are displayed.
spots.price: adults (high school students or older):¥150, children:¥50

spots.name: Hitachi Civic Center
spots.local: 日立シビックセンター
spots.desc: There is a music hall and other facilities here where various events are held. Also a science museum, a celestial theater, and a library, too.

spots.name: Sōun Museum
spots.desc: On the south edge of the park is the small Sōun Museum, housing landscape and nature paintings by the Ashikaga clan's official artist, Tazaki Sōun (1815-1898), who exhibited his depiction of Mount Fuji at the World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago in 1893.

spots.name: Sanninudai
spots.desc: Believed by some to be an above-water portion of the mysterious undersea ruins (different from the Yonaguni Monument) because it is shaped almost like a sort of stairway. The strangely-shaped rocks of Gunkaniwa can be easily seen from here. Also, there's a rock here with some writing on it which is mysterious. It bears little resemblance to kaida-dii, the island's indigenous writing system, and…

spots.name: Warei Shrine
spots.desc: A large, comparatively staid Shinto shrine, probably Uwajima's best-known attraction among the Japanese. Not worth a detour, but you'll be passing by on your way to the Taga Shrine anyway.

spots.name: Warei Festival
spots.desc: This annual festival features not only bull sumo but a series of parades featuring Uwajima's symbol: the black-bearded and red-robed bull demon (牛鬼 ushioni). Book accommodation early if in town during festival time.

spots.name: Taimeshi
spots.desc: This is the local dish. It is sea bream/red snapper on top of dried kelp and gently boiled over rice in an unfinished earthenware pot. Variations occur up and down Ehime, but Uwajima style — raw and flavored with sake — is considered the principal upon which all others are built.

spots.name: Yashima Ski Area
spots.local: 鳥海高原矢島スキー場
spots.desc: Ski area in Yashima. Ski and snowboard rentals available. Small gear shop. Two restaurants. Two ski lifts (4 person and 2 person).

spots.name: michi-no-eki Yonezawa
spots.desc: A large roadside souvenir shop and tourist information center where you can buy local sake, Yonezawa beef products, and other local goods.

spots.name: Echizen Daibutsu
spots.desc: Built in 1987, this is the largest indoor Buddha in Japan. Sadly, its relative newness causes it to be overshadowed by Todaiji temple in Nara. The temple complex, which includes a large pagoda, is beautiful and surrounded by forested hills.

spots.name: Daishō-in
spots.desc: The Mori warlords who aren't at Toko-ji are buried here - along with the graves of several retainers, who committed seppuku upon the death of their masters. The atmosphere at Daisho-in is strikingly calm, though, compared to the pomp of Tokoji. Daishoin is listed among the temples of the Chugoku 33 Temple Pilgrimage.

spots.name: Hikobe Manor
spots.desc: A fully restored Samurai residence dating back over 400 years. Hikobe direct descendants still live on the property. Declared a National Important History Site. One of the oldest private homes in the Kanto region.
spots.hours: weekends 10:00 - 16:00 (reservations required for weekday tours). Closed on weekdays (unless you have a reservation.)

spots.name: Chichibu Temple Pilgrimage
spots.local: 秩父札所三十四観音霊場
spots.desc: In Chichibu and the surrounding area are a circuit of 34 temples, dedicated to Kannon, the goddess of mercy and compassion. These are traditionally visited by walking, but this would take more than a few days. A bicycle is a wonderful way to not only visit some of the temples, but also see some of the surrounding area.

spots.name: Mt. Hinoto
spots.desc: A round trip climb up and down Mt. Hinoto takes around 5 hours. Get supplies in Jinego before going to the trail head. For a few kilometers leading to the trail head, the road is unpaved. The mountain is 1,145 m high.

spots.name: Pottery Footpath
spots.addr: 愛知県常滑市栄町３丁目８

spots.name: Okozu Salt Works
spots.desc: An ancient salt production site.

spots.name: SL Paleo Express
spots.desc: Travel on a steam locomotive.

spots.name: Akata Giant Buddha
spots.desc: A large Buddha statue.

spots.name: AEON MALL Nagakute
spots.desc: If you don't want to have lunch at the Toyota Automobile Museum, this is the place you usually go, then.
spots.addr: 愛知県長久手市勝入塚501番地

spots.name: Iwamura Sake Brewery
spots.desc: Brand name: Onna Joshu (女城主, Lady of the Castle). Sake brewery with many interesting flavors. On Sundays in February, visitors can get tours of the making process and drink a few varieties as much as they like for a small fee.

spots.name: Shiraito Falls
spots.desc: Beautiful waterfall named for the "white threads" that create a waterfall-like appearance. It's most popular during the fall when many people come to see the autumn leaves. In winter, you can see the waterfall frozen, forming fragile icicles.

spots.name: Suwa Fireworks Festival
spots.local: 諏訪湖祭湖上花火大会
spots.desc: An enormous event on the lake on August 15th. Get there early, mark your sitting spot the night before or the early morning of, eat stand food, drink beer, watch one of the top 5 fireworks shows in Japan. Come early to the fireworks and visit the Taiko Festival in neighboring Okaya a few days before.

spots.name: Shukunegi
spots.desc: On the south coast, close to Ogi, lies the small and picturesque harbour of Shukunegi with traditional wooden houses reminiscent of the Edo period. This settlement is close to Yajima-Kyōjima (矢島経島), one of the most famous places on the island to try Taraibune (see Do section)

spots.name: Oi Shrine
spots.desc: A Shinto shrine that enshrines the spirit of the Oi River and is known for the Shimada Grand Festival (Obi Festival) held for three days in mid-October once every three years (years of the tiger, snake, monkey, and boar).

spots.name: Aki-Takata City History and Folk Museum
spots.local: 安芸高田市歴史民俗博物館
spots.desc: This local museum covers the history of Aki-Takata city and its culture through historical items, with a particular focus on Yoshida-Koriyama Castle and the Mōri clan. Displays are in Japanese only. Photography is not allowed in the exhibit rooms. Gift shop sells goods and books related to the Mōri clan, as well as castle stamps on Yoshida-Koriyama Castle and adjacent castles in the city.…
spots.hours: Daily 09:00-17:00, closed on Tuesdays (except for holidays), the day after holidays (except on weekends) and 29th…

spots.name: Ino Tadataka Museum
spots.desc: Located on the historical street. Ino Tadataka is famous for creating the first scientific, highly accurate maps of Japan.

spots.name: Suigo Sawara Dashi Kaikan
spots.desc: Sawara's summer and autumn festivals have been designated as an important intangible folk-cultural properties. This museum displays two floats used in those festivals.

spots.name: Ushiku Chateau
spots.desc: Former winery buildings, registered as a Japan Heritage in 2020.

spots.name: Saigō Takamori Statue
spots.desc: Near the main entrance to the park from JR station stands an unassuming statue of a pudgy man walking his dog. This is Saigō Takamori, a famous samurai general best known for leading the doomed Satsuma Rebellion against the Meiji government (and the inspiration for Hollywood blockbuster The Last Samurai). These days, it's the canonical place for meeting people at the park.

spots.name: Izumifumoto
spots.desc: This Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings was used as a defensive base for the Satsuma clan. It is composed of samurai residences sandwiched between stone walls made of cobblestones and high fences was a living base for the samurai. The Izumifumoto Historical Museum displays ancient documents and weapons.

spots.name: Yoshokan
spots.desc: Built in 1869, the Yoshokan was the home of an Ito Clan member. The garden has also been preserved.

spots.name: Takeo Shrine
spots.desc: The shrine is home to The Great Camphor Tree, a 3000-year-old tree sacred tree. It is known as a "power spot" and must be seen to be believed.

spots.name: Sawara Matsuri
spots.desc: Actually, there are 2 three-day long festivals each year. The summer festival is on a consecutive Friday, Saturday, and Sunday between July 9 and 18. The fall festival is on a consecutive Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, on the week of the second Saturday of October. During the festival around a dozen dashi (floats) are pulled and pushed around Sawara buy dozens of people. Inside each dashi are…

spots.name: Fukuma Beach
spots.desc: Known as "Kyushu's Shonan", it is one of the prefecture's leading marine leisure areas, making it a popular spot with restaurants and other establishments lined up along the coast.

spots.name: Satsuma Kinzangura
spots.desc: Satsuma Kinzangura is one of Ichikikushikino's attractions, utilizing an actual Kushikino gold mine tunnel with hundreds of years of history as a shochu (Japanese spirit) distillery and aging cellar. Visitors take a 'torokko' (tram) into the mine tunnel, where a cool, stable temperature of around 19°C (66°F) is maintained year-round, and can witness the magnificent sight of countless shochu aging…

spots.name: Hamada Shuzо̄ Denbeegura
spots.desc: You can go on a brewery tour, and you can try the shochu liquor from the brewery.

spots.name: Legoland Discovery Center Osaka
spots.local: レゴランド・ディスカバリー・センター大阪

spots.name: Saga Prefecture Science and Space Museum
spots.desc: Promises science fun for the whole family.

spots.name: Poison Gas Museum
spots.local: 大久野島の毒ガス製造
spots.desc: tells the story of the islands role in producing poison gas during World War II, and "was established in order to alert as many people as possible to the dreadful truths about poison gas.".

spots.name: Raigō-in
spots.desc: A temple famous for its Buddhist chants, visitors can hear these chants for free on Sundays at 13:00. Sutra copying is also offered for ¥1000.

spots.name: Shorin-in
spots.desc: The priest Hōnen's famous question-and-answer session was held in the temple's hondō (main hall). At the session, he is said to have shined the temple's principal Buddhist sculpture using only his prayers.

spots.name: Asuka-ni-imasu Shrine
spots.desc: Asuka Niimasu Shrine (Asuka-imasu Jinja) is an ancient Shinto shrine in the hills north of Asuka village. Dedicated to several deities associated with the protection of the region and fertility, the shrine is particularly known for its unusual fertility symbolism. Its annual Onda Matsuri in February is famous for its fertility rituals and humorous performances. The present shrine buildings are…

spots.name: Yubatake
spots.desc: Literally "Hot Water Field", this hot spring in the center of town gushes out 5,000 liters of 70°C water per minute, making it Japan's largest. There is an elaborate cooling system of wooden conduits and a number of baths directly around it.

spots.name: Tropical zoo Kusatsu Nettaiken
spots.desc: A tropical area which people can see different types of animals. In the jungle dome, they create subtropical area by using the hot spring heat and keep in the dome warm, so animals are able to survive.

spots.name: Kusatsu international ski area
spots.desc: In the winter time, Kusatsu is famous for its skiing area and this place is good to visit. It also is a nice hiking area in the warmer months.

spots.name: Nakanojo Museum of Folk and History
spots.local: 中之条町歴史と民俗の博物館
spots.desc: Nakanojo Museum of Folk and History displays archaeological finds and historical objects from Nakanojō and the surrounding Agatsuma region of Gunma Prefecture. Exhibits include pottery and stone tools from prehistoric settlements, materials relating to the area's development during the Edo period, and tools, household objects and documents illustrating traditional farming and rural life.

spots.name: Sadamisaki Lighthouse
spots.desc: This lighthouse stands at the tip of the peninsula, overlooking the Hōyo Strait. On clear days you can see across to Kyūshū. 1.8 km of hiking trails and a campground lay at its feet.

spots.name: Naoshima Bath House I ♥ Yu
spots.desc: A fully functional art installation with Japanese traditional public bath. Designed by Shinro Ohtake collaborated with graf. Naming "I ♥ Yu" is a pun, word playing on you and yu means hot water in Japanese.

spots.name: Sawatari Onsen
spots.desc: Sawatari Onsen is a small, traditional hot-spring resort near Nakanojō. that is quieter and less developed than nearby Kusatsu Onsen, it is known for its clear, mildly alkaline spring water, traditionally associated with soothing the skin. The compact settlement has several Japanese inns and a public bathhouse, Sawatari Onsen Public Bath, where visitors can bathe without staying overnight.

spots.name: Mount Mitsumine
spots.desc: Home to the 2000-year-old Mitsumine Shrine (三峯神社 Mitsumine-jinja, ) on the summit of this fairly tame 1100m mountain. The easiest methods of access are via cable car from Chichibu Railway Mitsumine-guchi (¥ 950/1650 one-way/return, every 30 min from 09:00 to 16:30) or direct bus from Seibu Chichibu station (¥900, 5 daily). Still, you may find it more rewarding to hike up (or down), there…

spots.name: Uezu House
spots.desc: This traditional Okinawan style house was built in 1726. It is the former home of the governing parties during the Ryukyu Kingdom era.

spots.name: Manazuru Hantō Prefectural Natural Park
spots.local: 神奈川県立真鶴半島自然公園

spots.name: Kumata Shrine
spots.desc: Established in 861 (Jogan 3), this ancient Shinto shrine serves as the guardian of the Hirano Old City. It is also famous for its dynamic summer festival called Hirano-gō Summer Festival held annually in July, featuring traditional Danjiri float processions.
spots.hours: Open daily, daytime hours for the main shrine grounds.

spots.name: AEON Kire-Uriwari
spots.local: イオン喜連瓜破ショッピングセンター
spots.desc: The largest shopping centre in Southeast Osaka, at Kire-Uriwari Station, with a supermarket, specialty shops, and food court.

spots.name: Ganko Hirano-gō Yashiki
spots.desc: Japanese restaurant in a 400-year-old merchant house, with a garden and a small living-culture museum attached.

spots.name: Onioshidashi Volcanic Park
spots.desc: Onioshidashi Volcanic Park is a striking landscape of jagged black lava rocks on the northern slopes of Mount Asama, on the border of Gunma and Nagano prefectures. The rocks were created by the volcano's catastrophic 1783 eruption, when a massive lava flow engulfed the surrounding landscape. Walking paths wind through the formations, with views of Mount Asama and a Buddhist temple dedicated to…

spots.name: Pirates of Tokyo Bay
spots.local: パイレーツ・オブ・東京湾
spots.desc: Tokyo's long-running English and Japanese improv comedy group has performed unscripted shows at What the Dickens! since 2010. The international cast takes audience suggestions in both languages and builds scenes on the spot using physical comedy and pantomime, keeping things accessible regardless of language ability. Book tickets online in advance as shows can sell out.
spots.hours: Last Sun of each month, doors 19:00
spots.addr: What the Dickens!, Roob 6 Bldg 4F, 1-13-3 Ebisu-nishi, Shibuya-ku

spots.name: Dentsu Shiki Theater Umi
spots.desc: A theater in the Caretta Shiodome complex where musicals play.

spots.name: Oku-Iya Niju Kazurabashi
spots.desc: For considerably more atmosphere and far fewer crowds (if any at all), the Oku-Iya Niju Kazurabashi (奥祖谷二重かずら橋 Deep Iya Double Vine Bridge) can be found at the eastern end of the valley, before the final ascent to Mi-no-Koshi.

spots.name: Seikan Tunnel Museum
spots.desc: If you hope see the tunnel, take Funicular can go to tunnel level. Closed in winter: early November to mid April. (The funicular stopped service for vehicle damage in Sept 2023. Cloud funding for repair is going on Readyfor).

spots.name: Hirano "Machigurumi" Museum
spots.desc: Town-wide ecomuseum network started in 1993; the walk between the 16 museums is part of the experience. Internationally recognized as one of Japan's pioneering ecomuseum initiatives, it is organized entirely by local residents, with no government involvement.

spots.name: Kichijoji Theatre
spots.desc: A live show venue. Shows are only in Japanese.

spots.name: Hirayu Waterfall
spots.desc: A 64-meter-high waterfall, well marked and easily accessible along a short path. In winter the frozen waterfall is illuminated. Occasional buses, but check schedules carefully so you don't get stranded.

spots.name: Hirayama Ikuo Museum of Art
spots.desc: The home museum of celebrated modern painter Hirayama Ikuo (1930–2009), who explored themes like the Silk Road and the Hiroshima bombing through classical Japanese paintings.

spots.name: Mitarai Preservation District
spots.desc: The town of Mitarai grew as a port for ships waiting for rising tide or favourable winds. Today, the town includes gabled houses with sangawarabuki roofs and is dotted with Western style houses. The port area retains its historical character with groynes, stepped piers and a lighthouse, and is gazetted as an Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings.

spots.name: Sumiya
spots.desc: A conserved historic former teahouse in what was once the red-light district of Kyoto, it is today a museum. Only open to the public seasonally.

spots.name: Jōnan-gū Shrine
spots.desc: Although Jōnan-gū Shrine is rarely visited by foreign tourists, it is a beautiful shrine with extensive history. It was established by Emperor Kammu when Kyoto became the nation's capital. At the end of the Heian period, it became home to retired emperor Goshirakawa. As a result, the beautiful Rakusui-en Garden was constructed. As a former Imperial Villa, Jōnan-gū Shrine is a great alternative…
spots.price: Entrance to the shrine grounds is free, but the garden costs ¥500 to enter

spots.name: Shōji-ji
spots.desc: Nicknamed Cherry Blossom Temple (hana no tera), it hosts a beautiful display of blossoms in the spring.

spots.name: Basho Museum
spots.hours: 9:30-17:00 (last admission 16:30), closed second and fourth Mondays unless a national holiday, closed Dec 29-Jan 1…
spots.price: Adults & High School: ¥200, Elementary & Junior High ¥100

spots.name: LaLaport Toyosu
spots.local: アーバンドック ららぽーと豊洲
spots.desc: Large shopping complex.

spots.name: Osagoe Minkaen
spots.desc: A small folk village with five historic thatched-roof houses on display as an open-air museum.

spots.name: Old Battlefield of Kawanakajima
spots.desc: Kawanakajima Battlefield is the site of the famous battles fought between Takeda Shingen and Uesugi Kenshin in the 16th century, most notably the fourth battle in 1561. The battlefield was part of the wider plain where the forces of the two warlords repeatedly clashed during the Sengoku period. Today the site is a peaceful park with a shrine, monuments and information panels, including a statue…

spots.name: Colette・Mare
spots.desc: This is a big mall which opened in 2010. Many shops, restaurants, bars, theater, and lifestyle things are in. It takes only a minute to go here from Sakuragicho Stn of JR line.

spots.name: Crea Mall
spots.desc: The shopping strip running between Kawagoe and Hon-Kawagoe stations, offers many of the usual chains and numerous ramen shops. There is a good kaiten sushi place towards the Kawagoe end.

spots.name: Urawa Art Museum
spots.desc: The museum collects and displays art of and from books. They also aim to foster local artists by featuring their works.

spots.name: Urawa Corso
spots.desc: A mall with a variety of shoes and clothing shops, as well as some specialty shops.

spots.name: Romantic Mura
spots.local: 道の駅うつのみや ろまんちっく村
spots.desc: The park has a huge onsen, a brewpub and food court, and a FlowerDome containing tropical plants, hydroponically grown herbs, and a wide variety of orchids.

spots.name: Tachikawa Stage Garden
spots.desc: A large event venue with interesting architecture and near-daily concerts.

spots.name: Shitamachi Museum Annex
spots.local: 下町風俗資料館付設展示場
spots.desc: Many buildings scattered around the Yanaka district survived the bombings of World War II, including this former sake store built in 1910. Characteristic of Meiji-era architecture, the building now houses a small museum of sake and beer equipment.
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 09:30-16:30, closed Mon, also Tue following a holiday. Closed until March 2025 for renovations

spots.name: Myōkō-ji Temple
spots.desc: According to legend, the grave of Lady Oiwa (Oiwa-san) in Yotsuya Kaidan, Japan's best-known ghost story and a direct inspiration for the Ring horror movies, is in this temple. In a nutshell, the beautiful Oiwa was disfigured, divorced and killed, and then comes back to haunt the people who wronged her.

spots.name: Sugao no taki waterfall
spots.desc: This waterfall in Kokura Minami ward is cool and popular with Japanese residents in the summer. Watch out for baby wild boars (uribo) which have been known to nibble at feet in search of food (from personal experience). You can rent bicycles from Dobaru cycling terminal and cycle around the whole area for a few hundred yen. Buses run to here from Kokura Station.

spots.name: Zenringai
spots.desc: On the road to Chōshō-ji Temple, here is a collection of 33 Zen temples moved or built here to spiritually safeguard Hirosaki Castle.

spots.name: Sazaedo
spots.desc: An architectural wonder, the Sazaedo contains two spiral staircases running opposite one another so that those going up will never cross paths with those going down. It's a temple with 33 statues that represent the temples of the Saigoku 33 Pilgrimage in the Kansai area. Visitors are meant to pray at each to receive special blessings in lieu of visiting each of the real temples.

spots.name: Fukushima Inari Shrine
spots.desc: A historic Shinto shrine dedicated to Inari, the deity of prosperity and agriculture. Known for its striking red torii gates. The shrine hosts seasonal festivals, including the Fukushima Inari Festival in autumn.

spots.name: Bansui Sōdō
spots.desc: The former residence of Bansui Doi, a famous poet and scholar of English Literature in Japan, but generally unknown to non-Japanese. Best known for writing the lyrics to "Kōjō no Tsuki" (荒城の月, "The Moon over the Ruined Castle").
spots.addr: 〒980-0804 宮城県仙台市青葉区大町1-2-2

spots.name: Toyama matsuri
spots.desc: Toyama festival is held in August and includes a fireworks display and various local activities.

spots.name: Hamafukutsuru-Ginjo Brewery and Shop
spots.desc: Offers factory tours, rather than just a museum. Can watch actual processes from behind glass walls.

spots.name: Kandu Makuhari
spots.local: カンドゥー幕張新都心
spots.desc: Edutainment indoor amusement park, allowing children to role play adult jobs and earn currency. Similar to KidZania.

spots.name: Hideyo Noguchi Memorial Park
spots.desc: The laboratory of bacteriologist Hideyo Noguchi, who discovered the bacteria that causes syphilis and worked on yellow fever vaccines, and whose face adorns the ¥1000 note. The original building was destroyed in the Great Kanto Earthquake, and the present structure dates from 1997.

spots.name: Hiyoshi Park
spots.desc: There is a fountain, playground equipment, and a big grass square. There are many beautiful Japanese apricot trees in spring with white and pink flowers. You can enjoy ball games there too.

spots.name: Nagashima Memorial Hall
spots.desc: This is a memorial museum that uses Kyosuke Nagashima's birthplace.
spots.hours: Wed-Sun 10:00-16:00 (closed summer and New Year's holidays)

spots.name: Red Voltage
spots.desc: This is the official souvenir shop for the Urawa Red Diamonds soccer team, three time Asian champions.

spots.name: Heiwa Kannon
spots.desc: 28 meter tall stone statue commemorating the victims of the Second World War. Across the street from Tenkaisan temple.

spots.name: Kotori No Mori
spots.desc: It's a steep walk up a small mountain. The trails at the top are short and quiet. It is very peaceful but not so special except for bird watchers.

spots.name: Fukui City Museum of Natural History
spots.desc: A museum showcasing the local flora, fauna and geology.

spots.name: Ruins of Nedo Castle
spots.desc: This castle was built by Ota Dokan.

spots.name: School of white birch curry
spots.desc: The curry made by Kaneko Yanagi.

spots.name: Izumo Taisha Saitama Branch
spots.desc: A shrine and church of the Izumo Taisha sect.
spots.addr: 2-20-18 Honmachi 埼玉県朝霞市本町2-20−18

spots.name: Utsunomiya Fairy Museum
spots.local: うつのみや妖精ミュージアム
spots.desc: An fairy-theme art museum.

spots.name: Haijimadaishi Temple
spots.desc: Buddhist temple next to Haijima Park.

spots.name: MoriTown
spots.desc: Shopping center.

spots.name: Mori Building Digital Art Museum: teamLab Borderless
spots.local: 森ビル デジタルアート ミュージアム：エプソン チームラボボーダレス
spots.desc: Art museum with immersive art exhibits.
spots.price: ¥3600-5600, depending on how far in advance you buy
spots.addr: Azabudai Hills Garden Plaza B B1 5-9, Toranomon, Minato-ku,

spots.name: Misen Chubu International Airport
spots.desc: Surprisingly inexpensive ramen in the airport. The restaurant is famous for its spicy ramen, Taiwan ramen (台湾ラーメン), since spicy food is rare in Japanese cuisine. Taiwan ramen has been seen as a classic Nagoya cuisine, so it may be worth trying one. If you are not ready for something very spicy, try American ramen (アメリカン) first.

spots.name: Tokonyan
spots.desc: A big cat statue in the city. Need to take a walk to get there.

spots.name: Costco Wholesale Chubu Airport Warehouse
spots.local: コストコ中部空港倉庫店
spots.desc: Well, you can have an enjoyable experience when you have a Costco membership and a car, just like other Costco Warehouses. While any Costco member can enter every Costco Warehouse in the world, only a car can carry large goods from Costco. Therefore, only buy from Costco if considering driving in Japan. It also has a petrol station, so you can fuel there before returning the car to the car rental…
spots.addr: 愛知県常滑市りんくう町1-25-14

spots.name: Omushi Shrine
spots.desc: It is said that this shrine has more than one thousand years of history. The shrine was rebuilt in 1996. There are two figures of male gods which are National Important Cultural Properties. A large rock god, Oiwasama, is enshrined here. Pure water called Ishigami-no-mizu is used by many people to wash their hands or rinse out their mouths. This water was once used as part of the town’s water…

spots.name: Hino Shrine
spots.desc: This shrine is located at the entrance of Mt. Hino, known as the Mt. Fuji of Echizen. The shrine and all of the mountain is thought to be a sacred place. There is another shrine at the top of the mountain. The Mt. Hino festival takes place during the summer. Dances are performed to honor the god of Mt. Hino. At night, participants climb Mt. Hino with lit torches to watch the sunrise from the top…

spots.name: Gōshō-ji Temple
spots.desc: Gōshō-ji Temple is one of the headquarters of Shinshū sect in Buddhism. It is a very sober experience to walk under the valuable, decorated gate which is made of zelkova wood. The temple was built in Kyoto by Shinran in 1223. It was moved to Echizen City in 1615. The spacious temple contains Shinran Hall, Amida Hall, a warehouse of sutras, and a bell tower. Inspired after visiting the temple in…

spots.name: Okafuto Shrine & Otaki Shrine
spots.desc: These shrines stand side by side on the top of Mt. Gongen, and a combined shrine, which was rebuilt through the advanced skills in constructing shrines in the latter half of Edo Era, lies at the foot of the mountain. The goddess of paper, -- the only one in Japan -- "Mistress Kawakami," is enshrined here. Legend says she taught people how to make paper 1,500 years ago. In 1985 these shrines were…

spots.name: World Divine Light Headquarters
spots.desc: The surreal world headquarters of the Japanese new religion of World Divine Light (世界真光文明教団 Sekai Mahikari Bunmei Kyodan) looks like something straight out of anime, with a cantilevered five-level temple roof perched on a remote hillside. Known of its divine light healing rituals, the religion is widely considered a cult, but visitors are welcome (although two days' notice is requested) and…

spots.name: Kiryu Nature Sanctuary
spots.desc: Situated in a woodland area at the foot of the mountains on the west side of Kiryu, the Nature Centre has exhibits and a lecture room. The park features many nature trails, an observation building for bird-watching. A large variety of plants and animals can be viewed throughout the seasons.

spots.name: Caribbean Beach
spots.desc: One of the largest all-season indoor water parks in the Kanto region. Facilities include a wave pool, a current pool, water slides, jacuzzi and an Olympic size swimming pool.

spots.name: Ikaho Onsen
spots.desc: Ikaho Onsen is a historic hot-spring resort on the slopes of Mount Haruna, known for its distinctive 365 stone steps running through the centre of the old town. The staircase is lined with traditional inns, souvenir shops, cafés and bathing facilities, including the public bath Ishidan no Yu. The area's iron-rich spring water, known as Kogane-no-yu (“golden water”), has a brownish colour, while a…

spots.name: Yonehara Beach
spots.desc: Offers nice sand and better coral reefs within easy snorkeling distance, and it's probably the most rewarding place to snorkel near the shore anywhere in the Yaeyama Islands. The reef begins within meters of the beach and hosts enough life to interest experienced snorkelers and beginners alike. Caution should be taken, however as Yonehara's rip currents are notoriously strong. There is a sign…

spots.name: Honjo Park
spots.desc: Have a picnic. In April or May, watch cherry blossoms in the park.

spots.name: Kiryu Yagibushi Festival
spots.desc: The festival is the largest event of the year in Kiryu. During the 3-day long event, more than 500,000 people from Gunma Prefecture and other parts of Japan visit the city. The major focus is Yagibushi folk dancing which takes place at various locations on the streets of downtown Kiryu. Traditional musicians sit on bandstands, around which festival-goers dance through the evening. The…
spots.hours: first Fri, Sat and Sun in August

spots.name: Kiryu Fashion Week
spots.local: 桐生ファッションウィーク
spots.desc: Various events are held at locations throughout the city during a one-week period. Events include fashion shows, textiles, art, & local history and culture. The Classic Car Festival, held since 2006, brings together distinctive automobiles from Japan and overseas. Held on the campus of Gunma University School of Science & Technology.

spots.name: Kurohone Summer Festival
spots.desc: Catching trout by hand, Yagibushi dancing, & fireworks are the main attractions.

spots.name: Iyo Satsuma
spots.desc: It is a dish made from fish mashed with mugimiso and stock. It creates a roasted, salty, sauce-like concoction. It is usually served over a bowl of hot rice.

spots.name: Miroku Nature Park
spots.desc: At the northern foot of the Sanuki Mountains in the Okawa district of Sanuki City, Kagawa Prefecture. There are sports facilities, leisure facilities, and accommodation facilities. There is a roadside station Miroku in a nearby facility.

spots.name: Noboribetsu Date Jidaimura
spots.desc: Theme park about Edo era.

spots.name: Chokai Ballpark
spots.desc: This ballpark hosts youth and adult baseball games.

spots.name: Kannabe Valley
spots.desc: Hiking.

spots.name: Katsuura Castle
spots.desc: Historic site designated by the city.

spots.name: Sado History and Traditional Museum
spots.desc: Close to Mano Goryo is a small museum about local legends, with displays from the craft master Sasaki Shodo. One of the tourist "attractions" (for a lack of better word) is the former US soldier Charles Jenkins, who as of 2008 works at the souvenir shop of the museum. You will probably recognize him after the dozens of photographs with Japanese TV celebrities found all over the place, and many…

spots.name: Osonehachiman Shrine
spots.desc: A Shinto shrine founded in 1503 dedicated to the kami Hachiman, the god of war.

spots.name: Amuse Musical Theater
spots.local: 六本木ブルーシアター
spots.desc: Musicals in the theater where Blue Man Group did 1400 performances.

spots.name: Satsuma Students Museum
spots.local: 薩摩藩英国留学生記念館
spots.desc: Satsuma Domain was a British international student who learned cutting-edge technology and others in England in 1865 and tried to modernize Japan. The exterior is an image of the "Satsuma-style Yangok" with a Japanese tile roof on the exterior wall using red bricks in the early Meiji period. There is a museum shop and cafe, so you can enjoy British tea time.

spots.name: Shibi Shrine
spots.desc: It enshrines the so-called 'Hyuga Sandai' of Ninokigi no Mikoto, Hikohohidemi no Mikoto, and Ubukigusabuki Fugai no Mikoto. It is dedicated at the autumn festival on September 23rd.

spots.name: Hizen Yume Kaido
spots.desc: A theme park of ninjas. If you visit Ureshino and your children are interested in ninjas, it won't hurt to visit the park.

spots.name: Kumano Shrine
spots.desc: It enshrines the three gods of Kumano: Izanami no Mikoto, Yomotsu no Mikoto, and Hayatama no Mikoto.

spots.name: Takaono Nakanoichi
spots.desc: A two-day market held every March at the equinox to celebrate the arrival of spring, with about 300 stalls selling seedlings, flowers, miscellaneous goods, food, and more. It attracts 100,000 people. There are performances by Takaono Heiroku Taiko and Nodago Shimazu Taiko drums, as well as events such as jumbo soba eating competitions.
spots.addr: The area around the Takaono Station on the Hisatsu Orange Railway

spots.name: Anmitsukan
spots.desc: The Cymbidium is a western type of orchid. Interestingly, the majority of all Cymbidiums worldwide are breeds that were 'born' in Mima. Around 40 different kinds of Cymbidium products are sold here, from Cymbidium hair tonic to wine and tea.

spots.name: Fuji no Kuni Tea Museum
spots.local: ふじのくに茶の都ミュージアム

spots.name: Kannoji Temple
spots.desc: A temple of the Shokokuji school of the Rinzai sect.

spots.name: Takamatsuzuka Mural Museum
spots.desc: Takamatsuzuka Burial Mound (Takamatsuzuka kofun) is a small 7th-century burial mound famous for the richly coloured wall paintings discovered inside in 1972. The paintings depict figures including the celebrated Asuka Beauties, as well as the Four Guardian Gods and representations of the sun, moon and stars. The original tomb is carefully protected and is not open to visitors, but the nearby…

spots.name: Asama Volcano Museum
spots.desc: Good for from kids to adults to experience power of volcano and a global beat of the earth.
spots.hours: April to November: Thu-Tue 08:30-17:00, last entry 16:30

spots.name: Kawakita Onsen
spots.desc: A free outdoor hot spring in mountains..

spots.name: Ainokura Village
spots.desc: Ainokura Village is a small historic mountain village in Gokayama, Toyama Prefecture, renowned for its traditional gasshō-zukuri farmhouses, with steep thatched roofs designed to withstand heavy winter snowfall. Nestled in a secluded valley, the village has around 20 surviving traditional houses, some of which are several centuries old. A number remain inhabited, while others serve as museums…

spots.name: Suganuma Village
spots.desc: Suganuma Village is a small, picturesque historic settlement in Gokayama, Toyama Prefecture, known for its traditional *gasshō-zukuri* farmhouses with steep thatched roofs designed to withstand heavy snowfall. The village has nine surviving traditional houses, set among fields and wooded hills beside the Shō River. Some buildings contain small museums illustrating local life and the region's…

spots.name: Shōryūdō
spots.desc: The only limestone cave accessible by a 600-m-long self-guided walking tour, without special equipment.

spots.name: Aomori Spring Ski Resort
spots.local: 青森スプリング・スキーリゾート
spots.desc: Formerly known as Naqua Shirakami Resort. Ski resort in Ajigasawa Town. Golf in the summer.
spots.addr: 〒038-2712青森県西津軽郡鰺ヶ沢町大字長平町字西岩木山75

spots.name: Kichijoji Anime Wonderland
spots.local: 吉祥寺アニメワンダーランド
spots.desc: A large animation festival that occurs in mid-October every year. English-language tours of the festival may be available from tour operator H.I.S. The last edition to date was held in 2020, with its future unsure.

spots.name: Festival Jindai Odori
spots.desc: It is a traditional folk dance festival and considered a protected cultural asset for its long history and unique style. Costumed participants dance to beating taiko drums at the grounds of a shrine hidden in the forest atop a small mountain. Held annually on June 25th of the lunar calendar (approximately mid-end July), the turn off for the shrine is a couple hundred meters from the Kazurabashi…

spots.name: Hakusan shrine
spots.desc: The place to worship Japanese God. There is a big portable shrine, a big box and the Japanese believe that Japanese God rides to it while Japanese festival is being held. Every fall, there is a festival where Japanese carry the big portable shrine through the city by walking. It is a very ancient tradition. You can see this festival. And Hakusan shrine is famous for the zelkova tree. It has two…

spots.name: Izena Tamaudun
spots.desc: One of only three royal mausoleums in Okinawa, where much of the Shō family is buried. (The kings, though, are at the main Tamaudun near Naha.)

spots.name: Oboke Michi-no-Eki
spots.desc: (Road Station rest stop) This large curvy wood building has 24-hour bathrooms, lots of local souvenirs, a cafe, and plenty of travel information. It also holds a paid museum about traditional Japanese mythical monsters (called "Yokai"), many of which have their origins in this area. Local travel information and brochures are available.

spots.name: Naruko Gorge
spots.desc: This is a steep 2.5-km-long ravine famous for its fall colors in October and November.

spots.name: Lake Hamana Music Box Museum
spots.local: 浜名湖オルゴールミュージアム, Hamanako Orugoru Myujiamu
spots.desc: The collection includes dozens of self-playing orgels and music boxes from around the world. Performances begin hourly at 20 after the hour, and there is also a special hands-on exhibit. The view of Lake Hamana from outside the museum is spectacular as well.

spots.name: Gohyaku-rakan
spots.desc: Also known as the "Hills of 500 Buddhas", is next to the Toyama Folk Village. Even from a short distance away, nothing is visible but a few trees and a small, dilapidated temple. When you get closer however, you find yourself surrounded by hundreds of eerie and atmospheric Buddha statues, dressed in multi-colored ribbons. The statues are disciples of Buddha.

spots.name: Toyama Castle
