spots.desc: Car parking from ¥1,000 per day. Length of beach: 300 m, sea is 100 m from sand dunes with 1.5 m in depth. Barbecues, wind surfing (outside of swimming areas). A stylish beach near Marina City.

spots.name: Banchaya
spots.desc: Japanese green tea stores. Green tea soft serve ice cream. Tax free available.

spots.name: Boutique Shima
spots.desc: Best knitwear shop. The shop is Shima Seiki retail shop. Shima Seiki is leading company on knitting machines in the world. You get a WHOLEGARMENT knitwear is a low price.

spots.name: Meat Maruhikotei
spots.desc: Yakibuta Berger is boast pork and boiled pork with mandarin roll.

spots.name: Surugaya
spots.desc: Yōkan was invented in Japan. Yōkan is a thick, jellied dessert made of red bean paste, agar, and sugar.

spots.name: Hotel de Yoshino
spots.desc: Tateru Yoshino's French cuisine restaurant. Stella Maris, chef Yoshino's Michelin-starred restaurant in Paris, earned its stellar reputation based on high-level French cooking (with subtle Japanese influences) and excellent game dishes.

spots.name: Surfing
spots.desc: Chiba is known as one of the more consistent areas for surfing in Japan. World Tour contests have been held at Katsuura and other areas of Kujyukuri coast. If traveling by train, one of the more convenient stops is Kamogawa. The beach is just minutes from the station, with surf shops, and plenty of hotels. If by car, explore the coast. Typhoon season is best.

spots.name: Inohana Castle
spots.desc: Razed in 1516, a reconstruction of the castle tower was built here in 1967 to house the Chiba Folk Museum.

spots.name: Aoba no Mori Koen
spots.local: 青葉の森公園, Green Leaf Forest Park
spots.desc: Nothing spectacular, but during the Sakura (Cherry blossom) season a nice place to get away from the concrete jungle.

spots.name: Makuhari Techno Garden
spots.desc: An impressive complex of shopping malls, restaurants and office towers; white tile, glass and polished steel with atmospheric lighting and realistic plastic plants, with footsteps echoing in the quiet walkways and aerial bridges.

spots.name: Bay Town
spots.desc: The view of town is very modern and constructions are very colorful. It's not so common in this area, so some TV shows in Japan use this town as a location. You can buy houses or rent them.

spots.name: Sakura Park
spots.desc: A park which has many beautiful cherry blossom trees.When spring comes, a lot of people come to enjoy seeing them.

spots.name: Izumiya park
spots.desc: Has fireflies in this park, but you cannot see them often because they have been protected carefully.

spots.name: Rokutsu Temple
spots.desc: It was built in 1677 (the Edo era). At that time, many farmers tried to develop this area and building the temple was one of their activities. It is not so huge but has been loved by local people. In September 2007, Chiba was hit by a typhoon, and the temple was destroyed, but people living in the area decided to use the community chest for its restoration. Finally, it was repaired and reborn by…

spots.name: Aeon Town Oyumino
spots.local: イオンタウンおゆみ野
spots.desc: It has countless shops, restaurants and big movie theaters. From kids to elder people, all generations can have a fun here.

spots.name: Karaoke Arthur
spots.desc: The atmosphere of this karaoke parlor is like Ancient Greece and Rome. You can enjoy Karaoke, a Japanese young culture. First, choose one song from song lists (Western songs are popular). Then, you are supposed to sing like a singer with the recorded music. If you have never been to karaoke before, try this in Japan.

spots.name: Costco
spots.desc: Japan has more than 30 Costcos, and one of them is in Makuhari. This way of displaying items is uncommon in Japan, so many people are interested in it and go there. Entering the building can be done without a membership card if entering at a busy time; the only time memberships are absolutely checked for is at the cash register. For some Japanese, the items are too big or too much, so people like…

spots.name: Harbor City Soga
spots.desc: Retail development with a huge Ito Yokado and adjoining Ario shopping mall, equally huge Homes home centre and The Culture Walk with cinema, bathhouse and other attractions. Now Chiba-ites don't need to go all the way to Tokyo or Funabashi to spend their hard earned yen!

spots.name: Costco
spots.desc: Just like everywhere else they operate, Costco's hot dog and soda combo is the cheapest meal in the area. Here it's ¥180. Alternatively, if you have a membership card, go inside and buy some fresh sushi- ¥1200 here gets you eight nigiri and eight maki pieces, four each of salmon and tuna.

spots.name: Big Texas Oyumino
spots.local: ビッグテキサスおゆみ野店
spots.desc: The atmosphere of this restaurant is imaged like Western America. You can have gorgeous, wonderful and tasty steaks and hamburger steaks there.

spots.name: Leaf Dinning
spots.local: リーフ ダイニング
spots.desc: 3 min from Oyumino station, this is a casual European food restaurant in Oyumino. You can feel as if you were at home because of the atmosphere.

spots.name: Ocean Deep
spots.desc: Different theme every night from belly dancing, salsa, and DJs costume parties. Good food and a vast variety of special drinks.

spots.name: Amataro
spots.desc: Chain izakaya, so don't expect anything unusual in terms of food or drink, but the high level offers a nice view of Chiba city.

spots.name: Nanpudo
spots.desc: Resembling the laboratory of a mad Victorian scientist, this wood-paneled fever dream is packed with ancient-looking distilling equipment and other steampunky bric-a-brac. Serves up the standard Japanese coffee shop menu of pizza toast, pastas, curry rice and the like. Open very late (06:00 on F Sa nights) and also has an extensive bar menu.

spots.name: Higashiyama Kaii Memorial Hall
spots.desc: Small museum for the famous nihonga (traditional Japanese painting) artist.
spots.price: Admission:¥500 for adult, ¥400 Above 65 years old, ¥250 High school, University Student

spots.name: Yamazaki Plaza Ichikawa
spots.desc: Yamazaki Baking is the largest baking company in not just Japan but the entire world, and Yamazaki Plaza is their original headquarters, hosting no less than three restaurants. The ground floor has a casual bakery-cafe where you can watch pastries being made, while the second has a casual Western-style restaurant (hamburg steaks etc) and the downright fancy French restaurant Lumiere. And if…

spots.name: L'agente
spots.desc: Excellent Italian food, the chef trained in Italy and everything including pasta, bread and biscotti is handmade. Both lunch (3/4 courses) and dinner (8-10, a la carte also available) are incredible value. The restaurant is small, so book ahead, and it's a one-man show, so expect to spend a few hours if you go with the full dinner course.

spots.name: Suwa Jinja
spots.desc: Very popular among local people. During New Year time it attracts people from all neighboring cities. If you want to visit during hatsumode (1st-3rd of January), you might stand in line around 1 hour.

spots.name: Old Tega Church
spots.desc: The oldest Christian church in the Greater Tokyo Area, established in 1881. In fact, it is an Orthodox Christian church in an old Japanese-style building. So, it may not be as impressive as Nikolai-do at Ochanomizu, but delivers a unique Japan-only experience.

spots.name: Takashimaya
spots.desc: This high-end department store chain is located within Kashiwa station.

spots.name: Ario Kashiwa
spots.desc: This is a massive shopping center on Route 16, a little less than a half hour by car east of Kashiwa station. Not very easy or fast access by bus but easy access by car if driving on a road parallel to the often crowded Route 16. It has three floors of mall atmosphere, including a very large game arcade, a toy museum, and some chain boutique stores otherwise only in the Tokyo area. A good way to…

spots.name: Osakana Club Hama
spots.desc: Sushi place on the first floor of Atmosphere and Ocean Research Institute of Tokyo University in Kashiwa campus. You can get seafood donburi for ¥550 and sushi set with udon for around ¥800. Budget option if you somehow ended up near Kashiwanoha-campus station.
spots.hours: Open during weekdays and during lunch on Sat

spots.name: White Gyoza
spots.desc: Famous chain from neighboring Noda city. Serves two types of dumplings - fried (more famous) and boiled.

spots.name: Yakiniku bar Tomosankaku
spots.desc: Kashiwa-exclusive yakiniku chain. Promises high quality beef for reasonable prices. Has several spots near Kashiwa station.

spots.name: Chaka
spots.desc: Impeccable English speaking service, reasonably priced fusion cuisine, charming mellow atmosphere, extensive wine list as well as an exceptionally long staff sung birthday celebration. Good for a date.

spots.name: Raja
spots.desc: Chain Nepalese Curry restaurant in Minami Kashiwa. Good service, reasonable curry (raja set ¥1000) and cheap lunchtime deals.

spots.name: Station Mall
spots.desc: Kashiwa station mall 7th floor has a bevy of restaurants from Chinese to Italian plus sushi and Tempura.

spots.name: HUB
spots.desc: Chain pseudo-British pub. Friendly staff, big screen sports, English menu and easy order at the bar make up for slightly expensive drinks (pint of lager ¥690) and occasional harassment from English teachers/learners. Reasonably priced bar food available.

spots.name: Cavern House
spots.desc: Another, more accurate, rendition of a British pub, but this time with a twist. This "Beatles" theme bar is rammed with memorabilia of the Fab Four. The Beatles are unsurprisingly constantly playing but you can request your favourite track via the request forms on every table. The drinks aren't cheap and there's a steep seating charge but worth a look.

spots.name: Tozenji Temple
spots.desc: In the spring season there are a lot of cherry blossoms in the temple, the most beautiful cherry blossom is thought to be the 'Shidarezakura'. During the spring Japanese people go to see cherry blossoms and hold a party under the trees.

spots.name: Kento Festival
spots.desc: A votive lantern (kento) festival. This traditional festival has been held on Aug. 9 and 10, continuing the tradition of "Toumorokoshi Ichi" (maize market), since Edo period.

spots.name: Narita Tourist Pavilion
spots.desc: Learn about Japanese Tea Ceremony every Thursday from 10:30.
spots.hours: Jun-Sep: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, Oct-May Tue-Sun 09:00-17:00, closed during year end period

spots.name: Cafe Le Bon
spots.desc: It opens at 17:00 with drinks starting at 16:30. It consists of one small upper room with a semi circle of hot plates, on which your food is cooked in front of you and two small tables. The menu consists of one item: an all-you-can-eat meal including a huge drink, Japanese salad, gyoza, oriental chicken, wedges and ice cream, starting around ¥1680 depending on what you're drinking. Stuffy and…

spots.name: Lion's Den
spots.desc: Old airline crew hang out. Local mom and pop restaurant with cheap dining selections.

spots.name: Ramen Bayashi
spots.desc: A good ramen restaurant with menu in Japanese and English (and pictures). ¥1000 gets you ramen with beef or chicken, ¥500 a medium draft beer. The gyoza are particularly good. Popular with airline crew, look for the many stickers above the door and the books of crew comments by the door. Friendly staff, nice atmosphere.

spots.name: Barge-Inn
spots.desc: Omote-sandō (the road leading to the temple), Great pub serving western-style food, plus local & international beers. Every Saturday there's live music and/or dancing.

spots.name: The JetLag Club
spots.desc: About 45 m round the corner from the Barge, there's another watering hole run by a Belgian guy named Vince. The beer's great, and the atmosphere is really friendly. Free popcorn is provided, as well as a delivery service from 'Papas'.

spots.name: Akagi Shrine
spots.desc: A shrine on Mount Akagi dedicated to the god of Lake Onuma, Akagi Daimyojin. It features a long and scenic bridge over the water and lots of blooming flowers around the lake during the summer months.

spots.name: Akagi Nanmen Cherry Blossom Festival
spots.local: 赤城南面千本桜まつり
spots.desc: A very picturesque road lined with cherry blossoms. The trees blossom among rape blossoms, creating a colorful mix of pink and yellow (and blue on clear days). It is listed as one of the nations top cherry blossom spots. The road also leads into Miyagi Senbonzakura no Mori Park (みやぎ千本桜の森) where you can see the cherry blossoms bloom amidst the purple shibazakura.

spots.name: Benten-Dori
spots.desc: This covered open-air shopping arcade is a fun place to explore, with numerous small shops, video arcades, and restaurants in the area. The north end opens onto Hirose Riverside Park, with plenty of seating for an impromptu picnic or just to sit and relax.

spots.name: Katsudon Nakaya
spots.desc: A katsudon restaurant serving the local sauce katsudon along with other varieties.

spots.name: Torihei
spots.desc: A local chain restaurant serving chicken dishes. This is the original and head restaurant of the chain.

spots.name: Tumuli
spots.desc: A collection of ancient keyhole tombs ('Zenpou-Kouen-Fun') along with an archeology museum (and a literature museum, probably of negligible interest). The tombs are roughly 1500 years old and in a distinctive 'keyhole' shape. One has been restored to look as it would have 1500 years ago, complete with haniwa clay figures and pots. English information is good and plentiful.

spots.name: Gunma no Mori
spots.desc: A forested park. The buildings of these two museums are both notable for their architecture.

spots.name: Haruna Shrine
spots.desc: A "power spot" built into the side of large rocks. It was established in 587.

spots.name: Otsuka Pharmaceutical factory tour
spots.desc: If you are a huge fan of the Pocari Sweat sports beverage, and have some Japanese language ability, you can tour one of the facilities where it's made. Reservations need to be made between two weeks and two months ahead of time by calling the phone number listed, after which they send you an application form that needs to be filled out and returned.

spots.name: Shōya
spots.desc: Chain izakaya at a convenient location. This is a pleasant place to sample a wide variety of specialty snacks and sake from around Japan while you wait for train connections. Its catch phrase is kutsurogi no sato 'a place to relax' and the happi coats of the staff say yorokonde 'my pleasure'. Not much English spoken, but there are picture menus for both food and sake.

spots.name: Warp Station Edo
spots.desc: Backlot owned by Japanese public broadcaster NHK, used for the filming of their flagship Taiga dramas, which are annual year-long historical drama series that are broadcast every Sunday. Come here to see the outdoor sets depicting the Edo and Meiji periods.

spots.name: Kobuntei
spots.desc: This well-preserved, old-style samurai residence on the grounds of Kairakuen is well worth seeing, with its fine natural woodwork, thatched roofs, hand-painted paper doors, surrounding garden, and beautiful vistas from the higher floors. Look for the Chinese-character cheat-sheets on the walls of the Chinese poetry composing room.

spots.name: Tokiwa Shrine
spots.desc: This large Shinto shrine is dedicated to Mito clan lords Tokugawa Mitsukuni (1628-1700), known as Mito Kōmon, and Tokugawa Nariaki (1800-1860).

spots.name: Giretsukan
spots.desc: This small museum on the grounds of Tokiwa Jinja houses a huge rolling taiko drum, an ancient large-barrel cannon (or mortar) on wooden wheels, a lineage chart of the Tokugawa shoguns and their Mito cousins, the 400-odd volumes on Japanese history compiled by the Mito School, and other items from Mito's samurai glory days. Few signs and no pamphlets in English.

spots.name: Seizansō
spots.desc: The final residence of Edo era samurai Mitsukuni Tokugawa, where he lived into old-age after traveling around Japan as Mito Kōmon. This site offers a variety of scenic views, including blossoming cherry trees in the springtime and maple trees aflame with red and yellow leaves during fall.

spots.name: Art Tower Mito
spots.desc: Founded by the city in 1988 to commemorate Mito's 100th anniversary as an official city in 1989, its spiral tower rises 100m above the ATM plaza. Popular with locals due in part to its proximity to Mito Station, it is meant to symbolize the movement from the past to the future and from tradition to creation.

spots.name: Kōdōkan
spots.desc: The former Han school (an education institution for Samurai) founded in 1841 by Noriaki Tokugawa, the same local lord who founded the Kairakuen Gardens. The school was closed in 1871, after the Meiji Revolution, but most of the buildings survived and were declared national heritage of great significance. Kodokan is located northeast of the train station, five minutes walk.

spots.name: Kōmon Festival
spots.local: 水戸黄門まつり Mitokōmon matsuri
spots.desc: This summer festival was started in 1961 (Showa 36), and it is held every year on the first full weekend in August. During the festival, the popular fireworks display can be observed not only in the sky but also beautifully reflected in the lake.

spots.name: AEON Mall Mito-Uchihara
spots.local: イオンモール水戸内原
spots.desc: It was the largest shopping mall in Japan when it opened in 2006. While other bigger options have since been built around the country, Uchihara's mall remains more than adequate for almost anyone's shopping or eating needs.

spots.name: Sansui
spots.desc: A popular restaurant featuring some of Mito and Ibaraki's specialty cuisine, such as anko (monkfish) nabes and various natto dishes.

spots.name: Tsukuba Space Center
spots.desc: JAXA research center with free exhibits and guided tours five times daily. Facility includes exhibits on rockets, satellites, and Japan's involvement with the International Space Station. Guided tours in Japanese three times a day, reservations needed.

spots.name: Science Square Tsukuba
spots.desc: Science Square Tsukuba is a museum that highlights some of the exciting research that is happening at the National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST). You might think that a museum about research would be boring, but that is not the case for Science Square Tsukuba. At this museum, you can get a sense of what life will be like in the near future. It's almost like going…

spots.name: Tsukuba Expo Center
spots.desc: Features a model of the H2 rocket and a planetarium as well as robots and undersea vehicles. There is also the famous organ-playing robot with a TV-camera in his head that was presented during the Expo.

spots.name: Mount Tsukuba Shrine
spots.desc: Notable for a huge bell and Nikko-style carvings, this shrine lies at the foot of the hiking path/cable car.

spots.name: Mount Tsukuba
spots.desc: There are several hiking paths up the mountain, the most direct of which will get you to the top in about an hour. However, the longest trail offers the most cultural sights, such as shrines and a large stone looking like Buddha. The huge trees and rocks make for a fantastic walk. The not-so-fit can take the cable car to the top. The terminus of the cable car features several restaurants…
spots.price: Walking free, cable car ¥580 one way

spots.name: Iias
spots.desc: Shopping center one stop away (Kenkyuu Gakuen) on the Tsukuba Express line. It offers three floors of stores and restaurants, including a large movie theatre and a pet store.

spots.name: Right-On
spots.desc: Tsukuba is the flagship store of Right-On, a Japanese denim chain.

spots.name: Ton-Q
spots.desc: Great place to enjoy amazing tonkatsu (breaded, deep-fried pork cutlet). It is near the city center and the layout will remind you of a Denny's in the U.S.A.

spots.name: West House
spots.desc: While they also cook occidental food, their speciality is a 60 centimeters-high parfait (frozen dessert) for ¥3000, it is called "Bikkuri Thunder Mountain" and is supposed to be enough to feed 10 people.

spots.name: Menya AOI
spots.desc: Delicious miso ramen, in a thick soup. Large serving for the same price.

spots.name: Sankt Gallen Brewery Taproom
spots.desc: Taproom for the local brewery Sankt Gallen. 20 beers available on tap, including seasonal beers. Cheeses, sausages and light meals are also available.

spots.name: Free Culture
spots.desc: Expats and locals party at one of the few hot spots in the city.

spots.name: Tsurugaoka Hachimangū Shrine
spots.desc: The largest Shinto shrine in otherwise almost solidly Buddhist Kamakura, built by Yoritomo Minamoto (1147-1199) founder of the Kamakura Shogunate and the first Shogun in the Kamakura Period (1185-1333). Just a bit north of the station, this shrine attracts a million visitors on New Year's Day to see the first sunrise of the year (Japan Rail runs trains all night long). If you're lucky, you may…

spots.name: Kōtokuin
spots.desc: Home of the famous Great Buddha (大仏 Daibutsu), a bronze statue of Amida that at 13.35 meters is the second largest bronze statue in Japan (second only to that in Nara's Todaiji). Thought to be cast in 1252, the statue was originally housed in a giant temple hall, but the building was washed away in a tsunami. Visiting the inside of the Giant Buddha is possible for an additional fee but entry is…
spots.price: Entrance to temple ¥300, entrance to inside of Buddha statue ¥50

spots.name: Hasedera
spots.desc: This temple, also called "Hase Kannon", is home to the largest wooden statue in Japan, representing Buddhist deity Kannon. An interesting if somewhat claustrophobic grotto on the grounds is filled with statues of Benzaiten.

spots.name: Zeniarai Benten Shrine
spots.desc: An atmospheric shrine in the hills dedicated to the deity Benzaiten, but popularly named after the most common activity: according to legend, any money (zeni) washed (arai) in the cave here will be doubled. You can also purchase o-mamori (protective charm) and have a kannushi (shinto priest) strike sparks from a flint over it to increase its power. It is about a kilometer away from Kamakura…

spots.name: Shakado Kiritoshi
spots.desc: As Kamakura is surrounded by mountains on three sides and the ocean on the fourth, the town was easily defended in times of unrest, but the geography also left the town cut-off from neighbouring valleys. A network of narrow roads were cut through the mountains, providing the connections but keeping the site defensible. The Shakado Kiritoshi (pass) is one of the roads cut through solid rock. It…

spots.name: Taya Cavern
spots.local: 田谷の洞窟, Taya no Dookutsu
spots.desc: This is actually in Yokohama, but is closer to Kamakura both geographically and historically. From about the year 1200 to 1700, Shingon Buddhist monks gradually excavated this underground maze of tunnels as a site for spiritual training. You will be given a candle which you slip onto a wooden holder outside the entrance, and light at the candle inside the doorway. Damp, silent corridors lead to…

spots.name: Suenosato
spots.desc: A studio displaying beautiful and expensive handcrafted pottery and glassware that range from whimsical to Wabi-sabi.

spots.name: Yukai Sokai Taya
spots.desc: A spa housed in a building with the large neon character for bath on the roof.

spots.name: Fueda Park
spots.desc: This park has a baseball field, 4 tennis courts and a large multipurpose field. Sports equipment is available for rental. A soccer ball, basketball, or tennis racket costs ¥100 for 2 hours. 4 gloves, 2 bats and 4 balls cost ¥3000 per 2 hours including the field charge. Also, many people enjoy walking, jogging or riding around the park seeing the nice scenery. As this park is located at the high…

spots.name: Roastbeef Kamakurayama
spots.desc: Famous for its roast beef. It has a dress code, so you can't wear "rough" clothes like jeans or shorts. Reservation is always needed and the cost is high at this restaurant.

spots.name: Raitei
spots.desc: Soba restaurant. More expensive than other places, but delicious.

spots.name: Kawasaki Racecourse
spots.desc: One of the most accessible racecourses in Japan. Meeting on weekdays, including night races (March to December). Has a modest English website.

spots.name: Jackie Gyozarou
spots.desc: A sister restaurant of Gyoza Mania, a Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant. They specialize in a gyoza-stuffed chicken wing.
spots.addr: 210-0006 Kanagawa, Kawasaki, Kawasaki Ward, Isago, 1 Chome−1-3 ２F

spots.name: HUB Kawasaki
spots.desc: Part of the HUB chain of British-style pubs. Picture menus with some English descriptions are available. Happy Hour specials every day from opening time until 19:00.

spots.name: Chinriu Honten
spots.desc: A shop with products made of ume (Japanese apricot) since 1871. In the back of the shop, there is a historical section with a barrel more than 140 years old made to produce umeboshi (pickled ume) as well as a display of a series of pickles dated since the foundation of the company. The company was founded by Mr. Monya Komine, who was chief cook of Odawara castle, and is run by the Komine family…

spots.name: Odawara Hojo Godai Festival
spots.desc: Hojo Godai means "Five heads of the Hojo clan", who ruled the area in the 16th century. At this large and lively festival, there are many street stalls selling barbecued chicken, yo-yos, and more. Locals carry an omikoshi (portable shrine).

spots.name: Ajiichi Hojo
spots.desc: A ramen restaurant that uses a himono based broth and adds kamaboko on top. Noodles are served in a wooden bowl with an optional set of mix-in pastes based on local ingredients.

spots.name: Harekonami
spots.desc: Located a 3-minute walk from Odawara Station. Preparing a kaiseki course centered on fish dishes. Every morning, they cook fish and local vegetables auctioned off at Manazuru Port. At the end of the course, they serve handmade 100% buckwheat noodles. Reservation recommended.

spots.name: Fuchinobe Park
spots.desc: Contains an indoor pool called the Ginga Arena. The pool is divided into a shallow area and a deeper area. In wintertime the pool becomes a skating rink. The park is also home to the Sagamihara Stadium, in which pro baseball and high school basketball games are played.

spots.name: Myōgen-Temple
spots.desc: 11 minute walk from the station. This temple was built in 1598.

spots.name: Takatabashi Bridge
spots.desc: Sagamihara River is clean and safe enough to play in, and is a popular spot for riverside barbecuing. Some local events are held there, such as the carp-shaped streamer/flag/windsock festival in May. These fish-shaped windsocks are made from cloth. At the height of the festival, and estimated 1,200 carp windsocks swim in the sky above Sagamihara.

spots.name: Tsukui Lake
spots.desc: Contains a large lake in which fishing is permitted. There are flower markets, an observatory, and a mountain named Shiroyama (城山). Mount Shiroyama is easily climbed because it's only 375 meters high. In early April, this is a popular spot for cherry blossom festivals and picnics.

spots.name: CHAMP SAP
spots.desc: You can play darts and karaoke here. If you don't want to move to there from another place, you can have a party also. You can have dinner there.

spots.name: BUZZ
spots.desc: Known for its cheese fondue, this restaurant stocks 20 kinds of imported beer and has a big screen for watching sports.
spots.addr: Daiichi Okawa Building 1F, 4-1-7 Sagamihara, Chuo Ward

spots.name: Keiō University - Hiyoshi Campus
spots.local: 慶應義塾大学, Keiō Gijuku Daigaku
spots.desc: A campus of the oldest university in Japan. It is known for its campus' towering maidenhair trees, turning a lovely yellow in the fall. The Hiyoshi tunnels are underneath.

spots.name: Hiyoshi Tunnels
spots.desc: These tunnels were the headquarters of Imperial Japanese Navy during World War II. Naval commanders from these tunnels ordered Kamikaze attacks, directed ground battles such as the Battle of Okinawa, and naval engagements like the Battle of Leyte Gulf during the later years of World War II. There are many rooms. The university allows visits once per month.

spots.name: Street Performance
spots.desc: There are many street performers, especially in Yamashita Park and Granmall Park (middle of Landmark Tower and Queens Square in Sakuragicho) every weekend. Above all, fire performance is so dynamic.

spots.name: Cup Noodles Museum Yokohama
spots.desc: Museum dedicated to the creation of cup noodles by Momofuku Ando. Exhibits about the history of instant noodles. You can make your own custom designed cup noodles at the museum (¥300) - get a numbered ticket as soon as you enter as there is a daily quota. Kids activities include making chicken ramen in a test kitchen by hand (¥300-500) and an interactive park (¥300). There is a food hall…

spots.name: Anpanman Children's Museum
spots.desc: Museum showcasing the popular children's TV and book character Anpanman. Children can play with many hands-on exhibits and meet Anpanman and friends. You can buy anpan (bean-jam filled pastry) and many goods in the gift shop.

spots.name: Equine Museum of Japan
spots.desc: Exhibits on the history of horsemanship in Japan and the ecology and physiology of horses. There are also special events to interact with horses.

spots.name: Kamoike Park
spots.desc: True to the name, "Duck Lake Park" has a large lake, with ducks during the day and fireflies often visible at night in the rainy season.

spots.name: Kikuna Sakurayama Park
spots.desc: A small park called "carbon yama" by the locals with many trees all along the streets. If you go to there in spring, you can see beautiful deep pink double-flowered cherry trees called "yae-zakura" in Japanese. Yae-zakura is powerful rather than fine. The park is a popular place for cherry blossom flower viewing. In the summer, there are swimming pools. There is a pool for children, a 25-m pool…

spots.name: Negishi Forest Park
spots.desc: Redeveloped from a former horse racing track, this is a large rural park with the Equine Museum of Japan on its grounds. You can ride horses on the third Sunday of each month from 13:00. You can also give horses carrots every Saturday 13:30 to 13:45. It is closed on Monday, First of April, 28th December to 4th January

spots.name: Kikuna Shrine
spots.desc: A small Shinto shrine in the middle of the Kikuna neighbourhood. In the autumn, the shrine holds a Bon festival honoring ancestors. There are regular festival activities such as a Bon dance as well as food, floats, and amusement stalls.

spots.name: Yokohama Arena
spots.desc: This is the biggest arena in Japan. Many famous musicians have concerts there. If you want to go to those concerts, you need to buy the tickets in advance. There are also flea markets here sometimes. In this case, you don't need any tickets or admission. Check the official website for the detailed schedule

spots.name: Anniversaire Hills Yokohama
spots.local: アニヴェルセル ヒルズ横浜
spots.desc: It is a hall for wedding ceremonies. See wedding ceremonies and bless the bride and groom with not only their family or friends but also people who happen to be passing by. When you visit there at night, you can see illuminations.

spots.name: Okurayama Memorial Hall
spots.desc: A beautiful building with a hall, gallery, and assembly rooms. It is on the grounds of a park with Japanese apricot trees worth seeing. Local concerts are sometimes held at the hall.

spots.name: Manyou Club
spots.desc: It is near the Yokohama Cosmo World in Minato Mirai 21. It is a spa resort. There are many kinds of baths to try while making the rounds. At night, you can see the lights of Yokohama from a foot bath on the roof. You can enjoy and relax all day, because there are beauty salons, massages, and restaurants in this urban resort. ¥2620 (24/7).

spots.name: Hakkeijima Seaparadise
spots.desc: This large amusement park with aquarium, various attractions and shops was opened in 1993. Get off at Seaside line "Hakkeijima" station. There is an area called "Dolphin Fantasy" that exhibits dolphins, including a white one, with a 360° view. You can touch some animals like penguins.

spots.name: Zoo Nogeyama
spots.desc: Noge area, and 15 min from JR Sakuragi-cho Stn or Yokohama subway line on foot or you can use a city bus from Sakuragi-cho Stn. There are 100 kinds of animals in it including reptiles, birds, and mammals, and there is a petting zoo for small animals like rabbits, guinea pigs, and mice. 09:00-16:30. Free.

spots.name: ROUND 1
spots.desc: This is amusement park. You can bowl, sing Karaoke, and play billiards and darts in here. 15 min on foot from Yokohama Stn (west gate).

spots.name: Nissan Water Park
spots.desc: Shin-Yokohama. 12 min walk from Shin-Yokohama Stn, and 7 min walk from Kozukue Stn. This is an indoor pool inside Nissan Stadium. It has two parts; the indoor pool and the indoor hot-water pool. Even if you don't have enough swimming things, you can borrow swimwears, swimcaps, goggles, floats and towels at ¥100-300. Nissan Water Park is located indoor and you can borrow anything, so you can enjoy…

spots.name: Yokohama National Pool
spots.desc: Swimming pools and gyms. They are used global games and personal users.

spots.name: The Bon dancing festival
spots.desc: The Bon dancing festival' is held in Kamoi during the summer. It is a Japanese traditional festival. People wear 'yukata' (浴衣) which is Japanese traditional clothing. There are many booths. So, you can eat traditional foods. And also, people enjoy doing 'Bon dancing'.

spots.name: Karaoke Box
spots.desc: There is a karaoke box near the Kamoi station. Karaoke means people can sing songs in the room. It started in Japan because it was invented by Japanese. Therefore, it's Japanese culture. Some people can enjoy it. Some people can sing a variety of songs in there. Lately, there are many services in there. It has a high popularity among the young and the old.

spots.name: Landmark Plaza / Queen's Square
spots.desc: Giant complex starting from within the Landmark Tower, through to the Pan Pacific Hotel. If you like high-end shopping, then this is the place to check out. Also home to one of the five Pokémon Centers in Japan, wildly popular with kids.

spots.name: Pacifico Yokohama
spots.desc: Cafes, restaurants, shops and hotel. Sometimes concerts are held here.

spots.name: Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse "Aka Renga Souko"
spots.desc: At the fringe of the MM21 area near Bashamichi Station (馬車道駅) Historic port building dating to 1907. It has been restored and is home to many boutiques, fashionista or otherwise.

spots.name: Yokohama World Porters
spots.local: 横浜ワールドポーターズ
spots.desc: Near Cosmo World and Bashamichi Station (馬車道駅) Many shops and restaurants, slightly less expensive shopping mall experience perhaps catering to the tweens, teens and twenty-somethings you see walking around.

spots.name: JoinUs Yokohama
spots.desc: This maze-like shopping arcade is at the west exit of Yokohama station. There are some restaurants, supermarkets, boutiques, bookstores and so on in here. These shops are inexpensive. But depending on shops, this arcade can be a little complicated; so take care and "Don't lose your way".

spots.name: Kiyouken
spots.desc: A most famous shop of shuumai (焼売, Chinese steam meat dumpling). This is good souvenir and not so expensive at 6 for ¥320, 15 for ¥660, 30 for ¥1310. You can get central gate (中央口) of Yokohama station (between Keihinkyukou line and keihintohoku line).

spots.name: Isezaki Mall Shopping Street
spots.desc: Accessible via Kannai Station (関内駅) Great for the adventurous few who don't want to break the bank shopping at Minato Mirai. Anchored by Matsuzakaya department store, with countless mom and pop stores dotting the area. Lively by day, but be wary at night as the area tends to get a bit seedy.

spots.name: Sagami
spots.desc: Sagami is a kimono specialty store. The kimono is very expensive. However, you can buy the kimono at popular prices in this shop. The kimono set (kimono and belt) is about ¥10,000. You can rent the kimono. Japanese often put on the kimono at the New Year and a ceremony. At fireworks of summer, they puts on the yukata. Yukata is informal summer kimono.

spots.name: Minatomirai Tokyu Square
spots.local: みなとみらい東急スクエア
spots.desc: This is a building which has Japanese fashionable things. Just imagine a little Shibuya 109. Also, Starbucks is in here.

spots.name: Shitateya
spots.desc: Tiny local seafood eatery. Try the deep-fried oysters (kaki furai).

spots.name: Italian Bar BASIL
spots.desc: Though a stand-bar by nature, a great place to take in a nicely paced meal if you can get a seat. Lots of choices (izakaya-style portions) but focuses on a few ingredients, making for a refreshing take on the all-too-common Italian fare in Japan. Recommendations: any antipasto and risotto, complemented with sangria or wine of the day.

spots.name: Kua'Aina
spots.desc: Hawaiian-style burgers. Big menu with standard and gourmet burgers, as well as some American-style sandwiches.

spots.name: Tori Dori
spots.desc: Yakitori and other izakaya fare, as well as drink specials on weeknights (around ¥200) and all-you-can-drink (¥600) available for 4 or more people (a rarity for yakitori restaurants). No English menu, however knowledge of yakitori lingo should suffice.

spots.name: Shabu-Shabu Buffet Syabu-Yo
spots.local: しゃぶしゃぶブッフェ しゃぶ葉
spots.desc: While most all-you-can-eat shabu-shabu restaurants will typically serve pork, this one serves pork and beef for ¥2079. Vegetables, desserts, and a full range of drinks are set out buffet-style while staff keeps the meat coming. Has a very Japanese atmosphere (music, decor) without being over-the-top.

spots.name: Tinun
spots.desc: Classier version of the local Thai restaurant chain. Stir-fried noodles are a must.

spots.name: Yokohama Kurikoan
spots.desc: Famous for their version of taiyaki, a Japanese pastry usually made with red bean paste, but here they use chestnut paste (kuriko-an) instead.
spots.addr: 神奈川県横浜市西区南幸1-11-1

spots.name: Sante Ole
spots.desc: Shop known for its "coroquette burger", using potato inside instead of beef. Major Leaguer Daisuke Matsuzaka ate here in his school days.

spots.name: Bunnosuke Chaya
spots.desc: A shop serving Kyoto-style sweets (about ¥400-1000). There are also some light meals like soba dishes (most are around ¥1000). The shop's warabi-mochi (わらび餅) (bracken-starch dumpling) is recommended for its rich moderately sweet flavor of soybean flour.

spots.name: Rasuta
spots.desc: Ramen restaurant. Tonkotsu ramen with thick noodles is recommended. ¥800.

spots.name: Linden Baum
spots.desc: Restaurant known for its sweet baumkuchens, cakes, and roll cakes.

spots.name: Shinyokohama Ramen Museum
spots.local: 新横浜ラーメン博物館 Shin-Yokohama rāmen hakubutsukan
spots.desc: Paradise for noodle lovers, but not just because of the exhibits of the history of instant ramen noodles. The centerpiece here is the basement, which contains a recreation of 1950s-era Tokyo done in incredible detail, complete with operating branches of a rotating selection of ramen joints from around Japan and the world. Expect to queue, but if you really love your noodles, it's worth it. Small…

spots.name: Chano-ma
spots.desc: Cafe with Japanese and Italian fare. There is a large floor about 60 cm up where you can lie down with blankets and some pillows like a living room.

spots.name: Tachibana
spots.desc: Wanko-soba restaurant, which are Japanese noodles served in refillable small bowls.

spots.name: Manchin-Ro
spots.desc: Cantonese food restaurant with over 100 years of history in Yokohama's Chinatown. During lunch time it is run as a kind of self-service restaurant.

spots.name: Daidai-ya
spots.desc: This restaurant serves creative dishes, mixing Japanese and Western foods. In addition to the food, the view is very beautiful at night. You can see Cosmo World and the Cosmo Clock (a Ferris wheel) illuminated. By the window, there are some seats for couples - good for dates. Reservations are recommended for these seats.

spots.name: Sun road
spots.desc: A small Western-style restaurant near Kikuna Station. Syogayaki - ginger-flavored slices of grilled pork - is especially recommended. The owner/cook is very frank.

spots.name: Nagomi
spots.desc: A very small restaurant serving tempura The restaurant uses seasonal seafood and vegetables. Try the "Ten-Don", tempura donburi.

spots.name: Tonkatsu Sakurai
spots.desc: Tonkatsu restaurant with some mixed Japanese and Western dishes. No English is spoken. You can eat as much salad and bowl of rice as you want.

spots.name: Seryna
spots.desc: Steaks served Japanese teppanyaki-style, but set inside of a turn-of-the-century Western atmosphere. Sweeping views of Bashamichi's historic buildings and MM21.
spots.price: Lunch starting at ¥2000 with dinner jumping to around ¥12,000

spots.name: Benny's Place
spots.desc: American-style sports bar complete with baseball memorabilia, cable TV, darts, and a friendly owner who'll gladly tell you about his days in the U.S. Navy at "Yah-kohska". And the biggest hamburgers served this side of the Pacific.

spots.name: Downbeat
spots.desc: Another jazz bar, but this one features an extensive record collection, a "record menu" and a foreigner friendly staff. Request a song out of the menu and the owner will put it in the queue.

spots.name: Hogs Head
spots.desc: If you like the Windjammer, you will like this Irsh/American-themed bar too. The pub is trying hard to look as Irish/American as can be and is doing a very good job. The bartenders know over 200 cocktails and the “financial damage” per drink hovers around ¥1000. Basic food, pasta, pizza and snacks are also available. Unique about the bar is its size, which can be classed as rather large in the…
spots.addr: Naka-ku Tokiwa-cho 6-77, No 2 Hiyoshi Bldg 1F (中区常盤町6-77第2日吉ビル１F)

spots.name: Oriental Café
spots.desc: A small diner which plays house music continuously and the interior unique décor is in line with the music it plays.

spots.name: The Tavern
spots.desc: This, the first British pub/restaurant in Yokohama, is the regular watering-hole for expats and foreign business travelers who come back to Yokohama regularly. About 70% of the clientele is Japanese, and is single-lady friendly! When you enter, it's like walking into a pub in England, and the large selection of food and imported draught beers help keep the one of the busiest night-spots in…

spots.name: Windjammer
spots.desc: A classy jazz bar on the edges of Chinatown run by an American expat who loves to put on a show for his customers. Bands play downstairs most nights and there's a large screen for those on the second floor showing the action below. The decor is decadent and there's a chocolate fountain with fruit for dipping.

spots.name: Battleship Mikasa
spots.desc: She was Admiral Togo's flagship in the Russo-Japanese war (1904-1905), and in the Battle of Tsushima it led to the annihilation of the Russian forces. English signage is present, but English-speaking staff is hit or miss. The surrounding Mikasa park is free, and features a recurring fountain show.

spots.name: Perry Memorial Hall and Monument
spots.local: ペリー記念館、上陸記念碑
spots.desc: The monument marks the place where U.S. Navy Commodore Matthew C. Perry landed from his squadron of "black ships", forcing the Tokugawa Shogunate to sign a treaty of peace and friendship with the United States, thus opening the country to the world after 250 years of isolation. The park is in Kurihama (久里浜), a few stops away by either the Keikyu or JR train line.

spots.name: Kurihama Hana-no-Kuni
spots.desc: This "flower country" park is renowned for its 1 million blooming poppies from Mid-May to Mid-June, and beautiful cosmos flowers from September-mid October. It also has a nice herb garden and children's play area with a large Godzilla slide.

spots.name: Yokosuka Research Park
spots.desc: 3-4 Hikari-no-Oka (shuttle bus from Keikyu's YRP Nobi station). Not exactly a tourist attraction, this vast research complex is devoted to telecommunications in all shapes and sizes. You won't be able to see much if you show up unannounced, but symposia and meetings are held here regularly and usually include guided tours with companies showing off their latest and greatest.

spots.name: Sarushima island
spots.desc: Old fortress and nature preserve in Tokyo Bay. This is a private island and the only natural island in Tokyo Bay. Locals frequent it for hiking and it is a popular sun-bathing and barbecue in the summer. The island closes every evening, so make sure you don't miss the last ferry off (17:00 in Mar to Oct, 16:00 in Nov to Feb) or you will be marooned there alone overnight. There is no night staff.

spots.name: Downtown's "Blue Street"
spots.desc: Yokosuka's main street. See sculptures honoring Yokosuka as one of the country's gateways to jazz music as well as local street musicians and dancers.

spots.name: Dobuita Street
spots.desc: There are many kinds of shops visited by a lot of foreigners. Especially famous is Yokosuka jacket (called Sukajan - "Yokosuka jumper"). Fans of the Dreamcast game "Shenmue" will notice a lot of similarities between this place and 1986 Dobuita as depicted in the game. There’s an arcade but no hot dog truck.

spots.name: Chōgan-ji temple
spots.desc: A very historic temple. Not so large, but has a unique atmosphere. This temple holds a variety of events, including the festival that celebrates flowering is called Hanamaturi, and learning sessions about the religion. Everyone can take part in these events, but you need to contact the temple beforehand.

spots.name: Tanoura Pool
spots.local: 田の浦公園水泳プール
spots.desc: A small place. Some children swimming in the summer. Charge is very reasonable. It's recommend place when hot summer.

spots.name: More's City
spots.desc: Two floors of restaurants with a great view of the harbor. The basement floor has a food hall and small supermarket. There are many clothing stores and small shops. There is also an amusement arcade.

spots.name: Tomato & Garlic
spots.desc: More's 9F, Italian restaurant. Serves pizza, salads and dessert. Also a great restaurant if reserving for a party.

spots.name: Tommy's Chu-Hi Stand
spots.desc: Has no seats and customers must stand up while drinking at homemade wooden tables. The Chu-hi's are made here by mixing off-the shelf canned flavored chu-hi's with Shōchū. Has a very interesting blend of American and Japanese money on the walls with various drawings or sayings

spots.name: Jammin
spots.desc: Popular rock bar located on the Honch. Bar adheres to a strictly all rock policy. There are frequent live band performances from all over Yokosuka and sailors from the US Naval Base.

spots.name: Pumpkin Live House
spots.desc: Easily recognizable by the many band stickers and fliers adorning the bar's outside hall, the Pumpkin is a 'proper' live music venue specializing in punk rock. Contrary to popular belief, the bar welcomes Japanese and foreigners alike, and the staff speaks perfect English. The bar has a schedule for upcoming gigs for the month posted on the outside of the bar. Admission prices vary from gig to…

spots.name: George's
spots.desc: A country and western bar located on Dobuita Street across from Rock City. George also owns several other bars in the Honch, including Rock City. Has a beer pong table and also a pool table, a lot of "country" or people who grew up in small towns enjoy the atmosphere here

spots.name: Station Navy Bar
spots.desc: Amazing mix of Philippine and American style pub, great music, great atmosphere, a lot of room and great bartenders who speak flawless English. One of the top newer bars in the Honch area.

spots.name: Omiya
spots.desc: A separate city before it merged with its neighbors to become Saitama city, it holds many attractions all within walking distance of its huge train station: Hikawa Shrine, Omiya Koen (Park), A Museum History and Folklore, a bonsai art museum and artist's village, and short train journey away is the Railway museum. Well worth a day trip outside of Tokyo.

spots.name: Kawagoe
spots.desc: A former castle town, this is fittingly called 'Little Edo': an entire district of this city has barely changed since the Edo period, and is a bustling concentration of attractions. It's easy to slip down a small side road away from the crowds to soak in the peace and get a feel of what Japan was once like. A worthwhile 30-minute train journey from Tokyo.

spots.name: Aobadai Park
spots.desc: Has a water fountain which you can play in and a playground.

spots.name: Symbol Road
spots.desc: A pedestrian promenade on the site of a former US military base. Plenty of benches and rest areas. About 680 meters long.

spots.name: Crayon Shin-chan Buriburi Cinema Studio
spots.local: ゲーセン クレヨンしんちゃん 嵐を呼ぶ ブリブリシネマスタジオ
spots.desc: Museum dedicated to Crayon Shin-chan. You can find movie posters, DVDs, and life-size Crayon Shin-chan characters to take pictures with. You can buy Crayon Shin-can souvenirs here.

spots.name: Hattori Museum of Folklore
spots.desc: While there is, in fact, nothing relating to folklore in the folklore museum, the old Hattori family for which is warehouse is named, morphed into a medical company. So you'll find a small display of old medicines, advertisements... and sandals.

spots.name: Osawa Residence
spots.desc: Built it in 1792, this warehouse from where the Osawa family traded Miso and Soy, survived the inferno of the great fire, and today stands as the oldest storehouse in Kawagoe. The first floor contains a store while the second floor houses a small exhibition.

spots.name: Matsumoto Soy Sauce Shop
spots.local: 松本醤油商店, Matsumoto Shoyu Shouten
spots.desc: All kinds of soy sauce, you can taste several. Free visits of the cave every weekday at 13:00.

spots.name: Coedo Brewery the Restaurant
spots.desc: Run by a local brewery. Enjoy sweet-potato beer with Chinese and Asian ethnic dishes.

spots.name: Katakura Silk Memorial Museum
spots.desc: This memorial museum, certified as a modern industrial heritage site, uses the cocoon warehouse of the Kumagaya factory, Katakura Industries' last silk factory. There is no parking lot.
spots.hours: Wed-Sun 10:00-17:00 (closed during the summer New Year holidays)

spots.name: Sōji-in
spots.desc: A temple famous for its garden of hundreds of peonies which bloom from the end of April through the beginning of May.

spots.name: Tōgyoku Doll Museum
spots.local: 東玉人形の博物館 tōgyoku ningyō no hakubutsukan
spots.desc: Tōgyoku dolls are a famous local product and symbol. According to legend, a priest named Esho became sick while passing through the area. Although he recovered from the illness, it weakened him to the point that he couldn't leave the town. He began to pass the time by making dolls out of the local wood. His dolls slowly grew in popularity and the tradition of doll-making has been a part of the…

spots.name: Fuyō-en
spots.desc: This bonsai nursery nearest Omiya Koen serves as the garden of the president of the Japanese Bonsai Association.

spots.name: Kyūka-en
spots.desc: Established in 1929 by Kyūzō Murata, the caretaker of the imperial bonsai collection. The founder has now passed away,

spots.name: Sweets Shop Ogawaya
spots.desc: Famous sweets for Bonsai Monaka (盆栽最中) and Ōmiya Poppo (大宮ぽっぽ).

spots.name: The Three Little Lambs
spots.desc: A delicious lamb shabu-shabu restaurant which also serves lamb sashimi or lamb yakiniku. With drinks you can have a delicious, filling meal for under ¥3000.

spots.name: Torikukai Yakitori bar and grill
spots.desc: During the week master Suzuki san grills up the freshest chicken and on weekends the best ramen using the freshest chicken for a wonderful broth. During the week at dinner it's a Yakitori bar with a friendly lively local crowd. ¥5000 for a dinner for two depending on how much you drink and its all top quality cooking.

spots.name: The King George English Pub
spots.desc: A few minutes walk through the seedier side of Saitama from Omiya Station's East Exit. Turn right at the exit and then left down the brightly lit strip full of touts and hostesses in evening dresses. The King George is a way down on your right. This English-style pub is often full of expat English teachers, and hosts a lot of gigs and live events. Drinks are around ¥600.

spots.name: HUB Omiya Higashiguchi
spots.desc: From Omiya Station (East Exit) and take your first left. Walk for about a half a KM north until you will see the bar on your right. Every gaijin loves a Hub, and this one is arguably the best in the Kanto region, thanks to its massive interior and patio, as well as a non-smoking section that actually stays smoke-free. Food also available in addition to drinks.

spots.name: Yakushi-dō Hall
spots.desc: The Hall of the Medicine Buddha is known for a dragon painting on the ceiling. A monk is usually on hand to speak (Japanese only, some broken English if you're lucky) and strike a special block which produces a sharp, piercing echo if struck directly below the dragon's mouth. This is said to be identical to the cry of a dragon — not quite the roar of English legend but an attention-getter…

spots.name: Yomei-mon Gate
spots.desc: An incredibly ornate gate with over 400 carvings squeezed in. To the right of the main hall is the way to Ieyasu's tomb. Look out for another famous carving, this time of a sleeping cat (nemuri-neko). There are 200 stone steps, and steep ones at that; and then you finally reach the surprisingly simple gravesite.

spots.name: Tōshōgū Museum
spots.desc: A small museum of artifacts related to Tōshōgū and the Tokugawa dynasty. The introductory video is quite good, and the fascinating half-Japanese, half-Western suit of armor that Ieyasu is said to have worn at the Battle of Sekigahara is worth a look, but the rest of the exhibits are a bit lackluster: old scrolls, swords and knickknacks. The cafe is a nice place for a break though. Tickets can be…

spots.name: Woodsman's Village
spots.desc: Woodsman's Village is a place in the beautiful hills of Nikko, where one can rent a log cabin for a certain length of time to stay in. Also, there is an option for renting a barbecue grill.

spots.name: Hippari Dako
spots.desc: Enshrined in Lonely Planet, every other foreign tourist to Nikko seems to stop here for yakitori (grilled chicken skewers) and noodles, so you might as well join the crowd. Every available space is plastered with business cards and scribbled recommendations from visitors. Their menu contains several vegetarian options as well. The food is nothing special, but it's cheap, cheerful and has menus in…

spots.name: Gurumans Wagyu
spots.desc: Wagyu (Japanese beef) steak restaurant. Reservation needed. The dress code is not too strict, but no sandals, no running wear.

spots.name: Sobadokoro Gen-an
spots.desc: Roughly at the halfway point of the long slog between the shrines and the train stations, Gen-an features homemade soba noodles, hot or cold, with your choice of tofu skin, chicken or tempura shrimp. The other drawcard is the wacky collection of violins and other stringed instruments mounted on every available inch of the walls, including a banjo made from a giant Japanese beer can. English menu.

spots.name: Cafe Restaurant Bell
spots.local: カフェレストラン ベル
spots.desc: Either stop for a quick break with a hot beverage and some of their sweets, or go all in and taste yuba in various forms by ordering the yuba festa ("monk's diet"). Other dishes include ramen, curry, toast and more.

spots.name: Ramen Bonten
spots.local: ラーメン梵天 日光店
spots.desc: If you're searching for dinner in Nikkō, you might very well end up here as it's one of the few places with a lot of space that's open in the evening. The ramen may not be the cheapest, but the bowls are big and they taste good. The spicy char siu ramen have an adequate spice level for westerners, the super spicy only if you're used to it. Expect queues of a few tourists around 19:00 as…

spots.name: Orion Square
spots.desc: Orion Square plays host to various public events and festivals every weekend. Great place to stumble upon events if you have no prior knowledge.

spots.name: Tonarie Utsunomiya
spots.desc: The building contains several clothing and shoe stores, a ¥100 store, a bookstore, an electronic store, a pharmacy and a coffee shop. There’s also an excellent set of ramen and gyoza restaurants in the basement.

spots.name: Utsunomiya Station Stores
spots.desc: Several shops, a grocery store on the bottom floor, gyoza eateries, ramen shops, and souvenir shops.

spots.name: Bell Mall
spots.desc: The biggest mall in the area. Contains several floors of stores, a large grocery, movie theatre, and a large gym.

spots.name: Fukudaya
spots.desc: Not particularly large, but contains more eateries and shopping possibilities.

spots.name: C'est La Vie Restaurant Bar
spots.desc: Mageshi-cho 1-chome (near the Hotel New Asahi between Ō-dōri and Orion-dōri; opens onto the alley that meanders alongside the tiny Kamagawa). Open W-M (closed Tu) 11:30-15:30, 17:00-22:30. Offers a variety of interesting hors d'oeuvres, including carpaccio of ham, bonito (katsuo), or horsemeat (馬肉 baniku). The early bird (17:00-19:00) set menu, with choice of either pasta or paella, costs ¥1890.…

spots.name: Akai Tori
spots.desc: Baba-dori 2-3-10 (on the corner opposite Parco Department Store and Futaarasan Shrine). A coffee shop decorated with collectible Hawaiian and Polynesian kitsch mostly from the 1940s and 1950s. The friendly owner will do his best to accommodate your musical taste from his huge collection of CDs.

spots.name: Haijima Park
spots.desc: Has one of the oldest Wisteria trees in Tokyo: it's over 800 years old!

spots.name: The Furniture Museum
spots.desc: Houses over 1800 pieces of antique furniture, both Japanese and European.

spots.name: Sojibo
spots.desc: Serves fresh soba made from scratch. Gets rave reviews. Name means "monk of the buckwheat path".

spots.name: Mulberry Field
spots.local: マルベリーフィールド
spots.desc: Small cozy bookshop/cafe where you can read a book while drinking good coffee. Also sells sandwiches and various sweets.

spots.name: Fudaten Shrine
spots.desc: On the 25th on the month satokagura dance and music numbers are performed. The satokagura is a traditional Shinto dance.

spots.name: Aeon Cinema Theaters Chofu
spots.desc: Large cinema complex with eleven screens and ~1,600 seats in total. Opened in 2017.

spots.name: Kitaro Chaya
spots.desc: Shop and cafe themed for works of manga artist Mizuki Shigeru, who spent his later 50 years in Chofu.

spots.name: Ishi-i
spots.desc: This lively izakaya restaurant specializes in pork, served on skewers like yakitori. The friendly staff will help you sample almost any part of the pig, including heart, liver, head meat and oesophagus, pointing to their own body to describe it, if necessary. They have usual pork and beef dishes as well.

spots.name: Calends
spots.desc: This is a cut-above curry restaurant which has several curries which put the usual Japanese fare to shame. Try ordering the set menu with dessert, rum-topped ice cream is a nice finish after spicy curry. The owner may try to speak some English with you.

spots.name: Mitten Fuchu/Foris
spots.local: ミッテン府中、フォーリス
spots.desc: Large shopping complex which replaced Isetan in 2019. Has a food court on the first floor, restaurants on upper floors, and futsal courts run by the local pro team FC Tokyo on the top.

spots.name: Hōkyōintō
spots.desc: Grave of Matsugi Shichiro (松木七郎), a samurai during the Kamakura era. Small pagoda-like grave by a small shrine.

spots.name: Sengen Shrine
spots.desc: There are many festivals, especially the large summer festival.

spots.name: Fujimidai Park
spots.desc: The largest park near this station. On weekends lots of families come to picnic and play ball. Many people also bring their dogs. In spring, there's a lot of cherry blossoms. It is very beautiful, so this park is famous as a good park to see cherry blossoms.

spots.name: Nagaike Park
spots.desc: This park is so big and has lots of greenery. You can enjoy walking around while listening to birdsong. On weekends many people visit here. Moreover, there are Japanese rice fields (tanbo) and a water mill. There is a big pond named "Nagaike", this pond has a sad legend associated with it: A princess who lived 100 years ago died in this pond because her husband died on the battlefield. There used…

spots.name: Hachioji Icho Festival
spots.desc: There are about 770 Maidenhair trees (ichou), and in autumn, they change color and it is very beautiful.

spots.name: Senseless Records
spots.desc: Japanese and import punk records, CDs, and domestic and imported beer.

spots.name: Tama Green Walk
spots.local: ぐりーんうぉーく多摩
spots.desc: A shopping mall with a supermarket, about 20 shops and several restaurants.

spots.name: Yanawarabaxa
spots.desc: A Japanese woman runs the place by herself and serves traditional Japanese fare. Sets change by day and include a main dish and two sides, fruit, rice, miso soup, and coffee. Eat in and take out available.

spots.name: Waketagami
spots.desc: A noodle shop. The base of this noodle is tonkotsu (pork bone). The noodles are thin. This shop has many kinds of interesting and unusual toppings: cheese, umeboshi, soft-boiled egg, and more.

spots.name: Ukai Toriyama
spots.desc: The food doesn't challenge the non-Japanese palate too much — mostly chicken and sashimi, and to order you just pick one of three dinner sets. The great thing about this restaurant is the ambience. The restaurant comprises a number of traditional cottages situated within a beautifully maintained garden. Reservations are required. It's good to arrive early — give yourself time to walk…

spots.name: aprecio
spots.desc: An internet cafe. You can use computers, read books and you can play darts and billiards. A drink bar is included.

spots.name: Café Laguras
spots.desc: This cafe has cake and coffee. It also serves lunch. It's next to a park and along side a bike path, so in good weather, outdoor seating is particularly relaxing.

spots.name: Swagat Hanakoganei
spots.desc: Solid Indian restaurant. Good deal for lunch, plus the naan is quite large.

spots.name: Ciao em Cafe
spots.desc: Vietnamese cafe and restaurant with an amazing lunch set (the curry in particular). They also have a coffee pudding that is great.
spots.hours: Tue Wed Fri 11AM–2:30PM, 5PM–7:30PM; Sat Sun 11AM-7:30PM; closed on Mon

spots.name: Kogane Chaya
spots.desc: Cafe with a great and friendly atmosphere. There is a space where different variety of foods are sold depending on the day. At night it also doubles as a bar and can be quite lively on the weekend.
spots.hours: 10AM–11PM; all week, but closed on Tue

spots.name: Koganei Park
spots.desc: This is a very large park with many different attractions. There are fields for throwing frisbees, barbeque pits for rent, free outdoor basketball courts, tennis courts, baseball fields, large open areas for picnicing, and other such park-like attractions. The park is popular whenever the weather is good. It's also a good spot in February for plum blossom viewing and March for cherry blossom…

spots.name: Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architectural Museum
spots.desc: 29 relocated old buildings. Two of them serve as a cafe and a restaurant.

spots.name: Ganma
spots.desc: A small, bright, and shiny ramen shop specializing in tonkotsu ramen.

spots.name: Patisserie Dounel
spots.local: パティスリードゥネル
spots.desc: This bakery does a wide range of things: croissants, cakes, Japanese sweet biscuits, and finely detailed chocolate. There are a few tables for seating. Coffee and tea are available.

spots.name: Tonogayato Park
spots.desc: A beautiful Japanese garden. It is a perfect place to take a walk with someone special.

spots.name: Musashi Kokubunji Park
spots.desc: There are many kinds of trees; for example, cherry trees, zelkova trees, and maidenhair trees. You can see a fountain, a waterfall, and pond.

spots.name: Sugatami Pond
spots.desc: A beautiful Japanese pond. Many rare birds come to this pond, and birdwatchers come for the birds. Sugatami means a large mirror; ladies used the calm pond for checking their appearances.
spots.addr: Near Nishi-kokubunji station, along the Chuo Line

spots.name: Marui
spots.desc: The local branch of the famous fashion mall, with countless small shops on the 2nd through 5th floors. There are also food shops on the first basement floor. The shopping building is actually shared by Marui and Celeo Kokubunji, run by JR.

spots.name: Mezurashiya
spots.desc: A CD shop specializing in rare items, as the name suggests. There are three shops in Kokubunji.

spots.name: Panas
spots.desc: This restaurant serves a variety of good Indian food and drinks. They also incorporate a small bar and offer several Indian and Nepalese brews.

spots.name: Supuun
spots.desc: A special curry shop. Be sure to order the weekly special curry. The store has a relaxed and congenial atmosphere

spots.name: Ikkyu
spots.desc: This chain izakaya (Japanese-style pub) is one of the cheapest in Tokyo, so if you want to drink economically, this is perfect.

spots.name: Rubber Soul
spots.desc: A Beatles-themed bar with a very friendly staff. They often have live bands.

spots.name: Serigaya Park
spots.desc: A park with sculptures scattered in the lush greenery and water.

spots.name: Poke Lids -Pokemon Utility Hole Covers-
spots.local: ポケふた -ポケモンマンホール-
spots.desc: Find Pokemon Manhole in the park in the city where Pokémon creator Satoshi Tajiri spent his childhood. The poke lid is a Pokémon Go pokestop.

spots.name: Welcome gate
spots.desc: There is a local food market, a cafe and restaurant where you can enjoy cooking with Machida's local ingredients, a workshop where you can try your hand at making crafts, and a park where you can enjoy a BBQ and a picnic empty-handed.
spots.hours: Information and Direct sales office 09:00-17:00; cafe and restaurant 10:00-20:00; library lounge (rest area)…

spots.name: Yakushiike Park
spots.desc: There is a pond called Yakushiike, where you can enjoy cherry blossoms and wisteria in the spring, irises and lotus in the summer, and autumn leaves in the fall. There is another small temple called Notuda Yakushido.There are also relocated and reconstructed late-17th-century private homes and a doctor's office and residence, giving visitors a sense of old Japan.

spots.name: Machida Peony Garden
spots.desc: The Botanic Garden is a 7-minute walk north of Yakushi Pond. The park is open for a fee according to the blooming period of peonies and peonies (usually mid-April to early May). Free of charge except when the flowers are in bloom.

spots.name: Machida Calanthe discolor Garden
spots.desc: The Botanic Garden is a 10-minute walk north of Yakushi Pond. The garden is pay-per-open for a limited period of time from late April to early May when the orchid Calanthe discolor are in bloom. The park is opened free of charge during the hydrangea season (usually in early to mid-June).

spots.name: Machida Dahlia Garden
spots.desc: The garden is pay-per-open for a limited period of time from early July to early November every year when the Dahlia are in bloom. The rest stop and flower shop are open all year round. (Closed Jan 1-3.)
spots.price: ¥500; admission to the park is free for junior high school students and younger

spots.name: Furusato Museum of Agricultural Tools
spots.local: 町田市ふるさと農具館
spots.desc: Various farming equipment and agricultural tools on display. People of older generations are hopeful that their younger successors will carry on their farming traditions, hence this museum was built. The museum has a nice atmosphere.

spots.name: Machida Squirrel Garden
spots.desc: A park with about 100 squirrels. Guests can get close to the squirrels, play with them, and give them food. Squirrel feed can be purchased for ¥100.
spots.hours: Wed-Mon: Mar 16-Oct 15 10:00-17:00; Oct 16-Mar 15 10:00-16:00; Dec 1-26 10:00-15:00; closed Dec 27-Jan 2; closed first…

spots.name: Snoopy Museum Tokyo
spots.local: スヌーピーミュージアム
spots.desc: This is the world's only official satellite of the Schulz Museum of Art, the Peanuts fan's mecca in Santa Rosa, California, USA. Original drawings from "Peanuts" and a giant Snoopy sculpture are on display. There are workshops and a cafe based on the world of "Peanuts".

spots.name: Machida City Museum of Graphic Arts
spots.local: 町田市立国際版画美術館
spots.desc: The only museum in Japan that focuses on prints. Weekdays 10:00-17:00 (admission is until 16:30) Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays 10:00-17:30 (admission is until 17:00) Closed every Monday and 28 Dec-4 Jan. Fees vary depending on the exhibition. The mini-exhibition (permanent exhibition room) is free.

spots.name: Buaiso
spots.desc: The former Shirasu residence. You can enjoy an old Japanese house and a beautiful garden. Inside the house is a museum.

spots.name: Kojima Shiryokan
spots.desc: The head of the family, Shikanosuke Kojima, was a close friend of Isami Kondo of the Shinsengumi, so there is a display of materials related to the Shinsengumi.

spots.name: Taigan Historical Museum
spots.local: 泰巖歴史美術館 Taigan Rekishi Bijutsu Kan
spots.desc: Japanese sword and armor of samurai from the Sengoku period are on display. There is also a life-size replica of a part of the famous Oda Nobunaga's castle.

spots.name: Machida Chuo Library
spots.desc: It's a big library, so if you are looking for some books, you might find it here as it has a wide selection.

spots.name: Machida Eisa Festival
spots.desc: This is an Okinawan folk dance festival held annually. Many Eisa teams come to Machida. There are 23 pairs. The festival is very lively and fun, and various food items can be purchased from small stalls around the area.

spots.name: Bee
spots.desc: A dining establishment with darts, card games, and board games. A nice place to have a party with friends.

spots.name: Neko-no-mise
spots.desc: A cafe with a twist — there are cats running around that you can play with. Great if you want to play with cats but not raise one long-term.

spots.name: Round 1
spots.desc: This place has a wide assortment of games, including bowling, karaoke, billiards, and many arcade games.

spots.name: Sugawara Shrine
spots.desc: People worship the god of learning, Sugawara, at this shrine. In Heian period, Sahara was a scholar.

spots.name: Sports Park Partners Machida
spots.local: スポーツパークパートナーズまちだ
spots.desc: Holds 6,200 people. Many soccer games and university contests are held here.

spots.name: Flava
spots.desc: Live rock music, DJ live sets and dance performances throughout the week.
spots.price: Price depends on the event (normally includes 1 drink)
spots.addr: 原町田2-7-3 トップヒルB1F

spots.name: The Play House
spots.desc: Live house in Machida. Schedule can be accessed on their website. It is also a music school during weekdays.
spots.addr: 中町１丁目１８−１５ クローヴビル1F

spots.name: Natural Hot Spring Roten Garden
spots.local: 天然温泉 ロテン・ガーデン
spots.desc: This is the first genuine bicarbonate natural hot spring in Machida City, pumped up from 1,381 meters below ground.

spots.name: Manyou no Yu Machida
spots.desc: A hot spring facility where you can take a day trip and stay overnight.

spots.name: Tamasakai Natural Hot Springs Mori no Irodori
spots.local: 多摩境天然温泉 森乃彩
spots.desc: Surrounded by the rich natural environment of the Tama Hills and surrounded by greenery, you can enjoy an open-air bath with a flowing hot spring that has the effect of making your skin beautiful.

spots.name: FC Machida Zelvia
spots.desc: A J-League football club team based in Machida City. Machida Gion Stadium (Machida City Athletic Stadium) is their home ground.

spots.name: Pescadola Machida
spots.desc: An F-League futsal club team based in Machida City. Machida Sougo Taiikukan (Machida City General Gymnasium) is their home ground.

spots.name: Canon Eagles
spots.desc: A Top-League rugby club team based in Machida City. Canon Sports Park is their home ground.

spots.name: Bookoff
spots.desc: Second-hand shop including comic books, CDs, games, and more. If you are studying Japanese, comic books are helpful.

spots.name: Don Quijote
spots.desc: Popular chain of discount shops found all across Japan. Great selection and wide range of merchandise from groceries to electronics to designer handbags, at really low prices.

spots.name: Grandberry Park
spots.desc: This is a facility with a large outlet shopping mall and a large park. You can buy clothes, shoes and so on at cheap prices. There are foreign stores, but there are also Japanese brands of clothing. There are also many restaurants and an indoor food court. You can eat Japanese Chinese, Italian and so on. The all-you-can-eat Kentucky Fried Chicken is a popular choice. The mall also has a movie…

spots.name: Lumine
spots.desc: A big department store that includes clothes, dresses, sundries, small articles, accessories, shoes, a restaurant, a book store, a CD/DVD store, cosmetics, a hair salon and more.

spots.name: mina
spots.desc: There is a very large Uniqlo store if you need to pick up any cheap clothing during your travels. Also, there are cafes and knick-knack stores.

spots.name: Jorna Machida
spots.desc: The store is popular amongst teenagers and stylish young women. It includes clothes, dresses, sundries, small articles, accessories, restaurants, cosmetics, a hair salon, beauty salon and more. Uniqlo's sibling brand Gu is there. Gu is a cheaper price point brand than Uniqlo.

spots.name: Hokkaido Ramen Oyaji
spots.local: 北海道ラーメン おやじ 町田店
spots.desc: This is a famous and very tasty Hokkaido-style miso ramen shop. The "Oyaji Set" is notable.

spots.name: Tencyuu
spots.desc: This is a restaurant specializing in soy sauce dishes, a rarity.

spots.name: Yakitori Dokoro Daibu（formerly Gecchu）
spots.local: やきとり処 大舞 (旧名 月忠)
spots.desc: A yakitori restaurant. All the clerks are friendly and nice. They serve good yakitori and sake.

spots.name: Sabou Nakanoya
spots.desc: A cafe where you can enjoy Japanese sweets in a relaxed atmosphere.

spots.name: KFC Restaurant
spots.desc: All-you-can-eat Kentucky Fried Chicken. Some of the menu items are only available here.

spots.name: Syabu-Syabu Onyasai
spots.desc: All you can eat shabu-shabu and sukiyaki. Ninety minutes of greatness.

spots.name: T.G.I. Friday's
spots.desc: The famous American restaurant chain, one of a few locations in the Tokyo area. This is a great place to have lunch, or some after-work happy hour drinks (half-price on weekdays between 16:00 and 19:00). Staff are friendly, and the place has a lively atmosphere.

spots.name: HUB Machida branch
spots.desc: A branch of the popular chain of English pubs found all around Tokyo and other urban centers across Japan. Lively atmosphere especially on weekends. Reasonably priced drinks along with a decent selection of British pub fare, as well as darts, and TVs showing sporting events.

spots.name: MISHOP
spots.desc: The Mitaka International Society for Hospitality is an association for cultural exchange between Japanese volunteers and international visitors. It hosts various cultural events and also operates fee-based Japanese lessons. Alternatively, a system for connecting students with volunteer language partners is available for those who wish to learn Japanese on the cheap.

spots.name: Atre vie Mitaka
spots.desc: While not as big as the one at Kichijoji, there is a bakery, food, a ramen restaurant, a couple beauty/salon stores, and a flower shop.

spots.name: Mitaka Coral
spots.desc: Home to many small shops, selling items such as clothing, groceries, specialty food, and other items. Additionally, there are restaurants on the 4th floor and an art gallery on the 5th.

spots.name: Gutara
spots.desc: This ramen shop serves a broad range of customers: white collar workers, blue collar workers, and the nearby university's students. It has a particularly delicious spinach and pork ramen.

spots.name: cafe terrasse verte
spots.local: カフェ・テラス・ヴェルト
spots.desc: This cafe has a selection of western-style sandwiches, pastas, salads, and desserts. There are both indoor and outdoor seating areas.

spots.name: The Barn
spots.desc: This bar has a large selection of imported liquor with a British theme. The main focus is on scotch, though one can also find gin, whiskey, beer, and other standard bar fare. The master (Avi) speaks both English and Japanese. No charge. Closed on Mondays

spots.name: Toranoyu Iwaburo
spots.desc: This is an old Japanese bath house with rock walls. There are large changing areas, men's and women's baths, a small shop, and washing machines.

spots.name: Adarsha
spots.desc: This Indian restaurant has several kinds of curry. Sets come with curry, rice, nan, and a salad. It also has all-you-can-drink specials. Serving staff speaks English.

spots.name: Gyoza no Manshu
spots.desc: This restaurant specializes in gyoza and also serves ramen and Chinese food. The sets are very large.

spots.name: Janaki
spots.desc: This small Indian restaurant has many different kinds of curry. There are several different choices of nan, including a sweet chocolate nan and a very cheesy nan. The staff is very friendly.

spots.name: Kintoki
spots.desc: This is a small restaurant that serves multi-course "kaiseki" Japanese cuisine with an emphasis on vegetables. Along with the great flavors, the staff provide excellent explanations of the food and drink. Reservations are recommended.

spots.name: Nakazaki
spots.desc: A Japanese shokudo with handmade soba. The house special is a katsudon set.

spots.name: Restaurant Elle
spots.desc: This small eatery is a good lunch option for people visiting Musashino University. The servings are large.

spots.name: Sakura Sushi
spots.desc: A small sushi restaurant with a friendly and talkative chef.

spots.name: Todairo
spots.desc: This small Chinese restaurant is often filled with the smell of tasty food.

spots.name: Coffee Roast Musashisakai
spots.local: コーヒーロースト武蔵境店
spots.desc: This coffee roaster has a dozen kinds of beans. Order a cup, and if you like it, get a bag of beans roasted to take home.

spots.name: Skytower West Tokyo
spots.desc: This tall tower is perhaps the only iconic landmark in Nishitokyo. At night, it lights in varying colors.

spots.name: DyDo Drinco Ice Arena
spots.local: ダイドードリンコアイスアリーナ
spots.desc: This ice rink has ice hockey and public skating. On weekends, there are very limited public skating hours, so calling in advance to check on open skating times is recommended.

spots.name: Tamako Jitenshado
spots.desc: This 12-km bike and pedestrian path begins along the southern edge of Nishitokyo, runs fairly straight NW, and terminates far to the NW at two reservoirs. It makes for a nice walk or leisurely bike ride of any desirable length.

spots.name: Abiskar
spots.desc: A small Nepalese-Indian restaurant, great for budget travelers.

spots.name: Dropkick
spots.desc: This restaurant specializes in okonomiyaki and has a well-stocked bar.

spots.name: RAJ
spots.desc: An Indian restaurant that makes for a good late evening stop.

spots.name: Texas
spots.desc: This is a western-style steak house chain serving hamburgers, steaks, and desserts.

spots.name: Karaoke Mokomoko
spots.desc: This is a clean karaoke parlor with an extensive drink list. The song selection is quite extensive.

spots.name: Tachikawa Racetrack
spots.desc: Bicycle racing (keirin) takes place on a banked oval track. Keirin was invented in Japan for gambling purposes and became an Olympic sport in 2000 in its modified form.

spots.name: Tachikawa Festival
spots.desc: Many large fireworks are set off in Showa Kinen Park from 19:15–20:15.

spots.name: Adam's Awesome Pie
