spots.desc: In the Edo period, the Kitamaebune (see previous link) brought various imports from far-off Hokkaido to Nanao port. Such items included herring, salmon, furs, and kombu (edible kelp). The route these incoming ships took, called 'Kombu Road,' served as an important hub to the Noto region, and many ships stayed for long periods of time at Nanao port. With a 70 year history of producing kombu and…

spots.name: Sennari
spots.desc: The atmosphere of this izakaya is a strange but interesting mixture of European decor, Japanese food, and Irish jig music. The menu includes a wide variety of dishes including salads, pastas, grilled and skewered meat, rice, and more. Dishes are somewhat small and are best shared among friends. Although you should expect to pay at least ¥3,000 for a meal with drinks, the food is well worth it and…

spots.name: Advance
spots.desc: This izakaya has some of the best food in Nanao, albeit served as several small dishes, which is typical of pubs in Japan. While it loses out in style to Sennari, it easily rivals it in taste.

spots.name: Fish & Chips
spots.desc: Perhaps the only fish & chips restaurant in Ishikawa prefecture, those needing a taste of home can get it here. This seafood restaurant offers a variety of Japanese and Western-stle dishes including pasta, pizza, appetizers, and of course their famous 2 or 3-piece fish & chips platter. Good for large parties, as eight or more people can be accommodated easily.

spots.name: Ristorante Rio
spots.desc: The best Italian food in Nanao. It has a wide range of pastas, pizzas, appetizers and drinks. The atmosphere is a little dark, and the music can be a little loud, but it's interesting. It can also accommodate a large group of people for a party.

spots.name: Noa
spots.desc: This small, quiet, mom-and-pop-run lunch restaurant is a hidden gem. It has delicious Japanese-style lunch sets which include tempura, grilled pork, and others. The owners are a kind elderly couple, and the decor is straight out of the 1970s.
spots.price: Prices are very reasonable, with a full set lunch costing about ¥500

spots.name: Minoji
spots.desc: This izakaya offers many delicious Japanese dishes, including sushi roulette, a plate of rolled sushi with one or more pieces being loaded with wasabi. Decent beers on tap. buri (yellowtail) steak is recommended!

spots.name: Nihonkai Shoya
spots.desc: Offers many Japanese dishes and drinks, and considering the quality of the food, the prices are fairly reasonable. Complimentary dishes or discounts aren't uncommon on large bills as well. A good place to take your parents if they visit.

spots.name: Bee Spot
spots.desc: This small but friendly bar is run by a small but friendly mama-san. It's specialty is Japanese sake, and karaoke is available. Great for a few drinks and karaoke with friends.
spots.price: Prices are average for a karaoke bar

spots.name: Samba
spots.desc: The energetic mama-san will greet you warmly with a hug and a microphone as you enter this karaoke bar. Everyone who comes here has a great time singing and drinking and making new friends. It's easy to forget how much you sing and drink having so much fun though, so don't be surprised to see large bill at the end of the night.
spots.price: Prices are average for a karaoke bar

spots.name: Justice
spots.desc: This is a good addition to Nanao's lacking night scene. It blasts pop, rock, and hip hop music in a club-like atmosphere, though there is no dance-floor. It has karaoke, snacks, and cheap (¥500) drinks. But there is a "seating fee", which makes this bar only slightly cheaper than the average karaoke bar... depending on how much you drink.

spots.name: Wajima morning market (asaichi)
spots.desc: The morning market was one of the town's best-known attractions until it burned down in the fires that engulfed the city center during the 2024 Noto earthquake. Residents would like to rebuild and are accepting donations on their website. The Wajima Market website contains information about how to donate to rebuild the market.

spots.name: Chourakuji Temple
spots.desc: This temple has magnificent thatched roof buildings including a moon viewing temple used by the poet Bassho to write haiku. Behind the temple is the large rock Oba-iwa from which you can get great views across the valley.

spots.name: Zenko-ji Daihongan Branch Temple
spots.local: 善光寺大本願別院 Zenkou-ji Daihongan Betsuin
spots.desc: A sprawling complex on the hill above the Togura Kamiyamada Onsen with good views across the valley.

spots.name: Chishiki Temple
spots.desc: A quaint semi-rural temple with a Goddess image that is only shown in public once per year.

spots.name: Fukei Temple
spots.desc: This renovated temple has a beautifully crafted main gate and bell tower. A five 5-stone statue of Kannon, Goddess of Mercy and Bodhisattva of Compassion, gazes out over the Chikuma River valley from below the main gate.

spots.name: Takemizuwake Shrine
spots.desc: This large shrine complex has been holding the Daitousai festival (usually held on 15 September) for over 400 years, and the current buildings date from 1850. The grounds are resplendent with massive cedar and other trees, as well as numerous statues.

spots.name: Joyama Historic Park and Arato Castle
spots.local: 城山史跡公園荒砥城跡 Joyama Shiseki Koen Arato-jo ato
spots.desc: The site of a castle used in the Warring States era (1500s). It was destroyed in the Battles of Kawanakajima, and restored in 1995. Fabulous views of the Chikuma River valley.

spots.name: Mori Shogunzuka Keyhole Tomb
spots.local: 森将軍塚古墳 Mori Shogun-zuka Kofun
spots.desc: This very interesting tomb of an ancient ruler is about 1600 years old, and was beautifully restored in the 1980s. This 100-m-long tomb is perched high on a hill just east of the Shinkansen line and opposite the Anzu no Sato Agri Park. At the base of the site is Shinano no Sato Historic Park, depicting a village from the same era, and the Nagano Prefectural History Museum. Both are worth a visit…
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 09:00-17:00, closed Mon and the day after public holidays
spots.price: Adults ¥200, middle school students and younger free

spots.name: Kurashikan Museum
spots.desc: Closed for repair until Jan 2027. A beautifully restored traditional building with a fascinating museum out the back.
spots.price: Adults ¥200; high school age ¥100; others free

spots.name: Furusato Cartoon Museum
spots.desc: Focusing on the work of the political cartoonist Hidezo Kondo.
spots.hours: 09:00-16:30; closed Mondays and the day after national holidays
spots.price: Adults ¥200; high school age ¥100; others free

spots.name: Nagano Prefectural Museum of History
spots.desc: A comprehensive museum with a permanent display room, a special exhibitions room, a library reading and reference room, a visual media room, and a lecture hall.
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00, closed Mondays, days following national holiday and end of year period.

spots.name: Togura Juku Kitty Park
spots.desc: This is a very pretty park that has a great display of exquisite white cherry blossoms in spring. It is also a good place for a picnic, and there is play equipment for the kids. Beautiful lawns and a nice view across the Chikuma River valley from the pavilion at the top of the park.

spots.name: Agri-Park Apricot Village
spots.local: あんずの里アグリパーク
spots.desc: The best time to view the blossoms is usually in early April. Good viewing places include Sketch Park (スケッチパーク) and Uwadaira Viewpoint (上平展望台).

spots.name: Togura Kamiyamada Onsen Summer Festival
spots.local: 戸倉上山田温泉夏祭り
spots.desc: Enjoy lion dances, drum performances, fireworks and the spectacle of portable shrines being paraded through the streets.

spots.name: Togura Fireworks Festival
spots.desc: Listen to the big booms echoing up and down the valley during the massive fireworks display and eat your fill from the numerous food stalls.

spots.name: Jomon Festival
spots.desc: See reenactments from prehistoric times at the Sarashina no Sato Ancient Experience Park.

spots.name: Zuisho
spots.desc: Although it is the most expensive public bathhouse in Togura Kamiyamada Onsen, it is also the most well equipped with the greatest variety of baths. The separate male and female areas each have a large indoor bath decorated with colourful natural boulders. The indoor area also has a sauna, jet baths, and a freshwater (cold) bath. The outdoor bath area has elegant gardens and contains baths you…
spots.price: ¥650 for adults, ¥500 for morning bath; ¥350 for elementary school students, ¥250 for morning bath

spots.name: Kamenoyu
spots.desc: The separate men's and women's baths have two indoor baths, as well as one large outdoor bath and a ceramic pot bath in a nicely treed area. If you like your onsens hot, this is the place for you.
spots.hours: 10AM-11PM, closed on the 16th of each month

spots.name: Sanogawa Onsen Chikurin no Yu
spots.desc: A pleasant neighborhood onsen with 3 indoor baths of varying temperatures and large windows that catch the afternoon sun. From the baths you can access a zen-like outdoor garden area with benches, potted bamboo, and white gravel.

spots.name: Hakuchoen Hot Springs
spots.local: 湯のさと ちくま 白鳥園
spots.desc: New modern building completed in 2015. Several baths in different styles and a restaurant.

spots.name: Climb
spots.desc: Mt Gorigamine (五里ケ峰) (1094 m). Drive south on route 18 and take the first on the left after the Isobe Minami intersection. Cross the railway line, and take the first on the right. About half way up the hill is a car park. Follow the signs for Gorigamine. It's about a 2-hour climb to the top and involves an ascent of 600 m from the car park. On the way back down, follow a path to the left along…

spots.name: Hire bikes
spots.desc: And pick up a Hiking/Cycling brochure from Kamesei Ryokan and cycle along the Chikuma River cycle path.

spots.name: Crown Farm
spots.desc: Pick apples from October to early December, grapes in September.

spots.name: Shateki
spots.desc: Shateki involves shooting at targets with a cork gun and trying to win prizes. Look for the 射的 signs in the narrow alleys of Kamiyamada.

spots.name: Hijiri Kogen Summer Mountain Lift and Skyrider
spots.local: 聖高原夏山リフト・スカイライダー
spots.desc: A stainless steel slide that you ride down on luge type contraptions. The course is 710 winding metres long and drops over a 100 m from top to bottom. The ticket price includes going up on the chair lift. Free for infants, but children under 9 years old need to accompanied by an adult. Awesome fun for everybody!
spots.hours: Mid April to the end of October; closed Thursdays except in the first two weeks of August
spots.price: Adults 1 ride - ¥500; 3 rides ¥1300; 6 rides ¥2500. Elementary and junior high aged children: 1 ride ¥300; 3 rides…

spots.name: Ooi Pharmacy
spots.desc: English-speaking pharmacist that also has Chinese herbal medicine.

spots.name: Benjarong 2 Restaurant
spots.local: ベンジャロン2レストラン
spots.desc: Real Thai food made by real Thai chefs. Choose your spiciness level from 0 to 100%. Everything from the basic curry and pad Thai standards to the exotic.

spots.name: Cafe Jitenshaya
spots.desc: Funky Tex-Mex cafe serving drinks and meals, with an English-speaking proprietor who rode his bike across Australia and has the souvenirs to prove it.

spots.name: Daikoku Shokudo
spots.desc: A local institution. Ramen fans come from far and wide for the noodles. The garlic sauce pork filet "nintare tonkatsu" is a local favourite. The small shop is often crowded, but is worth the wait.

spots.name: Googies
spots.desc: Family-friendly American-style diner using a lot of local ingredients, with a menu that has most items in English. Enjoy gazing at the great collection of 1950s memorabilia and if you are lucky, Grease will be playing on the big screen.

spots.name: Hagoromo
spots.desc: Gourmet Japanese cuisine in a traditional setting. Sit at the counter and watch owner/chef Hata-san work his magic, or at one of the kotatsu tables with sunken floors.

spots.name: Kawana
spots.desc: Gourmet Japanese cuisine with reasonable set menu options (sets include salad, udon, pickles, side dish, fruit and rice). Good selection of wines, beer and sake.
spots.price: Lunch sets from ¥1050; dinner sets from ¥1260

spots.name: Kaya
spots.desc: Authentic soba noodles in a 250-year-old thatched roof building.

spots.name: Lapis Lazuli
spots.desc: Elegant French dining highlighting local ingredients. Extensive wine menu to match. Reservations required.
spots.price: Lunch set from ¥3675; dinner set from ¥6825

spots.name: Manzo
spots.desc: Mutton from Nagano's sheep capital, Shinshu Shinmachi. Charcoal grilled on a Mongolian-style grill. There are only 2 tables, so reservations are essential.

spots.name: Kameya
spots.desc: Kameya is particular about their ramen, using only locally grown "Sarashina" flour for their hand-made noodles. Take you shoes off and relax in this all non-smoking restaurant.

spots.name: Moridot
spots.desc: Serves pasta, as well as Japanese and Indian curries. Specialties include Apricot Curry using local fruit. The lunch set is enormous and great value at ¥800.

spots.name: Pasta & Pudding Cocoro
spots.desc: Stylish shop popular with ladies (Friday is Ladies' Night) and decorated with baseball memorabilia. 40 types of spaghetti and their signature pumpkin pudding.

spots.name: Shichifuku
spots.desc: "Oyaki" dumplings are Nagano's soul food. And Shichifuku is Kamiyamada's own little oyaki shop. Take Out is available but it is fun to eat in at this Showa-Retro restaurant.

spots.name: Silky
spots.desc: Cosy okonomiyaki joint with a friendly owner who speaks a bit of English. Also serves udon and curry rice.

spots.name: Steak-1
spots.desc: Cowpoke style steak and hamburger house with an all you can eat and drink salad and drink bar included with main courses. Plenty of room out the front to park your horse.

spots.name: Yakitori Tomoya
spots.desc: At Tomoya, the "master" is friendly, funny and loves to have foreign customers.

spots.name: Cafe Crossroad (Jakumaku)
spots.local: Cafe クロスロード 寂蒔
spots.desc: A pleasant coffee shop run by a local non-profit organisation. The menu is all in Japanese but the pictures are mostly obvious. They also sell light meals (e.g. pasta set ¥700) and desserts, as well as a small range of food stuffs made from local agricultural products and recycled materials (e.g. shoulder bags).

spots.name: Ushiwaka
spots.desc: Yakitori and drinks for people serious about yakitori (and drinks). Yo-chan, the man behind the counter, speaks decent English. You can try one of Nagano's specialties, raw horse meat, too (or not).

spots.name: Yuki
spots.desc: A fashionable izakaya pub featuring "kushi" and "yakitori", various meat and vegetable creations on skewers, including home-made "tsukune" (minced chicken patties with special sauce)

spots.name: Yakitori Yumi's
spots.desc: Run by an ex-geisha who hasn't lost her ability to entertain. Her English is not so good, but it doesn't get in the way of having a great conversation.
spots.price: Beer and Yakotori course from ¥2000; Yakitori à la carte ¥300 (2 sticks)

spots.name: Ueda Castle Park
spots.desc: Only 3 towers and gates remain of the original castle. As the base of the Sanada clan, it is famous for being a key to the Sanadas defeating the mighty Tokugawa clan's forces on two occasions in the 16th century. On the third attempt, the castle was destroyed, but it was rebuilt by the Sengoku clan in 1626, supposedly to the original plan. The maple leaves in the park in late autumn are…

spots.name: Anrakuji Temple
spots.desc: A beautiful and peaceful temple precinct tucked up against the hill. The temple stores important cultural objects from the Kamakura Period, and is the oldest Zen temple in Nagano Prefecture. The pagoda is the only remaining octagonal pagoda in Japan, and is designated a national treasure. Opening times and price refer to the octagonal pagoda section of the temple precinct only.

spots.name: Ueda City Museum
spots.desc: A small but diverse collection, including several well preserved sets of samurai armor used by the local Sanada clan members.
spots.hours: Thu-Tue 08:30-17:00. Closed the day after a public holiday
spots.addr: Ninomaru 3-3 (inside Ueda Castle Park) 二の丸3-3

spots.name: Yamamoto Kanae Memorial Gallery
spots.desc: Celebrates Yamamoto Kanae (1882-1946) who worked in oils and woodblock prints. He pioneered a radical New Art Education for Children method that involved encouraging children to draw objects freely, rather than copying classic works from books. He also started a movement that involved teaching local people woodcraft.
spots.hours: Thu-Tue 08:30-17:00. Closed the day after a public holiday

spots.name: Taroyama
spots.desc: Hill-lovers will enjoy this mountain at 1164 m in elevation. A 2-3 hour walk.

spots.name: Kaldi Coffee Farm
spots.local: カルディコーヒーファーム
spots.desc: A coffee store also featuring a very wide range of imported goods.

spots.name: Collabo Shokudo
spots.desc: Serves a different set lunch every day. The meals are made with lots of local ingredients, and are good value. The place is run by a non-profit organization whose aim is to preserve and propagate local food culture.
spots.hours: Lunch 11:30-14:00, coffee and tea 14:00-16:00, closed Thursdays

spots.name: Curry House Bengal
spots.desc: If you like your Japanese style curry with a dash of chili, this is your place. Mains include a cup of soup, pickle/salad, and sometimes a complimentary cup of milk tea to wash it all down. Serves are generous and the service is quick. The menu is in Japanese and English.

spots.name: Rin's Coffee
spots.desc: An elegant coffee lounge selling a wide array of local and imported coffees.

spots.name: Cafe Garden Berry
spots.desc: A cozy coffee shop with good quality coffee and various beverages and snacks made from local ingredients. The owner, Hoshino-san, speaks English.

spots.name: Shibata Castle
spots.desc: Construction of Shibata Castle was started in 1598 by the first clan leader, Mizoguchi Hidekatsu, and was completed in 1654. The Omote-mon gate and Sumi yagura turret remain from the old days and are designated as important national properties.

spots.name: Ichishima Residence
spots.desc: Wealthy former landowner's residence. Many antiques, such as vases and paintings, are on display in the rice warehouse.
spots.hours: 08:30-17:00 (Dec 21-Mar 20: 09:00-16:30), closed:Wed (or the day after Wed when it is a holiday), Dec 28-Jan 3
spots.price: Adults ¥600, elementary and junior high school students ¥300

spots.name: Sekisen-so
spots.desc: The garden can only be visited by reservation or as part of a JTB travel package.

spots.name: Sakutaro
spots.desc: A restaurant with Shibata beef dishes. The curry and Shibata roast over rice (donburi) are its most popular dishes.

spots.name: Tokamachi Snow Festival
spots.desc: Every February Tokamachi hosts a spectacular snow festival. It has a longer history than any other snow festival in Japan and is second in size only to one held in Hokkaido. The large amount of snowfall creates a picturesque winterland. The large snow sculptures are magnificent and well worth the trip to behold. Tokamachi averages near three meters of snow a year.

spots.name: Kimono Festival
spots.desc: Every spring in the month of May, there is a kimono festival that enlivens the city. The winter and early spring are characterized by cold wet weather and heavy snowfall; the bright and colorful kimono festival is a beautiful celebration that celebrates the region's fame for kimono textiles.

spots.name: Be-1
spots.desc: Great karaoke place! Unlike traditional karaoke boxes found in Japan, Be-1 charges per hour by the room, similar to places found in the United States.

spots.name: Mion Onsen
spots.desc: If you need a nice relaxing place to go to why not go to a hotspring that also has a waterslide with a pool! Located in Nakasato Village off the 49.

spots.name: Matsunoyama Onsen
spots.desc: Head to nearby Matsunoyama for one of the best medicinal onsens in all of Japan!

spots.name: Echigo-Tsumari Art Triennial
spots.local: 越後妻有アートトリエンナーレ
spots.desc: Every three years, Tokamachi hosts one of the world's largest international art festival. Besides it, Tokamachi also hosts works of art and related event through year.

spots.name: Sushi Doraku
spots.desc: One of the better sushi (on belt conveyer) places in town and still cheap.

spots.name: Kojimaya
spots.desc: Great soba place with two locations in Tokamachi. Offers hegisoba, buckwheat noodles with seaplant mixed in.

spots.name: Louis
spots.desc: It's across the Shinano river and up a small hill in the town of Kawanishi, a 5-minute car ride away from central Tokamachi. This quaint cabin style restaurant and bar is a wonderful mix of east meets west. Enjoy a beer and great food while the Beatles or Elvis play in the background. The place is somewhat small, but for the right crowd can be a venue for a great evening.

spots.name: Jyohachi
spots.desc: A great okonomiyaki (Japanese omelette/pancake thing) place. Also has amazing french fries!

spots.name: Tanaka Kuma Kichi
spots.desc: Nice relaxing atmosphere. Great food and drink. Miso meat pizza is to die for!

spots.name: Daikichi
spots.desc: Great place for yakitori (barbeque chicken). Has two stories and plenty of room to fit parties. The chicken cheese and free salad are highly recommended.

spots.name: Mos Burger
spots.desc: In nearby Muikamachi, the Japanese take on an American classic. The results are surprisingly good!

spots.name: Mister Donut
spots.desc: Little known fact, this donut shop actually started in America but was driven out by Dunkin Donuts. Now it is the most popular donut shop in Asia. Go get a donut and see why! The pon de ring donut comes highly recommended.

spots.name: Ramen Kuma
spots.desc: Good ramen and has amazing fried chicken that can compete with the rest of the nation!

spots.name: Sambal
spots.desc: In nearby Muikamachi, in front of the train station, the only Thai restaurant in the area serves up delicious Thai curry, noodles, and soup.

spots.name: Lumiere
spots.desc: On a narrow side street behind Dynamo Pachinko is a small cabin with a French patisserie and cafe inside. It has a nice view and really good sweets. Try the banana cream pie.

spots.name: Yummy
spots.desc: In nearby Urasa, excellent ice cream. A creative variety of seasonal flavors including jalapeno pepper, corn, sake and wine.

spots.name: Ark
spots.desc: Cool bar on the corner of Eki Dori and 117 with great cocktails and a nice second story view of the street below.

spots.name: Sengen Taisha Shrine
spots.desc: Walk straight north from station, past 7-Eleven and turn left at the stoplight called "Chuo-cho". Walk a few blocks downhill and you will see the big red torii gate on your right.

spots.name: Shiraito Waterfalls
spots.desc: Awesome waterfalls from the water running down from Mt. Fuji. Take the bus from Fujinomiya station at platform 3 to Shiraito no Taki bus stop. It takes about 30 minutes. Plenty of souvenir shops and vendors. There is a path that takes you to the scenic Shiraito Natural Park (白糸自然公園). Shiraito means "white threads".

spots.name: Lake Tanuki
spots.desc: Famous for its reflection of Mt. Fuji with the most famous being the "Diamond Fuji", where the sunrise shines at the peak so the mountain and its reflection create a sparkling diamond. The Diamond Fuji can only be seen around April 20 and August 20 (roughly visible for a week before and after these dates) from 06:00-06:15. 4-km path around the lake, good for walking. Can rent a bike. Lots of room…

spots.name: Hana no yu
spots.desc: Take bus 37 from the station or Sengen Taisha shrine and get off when you see the big yellow CoCo's sign (which is a Japanese family restaurant). Hananoyu is the big building with the floral mural on it. Has a variety of indoor and outdoor baths (including tea baths, wine bath, sulphur bath, bubbly bath, Jacuzzi, salt water bath, and more), sauna rooms with TV. Provides shampoo, conditioner, body…

spots.name: Paragliding
spots.desc: On the Asagiri plateau, 40 minutes by bus from Fujinomiya JR station.

spots.name: Yakisoba
spots.desc: Fujinomiya is famous for its own version of Yakisoba (やきそば) -- check out any of the small shops with the big Yakisoba flag outside (usually orange in colour). There are several near the station. Some will cook on the table right in front of you. One characteristic is the thick, chewy noodles, some are made by the "Marumo" food factory right in the city. The other characteristic is ground meat…

spots.name: caffe kofka
spots.desc: English menu and free Wi-Fi available. Serves breakfast. During the day serves bagel sandwiches, pasta and various desserts. Some veg options as well.

spots.name: Bayern Meister Bier
spots.local: バイエルンマイスタービール
spots.desc: A Braumeister from Bavaria, Germany brewing beer. Following the 500-year-old Bavarian "Reinheitsgebot", which means only water, hop, malt and yeast are used.
spots.addr: 静岡県富士宮市上井出字河原端1254-1

spots.name: Hatta-san Son'ei-ji Temple
spots.desc: Established in 725 by Emperor Shomu, this is one of the most important temples in the Enshu area. It is a famous place to pray for good luck, and special rice treats sold here, known as dango, are supposed to ward off bad luck. With 700 cherry trees, this is also a special place for hanami in the spring.

spots.name: Fukuroi Enshu Fireworks Display
spots.local: 袋井遠州の花火, Fukuroi Enshuu no Hanabi
spots.desc: Thousands of people come from around the prefecture and beyond for one of the largest fireworks displays in all of Japan. Dozens of food stalls available. Bring a blanket and a handfan and get there early to find a decent place.

spots.name: Shuzenji Temple
spots.desc: Shuzenji Temple has a small museum with some nice artifacts that are related to its founder, Kobo Daishi.

spots.name: Hakoyu
spots.desc: A cedar-lined public bath built in 2000 by the tourist association. Also has a three-story tower that gives a nice view over the roofline of the town.

spots.name: Shuzenji Bairin
spots.desc: A plum garden park atop Mt. Daruma. In February the tourist association holds a plum blossom festival.

spots.name: Tokko-no-yu
spots.desc: The historic spot where Shuzenji's springs were first discovered by Kobo Daishi. A small public rotenburo (open-air bath) in the middle of the town center — but it's not for bathing your whole body, only your feet!

spots.name: Shuzenji no Yoshokuya
spots.desc: A restaurant with curry, pasta, hayashi rice, and other dishes.

spots.name: Baird Brewery Gardens
spots.local: ベアードブルワリーガーデン
spots.desc: Scenic riverside brewery in Shuzenji, where the legendary Baird family craft brewers work their magic. The third floor tap room has up to 20 varieties on tap. Brewery tours including tasting flight on F Sa Su by prior reservation only (¥1000).

spots.name: Mishima Shrine
spots.desc: This shrine dates its history from the Nara Period (710-794), and became famous when Minamoto no Yoritomo became shogun during the Kamakura Period (1185-1333) and rebuilt the shrine.

spots.name: Rakuju-en
spots.desc: This garden dates from the Meiji era (1868-1912), and contains a lake "fed" by meltwater from Mt. Fuji. In the same area, there is also a small amusement park, a small zoo, and a city museum.

spots.name: Genpei River
spots.desc: The Genpei is a little stream right in the middle of Mishima city made of the springwater of Mount Fuji. It's shallow, clear and cold so children often play in it. Some Japanese killifish (めだか), minnow (ハヤ), crabs (沢ガニ), pond snails (タニシ) and fireflies (蛍) inhabit the stream. The city has restored parts of its waterways with stepping stones, waterwheels, little models and other such stuff to try…

spots.name: Tagonotsuki
spots.desc: This shop sells many different kinds of delicious Japanese sweets. One option is Fujisanchō (富士山頂), a custard-filled cake shaped like Mount Fuji. Try this delicious option, or try others to find your favorite!

spots.name: Izu Cruise
spots.desc: Around the bay depart several times every day from the harbour. The 20-minute "Black Ship" cruise on a modern replica of Perry's USS Susquehanna costs about ¥1,400/700 adult/child and departs every half hour.

spots.name: Cody Voellinger
spots.desc: If you need help in English, it is best to visit Shelley`s English School and Cafe close to the station and along the river. They have free internet access and can help with booking hotels or other travel plans.

spots.name: Shimoda Aquarium
spots.desc: Prides itself as the world's first aquarium that floats on water. Admission is ¥1700 and the 5000 fish are in many cases unique to the Izu Peninsula. The aquarium also offers the opportunity to swim with dolphins for ¥4500 (reserve in advance). +81 558 22-3567.

spots.name: Gorosaya
spots.desc: Good seafood and a bit more expensive with dinners around ¥3000. Closed Thursdays.

spots.name: Dining&Bar Naminami
spots.desc: Casual Hawaiian-themed restaurant serving up poke salad, burgers from Izu beef, spam musubis, inventive smoothies and more. It's hard to do this kind of fusion food right, but Naminami delivers in spades. Not to be confused with another unrelated Japanese izakaya in Shimoda also called "Naminami"!

spots.name: Doug
spots.desc: Tucked away in a quiet residential corner of Shimoura, Doug -- named after the owner's dog -- is a gorgeous little bakery pumping out absolutely impeccable French-styled pastries and chewy sourdough breads. Get there early before the good stuff sells out, and prepare to queue.

spots.name: FermenCo
spots.desc: This hipster pizza joint faces directly out onto the beach and churns out some of the best sourdough pizzas this side of Napoli, washed down with organic local juices or naturally fermented wines. The burrata starter is to die for.

spots.name: Tonkatsu Nishiki
spots.desc: A friendly restaurant. The menu includes several different variety of Tonkatsu.

spots.name: Soul Bar Tosaya
spots.desc: Nice little bar on Perry road. Relaxed atmosphere, soul music, many cocktails, beer starts at ¥500. Food and snacks on an English/Japanese menu. Offers internet to customers.

spots.name: Takatenjin Castle Ruins
spots.desc: Site of the largest battle between Ieyasu Tokugawa and Katsuyori Takeda, successor of Shingen Takeda, during the Warring States Period.

spots.name: Yokosuka Castle Ruins
spots.desc: After Takatenjin Castle was taken over by the Takedas, Ieyasu Tokugawa had this semi-modern castle built as a base for recapture efforts. Its ruins now rest in a pleasant park setting.

spots.name: Kakegawa Flower and Bird Park
spots.desc: A good rainy day outing, this 7000-m² indoor park houses many species of birds which fly freely throughout the enclosure, including owls, parakeets, conures, toucans, penguin, emu and assorted waterfowl. Visitors are encouraged to touch and interact with the birds, and there are opportunities to feed various kinds of bird, see owl, falcon, and eagle flight shows, and get souvenir photos with…

spots.name: Ganesha India and Nepal Restaurant
spots.desc: This restaurant is operated by people from Nepal and make very nice and tasty curry. If you are vegetarian or looking for Halal food, this is a must go place. They have variety of vegetable curries with rice or naan.

spots.name: Mama's Bar
spots.desc: Local foreigner bar with live jazz, soul, and hip hop, and good soul food. Call the owner over to your table for a chat, as he is an interesting character.

spots.name: Marine Park Omaezaki
spots.desc: A couple of nice sheltered beaches at the end of the cape. Lifeguards and concession stands. Camping is possible.

spots.name: Omaezaki Minato Summer Festival
spots.desc: Fireworks festival in early August. There were more than 125,000 people at last year’s festival.

spots.name: Miyajima Gorge
spots.desc: It is known for its clear countryside streams and beautiful scenery. There are 12 waterfalls in the area, including the Ichi-no-Taki Waterfall, otherwise known as the "Little Niagara", the Ni-no-Taki, and the Kannon Waterfall. Konadegawa Dam and hot springs can be found here as well.

spots.name: Kurikara Prefectural Park
spots.desc: Eight hundred years ago, the Taira clan clashed against the Minamoto clan at Kurikara. The Minamoto clan won this battle thanks to the ingenious General Kiso Yoshinaka, who led his army to victory by sending a stampede of angry bulls into the enemy's camp with flaming torches tied to their horns. The park is home to the Kurikara Temple and 6000 double-blossomed cherry trees, which bloom in the…

spots.name: Usugōri-Honpo Gorōmaruya
spots.desc: Traditional Japanese cake shop since mid 18th century. Usugōri ("thin ice") is sweet white wafers.

spots.name: Takaoka Great Buddha Statue
spots.desc: Claims to be one of Japan's Top 3 Buddhas, although it's actually only in the top three if the height of the halo is included.

spots.name: Zuiryū-ji Temple
spots.desc: A large Soto Zen temple, three of whose buildings have been designated as National Treasures.

spots.name: Arakura Fuji Sengen Shrine
spots.desc: Has a platform from which you can see the Chureito Pagoda with Mount Fuji, one of the most iconic views of the mountain, especially during the cherry blossom season. Not just a photo op, the shrine also has history. During the last eruption of Mount Fuji, an imperial envoy came here to pray for it to stop. The shrine is said to house a sword from the samurai warlord Takeda Shingen's father as an…

spots.name: Kana-dorii
spots.desc: A large torii gate that says "Fujisan" (Mount Fuji), standing as a gateway for mountain worshippers, and Mount Fuji can be seen from the gate.

spots.name: Yamataka Jindai-zakura
spots.desc: A legendary cherry blossom tree planted over 1800 years ago on the grounds of Jissoji Temple. It is said to have been planted by Yamato Takeru no Mikoto, a son of the 12th emperor of Japan, and is said to be the oldest cherry blossom tree in Japan. According to another legend, when the Priest Nichiren visited, the tree was nearly dead, so he prayed and the tree was miraculously revived. With so…

spots.name: Nakamura Keith Haring Collection
spots.local: 中村キース・ヘリング美術館
spots.desc: An art museum featuring the works of American artist Keith Haring.

spots.name: Sasago Gangaharasuriyama
spots.desc: It is said that Japan's national symbol, Mount Fuji, appears at its most symmetrical when viewed from Otsuki, so the area was chosen as the site to produce the image of the mountain that used to appear on ¥500 notes. The overlook is at the summit of this mountain.

spots.name: Saruhashi Bridge
spots.desc: Saruhashi literally means 'monkey bridge'. Saru means monkey and hashi means bridge. It is known for its unique architecture which, as the story goes, is said to have been built by monkeys. It is a beautiful bridge that runs over a stream with a nearby playground and two small shrines, making the site very pleasant. The bridge is built across a canyon, next to three other bridges, one of which is…

spots.name: Hiking
spots.desc: As Otsuki is within two hours from Tokyo, it makes an ideal place to enjoy a one or two day hike. The mountains behind the town are dotted with pretty villages and offer wonderful views over Mount Fuji. There are even a few hot springs to soak out the Tokyo vibe. The closest hike to Otsuki Station is Iwadono-san; the station has a free map showing hikes in the vicinity of the tracks. The…

spots.name: Zuigakuin
spots.desc: The monastery was founded in 1978 with the intention of establishing a center that precisely follows the teachings of Zen Master Dogen (the Japanese monk who introduced the Soto Zen tradition to Japan from China in the 13th century), and located deep in the mountains among tall pines, it provides a perfect environment to practice meditation and experience a simple Zen life. Zuigakuin is popular…

spots.name: Iwadono-san
spots.desc: This 600-m mountain is easily recognizable by the sheer rock face on the south side of the peak. Once the location of a local warlord's castle, it now has a small museum half-way up and excellent views from the top. The museum has an exhibition of photos of Fuji-san and some local history (in Japanese only). The climb up the improved trail on the west side of the mountain takes about an hour…

spots.name: Aeon
spots.desc: Sells groceries and prepared food, clothing, toiletries, stamps and small appliances.

spots.name: Aeon
spots.desc: This supermarket sells bento lunch boxes, donuts, and other prepared foods. In front of the store vendors sell okonomiyaki and fish-shaped bean-paste waffles (taiyaki) for dessert. The okonomiyaki is tasty, but go light on the mayonnaise. There are two large tables to eat at under an awning attached to the store.

spots.name: Fuefukigawa Fruit Park
spots.local: 山梨県笛吹川フルーツ公園
spots.desc: A fun place for families featuring Aqua Athletics (a water area with lots of places for kids to splash about and an obstacle course-like water playground), a road train, fruit orchards, a restaurant, workshops, a hot spring, and even a hotel. Most of the facilities are free, but rides on the train and workshops come with a fee. Reservations should be made if you want to participate in cooking or…
spots.hours: Wanpaku Dome and Kudamonokan 09:00-17:00, grounds always open

spots.name: Sakagura-dori Street
spots.desc: A street of seven densely-clustered sake breweries, along with shops and cafes. The breweries offer tastings and bottles of their products for sale. The walk between the breweries describes a 20- or 30-minute loop on foot.

spots.name: Kuromboya
spots.desc: Yoshoku (Japanese style Western cuisine), Hamburger steak, Tonkatsu (Pork cutlet). Accepts credit cards.
spots.hours: Daily 11:20-14:30, Tue-Sun 17:00-20:00, closed 1st Mon Tue of the month
spots.addr: 15-34 Saijo Honcho, Higashi-Hiroshima City, Hiroshima Prefecture

spots.name: Kuradokoro Taru
spots.desc: An izakaya serving the local specialties of kome-kara and bishu-nabe. Sizable heated tents, indoor western-style seats, and tatami floor seats. Casual, pubbish atmosphere with many locals drinking great quantities. Accepts credit cards.
spots.hours: Tue-Sun, National Holiday, Day before Public Holiday: 11:30-14:00 (Cooking LO 13:30 Drink LO 13:30) 17:00-23:00…
spots.addr: 広島県東広島市西条栄町-7-48

spots.name: Senkō-ji Park
spots.desc: The starting point for the Path of Literature, Senkōji Park is famous for its cherry blossoms (in season); there are also great views of the Seto Inland Sea and Onomichi's massive shipyards. Located atop a small hill, the park is best reached on the Mt.Senkoji Ropeway (every 15 min between 09:00-17:15. ¥500/700 one-way/round trip adults, half-price kids).

spots.name: Senkō-ji
spots.desc: Halfway down the Path of Literature, this is the largest temple on the hill, and #7 on the Old Temple Loop. Senkōji's specialty is the grinning Niko Niko Jizō doll, the "always smiling protector of children" that most Buddhist sages would have a fairly hard time recognizing as the boddhisattva Ksitigarbha. Look for the massive Kyō-onrō (驚音楼) bell tower, which rings in the New Year for Onomichi.

spots.name: Jikō-ji
spots.desc: The first stop on the Old Temple Loop, Jikoji is notable mainly for its imposing stone gate and the chance to create your own nigiri botoke, a miniature Buddha statue that is made by squeezing a lump of clay in your fist; the temple will fire the clay and send you the finished product by mail (¥1500 plus postage).

spots.name: Tenneiji
spots.desc: #6 on the Old Temple Loop. The 500 statues in the Rakan Hall are an impressive sight, and best followed by a visit to the (unconnected) Maneki-Neko Museum next door, which has a whopping 1,500 statues of Japan's famous Lucky Cats.

spots.name: Saikokuji
spots.desc: #17 on the Old Temple Loop. Giants tread here before you; check out the huge straw sandals hanging from the Niōmon Gate. The striking red pagoda is a National Treasure.
spots.price: Free to walk the temple grounds, ¥400 main hall

spots.name: Jōdoji
spots.desc: #23 on the Old Temple Loop. Jodoji is believed to have been founded more than 1400 years ago by Prince Shotoku, who wrote Japan's first constitution. Its main hall and pagoda are designated National Treasures, while the gate and Amida Hall are Important Cultural Properties. Despite the name, this is actually a Shingon (not Jodo) sect temple.
spots.price: Free to walk the temple grounds; ¥500 garden, ¥400 treasure hall

spots.name: Onomichi City Museum of Art
spots.desc: Features a modest collection of Chinese, Japanese, and Western art and handicrafts. However, the building itself tends to attract the most attention, having been redesigned by star architect Tadao Ando in 2003.

spots.name: Poppo no yu
spots.desc: If the residential neighborhood is uninspiring, once inside it will not matter. Offers several types of baths (different temperatures and types of water, an outdoor bath) and a sauna. Men/women separated. You can also eat there.
spots.price: adult ¥800, children ¥400, free under 3 ; towel rental ¥150

spots.name: Ichibangai Shōtengai
spots.desc: A classic Japanese covered shopping arcade, runs from just east of JR Onomichi Station for about a kilometer parallel to the shoreline. It is theoretically pedestrianised, but cyclists, scooters, and cars use it as a shortcut, so take care when walking there. It contains an eclectic mixture of shops, from ramen shops and the ever-useful ¥100 store to a shop that sells all kinds of edged…

spots.name: Miyachi
spots.desc: Good, cheap ramen and fewer crowds, thanks to its slightly out-of-the-way location. And if you're sick of ramen, they serve tempura and soba, too.

spots.name: Shu
spots.desc: This is the most famous Onomichi ramen shop, in the midst of the craze since it began, but with only 20 seats inside, it tends to have pretty long lines. Former name Shukaen (朱華園).

spots.name: Chai Salon Dragon
spots.local: チャイサロンドラゴン
spots.desc: Serves "chaider", a tea-flavored cider created in Onomichi. The owner is fluent in English and German, and a great source of local info.

spots.name: Bitchu Kokubunji Temple
spots.desc: Kokubunji Temples are special temples that were designated by the Emperor Shomu as provincial temples. This is the provincial temple of the former Bitchu Province (western Okayama prefecture). The large five-story pagoda, constructed in 1844, is one of the highlights of the Kibi trail. The area surrounding the temple is known as the Kibiji Fudoki-no-oka Prefectural Forest Park. For those wishing…

spots.name: Tsukuriyama Burial Mound
spots.desc: Not to be confused with the more famous Tsukuriyama Burial Mound nearby in Okayama, the burial mound in Soja is differentiated only by the characters used to write its name: 作山古墳. Like the mound in Okayama, visitors are free to walk atop this mound.

spots.name: Kinojo Castle
spots.desc: This site is one of the sites linked to the Momotaro tale. It is said that the demon Ura used this castle as the base from which he would pillage the nearby village, and its name which literally translates to "Demon Castle" was coined from the legend. As a historic site, it is believed to have been constructed between the 4th-7th century and is one of the oldest castles in Japan. Earthenware and…

spots.name: Gokei Gorge
spots.desc: A scenic gorge that is particularly popular in the fall when the valley is painted in red, yellow, and orange.

spots.name: Kibiji District Cycling Trail
spots.desc: The recommended course is to start at Bizen Ichinomiya Station in Okayama and bike towards Soja, but you could also begin at Soja Station and bike the trail in the opposite direction. The trail is well-marked for travel in both directions. You can rent a bike at Soja Station for ¥1,000 for the day. After you've finished cycling the trail, return your bike at the bike center just outside of Bizen…

spots.name: Kitchen Taro
spots.desc: Nice place that makes bento similar to Hokka-ben, but higher quality. Mostly take out, but has a small eat-in area.

spots.name: Former Residence of Mitsukuri Genpo
spots.local: 箕作阮甫旧宅 Mitsukuri genpo kyuutaku
spots.desc: Mitsukuri Genpo was an important figure during the time when Japan first encountered the West. He translated many Western texts into Japanese and helped create policies in dealing with the Western powers. His former residence is on Joto Street — look for the prominent signs.

spots.name: Tsuyama Archives of Western Learning
spots.local: 津山洋学資料館 Tsuyama yogaku shiryokan
spots.desc: A museum with information and artifacts relating the Japan's first contact with the West. It also gives information about the important role the city of Tsuyama played in interacting with the West.

spots.name: Tsuyama Folk Museum
spots.desc: As Tsuyama has been the center of Mimasaka culture since the province was established, the museum displays artifacts and information from the founding of Mimasaka to the present, including a replica of the original Tsuyama Castle.

spots.name: Tsuyama Museum of Science Education
spots.local: つやま自然ふしぎ館 Tsuyama shizen fushigikan
spots.desc: Also, known as Tsuyama Wonder Museum, it's a great destination for those traveling with children. The science museum features a variety of exhibits, from body organs to wildlife displays.

spots.name: Joto Old Town House
spots.desc: Located in the former Kajimura House (梶村家), a wealthy merchant family. The main house was built in the Edo Period and the houses behind were built in the Taisho and Showa Periods. Visitors can enter the house and other buildings and enjoy its lovely garden.

spots.name: Port Art & DesignTsuyama
spots.local: ポート アート＆デザイン津山
spots.desc: A local gallery featuring rotating exhibits. The building is as interesting as the art. It is architecturally built like a temple but was not a religious structure. It was built in 1920 as a local bank and was used as a bank until 1975. This becomes evident upon entering as the interior is well-preserved with the receptionist counters still intact.

spots.name: Shurakuen Garden
spots.desc: Constructed in 1657 by Mori Nagatsugu, one of Tsuyama's feudal lords, Shurakuen is a strolling garden used as a place to entertain guests. While the current garden is sizable, the original was three times larger. The garden is considered worthwhile in every season with cherry blossoms in the spring, lillies in the summer, autumn leaves in the fall, and snow in the winter (if you're lucky).

spots.name: Tsuyama Railroad Educational Museum
spots.desc: A museum about trains and rail travel in Okayama with models, dioramas, and memorabilia. The highlight is its train turntable with 13 cars around it.

spots.name: Sakura Shrine
spots.desc: The shrine was built where Mimasaka Province's head office was located. It honors Emperor Daigo and Kojima Takanori. It is said that upon failing to capture Emperor Godaigo, Kojima Takanori carved a phrase expressing his shame on a cherry tree near the shrine.

spots.name: Choboji Temple
spots.desc: A Tendai Buddhist temple constructed during the Heian Period. Today, it is famous for the 4000 hydrangea bushes planted throughout the temple grounds that typically peak in mid-to-late June.

spots.name: Yayoi no Sato
spots.desc: People have been living in Tsuyama and the surrounding area since ancient times. Yayoi no Sato has a museum (the Yayoi Culture Center) containing artifacts and displays about the villages that existed here during the Yayoi Period. Across the street from the center the Yayoi no Sato is a park area containing life-size replicas of Yayoi Period houses and other structures.

spots.name: Yokono Falls
spots.desc: A scenic waterfall made up of three falls; a small one at the top leading to a 7-meter fall that finally flows down a 16-meter waterfall. It's a popular place among locals to get away and enjoy the nature as well as a nice place to see colorful leaves in the fall. In the summer months there is a restaurant by the waterfall serving nagashi-sōmen (流しそうめん), noodles flowing down bamboo chutes that…

spots.name: Nakayama Shrine
spots.desc: A shrine built in 707 dedicated to the god of cattle and horses, the current shrine dates back to 1559.

spots.name: M&Y Museum of Art
spots.desc: This art museum showcases the works of Munakata Shiko (M) and Yanai Michihiro (Y). Yanai Michihiro was a poet from Kagamino, neighboring city of Tsuyama. Munakata Shiko was born in Aomori but visited Tsuyama many times and said it was among his favorite places. He is known throughout Japan for his paintings and woodblock prints. Many works by Munakata are on display.

spots.name: Umenosato Park
spots.local: 梅の里公園 Ume no sato kouen
spots.desc: For those in the area in February or March, just prior to the cherry blossoms, this park makes a great location to see Japan's other famous flowers; plum blossoms. With 3800 plum trees, it's extremely beautiful, not to mention fragrant, to see them all in bloom.

spots.name: Tokumori Shrine
spots.desc: Dating back to 1664, this shrine was built by Tsuyama's first daimyo, Mori Tadamasa. The shrine is dedicated to Amaterasu and it houses one of Japan's Three Great Mikoshi (portable shrines).

spots.name: Kibune Shrine
spots.desc: The shrine is believed to have come from Kurama's Kifune Shrine sometime during the reign of Emperor Sujin.

spots.name: Sōja Shrine
spots.desc: One of the top three shrines of the Mimasaka area. The current shrine dates back to 1562.

spots.name: Fukurikikō Shrine
spots.desc: It was built by the former rulers of Mimasaka Province to pray for a safe and healthy childbirth for the daimyo's daughter. The shrine is also said to protect people from viper bites.

spots.name: Yaide Tenmangu Shrine
spots.desc: Sugawara no Michizane stopped here for eight days, and so it was dedicated to him as the God of Learning, when he was posthumously deified.

spots.name: Kamo History and Folk Museum
spots.local: 加茂町歴史民俗資料館
spots.desc: Located in the Kamo Town Welfare Center, the museum features locally excavated artifacts with information about them.

spots.name: Kume History and Folk Museum
spots.desc: The museum features a variety of locally excavated artifacts from abandoned temples and the Nasuyama ruins.

spots.name: Green Hills Tsuyama
spots.local: グリーンヒルズ津山グラスハウス
spots.desc: Although it offers some gardens and areas for outdoor activities, most people come here for the Glass House, an indoor swimming area. It is divided into two sections: the pool zone for fun in the water, and the fitness zone for those interested in working out.

spots.name: Ueda Handmade Japanese Paper Workshop
spots.desc: Tsuyama's paper, known as yokono-washi, was once made for the local daimyo. They've preserved this tradition, and visitors can now come and participate in workshops to make their own paper. Reservations are required. There is also a shop for those who want to purchase paper products made by the pros.

spots.name: Kotokomachi Kimono Rentals
spots.local: 古都小町 町屋着物レンタル
spots.desc: Located on Tsuyama's historic Joto Street, kimono rentals are a nice way to enjoy the historic town in traditional clothing. They offer a variety of rental sets for women (which also include hair accessories), as well as options for men and children. The rental also includes optional parasols and scarves/shawls. A handful of other rental options are also available for additional fees. Standard…

spots.name: Tsuyama Cherry Blossom Festival
spots.desc: Tsuyama is known in Okayama prefecture as the best place to view cherry blossoms in the spring. The Cherry Blossom Festival features an impressive 5,000 cherry trees. Visitors can enjoy the beautiful flowers among the ancient castle ruins. There is also a Daimyo Procession parade.

spots.name: Gongo Festival
spots.desc: In honor of Gongo (a kappa, one of Japan's mythical creatures), the Gongo Festival is a lively celebration with parades in the daytime and fireworks at night. The festival is held alongside the Yoshii River and on the opposite side are various vendors and food stands. Lanterns are hung from above and the fireworks are shot over the river.

spots.name: Tsuyama Matsuri
spots.desc: The highlight of this festival is the Daimyo Procession, in which they carry a portable shrine (mikoshi) from the shrine down through the Tamachi District.

spots.name: Izumo Street Festival
spots.desc: This festival features a parade of individuals dressed in traditional Japanese clothing to remind everyone of the city's history as a part of the ancient pilgrimage to Izumo Shrine. Various other performances and events, such as tea ceremonies, are also held.

spots.name: Inaba Cosmetics
spots.local: イナバ化粧品店 Inaba keshohinya
spots.desc: While it may seem to be a typical cosmetics shop, it is actually owned by the mother of Koshi Inaba, the heartthrob vocalist of B'z, a popular music group. As a result, the store has gained fame and visitors can see pictures and memorabilia inside.

spots.name: AEON Mall
spots.desc: The largest shopping center in Tsuyama, AEON Mall Tsuyama contains two floors of shops, including entertainment, toys, restaurants, clothing stores, and many specialty shops.
spots.hours: 07:00-23:00, most shops 08:00-20:00, but times may vary

spots.name: Hashino Shokudo
spots.desc: A great place to try Tsuyama's famous horumon udon. They have various sauces for you to choose from, such as apple and yuzu.

spots.name: Mugiwarabosi
spots.desc: A restaurant serving the Tsuyama Burger, a hamburger with a sweet sauce, for ¥600.

spots.name: Namakuraya
spots.desc: A small shop selling the city's famous Tsuyama Senbei. It's a sweet senbei with three main varieties; plain, glazed, and yuzu-glazed.

spots.name: Bar Ritz
spots.desc: A bar that also offers pizza, garlic toast, and escargot bourguignonne.

spots.name: bar ABC
spots.desc: A sports bar complete with darts and a big screen TV. Free Wi-Fi access. English menus are available.

spots.name: Nima Sand Museum
spots.local: 仁摩サンドミュージアム
spots.desc: A museum about sand, featuring a large hourglass, sand samples from across Japan and the world, and lots of information about how sand forms and why there are different kinds of sand. Also houses the largest sandglass in the world, which times one full year.

spots.name: Ryugenji Mabu Mine Shaft
spots.desc: The only mine shaft that visitors can tour on their own without a tour, although guides are available. This covers only a fraction of the tunnels that were dug around here, but a walk through the shaft is impressive nonetheless.

spots.name: Okubo Mabu Mine Shaft
spots.desc: The largest and most impressive mine shaft in Iwami Ginzan. It is open to the public for guided tours. Reservations are not necessary but are recommended, as a limited number are offered per week. Meet at the Iwami Ginzan World Heritage Center, where a bus will take you to the mines. Despite the time, effort, and money required, it's well worthwhile for a full appreciation of Iwami Ginzan.
spots.hours: Tours begin at 09:30, 10:30, 12:15, and 13:15, lasting 2½ hours. Fri-Sun and holidays, Mar-Nov

spots.name: Iwami Ginzan World Heritage Center
spots.local: 石見銀山世界遺産センター
spots.desc: Typically the first stop visitors make when visiting the mines. This museum displays the history of the mines through artifacts, recreated scenes, and interactive computers. It's a nice place to prepare for everything you are about to see.

spots.name: Gohyaku-Rakan
spots.local: 五百羅漢, Rakan-ji 羅漢寺
spots.desc: An interesting temple cut into the side of the hill, housing 500 carved Boddhisatva statues.

spots.name: Gungendo
spots.desc: A very coolly stylish cafe and design gallery featuring handcrafted glassware, pottery, clothing, and decor.

spots.name: Gohanya Mitsu
spots.desc: Serves a variety of donburi (meat over rice) dishes, as well as ramen and curry.

spots.name: Tottori Nijisseiki Pear Museum
spots.local: 鳥取二十世紀梨記念館 なしっこ館
spots.desc: The Tottori Nijisseiki Pear Museum celebrates the prefecture's signature product, the 20th Century Pear. This is the only pear museum in Japan. It features interactive exhibits highlighting pear production, the history of pears in Japan, a tasting area, a dessert parlor, and more.

spots.name: Utsubuki Park
spots.desc: Every April, Utsubuki Koen is filled with people admiring the 4,000 cherry blossom trees and 40,000 azaleas in the park. Utsubuki Koen has been designated one of the top 100 city parks in Japan, and it is also known as one of the top 100 cherry blossom viewing sites in the country.

spots.name: Akagawara Craft District
spots.desc: In the Shirakabe area, these crafts shops offer visitors the chance to experience traditional Japanese crafts. Classes include Hakota doll painting, postcard-making, kite-making, and ceramics. Participants must reserve a spot in advance.

spots.name: Shirakabe Warehouses
spots.desc: The warehouses that line this street comprise some of the oldest buildings in the area, dating back to the Edo and early Meiji periods. Shops specializing in sake, oil, rice, or soy sauce once formed a prosperous shopping district, and the old-style buildings with white plastered walls, black wall panels, and red tiled roofs give an authentic glimpse back into old Japan. Many of these buildings…

spots.name: Chiyomusubi Brewing
spots.local: 千代むすび酒造 岡空本店
spots.desc: Daily tours of this excellent sake producer. The kura or sake brewery features a nice gift shop, a small restaurant for tasting, and of course fine sake. The company also produces an unusual sparkling sake.
spots.hours: Tours Mon-Fri at 11:00 and 14:00; Sat Sun holidays 10:00, 11:00, 14:00, and 15:00

spots.name: Iroha Sushi
spots.desc: Excellent and a good value for lunch. Get there early as the master only uses the freshest fish and when he runs out lunch service is finished.

spots.name: Shizuki Park
spots.desc: Surrounding the castle ruins, this park is a popular spot for cherry blossom parties in the spring. Also here are a small shrine, a teahouse, the Jozangama pottery kiln (城山窯), and a hiking path leading up to the peak of Mt. Shizuki (about 140 m).

spots.name: Asa Mōri Samurai Residence
spots.local: 旧厚狭毛利家萩屋敷長屋
spots.desc: A longhouse dating back to 1856 belonging to the Asa Mōri family, descendants of Mōri Motonari who were granted land in Asa (present-day Sanyo-Onoda). It was part of a larger estate that included the main house and other buildings however, none of the other buildings remain. Since it is a longhouse, each section is opened as their own exhibit. As you walk from one end to the other, you can see…

spots.name: Hagi Christian Martyrs Memorial Park
spots.local: 萩キリシタン殉教者記念公園
spots.desc: The park contains the graves of Christians exiled to Hagi from Nagasaki in 1868 with a monument for Christian martyrs. It is also associated with the story of Kumagai Motonao and Amano Motonobu. During the construction of Hagi Castle, the two men were accused of stealing stones meant to be used to make the castle walls causing a 2 month delay in the castle's construction. Mōri Terumoto, who…

spots.name: Aoki Shusuke Residence
spots.desc: The home of Aoki Shusuke (1803–1863), a doctor and prominent scholar in Dutch medicinal studies. He was the personal doctor of the feudal lord Takachika Mori and treated Takasugi Shinsaku, who would light the spark that would lead to the end of the Tokugawa, for smallpox at the age of 10. The house is divided into the public doctor's office and the family area.

spots.name: Kido Takayoshi's Childhood Home
spots.desc: A student of Shoin Yoshida at the local Meirinkan, later in life, at the behest of mentor Sakamoto Ryoma, Kido Takayoshi (1833 – 1877) joined Takamori Saigo and Toshimichi Okubo to form the new government during the Meiji Restoration and establish the Five Charter Oath, which abolished the provinces and created the modern prefectures.

spots.name: Kubota Residence
spots.desc: The Kubota family were kimono merchants who moved to Hagi from Omi Province (present-day Shiga). Subsequent generations abandoned kimono-making to start a sake brewery.

spots.name: Kuchiba Residence
spots.desc: Built between the late 18th century and early 19th century, it's one of the oldest samurai residences in Hagi. It was home to one of the domain's top officials. The house has a nice view of the Hashimoto River.

spots.name: Masuda Residence
spots.desc: The Masuda from Masuda in Iwami Province lived here, but it is also believed to have been a secret spy location with a tower used to monitor who entered and exited the castle town.

spots.name: Takasugi Shinsaku's Birthplace
spots.desc: A highly-influential samurai who trained at the Shoka Sonjuku. He was the first to create a militia that recruited commoners that became known as the Kiheitai. After witnessing the defeat of his domain by Western powers, he pushed for modernization in the military, giving rifles to his Kiheitai soldiers. The simple belief that modernization would benefit Japan evolved into anti-Tokugawa sentiment…

spots.name: Tanaka Giichi's Birthplace
spots.desc: A signboard marks the location of the former Prime Minister's birthhome. Nothing remains of the house, but those interested in the man should visit the Tanaka Villa further south in the Hiyako area.

spots.name: Kodama Residence Garden
spots.desc: Former residence of a high-ranking samurai. It has its own docking port connected to the Hashimoto River that allowed the family to come and go by boat directly from their home. A nice garden was built around the docking port that you can still see today.

spots.name: Tanaka Villa
spots.desc: The summer villa of Tanaka Giichi who served as a decorated member of the Imperial Army before becoming Prime Minister of Japan from 1927-1929. As a military officer, he influenced armywide policies and developed strategies that aided in Japan's victory in the Russo-Japanese War. After the war, he worked in Manchuria to protect Japanese interests and directed the military to go after Communists…

spots.name: Former Hagi Domain Boathouse
spots.desc: A structure built to house the ships that were being constructed to protect Hagi from nautical attacks. The sea once reached the boathouse, so ships could enter and exit the port.
spots.hours: Only open during special periods, but it can always be viewed from the outside

spots.name: Koike Family Warehouse
spots.desc: A storehouse believed to have been used to house cargo from Hamasaki Port.

spots.name: Yamanaka Residence
spots.desc: The Yamanaka family were local seafood salesmen. They sold from here as well as sending fish to buyers in Kansai. Visitors can see items from the former business used by the Yamanaka's.

spots.name: Yamamura Residence
spots.desc: A wealthy family, the Yamamura's had their main house, a teahouse, and a storehouse around a central garden.

spots.name: Umeya Shichibei House
spots.desc: A sake brewer and local arms dealer, he traveled in secret to Nagasaki to procure 1000 Chinese guns for the Choshu Domain, which helped them win the Boshin War and eventually bring down the Tokugawa shogunate.

spots.name: Kasayama
spots.desc: It is the smallest active volcano in East Asia, and offers panoramic views of the Sea of Japan. Look for the lovely camellia flowers during February and March.

spots.name: Ajio Falls
spots.desc: A unique waterfall that falls down columnal joints from the Abu Volcanoes.

spots.name: Hirobumi Ito House
spots.local: 伊藤博文旧宅 itō hirobumi kyūtaku
spots.desc: The former residence of Hirobumi Itō, the aforementioned first Prime Minister of Japan, and himself a former Shoin student. He served four terms as prime minister and drafted the Meiji Constitution. After serving as Prime Minister, he went on to secure the signing of the Japan-Korea Treaty of 1907, which gave Japan power over Korean affairs, and instated himself as Resident-General of Korea.…

spots.name: Tamaki Bunnoshin Residence
spots.desc: The home of Yoshida Shoin's uncle who first established the Shoka Sonjuku as a local private school.

spots.name: Aibagawa Canal
spots.desc: It was built for transportation of goods, and also to supply water for extinguishing fires. Today, the path along the canal makes for a nice stroll.

spots.name: Chomon Gorge
spots.desc: The gorge was featured in the ukiyoe series Selected Views of Japan by Hasui Kawase in 1922 and recognized as a National Place of Scenic Beauty in 1923. The gorge follows the Abu River from Yamaguchi to Hagi via a 5.1km hiking trail.

spots.name: Kannon-in
spots.desc: Part of the Chugoku 33 Temple Pilgrimage, Kannon-in, also known as Tamae Kannon (玉江観音), was built overlooking the Hashimoto River. It is said that private meetings were held here by some of Hagi's most prominent and influential figures in the years leading up to the fall of the shogunate. The temple offers an incredible view of Mount Shizuki, the castle town, and the Sea of Japan.

spots.name: Kumaya Art Museum
spots.local: 熊谷美術館・熊谷家住宅
spots.desc: Located in the former residence of the salt-merchant Kumaya family, the museum features over 3000 items from the family's collection, such as paintings from Sesshu and a Siebold piano (the oldest piano in Japan).

spots.name: Ohitayama-tatara Iron Smelting Works
spots.local: 大板山たたら製鉄遺跡
spots.desc: Traditional iron-smelting technology (tatara) from the ancient Kibi Kingdom in Okayama, traditionally used for swords, was given new purpose in Hagi to produce iron for warships. The Heishin-maru is one of the ships known to be made with this iron. Today the ruins are listed as part of Hagi's World Heritage listing.

spots.name: Sasanami Historic Preservation District
spots.local: 佐々並市伝統的建造物群保存地区
spots.desc: A small town built along the Hagi Okan (萩往還) in the Edo Period to connect the capital of Nagato Province (Hagi) to the capital of Suo Province (Hofu). It was used by travelers as a resting point with inns and shops. Many of the buildings still exist today.

spots.name: Yukawa Residence
spots.desc: A samurai residence that uses water from the canal to form an attractive garden. The water is even directed into part of the house for domestic use.

spots.name: Katsura Taro Residence
spots.desc: The second-longest serving Prime Minister of Japan who served from 1901 to 1913 and the first to be removed from office after a no-confidence vote, this is his childhood home. He studied at the Meirinkan from here. He was well-accomplished before becoming Prime Minister as a general in the Sino-Japanese War and the Governor-General of Taiwan. As Prime Minister, he oversaw Japanese victory in the…

spots.name: Watanabe Kozo Residence
spots.desc: Considered a leader in shipbuilding who helped construct the Tategami dock, said to have been the best dock in all of Asia at the time. In his youth, Watanabe studied at the Shoka Sonjuku before traveling to the United States and United Kingdom to study naval architecture. He returned to become one of the heads of the Nagasaki Shipyard. The house is larger than most in Hagi. In addition to the…

spots.name: Boat Cruise
spots.desc: The Hagi Tourist Association runs pleasant cruises on the Hashimoto River and the Sea of Japan, with a guide to direct attention to the Eight Fine Views.

spots.name: Kurumayado Tenjuppei
spots.desc: Rickshaw tours of the historic sections of the city center. They have standard itineraries to match the tour length, but substitutions can be made.
spots.price: For two people, expect to pay ¥6000 for 30 minutes, ¥10,000 for one hour, or ¥20,000 two hours.

spots.name: Yuzuya Honten
spots.desc: The natsumikan is a citrus fruit that's grown in many local gardens, and squeezed into a tasty juice. At Yuzuya Honten, you can buy natsumikan and other local fruits whole, enjoy them as ice cream, or lend a hand at turning them into juice or marmalade. It's on a peninsula directly north of the city — either take a cab or walk west from JR Koshigahama Station.

spots.name: Susa Bay Geocruising
spots.local: 須佐湾遊覧船ジオクルージング
spots.desc: A cruise of the bay to enjoy local geological features along the coast with the hornfels cliffs as the main highlight. Advance reservations required.
spots.hours: 60 min ride from reserved time between 10:00-15:00 from May to October
spots.price: ¥2200 for 5 people or more, ¥11000 total for less than 5 people

spots.name: Hagi Hina Festival
spots.desc: Hina doll displays are set up in many of the historic samurai residences in the Horiuchi area. On the last day of the festival, there is a ceremony where girls put special dolls in the waters of the Aibagawa Canal called nagashibina.

spots.name: Hagi-yaki Festival
spots.desc: This festival is at the beginning of May. About 50 pottery shops from around the city come to the City Gymnasium to exhibit and sell their wares. It's a great opportunity to buy hagi-yaki at a low price.

spots.name: Hagi Summer Festival
spots.desc: This festival at the beginning of August. On the first day, about 8,000 fireworks are lit over the sea off Kikugahama.

spots.name: Hagi Lantern Festival
spots.desc: The lanterns surrounding the Mori Clan graves are lit up at Daishoin Temple on August 13 and at Tokoji Temple on August 15

spots.name: Hagi Historical Festival
spots.desc: During weekends in November, this festival involves people in traditional Choshu garb on parade through the center of town.

spots.name: Hagi-yaki
spots.desc: It is the local form of Japanese pottery and the top souvenir from a trip to Hagi. It is unique because of the way it reacts to water; over time, you'll notice delicate changes in its color. A few pottery shops offer visitors the chance to cast their own hagi-yaki — check with a tourist information office to see what is available.

spots.name: Hagi Pudding
spots.desc: As the name suggests, they make their own puddings that you can purchase as a unique local souvenir. They also sell soft-serve that you can eat while you walk.

spots.name: Ajiro
spots.desc: Kaiseki sets of the best of the local seafood catch. May not be suitable for single diners.

spots.name: Fujitaya
spots.desc: A local institution — though a bit tricky to find — Fujitaya serves hot tempura and other dishes, but the specialty is seiro-soba, in which tasty soba noodles are delivered to your table in a steaming basket.

spots.name: Grill Restaurant Kenran
spots.local: 網焼きレストラン 見蘭
spots.desc: A grill restaurant known for Kenran Beef from a local farm. It can be eaten as steak, yakiniku, and in other dishes. In the same complex, they also have the Midoriya Honten, which in addition to offering meat to buy directly, they have foods that you can eat while you walk, such as croquettes and fried beef cutlets, as well as takeaway bentos, all of which feature their signature Kenran Beef.
spots.hours: Restaurant 17:00-22:00, Midoriya Honten 17:00-22:00, lunch by reservation 11:30-14:00 (closed Tue)

spots.name: Hotori Tei
spots.desc: Lunch sets in a lovely garden setting, in Jokamachi. Later in the evening, the same folks run Sam's Irish Pub (see Drink).

spots.name: Tangotei
spots.desc: Delicious, freshly caught seafood, including knockout sashimi.
spots.price: Sets from ¥1380, or a feast for ¥5800

spots.name: Manetsu
spots.desc: A Chinese restaurant serving ramen, gyoza, fried rice, and other popular Chinese dishes.

spots.name: Kakure Tsubaki
spots.desc: A lunch-only curry restaurant that also serves hot sandwiches.

spots.name: Vengo
spots.desc: An Italian restaurant with a variety of pasta dishes and Italian wines.

spots.name: Seisei-an
spots.desc: A café with a beautiful Japanese garden, right by the Kikuya House. They have a selection of hagi-yaki on display.

spots.name: Hagi Samurai
spots.desc: Hiroshima okonomiyaki made with sauce from Mihara (where the owner is from) and noodles from Onomichi. Food and drinks are served by "real" samurai with authentic chonmage, the shaved side and topknot hairstyle worn by samurai.

spots.name: Laughable
spots.desc: Hōfu's main bar, most easily found by looking for the neon yellow shower curtain that serves as its door.

spots.name: Paper Goldfish Festival
spots.local: 金魚提灯祭り Kingyo Chōchin Matsuri
spots.desc: The festival is in honor of Yanai's most famous and noteworthy product: the goldfish lantern. Various teams compete to parade and spin large versions of the lanterns to the beat of a Taiko (Japanese Drum) and chorus. A large firework display concludes the festival.

spots.name: Yanai Daishi Ennichi
spots.desc: This event is a day when memorial services are held for Kouboudaishi. On festival day, about 20 markets are held.

spots.name: MadDope
spots.desc: An eclectic shop featuring locally produced Japanese hip-hop CDs and Japanese fashion.

spots.name: Kamaya
spots.desc: A local family-run udon establishment featuring freshly made udon.

spots.name: Sanzoku
spots.desc: Literally translating as "Mountain Bandit", this establishment features coal roasted chicken and meat dishes with gift shop and koi pond located on a sprawling outdoor arboreal setting.

spots.name: Taiwanya
spots.desc: There is a long menu, but most regulars eat 'shiru-soba','shiru-bihun','yaki-soba'and 'yaki-bihun.' The restaurant is run by a man and his wife. Take-out available on request.

spots.name: Oyunuma
spots.desc: A roughly 1-km-circumference volcanic lake formed by an eruption of Mt Hiyori. Sulphurous water rises from springs around 130°C at the bottom of the lake, while the surface is typically around 40–50°C. A particularly atmospheric extension of the Hell Valley walk, with several short paths and viewpoints around the lake.

spots.name: Mt Hiyori
spots.desc: A 377-metre active volcano immediately above Oyunuma, still emitting white volcanic smoke. Short trails and viewpoints around Oyunuma provide views of the volcano and the surrounding volcanic landscape

spots.name: Dai-Ichi Takimotokan
spots.desc: This famous hotel makes a credible claim to being the largest spa in Asia. ¥2,250 gets you one day's access to the 29 large baths, the largest of which is nearly 4,950 m² in size. Day-visitors must exit before 9pm.

spots.name: Yumoto Sagiriyu
spots.desc: A much cheaper and more local alternative to the large hotel baths. This public bath uses two types of natural hot-spring water and is the only bath in Noboribetsu Onsen offering alum spring water. ¥500, 09:00–21:00, last admission 20:30. (2)

spots.name: Ako Marine Science Museum
spots.desc: Ako was historically a center of sea salt production. At this marine science museum, not only will you learn everything you wanted to know and then some about salt, but you can try your hand at making your own from seawater. Salt-making is included in price of admission, reservations recommended but not mandatory.

spots.name: Akashi Kaikyo Bridge
spots.local: 明石海峡大橋, Akashi Channel Bridge
spots.desc: Completed in 1998, this majestic bridge dwarfs the village of Iwaya below. The bridge's total length is 3,991 m, and the main span's length of 1,991 m made it the longest suspension bridge in the world (surpassed by Çanakkale Bridge in 2022). The bridge is attractively lit at night.

spots.name: Sumoto Castle
spots.desc: A ruined castle and keep. It is the oldest reconstructed castle in Japan, having been rebuilt prior to WWII in 1928. Getting there requires quite a hike, but the view from the top is extraordinary.

spots.name: Water Temple
spots.desc: A famous Buddhist temple building designed by Japanese architect Tadao Ando. The same architect also designed nearby Yume no Butai.

spots.name: Nojima Fault Preservation Museum
spots.desc: A section of the Nojima Fault, responsible for the 1995 Great Hanshin earthquake, is preserved here.

spots.name: Ikkyuji
spots.desc: Constructed by the Ikkyu-san, a famous Zen master, around 1456. Ikkyu-san was a real person, but famously features in children's folktales as a child monk who is able to outsmart adults with his quick wit and word-play. He lived here in the late parts of his life and his relics are buried within the temple grounds. The temple features a beautiful Zen rock garden, a statue with actual hair from…

spots.name: Kirara Shotengai
spots.desc: The Kirara Shotengai is dedicated to the city's mascot, Kirara-chan, a cheerful girl with rainbow pigtails. Along with restaurants and other shops, the shotengai has the Kirara no Eki, which is where you buy Kirara-themed souvenirs. You can also get some information about the town and purchase other local souvenirs. Across the street at the butcher shop is where you can buy the Kirara Croquette…

spots.name: Imamura Hosuien
spots.desc: A famous local sweets shop known for the Ikkyu Roll and Kyotanabe Roll featuring the local gyokuro (tea). The shop has been operating here since 1932.

spots.name: Pinocchio
spots.desc: A high-quality Italian pasta restaurant offering spaghetti dishes with various meat, tomato, and white sauce dishes. They also have a nice variety of pizzas and soups.

spots.name: Maizuru World Brick Museum
spots.desc: The museum displays bricks from all over the world and all over Japan, as well as ancient ones from Mesopotamia, Egypt, China, and Greece. Part of Maizuru Brick Park which consists of many brick buildings formerly used by the Imperial Japanese Navy.

spots.name: Tanabe Castle
spots.desc: The castle gate and a turret have been reconstructed and operate as small museums with information about the castle and a small collection of artifacts. The grounds have a few preserved stone walls and a garden that's worth a look if you're here. While the leader of the castle Tadaoki Hosokawa (formerly Nagaoka) was off preparing to fight in the Battle of Sekigahara, the castle was left to his…
spots.price: ¥200 to enter castle buildings, park grounds are free

spots.name: Admiral Togo's Official Residence
spots.desc: Heihachiro Togo was the first admiral of Maizuru Naval District. He famously commanded the Japanese Combined Fleet to victory over Russia at the Battle of Tsushima in the Russo-Japanese War. This was considered to be the first time a non-Western nation won a war against a Western nation and ended Russia's naval dominance in East Asia. He was awarded the Order of the Chrysanthemum and featured on…
spots.hours: first Sun of the month only

spots.name: Repatriation Museum
spots.desc: Exhibits materials about repatriation from China and Korea after the World War II.

spots.name: Iga Ninja Museum
spots.desc: Ueno's top attraction by far, this old Japanese house was actually used by the Iga clan and is full of spiffy ninja secrets like trapdoors, revolving walls and more, all demonstrated by kunoichi - cheerful lady ninjas in pink garb. There is a museum on the grounds with good English displays, and there are also live demonstrations of ninja weaponry and techniques - hourly from 11:00 to 15:00…

spots.name: Bashō Museum
spots.desc: This museum pays tribute to the haiku master Matsuo Bashō, who is thought to have been born in Iga. It's not often open, but the building itself, shaped like the hat Bashō wore, is a curious sight.

spots.name: Iga Ueno Castle
spots.desc: This castle was a frequent target for ninja attacks in the old days. Resist the temptation to slip on a mask and go skulking around as if nobody can see you; the sleepy guard inside the castle doesn't need the hassle. It's one of the better-looking castle reconstructions in Japan, but the museum inside is not really worth a visit.

spots.name: Ueno Tenjin Festival
spots.desc: The festival is held every year October 23rd to 25th. Between the festivals the portable shrines are shown in the Danjiri Museum.

spots.name: Seki-juku
