spots.desc: The 47th stop of the Tokaido, an old road that connected Tokyo to Kyoto. The Seki-juku is located along a fairly long road of well-preserved historic districts; One of the best stations of the entire Tokaido Route.

spots.name: Shishiiwa
spots.desc: Kumano's famous lion rock formation. There is a cafe on one side which is in the perfect spot for viewing.

spots.name: Onigajo
spots.desc: The demon castle is a stunning rock cave formation against a backdrop of ocean and mountains which you can walk right through.

spots.name: Maruyama Senmaida
spots.desc: Senmaida means "One thousand terraced rice fields", built into a hill where no machines can reach. It must be planted by hand every year and many of the town's residents show up to pitch in. For travelers, the view of the rice terraces is highly photogenic. It is listed as one of the top 100 rice terraces in the country, a list which focus on scenic beauty.

spots.name: Hike the Kumano Kodo
spots.desc: Kumano is home to several sections of the ancient pilgrimage route, the Kumano Kodo. Matsumoto Toge and Kannon Michi are great places to hike.

spots.name: Go to the beach
spots.desc: Kumano has two beautiful beaches that you'd swear are private groves in a tropical land. Odomari beach is only one station north of Kumano, head straight down the hill from the station. Atashika beach by Atashika station is a bit more remote, but larger than Odomari. Both overlook mountains and small villages in the distance. Swimming season usually lasts from June until the end of August.…

spots.name: Hanabi Taikai
spots.desc: Kumano's biggest festival, and actually one of the biggest fireworks festivals in Japan, occurs on August 17th of every year. People come from all over Japan, clogging the trains and highways, camping out on the beach and in the Aeon department store, just for this day. Fireworks will shake the ground, take up the entire horizon, and last for hours and hours. Takes place on Kumano's endless…

spots.name: Doro Kyo
spots.desc: Doro Kyo is a natural gorge that you can hire a boat ride through.

spots.name: Kiwa Town
spots.desc: Although it is now a part of Kumano, it still kind of feels like its own town. It's a charming place - about 40 minutes from Kumano proper, there are no train lines at all, and when it was independent it had fewer than 2,000 residents. It also used to be known for its mining industry which you can learn about at the mining information center/museum off route 311 in the center of town. Not far…

spots.name: Tennyoza
spots.desc: A unique cafe near Hadasu station overlooking the ocean and mountain scenery. Also a home to a collection of old instruments and the owners would be happy to give you an impromptu concert.

spots.name: Cafe Rosen
spots.desc: Cafe Rosen is a bit more than just a cafe — it has a beautiful wood interior and a full dinner menu of familiar western-style food.

spots.name: Shinbashi
spots.desc: A local favorite is a bar called Shinbashi, which is located near the police station and not far from the Aeon shopping center. They offer chuhai drinks in every flavor from banana to ramune.

spots.name: Kyūka Park
spots.desc: This park and water course, which lies at the site of Kuwana Castle, boasts its own outdoor sumo rink.

spots.name: Rokkaen
spots.desc: An Important Cultural Property, built for a local businessman called Seiroku Moroto (1888-1969) and completed in 1913, it consists of a Japanese-style building and a Western-style building, the latter being the only example in the area of the work of the influential British architect Josiah Conder (1852-1920).

spots.name: Nagashima Spa Land
spots.local: ナガシマスパーランド
spots.desc: This venue is an amusement park and a shopping outlet mall that hosts one of the world's largest rollercoasters. In summer the amusement park also has various waterslides on offer.

spots.name: Matsusaka Castle Ruins
spots.desc: While there are no longer any buildings from the original castle, a beautiful set of ruins remain and function as a local park. The ruins are known for their well-preserved castle walls, and the grounds are particularly beautiful during spring and autumn. Cherry blossoms and wisteria bloom in the spring, and there are many colorful autumn trees in the fall. Historical monuments and markers dot…

spots.name: Gojoban Yashiki
spots.desc: A traditional street right outside the castle with preserved houses from the Edo period that were inhabited by samurai, and are now inhabited by their descendants. Be mindful with noise and pictures as people do live in the houses here. An open house is found towards the end of the road across the street from the castle where you can walk around one of the houses for free.

spots.name: Museum of Motoori Norinaga
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to a renowned scholar who came from the city. While largely unknown outside Japan, it's still quite interesting to tour his house and take a glimpse into the daily life of someone living in 18th century Japan.

spots.name: Matsuura Takeshirō Museum
spots.desc: This museum is a bit difficult to access but is an interesting experience. You can learn about the exploration of Hokkaido by the man from Matsusaka who gave the island its name. It's also fun to try on traditional Ainu clothing.

spots.name: Bell Farm
spots.local: 松阪農業公園ベルファーム
spots.desc: A short bus ride away from Matsusaka station, Bell Farm is a local agricultural park that is very popular with locals. The park is famous for selling ice cream, though the place sells a little bit of everything. Local artisans sell handmade goods at the market, and farmers sell locally grown produce at the grocery store there.

spots.name: Magose Toge
spots.desc: A popular hiking trail on the Kumano Kodo - Ise-ji Route. There is a hiking trail which leads to Mt. Tengura, overlooking Owase City.

spots.name: Kumano Kodo Center
spots.desc: Constructed entirely from cypress wood (the tree of Owase), the Kumano Kodo Centre features exhibits on the origins and history of the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route. A playground, also made entirely from cypress, is located nearby.

spots.name: Yume Kodo
spots.desc: A deep sea water onsen, which has healing properties, as well as sauna rooms.

spots.name: Owase Jinja
spots.desc: This shrine is a historical monument in Owase. It's well known for an ancient, sacred tree which is aged over 1,000 years old. Also the venue for every year's Ya Ya Matsuri.

spots.name: Kongō-ji
spots.desc: Built during the Edo Era, the Kongō-ji has two fierce-looking deity statues guarding the entrance.

spots.name: Sugari
spots.desc: Sugari is best accessed by a 20-minute ferry ride from Owase Port. It is an untouched, beautiful fishing village with friendly residents who would be more than happy to show visitors around. As of 2008, Sugari has a declining population of less than 200 people, with the majority aged above 60 years old.

spots.name: Fusaiji Temple
spots.desc: A Sōtō Zen temple founded in 1624 that has watched over the fishing village of Sugari for around 400 years. Its current main hall was rebuilt in 1861 by a master carpenter who was an ancestor of the Takenaka Corporation, one of Japan's oldest construction companies.

spots.name: Kuki
spots.desc: Like Sugari, Kuki is also a beautiful fishing town. If you are lucky, you will be able catch seagulls and comorant fishing at its best. Try the famed Kuki's tiger rolls, which come in two flavours - red bean or fresh cream.

spots.name: Itadaki Market
spots.desc: A monthly market featuring over 40 stalls where you can buy Owase's local produce such as fresh seafood, dried fish, sea salt, and jam. At the market, you'll also be able to enjoy special dance and taiko performances by the locals.

spots.name: Ya Ya Matsuri
spots.desc: The biggest festival in Owase is the Ya Ya Matsuri. In the evenings of the 2nd to the 4th, men parade around the streets, jostling each other and chanting "Ya Ya" while drinking sake before the "chosen" ones dive into the sea to purify themselves. The festival ends off with a day-long street parade on the 5th featuring dance performances and finally, an archery contest at Owase Jinja.

spots.name: Hachiman Jinja Matsuri
spots.desc: This festival marks a tribute to the Hachiman Jinja, located near the Owase Port. It begins with a day-long parade before culminating at the shrine.

spots.name: Kotobuki Shokudo
spots.desc: This old restaurant has food that is great tasting and comes in huge portions. Recommended eats include the Giant Katsu Set, Giant Ebi Fry Set, Inoshishi (wild boar) Don and Champon (Nagasaki Noodles).

spots.name: Moriba
spots.desc: Moriba is well loved for its Tempura, Tebasaki (Chicken wings) and Miso Katsu.

spots.name: Oni Gawara
spots.desc: If you'd like to experience the freshness of Owase's sea produce, this is the place to go. The sashimi set meal comes in 3 sizes and is highly recommended for sashimi lovers.

spots.name: Hao Hao Han Ten
spots.desc: A Chinese restaurant offering refined Chinese food. Popular dishes include the ten shin han, mapo han, and the pirikara szechuan ramen.

spots.name: Hei Wa En
spots.desc: For a taste of authentic Chinese food, visit Hei Wa En. The owners come from Dahlian, China and serve traditional Chinese food.

spots.name: Inaka
spots.desc: Famous for its affordable lunch sets consisting of 8 small side dishes, typically usually sashimi, a stewed meat, vegetables, soup, and rice.

spots.name: Nakao
spots.desc: Get your fill of collagen filled tonkotsu ramen at this ramen house.

spots.name: Yume Kodo Mother's Lunch Buffet
spots.local: 夢古道 お母ちゃんのランチバイキング
spots.desc: Popular for its "all you can eat" country style buffet every Sunday. Run by an NPO, meals are prepared by 4 groups of volunteers (very friendly obasans), who take turns to cook every week. It's delicious country-style, home-cooked food that you won't be able to taste in typical Japanese restaurants. The buffet is so famous that some people travel from Nagoya or Osaka to eat it. Go early to…

spots.name: Parque Espana
spots.local: パルケ エスパーニャ（志摩スペイン村）
spots.desc: An ersatz Spanish "village" theme park and probably Shima's main attraction.

spots.name: Rockontei
spots.desc: Soba restaurant inside the Okagero ryokan. Doesn't have English menus, however some of the staff speak English.

spots.name: Ancient Site of Fujiwara Palace
spots.desc: Fujiwarakyo (藤原京), the first palace in Japan to be modeled after Chinese style was built on the land covering this city in 694 AD. Fujiwarakyo was the capital of Japan until the palace was moved to Heijōkyo (contemporary Nara) in 710 AD.

spots.name: Unebi Yama
spots.desc: This hill is an easy 20 minutes hike. Nice view of the surrounding area from the top.

spots.name: Kawabata Yasunari Museum of Literature
spots.desc: On display are about 400 items including books authored by Kawabata, his personal belongings, letters, manuscripts and calligraphic works as well as photographs and videos that shed light on the author's career.

spots.name: Ibaraki History Museum
spots.local: 茨木市立文化財資料館
spots.desc: On display are artifacts belonging to the cultural history of Ibaraki such as bronze bells, earthenware, ancient documents, etc.

spots.name: Meio-ji
spots.desc: A temple run by the Bentenshu (辯天宗) Buddhist sect. It has a tranquil atmosphere and unique architecture, including a pointed tower/stupa. It is a popular site for cherry blossom viewing around April, with illuminations during the evenings as well. Every year on August 8, there is a fireworks show from 7:30-8:30 PM.
spots.addr: 大阪府茨木市西穂積町7-41

spots.name: Church of Light
spots.local: 茨木春日丘教会 Ibaraki Kasuga-oka Kyoukai
spots.desc: Tadao Ando-designed modern architecture (1989). Call or email for reservations to see the church outside of normal hours.
spots.hours: Sun worship service begins at 10:25. Church is open by reservation Sun 15:00-18:00, Mon Tue Thu-Sat 10:00-18:00

spots.name: The Farm Universal Osaka & Strawberry Farm No. 15
spots.desc: Located in the picturesque old village of Saho (佐保), this is a sprawling, photogenic garden center that feels more like a nature theme park than a plant nursery. The complex is divided into several zones, including a greenhouse filled with succulents and cacti for sale, a "Farmer's Kitchen" restaurant serving organic vegetable-heavy dishes, and an outdoor play area with treehouses and friendly…
spots.hours: Daily 10:00-18:00 (Strawberry Farm closes at 15:00 or when supplies run out)
spots.price: Free entry to garden center. Strawberry Farm: Entry ¥500, plus ¥6 per gram of picked fruit.

spots.name: Aeon Mall Ibaraki
spots.desc: A wide variety of stores, incl. Saty, Vivre, Warner Bros Cinema, Konami Sports Club.

spots.name: Ramen Kiraku
spots.desc: Cheap small ramen restaurant run by two old women. Prices start from ¥250 for ramen.

spots.name: Ikeda Castle
spots.desc: The original castle was built by the Ikeda clan in 1334. The modern reconstruction was built in 2000.

spots.name: Hikiyama Museum
spots.local: 長浜市曳山博物館 nagahama-shi hikiyama hakubutsukan
spots.desc: Nagahama Hikiyama (Float) Matsuri (festival) having more than 400 years of history is known as one of the three great float festivals of Japan. In this museum, the gorgeous and splendid floats that are paraded around the city during the Hikiyama Festival are exhibited. A movie showing highlights of the festival, such as kabuki played by boys aging from 5 to 12 just like the old days, are screened.

spots.name: Kaiyoudou Figurine Museum Kurokabe
spots.local: 海洋堂フィギュアミュージアム黒壁 kaiyōdō figyuā myūjiamu kurokabe
spots.desc: An otaku's paradise! Figurines of all shapes and sizes inhabit this museum, depicting dinosaurs, anime characters, etc., are exhibited in a diorama style. Those figures are sold in the shop on the first floor of the museum. There are some seriously heavy-duty collector's items in here!

spots.name: Daitsūji Temple
spots.desc: It is said that Daitsuji was built from the remains of Fushimi Castle in Kyoto. In the temple building, there are sliding door paintings by Oukyo Maruyama and by painters of the Kano school reflecting the gorgeous atmosphere of Momoyama culture. Daitsuji's garden is designated as a national scenic garden. Along the street approaching Daitsuji, there are many shops built in the Machiya style, the…

spots.name: Jinshōji Temple
spots.desc: Jinshōji is the oldest temple in Nagahama and was founded in 895 (Kanpyo 7). There are many valuable cultural assets such as statue of a multi-armed deity, and a Cetaka statue looking over his shoulder. Kinginto Sukashibori Keko (flower basket motif in lace worked arabesque carving in gold and silver), a national treasure, is especially worth noting since it has been exhibited in the Boston…

spots.name: Hachiman-gū Shrine
spots.desc: This shrine has over 1000 years of history. It is a shrine protecting the community of Nagahama. Every April 15, you can attend the Hikiyama Matsuri!

spots.name: Ōmi Kōhō-an Temple
spots.desc: Ōmi Kōhō-an is a temple located in the tranquility of the mountains and greenery which consoles the spirit of Enshuu Kobori (1579 - 1647), Lord of Komuro Castle, known as one of the three great tea ceremony masters. Enshuu constructed Kōhō-an in Daitoku Ji (temple) in Kyoto, and this temple in contrast is called Ōmi Kōhō-an. The garden of this temple is well noted for using the natural…

spots.name: Nagahama Railway Square
spots.local: 長浜鉄道スクエア nagahama tetsudō sukuea
spots.desc: There are three buildings within the Square. The old Nagahama station house is the oldest existing station house in Japan and its stationmaster’s room and waiting room are kept as they were in the old days. In the second building, the Nagahama Railway Cultural Pavilion, a large number of valuable materials about railways are exhibited. In the third building, the Museum for Commemoration of the…
spots.price: Adults ¥300, children 15 and under: ¥150. 20% discount for group with 20 or more people

spots.name: Hikiyama Festival
spots.desc: Every April 15th. Begins at Hachimangu Shrine and snakes its way towards Kurokabe Square. Young boys perform traditional kabuki plays on floats.

spots.name: Nagahama and Kita-Biwako Fireworks Festival
spots.local: 長浜と北琵琶湖花火大会
spots.desc: Every August 5th, a massive fireworks festival launched in the harbor area of Lake Biwa. Green Hotel Yes Nagahama Minato-kan offers the best view, but generally any rooftop will do nicely. Remember to wear your yukata!

spots.name: Nagahama Shusse Festival
spots.desc: This festival started in 1983 commemorating the reconstruction of Nagahama Castle. It's now a major October event in Nagahama. The festival includes various events, most notably the “Great Kimono Garden Party” where thousands of young women from near and far dress up in extraordinarily ornate kimono and parade about town.

spots.name: Art in Nagahama
spots.desc: Artists from various fields gather from all over Japan to exhibit, demonstrate, and sell their works in various spots in Kurokabe Square. In other words, this event is an open air market for artists. Usually takes place during the Shusse Festival.

spots.name: Nagahama Bonbai Exhibition
spots.desc: Bonbai is a Japanese apricot tree in bonsai style. This annual exhibition began in 1952 when the late Shichizo Takayama donated his bonbai to Nagahama City. A 400-year-old tree is among the exhibits. The Nagahama Bonbai Exhibition has been referred to as the No. 1 bonbai exhibition, both historically and scale-wise.

spots.name: Kurokabe Glass Shop
spots.desc: The namesake of Kurokabe Square, which was built in 1890 as Daihyaku Sanju Bank Nagahama Branch. Two storeys of glass art, jewelry, stemware, etc. The first floor is a shop for glass accessories and sundries, while the second floor displays glassworks from all over the world which are also available for purchase.

spots.name: Studio Kurokabe
spots.desc: Everything sold in this studio is handmade by artists who work in-house. There's a window where you can watch them at work.

spots.name: Yum Thai
spots.desc: Cheap Thai food in Japanese suburbia. Who'd've thought? Yum Thai is very delicious and the staff is friendly. Some of the waitstaff speak English, but the chef/owner lady only speaks Thai and Japanese.

spots.name: Nagahama Roman Beer
spots.desc: Nagahama's only brewery. Decent beer and nice atmosphere, but the food is pricey.
spots.price: Ranging from ¥380 to ¥2600 for beers. Food averages ¥1000 per dish

spots.name: One Coin
spots.desc: It's a pain to get to it, but once you're there, it's awesome! Sumi and his incredibly old mother love foreigners of every stripe. Sumi speaks incredible English and has a basic grasp of Portuguese and Spanish. If you're a new face, his mother will want to interview you. She'll even take notes.
spots.price: ¥600 for all drinks. Food costs more.

spots.name: Curry & Bar Sai
spots.desc: Sai has a variety of foods and cocktails. Try curry or omelet rice with Heartland (special Kirin beer). It basically opens until customers leave.

spots.name: Ikeda-cho Western Houses Street
spots.desc: The Western Colonial-style houses behind the long brick wall along this street were designed by Vories during the Taisho Era (1912–1924). They are not open to the public but may be viewed from the street. A bilingual sign on the wall explains more about the illustrious architectural career of Vories, who married a Japanese noblewoman and became a Japanese citizen in 1941.

spots.name: Obata-cho and merchant mansions
spots.desc: The Visitor Center at Obata-cho offers parking and leads to the rich merchant mansions that line both sides of Shinmachi Street between Obata-cho and the Hachiman Canal. Bilingual signs in Japanese and English name some of the rich merchants and note their far-reaching commercial activities throughout the Edo Period.

spots.name: Hachiman-bori Canal Walk
spots.desc: The canal was once a castle moat, but later served to carry heavy cargo, especially the roof tiles for which the city was famous, across the lake to larger cities. Stone walkways beside it give a vivid sense of what the architecture of the town looked like hundreds of years ago. The walkway is a wonderful place to view cherry blossoms in the spring, and to hear cicadas buzzing in the summer. It…

spots.name: Kawara Museum
spots.desc: This tile museum on a picturesque corner of the canal shows the history of Omihachiman roof tiles and the manufacturing process. It also displays images of the city, including a large 3-dimensional photograph of the roof tiles in Shincho-dori.

spots.name: Chohoji
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple, founded in 1000 CE. It is the Kishu Tokugawa family temple.

spots.name: Chohoji Main Hall
spots.desc: National Treasure of Japan. It was rebuilt in 1311. It is an East Asian-style hip-and-gable roof.

spots.name: Chohoji Chinjudo
spots.desc: Important Cultural Property. It was rebuilt in the Kamakura period.

spots.name: Onzansouen
spots.desc: National Site of Scenic Beauty. It is a style of garden that features a path around a pond. Japanese Imperial family often came here.

spots.name: Hike the Kumano Kodo
spots.desc: This ancient pilgrimage route offers several possibilities. A popular 2-day trip starts from Takijiri (40 minutes bus ride from Tanabe) and goes to Hongu. From here you can either continue to Nachi or head north to the Koyasan. The tourist office will give you a free map and will shuttle your luggage for a fee.

spots.name: Choshi Port Tower
spots.desc: Tower with observation deck at 46m above surface. Provides a good view around Choshi, Inubozaki Lighthouse and Mount Atago.
spots.hours: Aug and Apr-Sep's Sat Sun and holiday 09:00-18:30. Other times 09:00-17:30.

spots.name: Nure senbei
spots.desc: The (nure senbei) moist rice crackers are available in multiple flavors and baked fresh daily at the Inuboh station. Other foods and souvenirs are also sold in the shop.

spots.name: Wosse 21
spots.desc: Fish market and seafood restaurant directly connected to the Port Tower.

spots.name: Kisarazu Kaigan Shellfish Gathering
spots.desc: You can go shellfish gathering on the seaside, which is called ‘kisarazu kaigan′. The best occasions is to in the middle of March for in the end of August.
spots.hours: Hours vary according to the tide

spots.name: Mitsui Outlet Park Kisarazu
spots.local: 三井アウトレットパーク 木更津
spots.desc: There are outlet stores and restaurants. This has become the new tourist destination of Kisarazu.

spots.name: Brazilya Coffee
spots.desc: A coffee shop with many different kinds of beans. The shop also sells cute "washi" wrapping paper.

spots.name: Kantaro Suzuki Memorial Museum
spots.desc: a museum dedicated to the life and achievements of Admiral Kantarō Suzuki (1868–1948) focusing on his life, naval career, and pivotal role in Japan's surrender, featuring artifacts and a historical archive building from his former residence.

spots.name: Aizawa Tadahiro Kinenkan
spots.desc: Aizawa Tadahiro was the first to discover artefacts demonstrating the presence of human settlements in Japan during the paleolithic era. Many artefacts from the Iwajuku Site are on exhibit.
spots.price: adults (high school students or older):¥500, jr high/ elementary school students:¥250

spots.name: Gunma Insect World
spots.desc: Built on a traditional Japanese landscape, the museum contains a large collection of living insects, along with an array of butterflies among whom visitors can walk all year round in the heated observatory. Other buildings on the grounds offer opportunities to experience various aspects of traditional Japanese culture.
spots.price: adults:¥410, university/high school students:¥200, jr high school students or younger: free

spots.name: Bakery Cafe Renga (former Kanaya Lace Mfg. Corp.)
spots.local: ベーカリーカフェ煉瓦：旧金谷レース工業
spots.desc: It was founded as Kanayoshi Textiles by Kanaya Yoshijiro during the Meiji Era. The large sawtooth roof mill was completed in Dec 1919 and included 8 sawtooth sections. The scratch-tile, 2-storey office building was constructed during the early Showa Era. The compound has a sawtooth roof mill, employee dormitory, family residence, warehouse, & family shrine. After closing in 2007, the mill was…

spots.name: Yanoen (Yano Store and Warehouse)
spots.desc: Yano Hisaemon came to Kiryu in 1717 from the Omi district of Japan. His heir established Yano Mercantile at this location in 1749. In addition to selling sake, miso & soy sauce, the shop also produced vinegar. During the Meiji Era, the shop, constructed in 1916, also sold household goods. The interior has been remodeled as a store & coffee shop.

spots.name: Jomo Railways Nishi Kiryu Station
spots.local: 上毛電鉄西桐生駅駅舎
spots.desc: This Mansard roof station was constructed in 1928 when Jomo Railways began service. The building is a fine example of early Showa Era modern style. The interior has maintained its original ambiance.

spots.name: Yotsuji no Saika
spots.desc: This building was the home of the Saito family which owned and operated Saito Textile Company (CEO Saito Kahei). The buildings were constructed at the first crossroads running east from Tenmangu Shrine, the starting point of Kiryu Shin Machi. The site consists of a storehouse constructed in 1878, and a residence for which a completion ceremony took place in 1923. The buildings reflect the…

spots.name: Kiryu Tenmangu Shrine
spots.desc: A Prefectural Cultural Treasure. Tenmangu is a classic example of Early Modern Period (mid 16th to 18th centuries) "gongen" construction designed for the enshrinement of a Shinto deity. Gables over the Inner Sanctuary and Hall of Offerings are resplendently finished in elaborate detail. Tenmangu is representative of the most highly developed architectural techniques of its era and as such has…

spots.name: Nishinomiya Shrine
spots.desc: In 1901, the god enshrined at Nishinomiya Shrine in Hyogo Prefecture was apportioned and brought to Kiryu. In 1905 a shrine was constructed in honor of the god. Nishinomiya is the only shrine in the entire Kanto area dedicated to the four gods Ebisu Okami, Amaterasu Okami, Susano'o no Mikoto and Okuninushi no Kami. Every year on November 19th and 20th the well-known Ebisuko Festival is held at…

spots.name: Mechanical Dolls Performance
spots.desc: Kiryu is striving to preserve its cultural heritage by resurrecting old traditions that once served to create Kiryu's unique local color. One of these traditions is "Karakuri Ningyo" or mechanical dolls which were an integral part of Kiryu's festivals in days gone by. Kiryu is the only city in the country which has revived this great tradition, making mechanical doll performances a valuable…

spots.name: Honcho1, 2 chome District
spots.local: 本町1、2丁目地区（重伝建地区）
spots.desc: More than 400 years have passed since Ono Sonkichi laid out the plans for Kiryu Shin Machi and established the long avenue which has become the commercial center of Kiryu, Honcho Street. The first two districts, 1 and 2 chome, have many buildings whose classical architecture reveal the nostalgic past. A stroll along Honcho Street, beginning at Tenmangu Shrine will give you a wonderful idea of the…

spots.name: Gunma University Memorial Hall
spots.local: 群馬大学工学部同窓記念会館
spots.desc: Registered tangible cultural properties. Founded on March 15, 1916 as the Kiryu School of Weaving and Dyeing Technology, in the following year it became the Kiryu Technical High School. After many years, in 1944, the name was changed again to the Kiryu School of Technology. Finally, in 1949, it became the Faculty of Engineering of Gunma University and has continued in this capacity to the…

spots.name: Kiryu Performing Arts Center
spots.desc: The roof of the structure resembles the shape of a cocoon, recalling Kiryu's long history of silk manufacturing. Closed on Tuesday.

spots.name: Seki no Magaibutsu
spots.desc: Designated a Prefectural Important Cultural Asset on November 15, 1972. There are three engravings on a boulder near the foot of the Fudo Bridge over Kaburaki River in the Seki district. This boulder was formed by the accumulation of ash from lava flows from eruptions on Mt. Akagi. The boulder is 128 cm in height, 60 cm in width and 80 cm in depth. The Amida Buddha in the center stands for…

spots.name: Suidoyama Memorial Hall
spots.desc: The Suidoyama Kinenkan (Memorial Hall) was constructed in 1932 as the Kiryu Water Supply Office. The office reported to the Motojuku Purification Plant regarding standing water volume and level, contributing to the smooth operation of the water purification plant. During the 6th Expansion Project for upgrading electrical and water meter equipment, conducted between March and November, 1972, an…

spots.name: Ebisuko (festival)
spots.local: 桐生ゑびす講, kiryū ebisuko
spots.desc: An autumn festival focusing on the sale of "kumada" and "otakara" or good luck charms for merchants. Streets and the area around the shrine are lined with stalls selling these talismans along with festival food and souvenirs. It bustles with people and the sound of shopkeepers hawking their wares.

spots.name: Kiryugaoka Amusement Park
spots.local: 桐生が岡遊園地, kiryū-ga-oka yūenchi
spots.desc: Located next to Kiryugaoka Zoo. Attractions in the amusement park are geared toward younger children. Famous site for viewing cherry blossoms in spring.
spots.price: Free admission; separates fees for rides

spots.name: Tenmangu Antiques Flea Market
spots.local: 天満宮古民具骨董市, tenmangū komingu kottōichi
spots.desc: Antique dealers from all over the Kanto area converge on this site. Everything from kimono to antique ceramics and furniture is on sale.
spots.hours: 1st Sat of the month (special dates set for January, August & November)

spots.name: Kaiba Sayaichi Market
spots.desc: Open air market selling textiles and miscellaneous goods & handicrafts. During the Edo Era, a type of silk called “saya” became popular. As a result, the silk market that was established on the compound of Tenmangu Shrine was named the “Saya-ichi” or Saya market. Later, in 1883, a shopping street was established for the sale of local products and became known as “kaiba” or “shopping place, ” or…

spots.name: Niisato Festival
spots.desc: Yagibushi dancing and a firework display are the main attractions of this summer festival.

spots.name: Daruma Fair at Fumonji Temple
spots.local: だるま市, daruma-ichi ; 普門寺, fumon-ji
spots.desc: The annual Daruma Fair will take place on the third Sunday of January at Fumonji Temple. Parking lots available. This fair was started in Kiryu in 1964. The “Daruma” figure is said to bring good fortune, commercial success, household safety and protection from dangers and is sold at the many stalls along the streets in the vicinity of and entrance to the temple.

spots.name: Mikagari Ceremony at Kamojinja Shrine
spots.desc: The Mikagari Ceremony is held every year on February 3 at Kamo Shrine in Hirosawacho. The ceremony dates back to the Edo Period, during the 19th century. This ceremony is said to serve to protect the participants from evil during the coming year. Young men, dressed in white, undergo a purification rite, after which they throw beans, a custom carried out all over Japan as away to ward off evil…

spots.name: Azuma Park
spots.desc: Azuma Park is a serene escape from the busy outside world. Very quiet area. As the seasons come and go, the park takes on different aspects, offering a multitude of flowers and trees for visitors’ enjoyment. Parking lots available. Main flowering plants (tulips: about 12,000 bulbs, irises: about 350 rhizomes, cherry trees: about 500, Azaleas: about 5,000 bushes). There is a tea house in the park.…

spots.name: Kiryu Minami Park
spots.local: 桐生市南公園, kiryū-shi minami-kōen
spots.desc: Plum grove, lawn open space, play field, tennis court, baseball field, jogging course. Enough parking space.

spots.name: Fishing spots
spots.desc: Umeda Lake (Kiryu River Dam: rainbow trout, bass, lake smelt). Kiryu River (iwana trout, yamame trout). Watarase River (ayu trout, iwana trout). Kurohone River ravine fishing (bait/fly fishing) Iwana trout, Rainbow trout, etc.)

spots.name: Higiri Jizoson Festival at Kan'nonin Temple
spots.local: 観音院日限地蔵尊縁日
spots.desc: On the 24th of every month, there is a temple festival called Ennichi. Main street is closed to cars for this monthly temple festival, and there are many street stalls. This temple festival is very lively. Not only people from Kiryu but also people from Saitama and Tokyo visit this event every month. Even the normal day, smoke of the incense stick by the visitors does not cease. The devotion is…

spots.name: Seven Herbs Porridge Gathering (Nanakusa Gayu) at Sozenji Temple
spots.desc: On the 7th day of the New Year, it is a Japanese custom to eat a gruel made of rice with seven herbs as a protection for good health in the year to come. The seven herbs are: seri or water dropwort; nazuna or shepherd's purse; gogyo or cudweed; hakobera or chickweed; hotokenoza or nipplewort; suzuna or turnip; and suzushiro or daikon. You also can enjoy beautiful trees and flowers during a year.

spots.name: Public Tea Ceremony
spots.local: 茶道体験：吾妻公園茶室「悠緑庵」
spots.desc: The Kiryu Tea Ceremony Association conducts tea ceremonies "Tsukigama" on the third Sunday of every month. Everyone is welcome to participate. No prior reservations are required.

spots.name: Kobo Kazahana (handmade textile workshop)
spots.desc: Located in the Bakery Cafe RENGA. You can make your own original silk stall by using hand weaving machine. Closed on Tuesday.

spots.name: Kiryu Youth Outdoor Activities Center
spots.local: 桐生市青少年野外活動センター
spots.desc: The Kiryu Youth Outdoor Activities Center was constructed by Gunma Prefecture. It is located deep in the mountains in Umeda, the northernmost district of Kiryu. The facility includes indoor overnight accommodation for 130 persons, outdoor camping facilities for 100 persons, classrooms, a gymnasium/play hall, a cafeteria, and campfire facilities. Reservations can be made for groups of 3 and over…

spots.name: Tourism & Products Shop "Watarase"
spots.desc: Open year round. Items: textile products, Kinopi goods, foods (Udon, Snacks, Sweets etc.), etc.

spots.name: Kiryu Orimono Kinenkan
spots.desc: Closed the last Saturday and Sunday of the month. Items: textile products made in Kiryu (bag, necktie, obi, kimono, wallets, silk fabric, sell-phone charms, wall ornament)

spots.name: Kiryu Local Industries Promotion Centre
spots.local: 桐生地域地場産業振興センター
spots.desc: Closed during the New Year holiday. Items: textile products, Kinopi goods, foods (udon, sake, Shiitake mushroom, snacks, sweets), etc.

spots.name: Umeda Furusato Centre
spots.local: 梅田ふるさとセンター
spots.desc: Closed during the New Year holiday. Items: foods, small items

spots.name: Textile Museum Yukari
spots.desc: Also open when Monday is a national holiday. Items: textile calendar and other textile products.

spots.name: Kiryu Washi Workshop
spots.desc: Handmade washi papers (various size and purposes of papers). Residence of Hoshino family.

spots.name: Furukawa Udon Shop -Park Inn Kiryu
spots.local: ひもかわうどん：ふる川
spots.desc: Furukawa is considered the home of the extremely wide (over 15 cm) himokawa udon noodles. Gunma Prefecture is a producer of wheat, and there is a long tradition of eating wheat noodles. Some say the extra-wide noodles are reminiscent of the kimono obi produced in Kiryu over the years. Furukawa Aioi Branch is located in 2-735-15 Aioicho. 5-minute walk from Aioi station of Tobu Line and Watarase…

spots.name: Shitamiya Honten
spots.local: ソースかつどん：志多美屋本店
spots.desc: Sauce Katsudon is by far Kiryu's most famous dish. While the name "souce katsudon" is used elsewhere, the popular flavor loved by locals is unique to Kiryu. There are restaurants in Kiryu specializing in this local favorite.
spots.hours: Fri-Wed 11:00-14:00; 17:00-20:00. Closed 3rd Fri of each month

spots.name: Kororin Shumai
spots.desc: The steamed dumpling-like shumai are then seasoned with a Worchestershire-like flavored sauce and topped off with some nori (dried seaweed) flakes. Closed on Mondays.

spots.name: Restaurant Chocolat Noix
spots.desc: French restaurant, Tu-Su lunch from 11:30, dinner from 17:00.

spots.name: Umeda Furusato Center
spots.local: 梅田ふるさとセンター
spots.desc: The Umeda Furusato Center sells many locally produced items. In particular, it is well known for its handmade soba and udon noodles. The noodles are served in the small dining area, where guests can relax and enjoy the beautiful natural surroundings. In addition to the dining room, there is a shop where locally produced items, including cucumbers, eggplant, tomatoes, fresh shiitake mushrooms…

spots.name: Kuri Manju (Fujikakeya)
spots.desc: These chestnut-shaped manju (cake buns) are filled with red bean paste. These extremely popular manju are available at the Fujikakeya Kuri Manju shop in Nishikicho, Kiryu. Closed on Tuesday.

spots.name: BUDDHA Indian cuisine
spots.desc: Closed on the second Wednesday and last Wednesday of every month.

spots.name: Sauce Katsudon Fujiya Shokudo
spots.desc: Sauce Katsudon is one of the Kiryu's specializing cuisine. Closed on Monday and 2nd Tuesday.

spots.name: Uotami
spots.desc: A large Japanese-style chain izakaya with a wide range of seafood and other snacks to go with an equally wide range of drinks, including regional sakes. Extensive picture menus for both food and drink, but not much English. Small bottles of sake run about ¥500 to ¥800, snacks start from about ¥250, with many choices in the range of ¥350–650.

spots.name: 1000人Rock Fes.Gunma
spots.desc: Shibukawa hosts this annual "Rock Festival" that's modeled after the Rockin'1000 project of Italy. If you are a vocalist, guitarist, bassist, or drummer, you can take part in a massive performance together with 999 newfound friends. Preparations to participate need to be made well in advance and might not be the easiest if you don't speak some Japanese, but spectators are allowed and just need to…

spots.name: Ganden-ji
spots.desc: Number 2 in a series of temples, Bandō 33 Temple Pilgrimage, dedicated to the Goddess Kannon. Ganden-ji was founded in the year 721 and is surrounded by green hills.

spots.name: Hiroyama Park
spots.desc: Panoramic view of Sea (Sagami Bay) and mountains around the area, including Mt. Fuji. There is a mini-zoo, with monkeys and small animals (free), and a small playground. There is also a hiking course from the north end of the beach (ask locals).

spots.name: Hisagi Ooike Park
spots.desc: A pond is surrounded by lush greenery and is a haven for water plants and wild birds.

spots.name: Jinmuji Temple
spots.desc: Another old temple (724 CE), surrounded by lush hills. There are many nice hiking courses nearby.

spots.name: Kotsubo
spots.desc: A small fishing village with views of Mount Fuji and summer Ayu Festival.

spots.name: Osaki Park
spots.desc: A similar view of Hiroyama Koen, but further away with fewer facilities. Fewer visitors come here.

spots.name: Zushi Beach
spots.desc: A crescent-shaped beach about a couple kilometers long. Mt. Fuji is visible on a clear day from the south end of the beach. Has a pleasant atmosphere in the off-season with people flying kites, walking their dogs, or windsurfing in the bay. In the summer (the end of June-the end of August), it becomes a swimming beach and is a host to a number of beach houses, which feature food and drinks, and…

spots.name: Napoli Pizzeria Cantina
spots.desc: Kanagawa-ken Zushi-shi, Shinjuku 1-3-15, 046-870-6440. 11:00-23:00. Large Italian restaurant with ocean and Fuji views. Pizza is made in a wood stove (specialty is Quattro Formaggi). Lunch sets are much cheaper than dinner and served quite late.

spots.name: Cinema Amigo
spots.desc: Set in a small old Japanese house with a nice atmosphere, it has a different chef everyday of the week serving meals (Japanese, Italian, Indian) with fresh ingredients. Lunches are usually about ¥1,000. Other times of the day, they play films (documentaries or art films) for ¥1,500, including a drink.

spots.name: Sushi-Ichiba Rikuzen
spots.desc: Fuji Bldg. 1F, 2-1-37 Yatsu (1 minute walk from Ageo Station).

spots.name: Hijiri Shrine
spots.desc: The large wado kaichin coins are the stand-out features of this shrine. The wado kaichin is known as Japan's first standardized coin.

spots.name: Chichibu Shrine
spots.desc: An old shrine with colorful ornate carvings commissioned by Tokugawa Ieyasu. If it reminds you of Toshogu Shrine in Nikko, it's because the same sculptor was hired for both. The shrine hosts the famous Chichibu Night Festival every December (see "Do").

spots.name: Hitsujiyama Park
spots.desc: A large park known for its shibazakura (phlox flowers) that bloom in the late spring.

spots.name: Oomura
spots.desc: This is a friendly soba restaurant. They also have very delicious tonkatsu pork cutlets. The mimosa salad is very good and has a lot of fried shrimp on it.

spots.name: LalaPort Shin Misato
spots.desc: This large shopping mall, housing 300 specialty shops, as well as cultural facilities, sports facilities, and other conveniences.

spots.name: Costco
spots.desc: Costco is the largest membership warehouse club chain in the United States.

spots.name: Ashikaga Machinaka Yūgakkan
spots.desc: This "play-learn" emporium not only exhibits locally made textiles and actual working looms and braiding and threading machines, it also offers weaving lessons on small handlooms. ¥400 per lesson (30-45 minutes).
spots.hours: Daily 09:00-17:00; closed 3rd Mon every month and at year end

spots.name: Coco Farm and Winery
spots.desc: Founded in 1950 as a boarding school for underachieving kids, it gradually evolved into a self-supporting vineyard, produced its first wine in 1980, established ties with Sonoma vineyards, then hired a California vintner, and provided the sparkling wine for the G7 summit in Okinawa in 2000. Per-glass prices range from ¥300 to ¥1000, with a variety of hors d'oeuvres at a similar range of…
spots.hours: Gift shop open daily 09:30 to 17:30; cafe open daily 11:00 to 16:00; winery tours at 11:00, 13:00, 15:00; closed 31…

spots.name: Kappō Kaiseki Chō-ya
spots.local: 割烹 会席 蝶や
spots.desc: A nice, unpretentious place to indulge in a leisurely Japanese kaiseki (multicourse "tasting menu") dinner, or a fine teishoku (one-tray set-menu) meal. Teishoku ¥1350–2000; kaiseki ¥4500, ¥5500; ¥6500.

spots.name: Santa Tori Maruyaki
spots.desc: This izakaya restaurant specializes in rotisserie chicken and relatively healthy side dishes. The sage and thyme on the rotisserie chicken was a delightful surprise, and so were the fulsome salads. Japanese-style seating except at the counter. Drinks by the glass include local wine (Coco Farms) and a fine Oyama sake (鳳凰美田 Hōōbiden) for about ¥500. Full chicken ¥1000, half ¥650…

spots.name: Southwest Paradise
spots.desc: A little bit of New Mexico in old Ashikaga. Various pasta or taco dinners ¥1280; drinks about ¥500; snacks about ¥400.

spots.name: Suzu Okonomiyaki
spots.desc: Run by a friendly, well-traveled couple whose souvenirs decorate the small but spotless restaurant. You choose your ingredients and cook okonomiyaki, monja, yakisoba, or other items at teppan tables. Typical menu items range between ¥400 and ¥800.
spots.hours: Sat Sun 12:00-21:30, Thu Fri Mon Tue 13:00-21:30

spots.name: Tonkatsu Sakae
spots.desc: (memory-aid: o-i-shi-i). This busy, family-run local favorite displays the Ashikaga Fine-Dining Club (Umaimono-kai) seal of approval and serves up food that well deserves it. The chicken katsu is all breast meat, no skin, no fat. Their fried oysters are great, too. Set-menu dinners run from ¥950-1900.

spots.name: Tori-tsune
spots.desc: This local favorite for 70 years offers a range of specialties, from yakitori sticks at ¥500 to a full unagi (eel) dinner at ¥2700.

spots.name: Uoe
spots.desc: Hosted by a friendly sushi chef who trained in San Francisco and Maui and understands a lot more English than he speaks, this longtime seafood restaurant in fresh new digs features fine fresh fish and regional sake, all presented creatively and deliciously. Lunch specials from ¥800; set-menu dinners from ¥1200; glasses of regional sake range from ¥450 to ¥950.

spots.name: Café de Furukawa
spots.desc: Founded in 1975 and run by a middle-aged couple who roast their own beans and make their own blends, Furukawa caters to those who want to savor their coffee while reading, listening to classical music, or conversing softly in an elegant, library-like atmosphere. No smoking, cell-phones, laptops, or cameras. A cup of coffee costs about ¥600.

spots.name: Cafe Mocha
spots.desc: Founded in 1974 and run by a father and his two sons who roast their own beans and make their own blends ranging from soft to bitter, Mocha is family-friendly, conversation-friendly, and smoker-friendly. The background music is most likely to be jazz. A cup of coffee costs about ¥450.

spots.name: Izakaya Shōhei
spots.desc: Specialty snacks include various udon, donburi, and curry dishes for ¥600-800, horse sashimi (ba-sashi) for ¥1200, and giant umeboshi for ¥100 each. The beer of choice is Sapporo and the cold sake is Akagi, at ¥500-800, depending on size.

spots.name: Le Vent Vert
spots.desc: Founded in 1995 but reopened in the new city museum in 2006. A cup of coffee costs about ¥500.

spots.name: Yakitori-kun
spots.desc: A well-known hangout for neighborhood regulars throughout the week, and for English teachers and other foreigners on weekends and on Wednesdays when most other small eateries and drinking spots take their regular day off. In warmer weather, tables appear on the sidewalk in front of the small stand.

spots.name: Yanagi-ya
spots.desc: This is a combination fresh seafood restaurant, izakaya, and sports bar, especially for fans of the Hanshin Tigers (and sumo). All the sake glasses, even those for Tiger sake, have the names of sumo wrestlers on them. The dishes are well presented and tasty, but there is no English or picture menu. Just ask for the day's specials (osusume) or point to the more reasonably priced items on the wall…

spots.name: Heart and Roses
spots.desc: A relaxed, small bar great for having a chat. The atmosphere is rich and warm and the bartender is friendly and speaks English. Prices range such that one can spend as much or as little as they like. Food menu varies depending on availability but is always good. Frequented by the local foreign English speakers on weekends for central location, pleasant atmosphere and lack of table charge.
spots.hours: Mon-Sat 21:00-02:00, closed on holidays (except Golden Week)
spots.addr: Isecho, ichi chome 2-1 ryoumo building 1F (伊勢町１丁目２−１ 1F)

spots.name: Furumine Shrine
spots.desc: Established by monk Shodo Shonin, the Furumine Shrine is dedicated to Prince Yamatotakeru, a mythological hero whose messengers in the form of long-nosed goblins, known as tengu, have been worshipped. In the main building, over 200 masks of tengu are on display. At the large room of the front shrine, there are 2 tengu masks which make up a length of 1.5 meters.

spots.name: Mori no VoiVoi
spots.desc: This pancake house serves western-style pancakes. It also serves waffles and hard-to-find smoked bacon. The building is a sort of imitation log cabin — beams are used instead of logs — which creates a friendly atmosphere.

spots.name: Yuzen-ya
spots.desc: A foreigner-friendly, family-friendly, and family-run izakaya that serves up an impressive variety of tasty meals, appetizers, and drinks.

spots.name: Shiroyama Park
spots.desc: Known as one of the city's symbol by Sano citizen. Famous spot for sakura and azalea, this park is always packed with visitors especially during peak viewing seasons in spring. Closed on M, 2nd Th of the month.

spots.name: Ume Garden
spots.desc: 140 white-blossomed and 80 red-blossomed plum trees. There are also sakura and azalea trees planted in the garden.

spots.name: Mt.Hourai
spots.desc: Mt. Hourai has flourished as a holy place. A promenade is provided for pedestrians. Seasonal nature is beautiful, especially colored leaves in autumn.

spots.name: Izuruhara Benten Ike Lake
spots.desc: Filled with carp swimming gracefully, Izuruhara Benten Ike was formed when water welled up from the limestone layer. the cleanliness of the water makes this lake one of the top 100 clearest waters in Japan's ranking.

spots.name: Sano Yakuyoke Daishi Temple
spots.desc: 'Yaku' means misfortune; 'yoke' means protection; 'taishi' means monk. Over 1 million worshippers come, especially during New Year Festival, pray for their own safety. Daily open.

spots.name: Kuzu Fossil Museum
spots.desc: Approximately 550 specimens (fossils, rocks and minerals), mostly from Kuzu (Sano City), from the exhibit of this museum. Closed on: M, day after a holiday.

spots.name: Yoshizawa Memorial Art Gallery
spots.desc: Displaying a lot of Japanese art painting and pottery art from Edo era. Closed on:Mon, Next day of holiday, Year-end and Nwe Year.

spots.name: Sano City Museum
spots.desc: From clay pot warrior flag, many relics associated with region are displayed. Closed on: M, day after a holiday, last day of month, New Year's Eve and New Year's Day.

spots.name: Strawberry Picking (Agritown)
spots.local: いちご狩り(アグリタウン)
spots.desc: Sano is one of the famous places growing Tochiotome strawberries. Fresh and tasty strawberries are available directly from farms.Reservation are preferable. Closed on:Jun-Nov (strawberry picking)

spots.name: Hikoma Japanese Paper Hall
spots.desc: Experience making Japanese Hikoma paper that has a long tradition and history. Closed on: M F. Reservation required, Paper making ¥200.

spots.name: Indigo Dyeing
spots.desc: (藍染) Experience dyeing your own handkerchief or even hijab! Very old and traditional way of indigo dyeing passed on from centuries ago in Japan.

spots.name: Yomogiyama Log Village
spots.desc: Outdoor recreation spot equipped with a cottage, bathhouse, tennis court, and playground equipment made from logwood. Accommodation facility is also provided. Closed on:Tuesday Reservation required:Hotel charges ¥10,800.

spots.name: Akiyama Hostels, Morisawa Woodland ＆ Ancient Times Village
spots.desc: (あきやま学寮、ウッドランド森沢、古代生活体験村）Multi-purpose accommodation facilities that are suitable for families or groups. Besides staying in a real log house, this hostel also provides a multi-purpose hall, training rooms, large indoor bath, barbeque house and the Akiyamaga Restaurant to be used for various purposes. Log houses are surrounded by a forest located at the bank of the Morisawa River. Enjoy the crisp…

spots.name: Sano City Kodomo no Kuni
spots.desc: The thems of children's park are adventure, creation, and discovery. Closed on Mon,2nd Thur.

spots.name: Sano Premium Outlets
spots.local: 佐野プレミアム・アウトレット
spots.desc: Approximately 170 stores of famous international and Japanese brands. Modeled after a town on the east coast of the United States. Closed on 3rd Thursday in Feb.

spots.name: Michi No Eki Domannaka Tanuma
spots.local: 道の駅どまんなかたぬま
spots.desc: A lot of Sano specialties are available and other delicious cuisines. 'Ashiyu'(foodbath) originating from the Tanuma Hotspring for free is also available. Illuminations at night during winter. Closed on Wednesday.

spots.name: Sano City Kanko Bussan Kaikan
spots.desc: As center of souvenirs of the city, this store has 800 items made in Sano. Daily open.

spots.name: Nissan Factory
spots.desc: Visit the factory where Nissans and Infinitis are made (including the GT-R).

spots.name: Toki-no-irodori
spots.local: 稲城天然温泉 季乃彩「ときのいろどり」
spots.desc: Day-bathing natural onsen facility known for its iwaburo (岩風呂, rock-bath) outside stone bath with free-flowing onsen water from the source. Has a restaurant, too.

spots.name: Ginza Blossom
spots.desc: This theater hosts a variety of different events. See the website for a partial listing.
spots.price: Cost varies by event and seating

spots.name: Tōkyō Kyūkyodō
spots.desc: Located right across the street from Wako and its landmark clock tower on Ginza's main intersection, this two-floor shop specializes in the traditional Japanese paraphernalia (papers, fans, calligraphy brushes, votive scents etc.). A popular stop for foreigners in search for something exotic and genuine.

spots.name: Itōya
spots.desc: Beside the huge Matsuya department store, which is beside the huge Mitsukoshi department store (both being prestigious and expensive), which in turn is across the street from Wako. A 9-floor building packed with all things stationery, from pencils to paintbrushes, you name it. Not exactly discount price considering its location and prestige, but a stationery shop with a collection of this size is…

spots.name: Hakuhinkan Toy Park
spots.desc: One of the oldest and largest toy stores in Japan (it first opened in 1899), this is the place to go for all the latest cute and strange toys.

spots.name: Apple Store Ginza
spots.desc: Easily recognized by its ultra-modern stainless steel paneled exterior.

spots.name: Tenshōdō
spots.desc: Jeweler and maker of luxury watches. The upper floors, however, are devoted to model trains, many of which match the watches in intricacy and price.

spots.name: Mikimoto
spots.desc: The inventors of cultured pearls, has their inaugural shop located right next to Wako.

spots.name: Morioka Shoten
spots.desc: A tiny bookstore in a quiet street, it is unique and strange since it sells only one book that changes every week. Authors of the featured book sometimes come in to discuss about it.

spots.name: Yoshinoya
spots.desc: One of a nationwide chain of rice bowl restaurants, the Ginza location is just north of the Apple Store on Chuo-dori.

spots.name: Mitsukoshi and Matsuya Ginza's
spots.desc: Basement floors offer a variety of foods at a reasonable price. Food ranges from pre-made bentos to bakeries to sandwich shops. You can also get a quick snack at no cost by trying the various samples that are offered. There are no areas to sit and eat and unless you can get a table on Chuo-dori on the weekend, you may have trouble eating the meals you've purchased.

spots.name: Nair's
spots.desc: The oldest Indian restaurant in Japan, founded in 1949. The Murghee lunch is a favorite: sit back and let the waiter cut up the chicken for you on your plate.

spots.name: Nataraj
spots.desc: A terrific Indian vegetarian restaurant in the midst of Ginza, offering an excellent lunch buffet for ¥1050, and beautiful decor as well.

spots.name: Chikuyōtei
spots.desc: The original store of Japan's best known unagi (eel) restaurant chain, serving up luscious kabayaki (grilled eel with sauce) since 1876. Full courses start from ¥7350 and climb up to twice that (reservations required), but a basic unadon with soup is an almost reasonable ¥2,625.

spots.name: Ginza Shiseido Parlour
spots.desc: Operated by the cosmetics giant Shiseido, the Parlour (founded 1902) is one of the swankiest places for Japanese-style Western food. Lunch specials go for ¥4,000, but the most famous item on the menu is the lobster and abalone curry for ¥10,000.
spots.addr: Shiseido Bldg 4-5F, Ginza 8-8-3, and several other nearby locations

spots.name: Sushi Kanesaka
spots.desc: The main branch of one of Japan's premier sushi restaurants with two Michelin stars, with another branch at the Palace Hotel, as well as two outposts in Singapore. Sushi is prepared fresh for you at the counter while you watch. Ordering dishes individually is not allowed, and the chef would select what he thinks are the best seasonal ingredients for customers. The restaurant is very small with…

spots.name: Sukiyabashi Jiro
spots.desc: This three Michelin star restaurant and its owner/chef, Jiro Ono, were immortalized in the 2011 documentary Jiro Dreams of Sushi. The highly expensive course is omakase only - Jiro himself selects 20 nigiri pieces daily based on that day's catch from the Tsukiji fish market. You are not expected to use soy sauce, as many pieces are already brushed with it. The restaurant only has ten counter…
spots.hours: 11:30-14:00, 17:30-20:30 (Closed Sat evenings, Sundays, public holidays, New Year's holiday and mid-August)

spots.name: Ginza Cafe Paulista
spots.desc: One of the oldest cafes in Japan and a favorite of John Lennon and Yoko Ono, the Paulista opened in 1909 with beans imported directly from Santos, Brazil.

spots.name: Meiji Shrine
spots.desc: Tokyo's grandest Shinto shrine, built in 1920 to commemorate the late Emperor Meiji, who oversaw Japan's rapid industrialization and rise to major world power status in the 19th and early 20th centuries. Like all of Japan's major shrines, it's large in scale but simple in structure, entered via a winding path and through a giant torii gate. On summer weekends you have a very good chance of…

spots.name: Yoyogi Park
spots.desc: In springtime, Yoyogi Park is full of cherry blossoms and people partying under the trees. Due to massive littering, park administration has designed trash collection points. The later evening gets, the more intoxicated some party people may be.

spots.name: Tōgō Jinja
spots.desc: This shrine was established for Admiral Tōgō Heihachirō, after his victory at the naval battle of Tsushima in 1905.

spots.name: Kiddy Land
spots.desc: A huge toy store on Omote-sandō, near the entrance to Cat Street.

spots.name: Laforet Harajuku
spots.desc: A large shopping mall owned by the same company that runs Omotesando Hills, but targeting a decidedly younger audience. In summer and winter, they have big sales.

spots.name: Omotesando Hills
spots.desc: Designed by Tadao Ando and built by Mori Building of Roppongi Hills fame, this is a super-chic shopping mall that caters to those "independent, style-conscious urbanites" (to quote the site) who couldn't possibly wear anything except the latest fashions or eat chocolates not prepared by a famous Parisian patissier. For the rest of us, it's still an interesting browse, and the restaurants on the…

spots.name: Oriental Bazaar
spots.desc: A kitschy Tokyo institution for tourists and expats alike, with four floors of shopping stocking everything from kamikaze T-shirts to foreigner-sized kimono. Still, this is definitely the easiest way to get your souvenir shopping done. The Bazaar is housed in an instantly recognizable building with a faux-Chinese temple roof.

spots.name: YM Square
spots.desc: Known for its two big used clothes shops: Kinji and Hanjiro.

spots.name: Tokyu Plaza Harajuku Harakado
spots.local: 東急プラザ原宿「ハラカド」
spots.desc: It is a shopping complex located in Harajuku. It features a bathhouse underground.

spots.name: Tenya
spots.desc: This fast-food tempura chain has an outlet on Meiji-dori just to the north of the Meiji-dori/Omote-sandō intersection.

spots.name: Kebab Box J
spots.desc: Whereas most doner kebabs in Tokyo are served out of a van, Kebab Box J's store is firmly attached to the ground. Friendly staff wear cowboy hats.

spots.name: Kyushu Jangara
spots.desc: One of the best-known tonkotsu ramen shops in Tokyo, where you can choose between five degrees of noodle thickness, three levels of soup texture, and three levels of soup fattiness.

spots.name: Sakuratei
spots.desc: A great Okonomiyaki restaurant where many local artists work.
spots.price: An all you can eat course is around ¥1300 for 2 hours

spots.name: Arms Burger
spots.desc: This small, Americana-inspired eatery is nestled right off the main footpath, and serves lots of Western food, including a wide burger selection (try the avocado burger!) Also serves fries, chili dogs, and other non-Japanese fare. American beer selection available. The place fills up pretty fast, so swing by before a stroll in Yoyogi and put your name in it.

spots.name: JS Burgers Cafe
spots.desc: Clean, bright, upmarket burger chain. A set meal of burger, fries and a drink costs around ¥1200. The thick chilli sauce is recommended.

spots.name: Eggs N' Things
spots.desc: American-style all-day breakfast joint from Hawaii. Eggs served every way imaginable - pancakes, Eggs Benedict, with sausage, etc. Wildly popular at lunchtime, with lines backing down the street, so go early or late (possibly after 19:00).

spots.name: R/O-426
spots.desc: Small burger and beer joint with the kitchen housed inside a small, Airstream trailer. Outdoor patio seating just above a small walkway where you can watch wannabe models and photographers capture bright-eyed moments in the afternoon sun.

spots.name: Cafe Studio
spots.desc: This restaurant/cafe often holds events including guest speakers and live shows. The hamburger menu is popular.

spots.name: Fonda de la Madrugada
spots.desc: Located in a cavernous basement, Fonda de la Madrugada is regarded as one of the best Mexican restaurants in Tokyo. Menu in English, Spanish and Japanese.
spots.price: Expect to pay around ¥5000 per person for food and drinks, plus a 10% service charge

spots.name: Fuji TV Building
spots.desc: An Odaiba landmark which looks like it's built of tinkertoys. The studio tour is of limited interest unless you speak Japanese and/or are familiar with Fuji's programming, but you can visit the second-highest story for free for some nice views.
spots.price: Going to the observatory usually costs ¥500

spots.name: Giant Gundam robot
spots.desc: An impressive 1:1 scale robot from the Gundam animation series. A must-see if you are passing by.

spots.name: Miraikan
spots.desc: Japan's National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation, created by Japan's Science and Technology Agency. As the name indicates new technologies like robots, space modules etc. are presented here as well as demonstrations and physical experiments for the inquiring mind are given.

spots.name: Museum of Maritime Science
spots.local: 船の科学館 Fune no kagakukan
spots.desc: It was a six-story museum shaped like a full-sized ocean liner. Being the oldest significant building on Odaiba, demolition of the main building started in February 2024. Now only Sōya, the first polar explorer ship for Japan (and WWII veteran, still in active use for training purposes!) can be seen.

spots.name: Odaiba Statue of Liberty
spots.desc: Small scale replica of the Statue of Liberty from New York City given to Japan to commemorate its ties with France. It is set against a backdrop of the Tokyo Tower, Tokyo Bay, and the Rainbow Bridge.

spots.name: Odaiba Marine Park
spots.local: お台場海浜公園, Odaiba Kaihin Kōen
spots.desc: Features one of two beaches in mainland Tokyo, but swimming is forbidden and not recommended anyway as the water is rather polluted. Along the beach runs a boardwalk dotted with couples, as this is considered the most romantic spot in Tokyo. The park also contains a copy of the Statue of Liberty, more popular than one might think. Have a picnic on Dai-San Daiba (第三台場 No. 3 Battery), nearby and…

spots.name: Shiokaze Park
spots.desc: Next to Nikkō and Le Meridien hotels this park is the largest in the area. The southern corner, close to the ventilation tower of the highway, features a barbecue place highly popular during the warmer season. Barbecue equipment and tools as well as ingredients available for rent, reservation may be required during main seasons (see phone number). The park farther to the south is Higashi-yashio…

spots.name: Immersive Fort Tokyo
spots.local: イマーシブ・フォート東京
spots.desc: World's first theme park on immersive experiences. Opened in March 2024.

spots.name: Decks Tokyo Beach
spots.desc: Features the Sega Joypolis gaming center (10:00-23:00), retro-themed arcade, a 1960s-style store, gift shops, 2nd-hand western clothing stores, fine home accessories.

spots.name: Aqua City Odaiba
spots.desc: Fashion for all ages, goods, etc. Restaurants in 4th, 5th, and 6th floors and a food court in the 1st floor. There is also a Toys'R'Us (including baby foods and goods, and children can touch and play with the toys there!) on 1F, and a small Shinto shrine on 9F.
spots.hours: 11:00-21:00 (including 1Fri food court), restaurants till 23:00 though some bars until early morning

spots.name: Wanza Ariake Bay Mall
spots.local: ワンザ有明ベイモール
spots.desc: Restaurants and a few shops north of the Tokyo Big Sight exhibition center.

spots.name: Sendai Nuclear Power Plant Museum
spots.local: 九州電力（株） 川内原子力発電所展示館
spots.desc: It is a museum on nuclear power generation run by Kyushu Electric Power Co.

spots.name: Sendai History Museum
spots.local: 薩摩川内市川内歴史資料館
spots.desc: It is a museum that informs the history of Satsumasendai City, and you can see the history from about 20,000 years ago to the present.

spots.name: Iriki-Fumoto Samurai Residences
spots.local: 入来麓武家屋敷群（薩摩川内市入来麓 重要伝統的建造物群保存地区）
spots.desc: It is a village where the places where samurai lived during the Satsuma period were preserved.

spots.name: Imutaike Prefectural Nature Park
spots.local: 藺牟田池県立自然公園
spots.desc: Imutaike Lake Park is a crater lake created by volcanic activity about 400,000 years ago. It was listed as a ramsar wetland in 2005.

spots.name: Sendai Space Hall
spots.local: 薩摩川内市せんだい宇宙館
spots.desc: Sendai Space Museum is an observatory and science museum located at the top of the Terayama Prefectural Natural Park in Satsumasendai City.

spots.name: Kacchū-koubō Marutake (Samurai armor studio)
spots.desc: It is a facility that makes armor for Japanese samurai, and you can watch the armor and tour the workshop.

spots.name: Satsuma Kokubunji Ruins
spots.local: 国指定史跡 薩摩国分寺跡
spots.desc: It was the place where Japanese temples were built around the 8th century, and only the site remains now. It is now used as a park.

spots.name: Nitta Shrine
spots.desc: It is the number one shrine in the region during the Satsuma State period.

spots.name: Maenohira Observatory
spots.desc: It is an observatory where you can see the sea and Napoleon rocks.

spots.name: Marunaka Hirasa-ten
spots.desc: It sells a variety of food and daily necessities to the supermarket.

spots.name: Hujino Sobaya
spots.desc: It is a famous soba restaurant. It also sells a variety of desserts using buckwheat noodles.

spots.name: Ishibashiri Ramen
spots.desc: Old Ramen shop. Selling Donkotsu Ramen and Miso Ramen for cheap.

spots.name: Ichibankan
spots.local: 黒豚とんかつ 壱番館
spots.desc: It is a store that sells tonkatsu made of black pork, a specialty of Kagoshima Prefecture.

spots.name: Coffee Funakura
spots.desc: Kitsaten sells a wide variety of coffee. It also sells a wide variety of desserts.

spots.name: Shuan Tomo
spots.desc: It is izakaya, which sells dishes using various specialties such as black pork shabu-shabu and sweet potato soju.

spots.name: Space Museum, Tanegashima Space Center
spots.desc: Japan's largest spaceport. Free exhibits and guided tours three times daily (reservations required). No entry during launch days, but there are designated viewing points around the perimeter.
spots.hours: Daily 09:30-17:00, Jul-Aug 09:30-17:30; closed Mon-Tue after long weekends and Dec 29-Jan 1

spots.name: Chikura Caverns
spots.desc: White sand beach with caves that can be entered at low tide. There are picnic tables at the edge of the beach. There are a couple food stands and drink machines.

spots.name: Takezaki Observation Stand and Beach
spots.desc: Prominent platform with a great view of the launch site; great for launch days. Long, white sand beach with areas for snorkeling close to the east side. Restroom with changing area and place to rinse feet is available beside the free parking area. Covered picnic tables nearby on lawn of space center.

spots.name: Cape Kadokura
spots.desc: Cape overlooking the rocks and shore where the first firearms entered Japan. Beautiful view. There is a lookout post shaped like an old ship. A small shrine is nearby. Restrooms available beside the free parking area.

spots.name: Ebinoe-tenbo Park
spots.local: 恵美之江（えびのえ）展望公園
spots.desc: A beautiful vantage point over cliffs, with a near-perfect view of the TNSC Launch Complex. The park also makes for a great place to see the stars or the morning sun. The linked page lists four officially designated observation sites in all.
spots.addr: Japan, 〒891-3702 Kagoshima, Kumage District, Minamitane, Hirayama, 長小田1352-27

spots.name: Komezuka
spots.desc: A nice small volcano cone to see on the way. It erupted 3000 years ago and now stands 80 meters high, with a perfectly symmetric shape. Climbing it is forbidden, in order to protect its cute green slopes.

spots.name: Kojirō-buchi
spots.desc: Friendly, reasonably-priced restaurant. Most dishes involve cooking your own meat using a fire in the centre of the table. Generous portions.

spots.name: Yatsushiro Castle
spots.desc: Ruins of the castle are located in the center of the city, by the torrent of the Kuma River

spots.name: 777 Steps
spots.desc: Visible from National Route 3 are 777 steps leading up the mountain. With markers detailing your progress up and rest benches and gazebos along the way, the stone steps are a good place to get some exercise and be rewarded at the top with a great view of the city.

spots.name: Myōken-sai
spots.desc: This is a really exciting autumn festival on Labor Thanksgiving Day (November 23).

spots.name: Nightlife Alley
spots.desc: Located alongside the city's shopping arcade, this main road hosts Shidax, many bars, and snack bars. Smaller roads branch from the Alley, letting you explore even more bars.

spots.name: Gassan Hiwa Castle
spots.desc: A former castle that was reconstructed using Inuyama Castle as its model. It operates as the Takajo Historic Museum (高城町郷土資料館).

spots.name: Miyakonojo Shimazu Residence
spots.desc: Former residence of the local lord with a preserved residence, storehouses, garden and more. Many of the lord's possessions are on display.

spots.name: Imari Nabeshima-yaki Gallery
spots.desc: Gallery and shop for Nabeshima ceramicware. Its restaurant serves everything on distinctive blue dishes.

spots.name: Niji no Matsubara
spots.desc: This pine forest was planted by the feudal lord Terasawa as a counter-measure against the strong winds and tides in Karatsu Bay. It stretches for 4 km along the coast and is one of Karatsu's most well-known tourist attractions. It's possible to access by bicycle from central Karatsu, but take care when riding on the road, especially at night.

spots.name: Nanatsu-Gama
spots.desc: Also in Minato is this group of seven caves, formed by the tumultuous Genkai Sea. Accessible by bus, with a bit of a walk from the main road.

spots.name: Tategami-Iwa
spots.desc: Located in the town of Minato, a scenic group of standing rocks along the coast. Can be accessed by bus.

spots.name: Nagoya Castle Ruins
spots.desc: Not to be confused with Nagoya Castle in Nagoya, this castle was the launching point for invasions of Korea during the Sengoku Period. Today the castle walls are all that remain. It's still pretty nice, and there's a modern museum on-site.

spots.name: Takashima
spots.desc: Not to be confused with the nearby Takashima (鷹島) in Nagasaki prefecture, this island in Karatsu Bay is dominated by a large hill, and is accessible by a ferry that leaves from the jetty near Karatsu Castle. There's a small village on the island with some picturesque little garden plots, as well as a shrine thought to bring luck in winning the lottery. It's possible to climb the hill to its…

spots.name: Udono Sekibutsu Statues
spots.desc: A cave of stone Buddha carvings. It is said that the famous priest Kukai stopped here after returning from China.

spots.name: Hikiyama Exhibition Hall
spots.desc: The floats of the famous Karatsu Kunchi Festival are all on display here everday except during the festival. They have informative English descriptions about each float, what it is, when it was made, and sometimes why it was chosen to be a float.

spots.name: Karatsu Burger
spots.desc: A food truck found along Route 202 in Niji no Matsubara, this local favorite serves up burgers, drinks, and nothing else. There's another one along Route 23 in Iwano on the way to Genkai.

spots.name: Funny
spots.desc: Located in Nanayama, this gem offers Bass ale on tap, and a number of delicious, pita-based dishes (among other things), as well as an impressive record and CD collection on display. Sadly, the owner passed away in 2020, but his widow and daughter still run the place. Highly recommended (if you can make it up to Nanayama, that is).
spots.addr: 佐賀県東松浦郡七山村大字滝川540-2

spots.name: Satobu Cafe
spots.desc: A Peruvian restaurant with good food and very friendly owners.

spots.name: Masala Master
spots.desc: A quality Indian restaurant just 2 minutes from Watada Station.

spots.name: Yobuko Manbō
spots.local: 呼子萬坊, also called Kaichū Restaurant (海中レストラン, "Restaurant in the Sea")
spots.desc: Japan's first restaurant that floats in the sea. A standard course of squid runs ¥2625, or splurge and get the three flavor course (squid, tai, and hamachi) for ¥3900 (but with half as much squid).
spots.hours: Mon-Fri 11:00-19:00, Sat Sun 10:30-20:00, open until 21:00 from Jul 21-Aug 31; last order 1 hour before closing

spots.name: Castle Mountain
spots.local: キャッスル・マウンテン
spots.desc: If you've run out of regular bar options, you can always try a hostess/"snack" bar. This one tends to be the most interesting; the employees don't seem to bat an eye when the drunk salarymen start whipping their shirts off and dancing on tables.

spots.name: Himeyuri Peace Museum
spots.local: ひめゆり平和祈念資料館, himeyuri heiwa kinen shiryōkan
spots.desc: Students from two girls' schools, together called Himeyuri, were mobilized to work as field nurses during the Battle of Okinawa in 1945. This memorial museum documents, from a personal perspective, their lives before and during the battle, in which many of them died. Exhibits are labeled in English. The museum gives voice to the victims and provides real stories and faces that help give the…

spots.name: Gushikawa Castle Ruins
spots.desc: Quiet ruins near Cape Kyan. It is unknown who built the castle, but excavation results indicate it was used from the end of the 12th century to the mid-15th century.

spots.name: Peace Park
spots.desc: This park has a beautiful view overlooking the ocean, and features several open-air memorials including the Cornerstone of Peace, wave-like walls of granite on which are engraved the names of those who died in the battle on the front as well as the back. It is a very interesting park.

spots.name: Okinawa Peace Memorial Hall
spots.desc: A separate memorial, marked by a high tower, with the Peace Memorial Statue and exhibitions of Japanese artists.

spots.name: Okinawa World
spots.desc: Theme park based on Okinawa wildlife and culture, built alongside a stunning natural cavern. Walk for nearly 1 km underground and gape at the limestone formations; see snake handlers abusing habu (the local poisonous reptile) for your amusement; admire the skill and energy of the folk dancers and musicians; try your hand at folk craft; enjoy the local beer and liquor; and a few other fun…
spots.price: ¥1100-1600 for adults, ½ price for children

spots.name: DMM Kariyushi Aquarium
spots.desc: Okinawa's second aquarium, not quite as immense as Churaumi up in Motobu but much more easily accessible. Includes a rather sad zoo where animals are kept in inadequately small enclosures.

spots.name: Ryukyu Glass Village
spots.desc: Here you can try making your own Ryukyu Glass items, such as dishes, vases, and jewelry along with other things like candles. Reservations are required in order to participate.

spots.name: Peaceful Illumination
spots.desc: An annual illumination event that always has a peace-related theme.

spots.name: Kenmin Steak
spots.desc: A local steak restaurant. Reservations can be made online or by phone.

spots.name: 730 Monument
spots.desc: This black rock mounted on a concrete plinth is not much to look at, but given its central location in downtown Ishigaki next to the port and the beginning of Route 390, the mysterious number warrants an explanation: it commemorates July 30, 1978, the day when Okinawa switched from driving on the right (like the US) to the left (like the rest of Japan). The 730COURT shopping mall is also nearby.

spots.name: Yoko Gushiken Bronze Statue
spots.local: 具志堅用高モニュメント
spots.desc: A statue of Ishigaki-born boxer, Yoko Gushiken, at Ishigaki Port. It's a popular photo op and something to see while waiting for your ferry.

spots.name: Ohana Nobumoto Memorial Museum
spots.desc: A museum for former Waseda University president, Professor Nobumoto Ohama.

spots.name: Yaeyama Peace Memorial Museum
spots.desc: A small museum outlining life on Ishigaki during World War II with special attention given to the prevalance of malaria on the island at the time, how the war pushed the disease to epidemic levels when the locals were evacuated into the mountains and aid was cut off, and the eradication of malaria from Ishigaki and the Yaeyama Islands by Americans after winning the war.

spots.name: Yōkō Gushiken Memorial Hall
spots.desc: A World Champion boxer during the 1970s-1980s who held the WBA light-flyweight title for 6 years from 1976 to 1981. He retired after losing the title and is most known today as a guest on variety shows. The museum focuses solely on his boxing career, with belts, trophies, gear, etc. from each of his boxing matches. Over a recreated boxing ring on the second floor, a television plays his full…

spots.name: Okanzaki Lighthouse
spots.desc: A popular scenic destination. Good views of Iriomote island when the weather is okay.

spots.name: Tojinbaka
spots.desc: This ornately decorated Chinese-style "Tang People's Grave" commemorates the sorry fate of some 400 Hokkien Chinese coolies, who mutinied and ran aground on Ishigaki on their way to California. Pursued by the English navy, those captured were killed, so many headed into the mountains where they starved or committed suicide, and only a lucky few were taken under the wing of friendly locals and…

spots.name: Kannonzaki Lighthouse
spots.desc: A little lighthouse on a little cape, not open to the public but there's a little park and viewing pavilion next to it. Not worth much of a detour but conveniently located across the road from Tōjinbaka.

spots.name: Kannon-dō Temple
spots.desc: Rounding out the trio of low-key attractions around Tōjinbaka is this quiet Okinawan-style wooden temple, with a grand lantern-lined staircase but little to see when you get there. The toilets, however, are kept in excellent shape.

spots.name: Ishigaki Stalactite Cave
spots.desc: The southernmost cave in Japan, created by coral reefs over 200,000 years ago. It's 3.2 kilometers long in total, making it the largest cave on the island, and 660 meters are open to visitors. It's known for its illuminations in the Senkyo area of the cave, but a variety of features throughout the cave are also of interest.

spots.name: Yaeyama Limestone Cave
spots.desc: An ill-maintained park with a high entrance fee, there is an unmanned gate where you can purchase a ticket. While the nature part of the park is impressive, overgrowth can make it difficult to see everything. It is sometimes compared to an experience of wandering into the mountains which is appealing to those who prefer a less curated experience. There are two caves on site. Visitors have noted…

spots.name: Banna Park
spots.desc: A large nature park home to a variety of unique plants and wildlife. There are a handful of lookout points from where you can see most of the island, rest pavilions, monuments, and playgrounds. Seishika Bridge, which runs over the largest lake in the park, is also a scenic point. There is a nearby lookout from which you can view and take pictures of the bridge.

spots.name: Yonehara Palm Tree Groves
spots.local: 米原のヤエヤマヤシ群落
