spots.desc: A short path that leads to a deck where you can see and enjoy the local Yaeyama Palm Trees.

spots.name: Yoneko Yaki Kobo Shisa Farm
spots.local: 米子焼工房 シーサー農園
spots.desc: Home of the "Shisa Garden"; a space featuring large, colorful sculptures of shisa in a variety of poses.

spots.name: Umicoza
spots.desc: Friendly dive shop that also caters to English-speaking divers. Free transfers from anywhere on the island, Visa, MC, Amex accepted.

spots.name: Tom Sawyer
spots.desc: This diving shop has a branch at the ferry terminal and offers diving courses, diving, snorkeling and underwater sightseeing cruises. A double dive is ¥13,000 and full diving rental is ¥4,000.

spots.name: Hanalee Adventure Tours
spots.desc: Offering jungle zip line tours around the base of Omoto mountain on Ishigaki. Snorkeling trips on board a 43-foot sailboat or via kayak from the beach. Sunset or nite sailing cruises. All tours conducted in Japanese and English by a native English speaker. Hotel pickup and drop-off in the Ishigaki city area included.

spots.name: Discover Ishigaki Tours
spots.desc: Offers English speaking guided snorkeling, hiking, sightseeing and family oriented tours around Ishigaki island.
spots.price: Snorkeling tour (4h) ¥9,500, Snorkeling + Sightseeing (4.5h) ¥11,000, Full day tours (6-7h) ¥16,000

spots.name: Sukuji Beach
spots.desc: 1 km of white sand beach, equipped with changing rooms, showers, toilets and other essentials. The view from the beach is stunning and on a clear day Uganzaki lighthouse is visible in the distance. The sea is the shallowest to be found on any of Ishigaki's beaches, which is great if you fancy a relaxing paddle in the ocean, but swimmers should look elsewhere. Trees at the rear of the beach…

spots.name: 730COURT
spots.desc: The first, best and only shopping mall in Ishigaki, conveniently located next to the port and the 730 Crossing. Restaurants including not one but two microbreweries, cafes and a couple of clothing shops.

spots.name: Ishigaki-shi Tokusanpin Hanbai Center
spots.local: 石垣市特産品販売センター
spots.desc: This city-sponsored retail center sells only authentic Ishigaki-made products, ranging from handicrafts to food items.

spots.name: Tezukurikan Kōbō Uminchu
spots.desc: Home of the ubiquitous Uminchu (Okinawan for "Sea People") T-shirts worn by approximately half the local population. A vast variety of designs from ¥2625.

spots.name: Yashiya
spots.desc: This little factory-shop cooks up tasty cane sugar candy, sold on premises for ¥500 per cake. You can also view the making process, which basically consists of mashing up sugarcane and then boiling the juice until it turns into brown sugar candy.

spots.name: Koubou Tumeya
spots.desc: Shīsā (シーサー) is a traditional Okinawan decoration, often found in pairs, resembling a cross between a lion and a dog. This workshop makes Shīsā using traditional materials from the island. A visitor (of any age) can also make a Shīsā with a step-by-step guidance from the staff.

spots.name: Beach
spots.desc: This friendly stucco-walled beach café trapped in a mall offers the Okinawan speciality taco rice in both "standard" (Mexican-ish) and "original" (Asian chicken) versions for ¥800 with tea/coffee or ¥1000 with a draught Orion beer.

spots.name: Māsan-dō
spots.desc: Specializes in Yaeyama soba, ¥500 for a basic bowl, ¥800 for the sōki version with a big hunk o' pork on top. Add your namecard to the vast collection on the walls.

spots.name: Marusa
spots.desc: Even locals come here for Yaeyama soba. Set lunches are a generous size.

spots.name: Uechi Jersey Bokujō Soft Cream Hanbaiten
spots.local: 上地ジャージー牧場ソフトクリーム販売店
spots.desc: This is the place to sample milk-flavored ice cream, made only from the milk of local Ishigaki cows.

spots.name: Yarabu Shokudo
spots.desc: An old traditional house with red-tile roof was transformed into this cozy restaurant. Here you can relax and enjoy Yaeyama soba, a noodle dish, or if you're craving a rice bowl, Su-chika-don (the local pork, marinated in salt) and the original Yarabu-don.

spots.name: Kato-soba
spots.desc: Some great choices are the Ebi-soba (local prawn noodle) \900 or the Yaeyama soba \550.

spots.name: St. Elmo's Café & Kitchen
spots.desc: This is a nice place to see the sunset. The sun will set into the ocean right before you and you couldn't ask for a better place to be. The food presentation is nice and the service is very friendly. If you are looking for a relaxed, calm and easy going place to have a drink and see the sunset, this is a good choice within a reasonable distance of Ishigaki town (if you have transportation).

spots.name: Yamburger
spots.desc: One of Ishigaki's most popular burger restaurants serving a variety of classic burgers, as well as the unique avocado wasabi burger.

spots.name: Kinjō
spots.desc: The lunch-only ¥2500 steak teishoku set with 150 g of Ishigaki beef to grill by yourself is one of the better deals around, especially when washed down with some Ishigakijima beer. Offers half-price dinner on the first day of the month, but you will have to stand in line for a good hour as that is a very popular night with locals in the know. Kinjo also has other branches around town.

spots.name: Hitoshi
spots.desc: An izakaya that specializes in tuna fish. Their tuna sushi and sashimi are something to dream for. There are two branches in town. This is a very popular eating place so it is best to book ahead.

spots.name: Ishigaki Beef MARU
spots.desc: Yakiniku (grilling meat yourself at the table) with different cuts of Ishigaki beef. Really tasty, and the staff are friendly; one even speaks pretty good English, though he probably has a day off once in a while. Menu is fully in Japanese, so ask for the 'three cuts of Ishigaki beef' (¥2600) or the 'top quality beef platter' (¥4280).

spots.name: Trattoria Romana Ishigaki
spots.desc: Italian chef coming from Rome makes authentic Italian cuisine. He is very friendly and can give you good tips about traveling around. All the ingredients are imported from Italy. If you are tired of eating Japanese foods and being surrounded by Japanese people, this is the place to relax in a lovely atmosphere. good veg menu

spots.name: Papa-ya
spots.desc: Billing itself as "Ishigaki's original juice", the shop sells fresh juices and juice blends made with pineapples, shikwasa, guava, papaya, and dragonfruits sweetened with sugarcane. The juice here is very fresh and the blends are really good. It's popular among locals and Japanese tourists. It is located just outside the entrance to the Yonehara Palm Groves, but this juice shop likely attracts…

spots.name: Ubudumaihama
spots.desc: From the cliffs here, there's an impressive view of much of Yonaguni's beautiful northern coastline.

spots.name: Hikawa Beach
spots.desc: Shaped like a crescent, it is the island's largest beach. Suitable for swimming. Very quiet, little-to-no waves because of a coral reef.
spots.addr: the southern shore of the island in Hikawa

spots.name: Kuburadake
spots.desc: Kuburadake is a Natural Conservation District in the west of Yonaguni, about 188 m above sealevel. It is valuable because it contains a Chinquapin mountain forest and a lowlands forest, home to such natural monuments as the colorful Emerald Dove (リュウキュウキンバト), Japanese Wood Pidgeon (ヨナグニカラスバト), Ryukyu Robin (ウスアカヒゲ), and others. From about halfway up the mountain to the summit, the trees are…

spots.name: Tunguta
spots.desc: Tunguta is a rice field in the middle of the island, of historical interest. In the period when a head tax was enforced by the Shimazu clan of modern-day Kagoshima prefecture against the people of the southern islands, causing much pain and suffering, all the inhabitants of the island were suddenly called to this ricefield. Those who did not get there by a certain time were slaughtered. This was…

spots.name: Yonaguni Ethnographic Museum
spots.local: 与那国民俗資料館 Yonaguni Minzoku Shiryōkan
spots.desc: This museum, at No. 49 in the Sonai area, is run by 100+ year-old "island auntie", Ikema Nae. There's a lot of information about the island's history, culture, and even language. If you want information about the island's indigenous writing system, kaida-dii, this is probably the place to go. Their informational pamphlets can also be very enlightening, but they are only occasionally offered in…

spots.name: Atlas Moth Museum
spots.desc: Has live caterpillars in season as well as various displays of local insects and other critters. You won't be able to see the adult moths, though, as the cocoons are returned to the forests. ayamihabiru is the local name for Yonagunisan moth.

spots.name: Open Coast Travel
spots.desc: Open Coast Travel is the only US based travel agency specializing in guided scuba tours to Yonaguni for Western travelers. All bilingual guides have lived in Japan.

spots.name: Yonaguni Diving Service
spots.desc: Kubura. The oldest and largest dive shop on the island, quite professionally run: they will cater to your experience level and will not head out to sites if the weather does not permit (in which case your money is refunded). Two boat dives start from 12000, full gear rental for a day is 6500. No credit cards accepted and only limited English spoken. Quite popular, so book ahead.

spots.name: SOUWES Diving Service
spots.desc: Yonaguni. The dive shop of Mr. Kihachiro Aratake. Mr. Kihachiro Aratake is a diving instructor who first discovered the underwater ruins.

spots.name: Yonaguni Marathon
spots.local: 一周マラソン大会 Isshu Marason Taikai
spots.desc: Every November. Despite the name, the race is either 10 km or 24 km (around the island), not a full marathon.

spots.name: Ōtomo Shoten
spots.desc: One of Kubura's two general-goods stores. Has a pretty good range of hanazake tucked away in the back.

spots.name: Yonaguni Kaien
spots.desc: This store sells salt harvested from Kuroshio Current. The best stuff comes in big crystals several millimeters in size, and supposedly tastes somewhat sweet.

spots.name: Shikoku Railway Culture Museum
spots.local: 四国鉄道文化館, shikoku tetsudō bunkakan
spots.desc: This lovely museum houses a first-generation 0 Series Shinkansen bullet train car and a JNR Class DF50 diesel locomotive (No. DF50 1), and a building displaying three more historical train cars. One building is dedicated to Shinji Sogō, known as the "father" of the bullet train, who is from the Saijō area.

spots.name: Kōmyō-ji
spots.desc: A beautiful modern Buddhist temple designed by legendary architect Tadao Ando.

spots.name: "Uchinuki no Kura"
spots.desc: This souvenir shop on Saijō's main shopping arcade specializes locally made crafts and clothing. Run by an NPO, each shelf in the store displays products by a different artisan, and popular goods include shirts made from repurposed kimono, cedar carvings, and indigo-dyed fabrics. (Ten minute walk from Iyo-Saijō station.)

spots.name: "Farmers' Markets"
spots.desc: There are several farmers' markets run by Japan Agriculture in the Saijō area. The largest is Shu-chan Market in the Tōyo region, but the most accessible for visitors is Suito Market, located next to Saijō High School at the city's center. Much of the produce and other food on sale is locally made: Saijō is famous for eggplant, persimmons, grapes, and spinach. Next door is a bakery that uses…

spots.name: Vita
spots.desc: Gelateria featuring classic flavors like chocolate or strawberry and original creations from regional ingredients like red kiwi, eggplant, komatsuna (mustard spinach) etc., Also has an espresso machine. Great for a sweet summertime dessert after the Aqua Route or the Ishizuchi climb. Very popular with high school students.
spots.addr: Saijo Shi Oomachi 856-16 (愛媛県西条市大町856-16)

spots.name: Taiwan Ryori Shoryu
spots.desc: Excellent Chinese, perhaps the most authentic in the entire Saijo area. Features Taiwanese and Sichuan specialties. Often frequented by local Chinese customers. Inexpensive, yummy, and filling, with cheap tap beer in a cold glass or shochu available.
spots.addr: Saijo Shi Tsuitachi 780-2 (〒793-0027 愛媛県西条市朔日市 台湾料理昇龍)

spots.name: Saijo Soba Kinoe
spots.desc: Renowned soba shop with a lovely wooden interior. The seasonal menu rotates through classic variations of soba. But you'll also find original creations like soba in a sauce made with local tomatoes or soba floating in a refreshing chilled yuzu citrus broth. The owner is very particular about using quality wheat for the noodles and the local uchinuki water for the broths. This is serious soba on…
spots.addr: Saijo Shi Tsuitachi 783-6 (〒793-00117 愛媛県西条市朔日市783-6)

spots.name: Hachijyuhachi (88) Udon Toyo Shop
spots.desc: Inexpensive yet excellent cafeteria-esque shop with satisfyingly firm sanuki udon in a clean setting. You choose your size, broth, and toppings from selections like ginger beef egg yolk and daikon bukkake. You can also add various tempura sides, or ask for the broth on the side. A middle size (chuu) is very filling. If you're still hungry, they have mini rice bowls with more toppings (donburi).…

spots.name: Dandanchakan/啖啖茶館
spots.desc: True to its name, Dandanchakan offers a large variety of teas, available hot or cold. Meals are also served of bimbmbap, kimchi and chige sets and green Thai curry, which make the place a gem in Tanbara, where such foods are hard to come by. In addition there are desserts including things like red beans, coconut ice cream and mango. Closed on Sundays and public holidays.
spots.addr: Saijo Shi Tanbara Cho Ikeda 1626-3/西条市丹原町池田１６２６－３

spots.name: Cafe Lamp
spots.desc: Simple yet scrumptious Italian pastas and desserts. The owner often changes and updates the menu on a blog and uses locally-farmed ingredients. Examples of dishes include a cream shrimp and mushroom carbonara and a mustard cress bolognesa. The cafe serves coffee and tea. Decor and seating is minimalist and comfortable with a few sofas. The space is very open and bright. The relaxing atmosphere…
spots.addr: Saijo Shi Tanbara Cho Kurumi 684 (愛媛県西条市丹原町来見684)

spots.name: Ushironoshoumen
spots.desc: Just a minute or so up the road from Cafe Lamp and lined with cherry trees, Ushironoshoumen is a lovely place to visit in spring. The lunch of the day specials available on weekdays start from ¥780 with optional add-ons like the salad bar with the cafe's dressing. They also have an assortment of desserts including cakes, crepes and ice cream.
spots.hours: 09:00-22:00 with a breakfast buffet from 09:00-11:30, closed on Thursdays
spots.addr: Saijo Shi Tanbara Cho Kurumi 777-1 (愛媛県西条市丹原町来見777-1)

spots.name: Paruju
spots.desc: Old-school piping-hot okonomiyaki in a down-to-earth shop with Showa-Era vibes. Located in a small residential neighborhood nearby the Kamo river. The Hiroshima-style (here they call it "soba-iri") Kamogawayaki is the most popular variation, grilled at your table on a steel surface until the edges of the noodles are seared golden-brown and crispy. Servings are large, with plenty of savory sauce…
spots.addr: Saijo Shi Oomachi 1183-22 (愛媛県西条市大町1183-22)

spots.name: cafe Kiko & Yvan
spots.local: カフェキコアンドイヴァン
spots.desc: Small cafe run by husband and wife. Each have decorated different rooms to their own tastes for visitors to enjoy. Dotted around the cafe are wares brought back from Finland which are also available for purchase.

spots.name: Marubun
spots.desc: Popular Japanese-style Italian fare in a cozy warm setting often frequented by families and newlywed couples. This store in Komatsu Town is the home store for a small regional chain. Great for an outing with locals who don't want to go to an Izakaya.
spots.addr: Komatsu Cho Shinyashiki Ko 407-1 (愛媛県西条市小松町新屋敷甲407-1)

spots.name: Koyo Tei
spots.desc: Lovely hotel restaurant with delicious traditional Japanese set meals and bargains at lunchtime. Generous helpings with a colorful array of side dishes. The menu changes seasonally. The shop is known for its crisp tempura, breaded chicken cutlet (chicken katsu), barbecued eel over rice, and fresh kaisendon (raw seafood over rice bowl). Service is polite and the windows let in a lot of natural…
spots.addr: Mitsuyaminami 6-29 Terminal Hotel Toyo (Toyo Area) (愛媛県西条市三津屋南6-29ターミナルホテル東予)

spots.name: Nagomi
spots.desc: This independent izakaya features sashimi, deep-fried breaded dishes, and nabe. There is a bar and tatami seating. The service is professional and friendly, with a lot to see behind the counter. There's plenty to drink, including regional sakes and bottled corona beer with a lemon slice. It is popular for local work parties, so reservations are recommended.
spots.addr: Saijo Shi Mitsuyaminami 7-11 (Nyugawa Station Area) (西条市三津屋南7-11)

spots.name: Shani Muni
spots.desc: Excellent, classy Izakaya run by a friendly local family. It has an intimate dark wooden atmosphere and private rooms with sliding doors. There are courses featuring nabe (hot pot), side-dishes, tasty grilled and fried chicken (yakitori and karaage), wonderful American-inspired appetizers, and fantastic salads. The store also has a great selection of fresh seasonal fish and chicken sashimi as…
spots.addr: Saijo Shi Oomachi 523-3 (〒793-0030 愛媛県西条市大町525-3)

spots.name: Torikko (とりっこ)
spots.desc: Fantastic Izakaya style restaurant, with both tatami floor and table seating. Food is divine with an excellent range of skewered chicken, beef, pork and anything else skewerable (each range from ¥50~200). Plenty of beautifully presented hotpots, donburis, deep fried foods, pizzas and other delicious morsels available too. They offer the full range of Japanese beverages and even have a page of…

spots.name: Issei Yakitori (一声焼き鳥)
spots.desc: The oldest and possibly the most famous restaurant in Toyo. This family-run restaurant is owned and operated by an incredibly friendly family that has been looking after the local foreigners for the last 25 years. The food is absolutely amazing and the service is even better.

spots.name: Taga Shrine
spots.desc: Although Taga doesn't get much press at the local tourist office, it's probably the most unusual sight in town: the shrine is an ancient Shinto fertility shrine, full of phalluses of all shapes and sizes, including a mighty carved log that gets carried about on festival days. It's on the north side of the river, not far from the better known Warei Shrine.

spots.name: Dekoboko Shindō
spots.desc: Located on the grounds of the Taga Shrine, this is essentially a three-story sex museum devoted to fertility and its graphical expressions. Two of them are found in the name: the kanji 凸 and 凹 usually mean "convex" and "concave" respectively, but the shrine's logo makes things clearer by placing the pointy bit under the one with the gap.
spots.price: Entry is fairly pricy at ¥800, and you need to pay a whopping ¥20,000 if you want to take photos inside. No…

spots.name: Bull sumo
spots.desc: It is Uwajima's main claim to fame. Two bulls decked out with holy ropes grapple each other by the horns and attempt to push each other out of a sumo ring. This is no modern gimmick, but an age-old tradition solemnly officiated by the same priests who run human sumo tournaments.
spots.hours: tournaments held in January, April, July, August, and October; matches start at noon and take around 3 hours
spots.price: Tickets: ¥3000. Buy in advance if possible

spots.name: Shinju Kaikan
spots.desc: Primarily a pearl souvenir shop, but to ensure you're not rushed when considering a purchase, they've helpfully included a restaurant and a hotel (rooms from ¥4000 single) on the grounds. Pearl rings and necklaces can be custom-made to fit your budget; on the cheaper side, try some pearl candy (¥650 for 15 pieces). It's a little way out of town, north on the Uwajima Highway from the JR…

spots.name: Taisōmen
spots.desc: It uses the same hearty fish, but this dish's beauty is in the noodles sculpted into waves and the seasonal nature of its presentation. Dip the noodles and fish into the tai sauce before savoring.

spots.name: Isshin
spots.desc: Seasonal seafood dishes, including the notorious fugu (for a premium), but chicken and beef as well.

spots.name: Kadoya
spots.desc: A good place to sample the aforementioned taimeshi and other local specialties.

spots.name: Higashi-Kagawa History and Folk Museum
spots.local: 東かがわ市歴史民俗資料館
spots.desc: Has exhibits and artifacts related to the former castle town, local culture, transportation, and daily living from different periods in the city's history.

spots.name: Hiketa Castle
spots.desc: Hiketa Castle, along with Marugame Castle, were built to help provide protection to Takamatsu Castle from the west (Marugame Castle) and east (Hiketa Castle). The castle was abandoned after the One Castle Policy was put into effect. Little is left of the castle aside from some stone walls but in addition to being a historic site, the hike to the ruins offers great views of the harbor and the Seto…

spots.name: Kagawa Gloves Museum
spots.local: 香川のてぶくろ資料館
spots.desc: Has exhibits and artifacts from over 130 years of glove-making in Kagawa.

spots.name: Sanshu Izutsu House
spots.desc: A historic building that now offers opportunities to make local specialties. You can mold and make wasanbon (和三盆), a traditional sugar sweet of eastern Kagawa and Tokushima. They also have glove decorating and leather keychain-making. Reservations must be made to participate in the activities. If you don't wish to or are unable to make the items, most can also be purchased at the second floor…
spots.price: Wasanbon-making 30 minutes ¥750, Personalized gloves 1 hour ¥600, leather trinkets 30-60 minutes ¥400-¥600 (depending…

spots.name: Kamebishiya
spots.desc: Both an attraction and a restaurant, the Kamebishiya is the most striking of the Hiketa Historic District's buildings with its bright vermillion colored walls. As a business, they've been making and selling soy sauce since 1753. The restaurant serves soy sauce udon, using their homemade soy sauce and moromi udon, which is only available here. Even if you don't plan to eat here, it's worth…

spots.name: Portivia Passo
spots.local: ポルティヴィア パッソ
spots.desc: An Italian restaurant serving a variety of pizza, pasta, and salads.

spots.name: Matsubara of Tsuda
spots.desc: One of Japan's "100 best white sand and green pine trees" sites. The beach beyond Matsubara is beautiful and attracts many swimmers in the summer.

spots.name: Yakushiyu Onsen
spots.desc: A cold mineral spring that springs from the Tawatakeyashiki. Because the source temperature is low, a heating/circulation filtration method is used.

spots.name: Prefectural Kamezuru Park
spots.desc: Including the hills around the park, the area is about 33 ha. On the site, there are " Sakura Namiki" and "Iris Garden", as well as "Kameshima", which is rich in natural forests where more than 300 tree species have been confirmed. It is one of the most famous cherry blossom viewing spots in the Tosan region. Especially, the embankment connecting the Kameshima side and the Usa shrine side is 20 m…

spots.name: Sukumo Castle
spots.desc: Also known as Matsuda Castle, the castle stood strong until the "One Castle Edict" was issued in 1615 which led the domain to tear it down. Today Ishizuchi Shrine stands where the keep once stood and all that remains of the castle are a few stone walls.

spots.name: German House
spots.desc: The site of a World War I prisoner-of-war camp for German soldiers. The stone bridges and cenotaph built by the prisoners are on display, along with documents that give us a glimpse of life during those times. The German prisoners were free to communicate with the local people, and much German culture remains in the area to this day. The present-day German House was built in 1993.
spots.hours: 09:30-17:00 daily; closed 4th Mon of each month and the day following a national holiday

spots.name: Otsuka Art Museum
spots.desc: The Otsuka family has created a "backup" of the world's painting masterpieces. Their museum displays no original paintings; all works on display are duplicates of originals that have been printed onto ceramic surfaces using the most advanced printing technology available. Buses run to Naruto Park from JR Naruto Station.

spots.name: Chukasoba Konno
spots.desc: Known for its duck ramen. A vending machine selling frozen duck ramen can be found outside.

spots.name: Akita Dog Visitor Center
spots.local: 秋田犬の里 Akitainu no Sato
spots.desc: Watch Akita dogs 0(9:30-16:45) in the city's tourism center. You can also rent bicycles (\500/day, \300/4hrs).

spots.name: Namahage Museum
spots.local: 男鹿市役所 なまはげ館
spots.desc: This is a museum about namahage, the demons that scare children in Akita every New Year's Eve.

spots.name: Shinzan Trail
spots.desc: This hiking trail goes from the Akagami Shrine to the Namahage Museum. It goes near the summit of Mt. Honzan (本山), which makes for a short side venture. The trail takes around 4 hours, one way, and bus service at either end is infrequent.

spots.name: Namahage Sedo
spots.desc: This namahage performance involves demons coming down from the forest to scare children. There is also dancing, drumming, and mochi throwing.

spots.name: Family Restaurant Sono
spots.local: ファミリーレストラン 園
spots.desc: A restaurant serving curry with cutlets, spaghetti, and other family-friendly dishes.

spots.name: Ogaya
spots.desc: Serves Oga Ramen, ramen made in local water from local ingredients.

spots.name: Kamakura-kan (Kamakura Museum)
spots.desc: Visitors can experience entering a real Kamakura (igloo-like snow houses) in a subzero space. There is a store where you can buy local products and a tourist information desk.

spots.name: Akita Prefectural Museum of Modern Art
spots.desc: This museum's collection of modern art is predominately from Akita, though some is from elsewhere.

spots.name: Kamakura (Yokote’s Winter Festival)
spots.desc: Small igloos (called "kamakura") are built in many locations across town. There are hundreds of kamakura, some large enough to enter. Some of these, in turn, become small eating establishments. Traditionally, amazake (a sweet winter-season drink) and mochi are served.

spots.name: Bonden (Yokote’s Winter Festival)
spots.desc: decorated staves called bonden are carried through the city and presented as an offering at Asahi-okayama-jinja Shrine.

spots.name: Yokote Gymnasium
spots.desc: This city gymnasium hosts a variety of sports and community events.

spots.name: Honjo Culture Hall
spots.local: 本荘文化会館 Honjō bunkakaikan
spots.desc: This building is the only large auditorium in Yurihonjo. It hosts many kinds of shows, such as dance shows, concerts, and karaoke contests.

spots.name: Iwaki Local History Museum
spots.local: 岩城歴史民俗資料館 Iwaki rekishi minzoku shiryōkan
spots.desc: This reconstructed village has some museum buildings with old clothes, weapons, scrolls, and, oddly, biology research. There are also some reconstructed buildings, as well as old looms and blacksmith tools. Next to the reconstructed village there's a large tower, surrounded by a small moat. There's a restaurant and gift shop on the first floor, and the top floor has nice views of Kameda. No…

spots.name: Chokai Snowmobile Land
spots.local: 鳥海高原南由利原スノーモビルランド
spots.desc: A snowmobile training and recreation area. Instructors can teach beginners, including children. Reservations necessary.

spots.name: Hotel Foresta Chokai
spots.desc: Onsen and hotel on the base of Mt. Chokai. There are indoor and outdoor baths. Bring your own towel for bathing.

spots.name: Shisuikan
spots.desc: This community center often hosts public events, such as guest speakers and concerts.

spots.name: Yunosawa Onsen
spots.desc: This onsen is part of Hotel Masaka. It makes a nice stop after skiing at Okojoland Ski Area.

spots.name: Kizakura Onsen Yurari
spots.desc: This is a large onsen. It has relaxing areas, baths, and an attached restaurant.
spots.hours: Daily 09:00-21:00; closed 1st and 3rd Sun of each month, or the following day if a national holiday

spots.name: Honjo Library
spots.local: 由利本荘市立本荘図書館
spots.desc: Largest library in Yurihonjo. Some English books are available, but most of these are in a storage room in back, so ask for help.
spots.hours: Mon-Fri 09:00-18:00, Sat Sun 09:00-17:00, closed 3rd Sun of the month, closed last day of the month (or preceding Fri)

spots.name: Kofuen Sumo Ring
spots.desc: This is an outdoor sumo practice ring, open for all to use. Contact the Honjo Board of Education (number above) for more information.

spots.name: Koryu Gakushu Center
spots.desc: This public building has a small public library, as well as a gym and kitchen. Private groups often reserve the gym or kitchen and use them for various events. This building used to be called the Koiki Koryu Center (広域交流センター).

spots.name: Tsurumai Kaikan
spots.desc: This community center has large and small rooms that can be reserved for various community events.

spots.name: Tsurumai Onsen
spots.desc: This is a popular onsen in central Honjo with a scenic location by a pond.
spots.hours: 08:00-21:30, closed 1st and 3rd Fri of every month, closed Dec 29-30

spots.name: Nishime Kominkan Seagull
spots.desc: This community center has a medium-sized auditorium. It often hosts community events like dance recitals and art exhibits.

spots.name: Nishime Yukkoland
spots.desc: This bath house is part of a hotel. It's one of the only 24-hour bath houses in Yurihonjo. The building is not noteworthy, but on the other hand, it's clean, and the bath is large. There's a large bath, a small mineral bath, a sauna, and an outdoor sitting area. Massages are available.

spots.name: Yurihonjo Sogo Gymnasium
spots.local: 由利本荘市総合体育館; Yurihonjō sōgō taiikukan
spots.desc: This large public gymnasium hosts a variety of sports tournaments. There is also a weight room with treadmills.
spots.price: Most events are free to watch; the weight room costs a few hundred yen per visit

spots.name: Nagasaka Ski Area
spots.desc: A small ski area with one t-bar and one slope. Open for day and night skiing.

spots.name: Cycling Terminal Yamayuri
spots.local: サイクリングターミナルやまゆり
spots.desc: This building has a tourist information center, a small gift shop, a small restaurant, public restrooms and vending machines, and maps. There may be bicycles for rent, as well. The annual Chokai Marathon running race starts and ends here. Closed in winter.

spots.name: Hanadate Milsey Dairy
spots.local: 花立牧場工房ミルジー Hanadate bokujō kōbō milsey
spots.desc: This dairy has tasty milk and ice cream. Offers hands-on tours.

spots.name: Yashima Nishinkan/Kominkan
spots.desc: Community center with library and small auditorium. There is free internet access in the library.
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00 daily, closed the 3rd Sun of each month, closed Dec 29-Jan 3

spots.name: Conbini Sato
spots.desc: Convenience store. Sells fresh fruit, local gifts, and post cards.

spots.name: Hottoin Chokai
spots.desc: Sells fresh and canned vegetables and gifts for tourists, such as postcards and t-shirts.

spots.name: Sairando
spots.desc: Sells fresh and canned vegetables and gifts for tourists such as postcards and t-shirts.
spots.price: In-season vegetables may be cheaper than at local grocery stores

spots.name: Mingei Saito
spots.desc: Sells crafts, food and drink from the region. For example, the shop sells many lacquer dishes and containers made in Akita, as well as local brands of sake and kiritanpo.
spots.hours: Mon-Sat 08:30-18:30, Sun 09:30-18:30, closed 1st and 3rd Wed of each month

spots.name: Saison Fugetsu
spots.local: セゾンふうげつ本荘店
spots.desc: Dessert store. Sells pieces and entire cakes, cream puffs, and other sweets.
spots.hours: 09:30-19:00, closed 1st and 3rd Tue of the month

spots.name: Nishime Rest Area
spots.desc: This rest area has a restaurant, gift shop, vending machines, and a large parking area. The gift shop has a large selection of local and regional foods, t-shirts, and crafts.

spots.name: Saison Fugetsu
spots.desc: Dessert store. Sells pieces and entire cakes, cream puffs, and other sweets.

spots.name: Lawson Station
spots.local: ローソン・由利本荘矢島店
spots.desc: Convenience store with ATM. For late night shopping, people from Yashima and Chokai go here, because it's the only option.

spots.name: Chokaiso
spots.desc: This hotel and onsen has a restaurant with a standard Japanese menu and tasty katsudon. Large rooms may be reserved for enkais.

spots.name: Cake Kobo Furian Nakamura
spots.local: ケーキ工房フリアンナカムラ
spots.desc: A cake and dessert shop. Also serves coffee and has magazines and a sitting area.

spots.name: Chiyogiku
spots.desc: The special is toromi ramen, and the tanmen is also quite good. Seats 24.

spots.name: Gobando
spots.desc: This izakaya serves standard fare. On Saturdays once or twice a month, it has open mic night for local bands.

spots.name: Ichikoma
spots.desc: This small udon shop has three tables and a counter. It serves many kinds of udon, and also oden. The shop is owned by a young couple, and their udon is quite good.

spots.name: Ichiyoshi
spots.desc: A traditional Japanese restaurant where you sit and eat on tatami mats. Specializes in fish. Reservations required.

spots.name: Grill Kind
spots.desc: A very nice steak restaurant. There are only 3 tables, so reservations are required.

spots.name: Masadon
spots.desc: This izakaya's special is half of a small chicken, deep fried. The chicken sells out, so it's best to call in advance and reserve a portion. Because the chicken is greasy and tasty, this is a good location for drinking after dinner.

spots.name: Oyaji Ramen
spots.local: ラーメンおやじ本荘店
spots.desc: Serves several kinds of ramen and tasty gyoza. Buy food tickets at the vending machine before sitting down.

spots.name: Ozono Ryokan
spots.desc: This ryokan is often reserved for large enkai (party) and used for formal dinners. The food is delicious. Reservations required.

spots.name: Pizza 10-4
spots.local: ピザ・テン・フォー本荘店
spots.desc: A delivery or carry out pizza place. Features a selection of seafood pizzas, along with a few meat and vegetarian options.

spots.name: Ramen Menmaru
spots.local: ラーメンめん丸本荘店
spots.desc: This ramen shop is centrally located and open fairly late. Its specials are assorted spicy ramen dishes. Also, the gyoza is quite good.

spots.name: Rin
spots.local: 鉄板ダイニング凛 Teppan dainingu rin
spots.desc: This restaurant has a large grill on which they cook their food. The menu is large, with an emphasis on okonomiyaki and steak.

spots.name: Warabeuta
spots.local: わらべ唄 お好み焼
spots.desc: An okonomiyaki restaurant. If you don't know how to cook okonomiyaki, the staff can help you learn.

spots.name: Yu
spots.desc: This Japanese izakaya serves traditional Akita fare, among other things. In particular, it often serves doburoku, a local sake variant. Reservations recommended.

spots.name: Restaurant Quebec
spots.desc: This Quebec-themed restaurant has various foreign food. Its pizza is fairly tasty, compared with normal Japanese pizza.

spots.name: Ibuki
spots.desc: This small shop has some of the best udon in Nishime. It also has blueberry and sesame soft-serve ice cream.

spots.name: Keijiro
spots.desc: This restaurant and izakaya serves various Japanese food, such as ramen, soba, and katsudon. It also serves kiritanpo, a famous Akita dish.

spots.name: Sakae Shokudo
spots.desc: This small restaurant serving standard Japanese fare has been around for decades, and the menu has grown in length over time. Regular customers recommend the tonkatsu, friend shrimp, and chili shrimp. A regular size dish here is the equivalent of a large dish at nearby restaurants.

spots.name: Yebisuya Ramen
spots.desc: Yebisu-style ramen. The store specialty is ginger (shoga) ramen.

spots.name: Oku
spots.desc: This is a small snack bar with karaoke. It is the only snack bar in Hitane.

spots.name: The Castaways Casual Bar
spots.desc: A small bar with karaoke. Seats 5-6 groups, or around 30 people. There's no seating charge, and reservations can be made for large groups.

spots.name: Silk
spots.desc: This is a fairly large bar with darts, a pool table, a few gaming machines, and a sitting area.

spots.name: Socket
spots.desc: This is a rather large bar with darts and karaoke. Drinks are fairly cheap.

spots.name: Kawarage Jigoku
spots.desc: Named as one of Japan's "hells" (jigoku) for its stark-white volcanic rocks and sulfide gases seeping from vents in the rocks, it was a place of ascetic worship long ago. Sanzensoji Temple was built here to worship, and like many places of ancient mountain worship, women were forbidden. Later it became a sulfur mine. Today there are walkways that allow visitors to explore the hell safely. The…
spots.hours: Closed in winter (Nov to early May)

spots.name: Oyasu Gorge
spots.desc: A scenic gorge with a walking path that winds past 98 °C hot spring waters emitting steam. There is a red bridge overlooking offering a view from above. It's particularly popular in the fall when the autumn foliage is in full effect.
spots.hours: Walking path is closed from mid-November to late April (specific opening date depends on snow conditions)

spots.name: Akinomiya Museum
spots.desc: This fascinating museum is essentially a collection of historical objects. There are few explanations of what you're seeing, but most of it is rather obvious -- old records, comic books, toys, TVs, pachinko machines, etc. The museum building is an old house, and the owner often serves tea and snacks at no extra charge. There is bath in the basement, right next to the river, which also may be used…

spots.name: Inaniwa Castle
spots.desc: A castle ruled by the Onodera Clan until the area was overtaken by the Mogami Clan. The castle has exhibits about the local history and culture.Unique among Japanese castles, you can ride a slopecar to reach the castle. Alternatively there is a walking path.

spots.name: Yuzawa-city Kawatsura Lacquerware Traditional Crafts Centre
spots.desc: Kawatsura Lacquerware has been made since the 17th century using lacquer to coat bowls that had been used to coat weapons. As the industry grew, other utensils, food items, and household goods were also made as lacquerware and sold. A museum on the second floor has exhibits about the local Kawatsura Lacquerware. The first floor is a shop and showcase where you can purchase your own. They also…

spots.name: Innai Ginzan Ijinkan
spots.desc: The museum outlines the history of the Innai Silver Mines, which was the top producer of silver in its heyday, with videos, pictures, and artifacts from the mines and miners. They also have a small collection of ancient pottery excavated from around the area. The building is a German-style brick building. The other part of the building is used as Innai Station.

spots.name: Takanoyu Onsen
spots.desc: This onsen, which is particularly pretty in the autumn, is located near a beautiful gorge and a man-made waterfall. There are indoor and outdoor baths for each gender, and a mixed bath (混浴, konyoku) near the gorge and waterfall.

spots.name: Kawarage Oyutaki Falls
spots.desc: This natural outdoor hot spring is a short walk from the road parking lot and Jizo Statue below Kawarage Jigoku. Bring a swimsuit.

spots.name: Abe Hajime Kokeshi Shop
spots.desc: The primary place to purchase Kijiyama Kokeshi, also sometimes called Kawatsura Kokeshi. The shop is owned by a kokeshi collector, so in addition to the local kokeshi, you can also buy the other varieties of kokeshi dolls. There are also some original kokeshi-themed goods.

spots.name: Caffe Gita
spots.desc: This shop has a good selection of coffee, by the bean or by the cup. They also have a small cake selection.

spots.name: Nakano Shoten
spots.desc: This is a general store with various kitchen, gardening, and household goods, but it also has a large tobacco selection, including cigarettes, fancy lighters, pipes, and imported cigars in a humidor. There is a small smoking area, as well.

spots.name: Daigen
spots.desc: The best miso ramen in Yuzawa. There's only counter seating, and the decor is eclectic. A side of chili paste is available on request, as is kimchi.

spots.name: Ramen Pleco
spots.desc: A small shop with a wide selection of ramen. This shop stays open later than most other ramen shops in southern Yuzawa, making it a convenient stop.

spots.name: Kikuchi Ryokan
spots.desc: This restaurant serves Japanese food in large portions, and often serves local mountain vegetables (sansai). It is part of a ryokan.

spots.name: Kanbun Gonenbudo
spots.desc: A popular Inaniawa udon restaurant with a variety of sets to choose from.

spots.name: Beer Bar Rosso Corsa
spots.desc: This bar has a wide selection of beers from Japan and abroad, including Belgian Trappist brews.
spots.hours: Closed Sundays, unless the following Mon is a national holiday
spots.price: Obscure beers are more expensive, with prices varying depending on the master's mood

spots.name: Pocket Bar
spots.desc: This bar has a great scotch selection. Some of their more obscure (expensive) scotch is not listed on the menu — ask a waiter.

spots.name: Tachineputa Hall
spots.desc: This museum is dedicated to Goshogawara City’s Tachineputa Festival. Although similar in origin to other area neputa/nebuta festivals, the 70 ft tall floats that dwarf most city buildings as they parade through the streets make this version quite unique. The Tachineputa Hall has several floats from previous years on display, as well as hands-on areas where visitors can make their own miniature…

spots.name: Shayokan - Osamu Dazai Memorial Hall
spots.desc: The writer's childhood home. An important cultural property built in the Meiji Period. Quite a large old house of interest to history and architecture buffs as well as Dazai fans.

spots.name: Tsugaru Shamisen Hall
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the Tsugaru version of the three-stringed Japanese lute. Closed in winter: December to March.

spots.name: Tachineputa Festival
spots.desc: One of the most spectacular summer festivals in the region, Goshogawara Tachineputa is famous for its gigantic floats. Measuring 70 ft tall and weighing more than 17 tons, the floats dwarf most of the surrounding buildings as they parade through the city streets. In addition to revelers yelling "yatte-mare, yatte-mare!", the parade procession is made up of taiko drum performances on gigantic…

spots.name: Tsugaru Kokeshi Museum
spots.desc: The museum is on the second floor of the building. It features kokeshi dolls from each of Tohoku's kokeshi schools along with specifics about the Tsugaru-style kokeshi. On the first floor, you can see "Japan's Biggest Jumbo Kokeshi", a 4.2-m-tall kokeshi painted to mimic the style of Mori Hidetaro, the founder of Tsugaru Kokeshi, to commemorate the opening of the Shin-Aomori Shinkansen Station…

spots.name: Takahashi Residence
spots.desc: A National Important Property, it's an Edo Period building used to supply the Kuroishi Domain with rice husks. It was also used as a secret meeting place for high-ranking officials. There was a hidden room with ways to sneak in undetected that has a moon-viewing window. The building has remained with the Takahashi family and as of 2025 the owner is the 14th generation of the family who operates a…

spots.name: Kanehiranarien Garden
spots.desc: A garden completed in 1902, it is considered to be an exemplary Oishi Bugaku-ryu-style garden, which originates from and was popular in Aomori at the time.
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 09:30-16:00 from late Apr to Nov, closed Mon

spots.name: Kokeshi Painting
spots.desc: You can paint your own Tsugaru Kokeshi under the guidance of an actual kokeshi artisan at the Tsugaru Kokeshi Museum. Same-day reservations are possible for single travelers or pairs, but advance reservations are required for larger groups. They can accommodate groups of up to 200 people.

spots.name: Ochiai Public Bathhouse
spots.desc: A small public hot spring frequented by locals. It's a convenient way to experience the less touristy local onsen in a place that still has tourist attractions.

spots.name: Tsugaru Komise Eki
spots.desc: A souvenir shop on the historic Nakamachi Komise Street where you can buy Tsugaru kokeshi and other local products and snacks. They also have live Tsugaru shamisen performances.

spots.name: Noresore Shokudo
spots.desc: 5-star buffet. Perfect for special occasions or if you are just craving delicious steaks.

spots.name: Grill Omiya
spots.desc: Popularly known as Pizza Curry, this restaurant is arguably the best example of the gastronomical collision of American and Japanese cuisine. They serve curry on a scale of spiciness ranging from 5-10-15-20-25 as well as Special 1, Special 2, and Special 3 for the brave of heart and teflon of stomach. Additionally, a "B Set" includes 2 pieces of a pizza toast. While the pizza is not faithful to…

spots.name: Tonki
spots.desc: Hamburger steak and Tonkatsu. Run by 2 generations of the same family and they are some of the nicest people you will meet.

spots.name: Marumiya
spots.local: 丸美屋, or Cheese Roll House
spots.desc: This is a local favorite. One of the first restaurants most new comers are taken to. They feature Ramen, Yakisoba (fried noodles), beef dungaree, and of course cheese rolls. If you want quality yakisoba that is not greasy or over rushed, this is the place and don't forget the cheese rolls. Very friendly staff.

spots.name: Hachimantai Dragon Eye
spots.desc: For two short weeks in late May/early June, the edges of this pond melt before the center, producing a stunning "dragon's eye" effect on a sunny day. Access requires driving up and navigating a muddy trail, so wear hiking boots.

spots.name: Hachimantai Ski Resort
spots.desc: This smallish ski resort has six lifts split across two separate areas 2 km apart, with combined ticketing and a free shuttle bus. Panorama (パノラマ) is more beginner-friendly with a dedicated kids area, while Shimokura (下倉) is for advanced powder hounds and features slopes up to 37°. Integrated with the Hachimantai Mountain Hotel for ski-in/out convenience.
spots.price: Ski pass from ¥5800/3400 adult/child per day

spots.name: Kitchen Cafe Kappa
spots.desc: The only cafe/restaurant in the Hachimantai Onsen area, serving up ramen, rice bowls and a few cafe dishes like waffles and homemade pudding. Food quality is a cut above the usual.

spots.name: Miyazawa Kenji Memorial Museum
spots.desc: A museum which highlights aspects of Kenji Miyazawa's life beyond just being an author. It especially focuses on his religious aesthetics, farming, and cosmology studies.

spots.name: Miyazawa Kenji Dowa-Mura
spots.desc: An art museum that takes the works of local author Kenji Miyazawa and turns it into a walkthrough interactive experience. There are 4 rooms inspired by different stories.

spots.name: Stellamigo Iwate Hanamaki
spots.local: ステラミーゴいわて花巻
spots.desc: Hanamaki is home to a professional futsal club in Japan's F. League.

spots.name: Genbikei Gorge
spots.desc: Genbi-kei, which roughly translates to "Gorge of Harsh Beauty" is a scenic gorge known for the white water rushing over rocks, a few waterfalls, and the dango made in a shop across the river and sent to customers via overhead cable. The surrounding area is also home to many hot spring hotels and ryokan.

spots.name: Ichinoseki City Museum
spots.desc: The permanent collection features a wide variety of objects and artifacts from around the city and prefecture, including a katana exhibit. They also feature special exhibits.

spots.name: Geibi-kei Gorge
spots.desc: Tranlated as "Lion's Nose Gorge", Geibi-kei is listed as one of the "100 Landscapes of Japan". There are flat-bottomed boats that take you upstream past Buddhist rock carvings to a scenic part of the gorge where visitors can exit the boat for a time to enjoy the views, walk around, and purchase ceramic stones to try to throw in a hole in one of the rocks for good fortune. The round-trip ride…
spots.hours: Boat departures vary by month, no closing days excepting typhoon days

spots.name: Tsuriyama
spots.desc: During the cherry blossom season in early spring, this large hill on almost a straight path west of the station, is lit by lanterns at night and is beautiful during the day as the trees bloom. Outside of cherry blossom season, the paths up the hill and the small park at the summit offer a pleasant place to explore and provide an overview of the city and Ichinoseki Station from above. According to…

spots.name: Yugen-do Cave
spots.desc: A 350 million year old cave (formed in the Paleozoic Era), said to be one of the oldest caves in Japan. It was discovered in 1980 and contains many interesting rock formations and fossils. The cave is also rumored to have been used as a hideout for Japanese Christians during the Edo period.

spots.name: Haishiwa Shrine
spots.desc: Situated at the top of a densely wooded hill, it is truly breathtaking, not only due to the giant, thousand-year-old trees at the top, but the incredibly long flight of stairs you must climb to get there.

spots.name: Okago Christian Martyrdom Museum
spots.local: 大籠キリシタン資料館
spots.desc: During the days when Christianity was banned, 300 Christians and missionaries were brought here and killed here where the Memorial Park is located. The small museum displays the history of Christianity in Okago and in the greater Tohoku Region. Other features of the park include the Okago Christian Martyrdom Memorial Kurusu Museum housing three Crucifixion statues (closed in winter), History…

spots.name: Ashi Tozan Memorial Museum
spots.desc: Ashi Tozan wrote a criminal code while he was imprisoned that was published 100 years later (it was banned from publishing when he wrote it) and eventually used as a model for Japan's penal code. The museum is dedicated to his life and works.

spots.name: Ichinoseki City Folk Museum
spots.desc: Located in a closed elementary school, the museum features exhibits of daily life among farmers, mountain dwellers, and in the river valleys.

spots.name: Hashino Iron Mine
spots.desc: A component of "Meiji Japan's Industrial Revolution Heritage Sites".

spots.name: Snake Eyes
spots.local: 蛇の目本店; Ja no me honten
spots.desc: Serves a wide variety of Japanese food to suit any taste. English-speaking staff is also available.

spots.name: Yoshi-zushi
spots.desc: Some locals say this is the best sushi in town. The restaurant serves blowfish and also has a large Japanese sake selection.

spots.name: Shark Museum
spots.local: シャークミュージアム
spots.desc: A museum showcasing the various kinds of sharks with information about them and their differences. Adjacent to Umi-no Ichi, a shopping/eating complex, which also houses an Ice Aquarium.

spots.name: Ruins of the Great East Japan Earthquake Kesennuma City Memorial Museum
spots.local: 気仙沼市東日本大震災遺構・伝承館
spots.desc: The earthquake and tsunami that occurred on March 11, 2011 devastated Kesennuma, including a large-scale fire caused by the earthquake. Over 1000 people were killed in the disaster and relief efforts and 212 people remain missing. This museum preserves damaged buildings and rubble untouched from the disaster, along with pictures, videos, and information about what happened in Kesennuma on that…

spots.name: Rias Ark Museum of Art
spots.local: リアス・アーク美術館
spots.desc: The museum is half art museum and half local history museum.

spots.name: Tsubaki Marathon
spots.desc: In the spring, Oshima is home to this marathon which bring in runners of all ages to compete against each other in a race that covers the entire island.

spots.name: Umi no Ichi
spots.desc: Kesennuma's central fish market. Many stores and restaurants are located here, as well as the tourist center and Ice Aquarium. Buy seafood or Kesennuma souvenirs.
spots.addr: 宮城県気仙沼市魚市場前７−１３

spots.name: Isaribi Park
spots.desc: This park has a large restaurant with ramen and other izakaya fare.

spots.name: Ganko Ramen
spots.local: がんこラーメン味噌家
spots.desc: This small ramen shop sells miso, shio, and shoyu ramen. It also sells gyoza.

spots.name: Hilltop
spots.desc: This is a steak restaurant with an all-you-can-eat soup, salad, and rice bar. The steaks are large, by Japanese standards, and are grilled at your table.
spots.addr: 岩手県一関市千厩町清田字峠下２５−１

spots.name: Domon Ken Photography Museum
spots.desc: Contains the complete collection of the Sakata born photographer, Ken Domon. The museum also features temporary exhibitions from other photographers.

spots.name: Honma Art Museum
spots.desc: The Honma Museum of Art is a converted old villa which once belonged to the Honma clan. The villa was used by the lords of the Sakai family in the Edo period. After Edo, it was used as a guesthouse of Sakata City. Some of the fine arts items in the museum's collection were donated by other clans in Japan, other furniture and fixings belonged to the Honma family. The museum has a garden from which…

spots.name: Sakata City Museum of Art
spots.desc: Contains a permanent collection which mainly focuses on the work of sculptor, Takahashi Go and painter, Saito Chozo. The museum is located 20 minutes from Sakata Station and has views of nearby Mount Chōkai.

spots.name: Dewa Yushinkan
spots.desc: A Tea House complex located beside Sakata City Museum of Art. It was built in 1994 and has a traditional Japanese design. You can buy green tea here for \300 and enjoy the views of the Mogami river and Mt.Chokai.

spots.name: Somaro
spots.desc: A traditional Japanese restaurant dating back to the Edo period, where guests can enjoy performances from Maiko dancers. The culture of Maiko dancing in Sakata is a result of the city's close trading relationship with Osaka and Kyoto in the past. The building has been carefully renovated and contains many traditional features. Maiko dancing performances take place daily at 14:00.

spots.name: Kaiko-ji Temple
spots.desc: Shingon Buddhism temple located in the centre of Sakata near Hioriyama Park. The temple contains the remains of two priests who starved themselves to death through a process of self-mummification called sokushinbutsu.

spots.name: Sankyo Storehouse
spots.desc: This storehouse was built in 1893 to store Shonai rice. On the storehouse's southern side, there is a line of 41 Zelkova trees, which were planted over 150 years ago to help keep the temperature of the storehouses low during the hot summer months. The modern day storehouse contains a small museum with information regarding the history and culture of Sakata, a restaurant and a souvenir shop which…

spots.name: Kachofugetsu
spots.desc: A popular local ramen restaurant known for including wontons. Has other branches around the prefecture.

spots.name: Chidokan
spots.desc: This clan school, for samurai children, was built centuries ago by Sakai Tadanori. It's the last of its kind in the region.

spots.name: Shonai Shrine
spots.desc: This shrine was built to honor Lord Sakai Tadatsugu and three of his contemporaries.

spots.name: Zenpoji Temple
spots.desc: This temple, founded in the 1200s, is known for its five-storied pagoda. There are several other temple buildings, too.

spots.name: Kamo Aquarium
spots.desc: With over 60 species of jellyfish, it has more jellyfish varieties than any other aquarium in the world. The "Jellyfish Dream House" featuring over 2000 moon jellyfish is one of the aquarium's top highlights. Although the jellyfish are the main draw, there are other exhibits and sea lion shows. The restaurant is also noteworthy for its jellyfish ramen and jellyfish ice cream, which both contain…

spots.name: Honmyoji Temple
spots.desc: Home to the mummy of Togashi Yoshibei, a samurai. His self-mummification was completed in 1683 making him the oldest of the city's mummies. It is also said to be the best-preserved.

spots.name: Nangakuji Temple
spots.desc: One of the temples housing a sokushinbutsu or Buddhist mummy. The mummy here is that of a man named Tetsuryukai who was said to have entered the temple at age 16 after being involved in a murder. He served the temple for many years until he mummified himself in 1881 at age 62.

spots.name: Churenji Temple
spots.desc: This temple houses the mummy of Tetsumonkai, a man who joined the temple at age 21 as repentance for murdering two soldiers. The temple is also said to have been built by the famous priest, Kukai.

spots.name: Uesugi Shrine
spots.desc: A shrine dedicated to Uesugi Kenshin, one of the top daimyo and samurai of the Warring States Period. The flags leading up to the shrine feature the character for "dragon", because Kenshin was known as the Dragon of Echigo Province where he ruled from, and the character "Bi" from the Buddhist war god Bishamonten who he worshipped and whom some followers believed he was the avatar. The shrine is…

spots.name: Yonezawa Castle
spots.desc: The castle was built by the Nagai Clan during the Kamakura Period. The Date Clan later took over and the famous warlord Date Masamune was born in the castle. It served as the head castle of the Date Clan for many years. After the Battle of Sekigahara, the castle was given to the Uesugi Clan as punishment for siding against Tokugawa Ieyasu who won the battle, and the Uesugi built up the castle…

spots.name: Uesugi Museum
spots.desc: A museum housing artifacts from the Uesugi Clan, including some designated as National Treasures. It has permanent exhibits as well as special exhibits.

spots.name: Toko Sake Museum
spots.local: 東光の酒蔵 Tōkō no sakekan, 酒造資料館
spots.desc: One of the largest sake museums in the Tohoku Region, the museum is located in a renovated historic sake brewery with an attached shop where you can sample and purchase sake.

spots.name: Yonezawa Uesugi Festival
spots.desc: Celebrates the history of the Uesugi Clan. On the final day there is a parade, and a reenactment of a samurai battle where you can don samurai armor and join in.

spots.name: Nasebanaru Autumn Festival
spots.local: なせばなる秋まつり Nasebanaru Aki Matsuri
spots.desc: Typical Japanese autumn festival featuring food stalls, traditional crafts and games. Lots of fun activities for children.

spots.name: Uesugi Snow Lantern Festival
spots.local: 上杉雪灯篭まつり Uesugi Yukidōrō Matsuri

On your way back, if going via the second/shorter route, keep an eye out for some whimsical corporate gravestones, including UCC's coffee cup, Yakult's drink bottle, Shin-Maywa's rocket and many more.

spots.name: Roppongi Crossing
spots.desc: The heart of Roppongi is this big intersection of Roppongi-dōri (六本木通り), under the elevated highway, and Gaien-higashi-dōri (外苑東通り). If meeting someone in Roppongi, outside hot pink Cafe Almond (カフェアマンド) is the place to be.

spots.name: Mohri Garden
spots.desc: In 2003, thousands of small Japanese killifish were liberated into this small park's pond after living in outer space as part as an experiment, they were the first animals to breed in space. You might also see duck families in Spring.

spots.name: Tokyo City View
spots.desc: This viewing deck gives you a 360º view of the city from 250 meters above sea level. Ticket includes admission to the Mori Art Museum.

spots.name: Toho Cinemas
spots.local: TOHOシネマズ 六本木ヒルズ
spots.desc: If you are going to put down the going rate of nearly ¥1800 for a movie in Tokyo, this is the place to do it. Only ¥1000 every 1st and 14th of the month for normal screens. The nine-screen cinema has futuristic decor, THX and reserved seating. On Fridays and Saturdays this theater is open all night, so you can catch a movie if you are staying out late and are planning to catch the morning train.

spots.name: Roppongi Art Night
spots.desc: Modern art invades the whole area from afternoon to the next morning. Many interactive exhibits, fun for kids too.
spots.hours: Every year on a Sat at the end of March, 17:00-05:00

spots.name: Roppongi Hills Bon Odori & Azabujuban Noryo Festival
spots.desc: Locals dance around drums in Japanese yukata dress in the Arena part of Roppongi Hills, expect Doraemon to make a surprise appearance to the delight of the kids. Continue your walk to the adjacent Azabujuban main street where all of the usually expensive restaurants set up a great variety of stalls and sell delicious food at reasonable prices.
spots.hours: Every year at the end of August 17:00-21:00 on Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.name: Don Quixote
spots.desc: Discount store, 5 floors of everything you can think of and some things you probably can't, including clothing, electronics, sex toys, costumes and Japanese souvenirs. Second floor sells drinks and food, with a large selection of snacks. One of the cheapest places in town to buy alcohol, including sake and Japanese whiskey.

spots.name: Tsurutontan
spots.desc: Huge delicious udon noodles. If you are very hungry, ask for twice or triple serving, it is free! Great udon, comfy atmosphere, but expect to wait 20 minutes before getting a seat.

spots.name: Abbott's Choice
spots.desc: Small, decent bar with NYC pop radio. Attracts a nice mix of tourists, expats and locals. A really welcome respite from the overpriced and overrated bars in the surrounding area.

spots.name: BrewDog
spots.desc: The only Japanese antenna of the Scottish franchise, this bar has twenty different European and Japanese craft beers on tap.

spots.name: Shot Bar Propaganda
spots.desc: An appropriately grubby joint decorated with propaganda posters and booming bass, playing mostly recent hits. While best known for its shots (check out the leaderboards!), their other drinks are pretty decent too and they have quite a selection of American whiskeys. The friendly staff parties as hard as the customers.
spots.price: Drinks ¥800–1000 (half price before 21:00), no cover charge

spots.name: Soul Sonic Boogie
spots.desc: Specializing in old-school funk/soul/disco. Put on your platform soles, comb your 'fro, and boogie on back to 1979.

spots.name: Terushima Shrine
spots.desc: Terushima Shrine (照島神社) is a shrine located on the coast of Ichikikushikino, characterized by the fact that the entire small rocky island of 'Terushima' constitutes the shrine grounds. It is connected to the mainland solely by a red, pedestrian-only bridge (Shinkyo), which provides the only access to the island. The main shrine hall (Honden) and other primary shrine buildings are located on the…

spots.name: Lake Kinrinko
spots.desc: A small lake (pond, really) at the east end of town, full of fish and flanked with art galleries, tea houses and the Shitanyu bath (below). Walk from the station to here, and you'll have seen most of what the town has to offer.

spots.name: Star Sand Beach
spots.desc: One of two beaches in Japan — the other is on Taketomi — where, for some reason, deposits of tiny white star-shaped shells regularly wash up. These days most of it ends up in bottles in souvenir shops. This area is also well suited for snorkeling. At low tide the corals form ponds that can be quite deep and semi secluded from others, so you may have to walk to get to the next pond.…
spots.price: Free; hot shower ¥300, ask the shop

spots.name: Udatsu Townscape
spots.local: うだつの町並み Udatsu no machi-nami
spots.desc: Straight from the Edo and Meiji Eras, Udatsu Townscape is a symbol of Wakimachi’s old days. Characteristic of the buildings are the presence of “Udatsu,” extensions of the roof that served as protection from the spread of fires. Udatsu were also symbols of fortune, and continue to proclaim the prosperity of the merchants even today. The charm of the old town continues to excite nostalgia, as the…
spots.price: Entrance free, free parking at Ai Rando Udatsu 09:00-17:00

spots.name: Ghibli Park
spots.desc: Opened November 1, 2022, the first phase includes three areas; “Ghibli’s Grand Warehouse,” “Hill of Youth,” and “Dondoko Forest.” Phase II "Mononoke Village" followed in November 2023 and Phase III "Valley of Witches" in March 2024. This is not an amusement park with big attractions or rides. It's a place to discover the wonders of Studio Ghibli where you can stroll through themed play areas…
spots.hours: Mon-Fri 10:00-17:00, Sat Sun holidays 09:00-17:00, closed on Tuesdays (or otherwise noted)
spots.price: Adult ¥1,000-4,500, child (4 yr-6th grade) ¥500-2,250, infant (3 yr or younger) Free
spots.addr: within Aichi Earth Expo Memorial Park, 1533-1 Ibaragabasama, Nagakute, Aichi

spots.name: Learn Zazen
spots.desc: Learn zazen (Buddhist meditation) with Sasagawa Roshi at his temple in the foot hills around Ono. Some spoken Japanese needed.

spots.name: Shichiken Asa-ichi
spots.desc: Fresh local vegetables are sold at this street market, whose history stretches back over 400 years.

spots.name: Former Imai Residence
spots.desc: The Imai family were producers and sellers of the local washi paper. The building was constructed in the Edo Period with the oldest udatsu in the town. The house's suikinkutsu, a bamboo water dripping garden ornament, is listed as one of the 100 Soundscapes of Japan (日本の音風景100選).

spots.name: Nakatsugawa Onsen Kur Resort Yubunesawa
spots.desc: Onsen with both indoor and outdoor baths, there are also some private baths and saunas for three to four people.

spots.name: Meijiza
spots.desc: Old kabuki theatre from 1894 that still holds kabuki plays and concerts.

spots.name: Azumino-no-sato
spots.desc: A cluster of various local cultural establishments including glasswork, photography, a cafe, a soba restaurant and vegetable market.

spots.name: Hotaka Shrine
spots.desc: The god Hokatami-no-Mikoto, the guardian deity of the region, is worshipped here. If you think you have seen plenty of shrines in Japan, this one will still surprise you with its main shrine building which is at least 100m long. Festivals include The Obisha (bow and arrow) Festival on March 17, and the Festival of Floats on the 26th (evening) and 27th September. Hokatami-no-Mikato is famous as…

spots.name: Maruyama Confectionary
spots.desc: Japanese sweets made from local apples, chestnuts, walnuts and so on.

spots.name: Tsuki-no-sakana
spots.desc: Izakaya serving sushi and soba. Try the Azumino sushi roll with Shinshu salmon and mountain potatoes

spots.name: Hōrō Art Museum
spots.desc: More than 170 works by the famous wandering artist, Kiyoshi Yamashita.

spots.name: Togariishi Jōmon Archaeological Museum
spots.desc: Togariishi Jōmon Archaeological Museum near Chino in Nagano Prefecture. The museum displays important Jōmon finds from the Yatsugatake region, including the famous National Treasure figurines Jōmon no Venus and Kamen no Megami. The nearby Togariishi archaeological site has reconstructed dwellings and remains of a large Middle Jōmon settlement.

spots.name: Patisserie Hirano
spots.local: パティスリー・ヒラノ
spots.desc: This shop draws customers from all around Nagano and the surrounding prefectures with its delicious assortment of cakes, pastries, and other rich desserts.

spots.name: Karuizawa Shaw Memorial Church
spots.local: 軽井沢ショー記念礼拝堂
spots.desc: The first church in Karuizawa, founded by the missionary A.C. Shaw. Shaw is also considered the founder of Karuizawa's resort area, which was initially used as a retreat for church workers and western expats in Japan.

spots.name: Mount Asama
spots.desc: Active volcano featured in 100 Famous Japanese Mountains (日本百名山 Nihon Hyaku-meizan), the book composed in 1964 by mountaineer and author Kyūya Fukada

spots.name: Old Karuizawa Main Street
spots.local: 旧軽井沢メインストリート
spots.desc: Stroll up and down the lively old main street which is packed with interesting shops. It is sometimes referred to as Old Karuizawa Ginza, because of the branches of stores from Tokyo's Ginza that open here in the summer. Keep your eyes open and you might see a fur coat in a shop window for a lazy ¥5,000,000 or so.

spots.name: Karuizawa Sengataki Onsen
spots.desc: Free-flowing onsen facility surrounded by the peaceful nature of Naka-Karuizawa. There's a Japanese garden, and on a clear night, you can see the stars from the outside bath.
spots.hours: Weekdays: 14:00 - 21:30; Saturdays, holidays, other "special days": 10:30 - 22:00. The last entry is 45 minutes before…
spots.addr: Sengataki Onsen, Karuizawa, Kitasaku-Gun, Nagano, 389-0111 〒389-0198 長野県北佐久郡軽井沢町千ヶ滝温泉

spots.name: Komagatake Ropeway
spots.desc: The ropeway whisks you up in 7 minutes from an elevation of 1662 meters to 2612 meters. The views towards the Minami Alps are great, and if you're lucky, you can see the figure of Mount Fuji on the horizon. You have the best chance of seeing it in the morning or in the winter. During the fall peak season, be prepared for long lines. It is recommended to descend before noon, as wait times can…
spots.price: One-way ticket ¥1210, return ¥2260; possible discounts available for foreigners, inquire at the ticket office

spots.name: Inagaki
spots.desc: Sauce Katsudon is a local speciality, and there is something of a competition among the local restaurants as to who makes the best. This restaurant consistently ranks at the top. The specials are sauce katsudon and green tea soba.

spots.name: Ajiwai Kobo Beer Restaurant
spots.local: 南信州ビール直営レストラン 味わい工房
spots.desc: A beer garden type of restaurant, where you can sample products from the local brewery.

spots.name: Suwa Geyser Center
spots.local: 諏訪湖間欠泉センター
spots.desc: A once an hour 10-min eruption. See the website for exact times.

spots.name: Fossa Magna Museum
spots.local: フォッサマグナミュージアム
spots.desc: Minerals and fossils dug up from fossa magna plates are on display at this museum.
spots.hours: 09:00-16:30, closed Mondays from December to February

spots.name: Itoigawa Geopark
spots.desc: A group of sites in the immediate environs of Itoigawa. It is part of the UNESCO Global Geoparks Network.

spots.name: Jade Beach
spots.desc: Itoigawa has some gravel beaches known for free jade collecting. Collecting jade in its origin, Kotakigawa River is prohibited, though. Fossa Magna Museum above offers appraisal services on reservation.

spots.name: Hands-on Agriculture School
spots.desc: Stay at a traditional Japanese inn, make soba noodles, catch insects, and create snow huts. Experience a rural life for the four seasons.

spots.name: Yummy Gelato
spots.desc: Great ice cream. A creative variety of seasonal flavors including jalapeno pepper, corn and wine.

spots.name: Sado Toki Preservation Center
spots.local: 佐渡トキ保護センター
spots.desc: Sado is home of the Toki (Japanese Crested Ibis), however there are no wild ibis left in Sado (the last known wild Japan-born Japanese Crested Ibis died in 2003), so visitors should head for the Sado Toki Preservation Center in order to watch the famed birds (from afar). The center is in Niibo, roughly in the middle of the island. In 2006 there were about 100 ibis on the premises.

spots.name: Nashinoki-jizo
spots.desc: Between Mano and Ogi on the road to Akadomari, look for the Nashinoki-jizo (梨の木地蔵), a small shadowy place in the woods dotted with hundreds of small statues or jizo, to which local fishermen pay their respect and which are said to cure the disease of children.

spots.name: Sadokoku Ogi Folk Museum
spots.desc: West of Ogi and very close to town itself is the Sadokoku Ogi Folk Museum (佐渡国小木民俗博物館), housing hundreds of everyday life items from old and less old times. The display is somewhat chaotic, but it is still an interesting place to visit. The museum also houses a full-scale replica of a 19th-century freight vessel, with plenty of explanations about the role of Sado as a major stop on old naval…

spots.name: Kassai
spots.desc: Basic Japanese shokudō eatery serving up all the usual prospects, freshly made. Try the fish of the day.

spots.name: Oasis
spots.desc: In Ogi. Restaurant & tennis court. Transplanted New Yorker Marcus Desoto & wife Kaoru own the Oasis. The restaurant specializes in New York staples--pasta, pizza & sandwiches--with decidedly Japanese touches. Oasis makes pizza dough the old-fashioned way, using whole grain flour seasoned with basil, naturally leavened, with fermented grapes and the crust is coated with virgin olive oil. Oasis…

spots.name: Benkei
spots.desc: in Sawata is a Sushi Bar of Sado, which will allow you to try the excellent local fish. For those staying longer on the Island, Benkei also offers delivery service.

spots.name: Nakabori-tei
spots.desc: good tonkatsu restaurant in the heart of Sawata with a very atmospheric ambiance.

spots.name: Hikoichijuku
spots.desc: They offer experiences in traditional Japanease life such as making buck wheat noodles, picking tea leaves, and splitting firewood.

spots.name: Hitsurugi Mountain
spots.desc: There are many activities at the top of this mountain including a fine view from the look-out point, walking courses, a 70-m roller slide and a campground.

spots.name: Kikugawa Sport Ground
spots.desc: The sports ground houses a baseball stadium, sport facilities and various playground equipment. Various big tournaments are held here.

spots.name: Blueberry no Sato
spots.desc: This place offers blueberry picking and sells pasta, wine, sweets and so on. All of the products are made from blueberries grown locally.

spots.name: Tomutomu no Sato
spots.desc: Local tomatoes. "Tomutomu" is a new variety of tomato locally invented.

spots.name: Sawayaka
spots.desc: Shizuoka's favorite hamburger steak restaurant chain originated here.

spots.name: Arai Sekisho and Hatago-Kinokuniya Archives
spots.desc: This important travel checkpoint on the Tokaido highway was established in 1600 by Ieyasu Tokugawa, and is the only surviving original building of such a checkpoint. The checkpoint enforced strict regulations to keep guns out of Totomi precinct, and to keep women in. The archives hall next door contains old checkpoint records.
spots.price: Adults ¥300, children ¥100, add ¥100/50 to enter the archives as well

spots.name: Honkō-ji Temple
spots.desc: The main hall is designated as a National Important Cultural Property. There is also a park here, a nice place to picnic.

spots.name: Ōigawa Railway’s Ōigawa Main Line
spots.desc: A variety of historical locomotives and carriages are used, both for the steam and for the electric services, making the line a favourite with train enthusiasts and photographers. It runs 40 km to Senzu station.

spots.name: Aokigahara
spots.desc: Also known as Jukai (樹海) or the "Sea of Trees", this forest is famous for its volcanic caverns and infamous as Japan's top suicide spot — in an average year, over 70 corpses are found.

spots.name: Lake Shoji
spots.desc: Lake Shoji is a small, horseshoe-shaped lake, idyllic-looking and with pretty views of Fuji. Boating and fishing rental available.

spots.name: Lake Motosu
spots.desc: Lake Motosu is the furthest out, also the deepest and clearest lake. Boating rental (paddleboat, rowboat) and a sightseeing boat available. You're not allowed to go out very far if you do rent a boat, though.

spots.name: View of Mt. Fuji on the ¥1000 bill
spots.desc: The image of Mt. Fuji on the back of the ¥1000 bill is taken here from the northeast shores of Lake Motosu.

spots.name: Kawaguchiko Konohana Museum
spots.desc: A museum of the popular Japanese children's book "Dayan the Cat" by Ikeda Akiko. Shows a lot of artwork from the artist's books in the world of Wachiworld. Has a lovely giftstore and cafe.
spots.hours: Mar–Nov: daily 09:00-17:00; Dec–Feb: Mon-Fri 10:00–16:00, Sat Sun holidays 09:00-17:00
spots.price: Adults ¥500, children ¥300 (discount for groups of over 15 people)

spots.name: Momiji Corridor
spots.desc: Another celebrated tree-viewing spot. A variety of beautiful trees, including maples and gingkos, line a small river on a gentle slope. The trees are lit up at night during the autumn tree viewing season.

spots.name: Itchiku Kubota Art Museum
spots.desc: This small but gorgeous museum on the northeast shore of Lake Kawaguchi was designed by Itchiku Kubota himself - one of the most famous kimono designers in Japan. Kubota's life work was reinventing the lost dyework technique of tsujigahana, a technique used heavily in Muromachi-period kimono and subsequently lost to time. The museum houses the results of the incredible series of tsujigahana…

spots.name: Fuji-Q Highland
spots.desc: One of Japan's largest amusement parks and home to Fujiyama (1996), briefly the world's tallest rollercoaster, and Dodonpa (2001), briefly the world's fastest.

spots.name: Appare sightseeing boat
spots.local: 遊覧船 天晴（あっぱれ）
spots.desc: Modeled on Japanese traditional warship, this boat runs frequent 20-minute sightseeing rides on Lake Kawaguchi during the day. A bit pricey for such a short ride, but the views of Fuji are excellent, and it's a good chance to see more of the lake. The ship is equipped with a 50-inch monitor for a rainy day!

spots.name: Miyajima History and Folklore Museum
spots.desc: A small, charming collection of folk crafts and pieces of Miyajima history, many donated by locals. The main building was built as the residence of a soy sauce mogul in the early 1800s, and has a traditional garden out back. The tour takes about one hour.

spots.name: Miyajima Brewery
spots.desc: Outdoor bar offering a selection of locally-brewed beers from Miyajima Brewery. Only small snacks are on offer, so plan to eat elsewhere before enjoying your beer at a standing table in the courtyard behind the bar.

spots.name: Kakiya
spots.desc: Restaurant specializing in oysters and only oysters. The Kakiya set offers a selection of seven traditional oyster dishes and is highly recommended.

spots.name: les Clos
spots.desc: Western European restaurant and café in a renovated 1912 mansion.

spots.name: Takaniyama Overlook
spots.local: 高谷山 霧の海 展望台
spots.desc: This overlook is at the top of a mountain just west of the town. It has great views, and is notable because you can often see the "sea of clouds" if visiting in the early morning hours, especially in the autumn and winter.

spots.name: Origami Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to showcasing some of the most intricate and beautiful examples of origami art.

spots.name: Bizen Pottery Art Museum
spots.local: 備前市立備前焼ミュージアム Bizen shiritsu bizenyaki myujiamu
spots.desc: This concrete block displays both old and new examples of Bizen-style pottery. It also has informative displays on how Bizen-yaki is produced, the various ways it is fired, and displays results of each of the firing techniques.

spots.name: Amazu Shrine
spots.desc: A shrine whose approach is lined with Bizen pottery tiles and zodiac animals. They even have ema made of Bizen pottery.

spots.name: Shizutani School
spots.desc: Ikeda Mitsumasa, a lord of Okayama, commissioned Tsuda Nagatada to build this school. Completed in 1701, it was open not only to samurai but also farmers — it is said to be the first school in the world to be open to all classes of people. Now designated a national treasure, the school is still in its original condition, and the shining ebony floor is an impressive sight. Naturally, the…

spots.name: Kei Fujiwara Museum of Art
spots.desc: A museum featuring the artwork of Kei Fujiwara, a renowned Bizen potter who was designated a Living National Treasure in 1970.

spots.name: Shoraku-ji
spots.desc: The third temple of the Chugoku 33 Kannon Temple Pilgrimage.

spots.name: BIZEN Latin American Museum
spots.desc: A museum containing a variety of historic artifacts from Central and South America.

spots.name: Bizen-yaki Traditional Pottery Center
spots.local: 備前焼伝統産業会館 Bizen-yaki dentō sangyō kaikan
spots.desc: The easiest place to give the lathe a spin, as it is on the third floor of JR Imbe Station. Workshops are held every weekend.

spots.name: Bishugama
spots.desc: Try your hand at pottery. Reservations required. Shipping can take several months.

spots.name: Curry & Cafe Shibabe
spots.desc: A famous Bizen curry restaurant with a variety of curry and rice dishes, including their own original "Cleopatra Curry" which includes local Muscat grapes.
