spots.desc: It is Hioki's most iconic shrine. Every October, there is a festival called Myoenge Myri.

spots.name: Yunomoto Hot Spring
spots.desc: It is a hot spring that has been passed down since the Edo period, so you can take a hot spring bath and eat around.

spots.name: Fukiage Hot Spring
spots.desc: It is a hot spring village located in the mountains. Various hot springs and ryokans are available.

spots.name: Super Center Nishimuta Ijuin
spots.local: スーパーセンターニシムタ 伊集院店
spots.desc: It is a supermarket located around Ijuin Station. You can purchase ingredients and daily necessities.

spots.name: Eguchi Horai-kan
spots.desc: These are markets and restaurants located around Eguchi Beach. Various kinds of seafood are also available at the market, and seafood-based dishes are available at the restaurant.

spots.name: Yunohana
spots.desc: It sells kaiseki, a traditional Japanese set meal. It is famous for its seafood dishes and hot pot rice.

spots.name: Hiyoshikichijitsu
spots.desc: This restaurant sells rice, desserts, and coffee. For the meal menu, there is an onigiri set meal.

spots.name: Matsukaze
spots.desc: It is a restaurant that sells yakiniku, a Japanese grilled meat. It sells wagyu grown in Kagoshima Prefecture.

spots.name: Cafe Kaora
spots.desc: It is a cafe in front of the sea. It also sells coffee, desserts, and simple meals.

spots.name: Hioki Chaho
spots.desc: It is a cafe that sells tea. It sells various kinds of tea and desserts using tea.

spots.name: Junchan no Daidokoro
spots.desc: This is izakaya, which has been remodeled and operated in a Japanese home. Satsumaage and raw chicken are famous.

spots.name: Sanosa Maturi
spots.desc: It is a festival of Ichikikushikino. With various stalls coming in, the event is held in July.

spots.name: Kushikino Sunset Park
spots.local: 串木野サンセットパーク
spots.desc: It is a coastal park in Ichikikushikino. It is characterized by being able to take a walk while looking at the sea.

spots.name: Former Kushikino Port Lighthouse
spots.desc: It is a lighthouse that was installed in 1951. The function of the lighthouse has now disappeared and has been transformed into a viewing facility.

spots.name: Hashimasaki Shrine
spots.desc: It is a shrine with a white dorii, which is rare in Kagoshima Prefecture.

spots.name: Mt.Kanmuri Scenic Park
spots.desc: It is a place where you can see the view of Ichikikushikino, and there is a large stone statue.

spots.name: Kannongaike Pond Civic Forest
spots.local: 観音ヶ池 市民の森
spots.desc: It is a forest with various flowers, especially many cherry blossoms. From March to April, 1,000 cherry trees bloom.

spots.name: Nishimuta
spots.local: ニシムタ 串木野店食鮮館
spots.desc: It is Ichikikushiki-no's mart and you can purchase a variety of ingredients.

spots.name: Daiwa Kushikino
spots.desc: It is a large supermarket near kamimura gakuenmae station. It sells a variety of ingredients and daily necessities.

spots.name: Misono
spots.desc: Tuna ramen is famous as a Japanese restaurant made using tuna, a specialty of Ichikikushikino.

spots.name: Kaisen Maguroya
spots.local: 串木野市漁協直営 海鮮まぐろ家
spots.desc: It is a restaurant run by the Kushikino Fishing Association, where you can enjoy fresh seafood dishes at an affordable price.

spots.name: Pasta＆Pizza silk veil
spots.desc: It's an Italian restaurant, and you can enjoy a variety of Italian food.

spots.name: IkeYa
spots.desc: It is izakaya, located around Terushima Shrine. In particular, it is famous for its seasonal raw fish and is the main dish of side dishes.

spots.name: Macchan
spots.desc: It's izakaya around the city. Motsunabe, a Japanese tripe stew, is famous.

spots.name: Paragon
spots.desc: It is a Japanese-style caffeine, Kitsaten, and you can enjoy coffee and various foods.

spots.name: Ekimae Dining Ryu
spots.local: 駅前ダイニングりゅう
spots.desc: This is izakaya located in front of Kushikino Station. We sell various side dishes and alcoholic beverages at low prices.

spots.name: Paiichi
spots.desc: This is izakaya near the city hall. It is small in size, so you can enjoy alcohol in a comfortable atmosphere. Ikageso is especially delicious.

spots.name: Eikokuji (aka Ghost Temple)
spots.desc: This temple is famous for a hanging scroll on which is drawn a grim ghost. Jittei Priest, the founder of the temple, drew the ghost of the picture which used to appear by a pond at night. After he showed the picture to the ghost, it never appeared because of its ugly appearance. The pond is behind the temple and there are lots of pond lilies in summer. It's also known for the place Takamori Saigo…

spots.name: Hitoyoshi Castle trace
spots.desc: Historical building and place to see cherry blossom with a view of Kuma river and town from the heights.

spots.name: Hitoyoshi Craft Park Ishino Koen
spots.local: 人吉クラフトパーク石野公園
spots.desc: Traditional handiworks and the specialties in Hitoyoshi and demonstrate some of them. You can also make them. There are seven plants; a place for making cutlery, a plant that you can see the process to make Shochu or Japanese alcohol, a traditional cultural industrial place, a papermaking plant, a carpentry plant, ceramics plant and a teahouse in the Japanese garden. These are samurai-style…

spots.name: Kuma River cruise (Kumagawa Kudari)
spots.desc: Departs from downtown Hitoyoshi three times a day. You sit in an old style Japanese boat and cruise downstream the Kuma river with a commentary in Japanese. The ride is relaxed and tranquil except for the odd rapids. You can pay for your car to be driven to where you disembark. It is a short drive back to Hitoyoshi. Rafting is also available.

spots.name: Mukashi Mukashi
spots.desc: Perfect place to buy traditional Japanese stuff. And what's the best is most of the items are very reasonable. You can also just enjoy watching the displays of ceramic arts, china, kimono, old toys and more! They also sell various kinds of coffee beans and teas. Free coffee is always served for the customers.

spots.name: Kijiya
spots.desc: This is a special restaurant to serve pheasant dishes. There are few restaurants to serve them in Japan. You can eat fresh meat of pheasants because they raise the pheasants by themselves. There are grilled meat, pheasant rice, sliced raw meat and so on. You can eat pheasant nabe in winter.

spots.name: Hananoki
spots.desc: You can enjoy your teatime looking at Kuma river and beautiful nature. Inside of the building is quiet and made of wood. Fresh banana and strawberry shake is popular.

spots.name: Mihokogaura
spots.desc: A beautiful bay which leads into Hososhima Commercial Port. This small beach is the only beach in Hyuga that is not constantly hammered by waves, making it the best place for swimming. Just across the road from the beach is a tiered park on the side of the hill that offers great views of the bay and some BBQ facilities.

spots.name: Isegahama
spots.desc: Isegahama was selected by the Japanese Ministry of the Environment as one of the top 100 swimming beaches in Japan. It is, however open to the ocean, thus gets both waves and riptides. There is a lifeguard stationed here during the summer.

spots.name: Okuragahama
spots.desc: Okuragahama is also among Japan's 100 top beaches according to the Ministry of the Environment. It is almost 4 km (2.4 miles), long. It is a beautiful white sand beach and the home of several surfing competitions every year. Okuragahama is the only place in Japan that has Suwabute Clams, used to make Hyuga's famous Go stones.

spots.name: Kanegahama
spots.desc: Kanegahama is another very popular surfing beach among locals.

spots.name: Umagase
spots.desc: This is the entrance to the walking path that leads to Umagase, the horse's back. This is the best place to see the coast and the beauty of the Nippo Quasi National Park. The path is paved and easy to access until you get toward the end, at which point it turns into uneven stone with railing.

spots.name: Mt. Komenoyama Overlook
spots.desc: The parking lot offers a great view of Hyuga and the surrounding area. Then, for a view of Cape Hyuga, follow the path to the 2-story concrete building and climb to the top. The building has seen better days, but the view it offers is fantastic.

spots.name: Omi Shrine
spots.desc: A small but spectacular shrine perched on some rocks right at the edge of the ocean. The design is very similar to the Great Shrine of Ise, earning Omi Shrine the nickname, the Ise of Miyazaki. This shrine is just next to Isegahama, an easy walk. Omi Shrine is most noted for the saza-ishi (a huge boulder made of naturally fused stones), a dragon egg (huge round stone), and the nearby which…

spots.name: Kurusu no Umi
spots.desc: Kurusu no Umi, or the sea cross, is a place in which the ocean wore the stone away perpendicularly forming a natural cross shape. This overlook offers a great view of the cross and more of the coastline. The rocks aparently split in a way that resembles the character 叶, "come true." The locals say that wishes made here come true, which is why some signs call this place "Sea-Cross – have ones wish…

spots.name: Hososhima Port Museum
spots.local: 細島みなと資料館旧高鍋屋
spots.desc: It was built as a residence of the Takanabe feudal lord, and transformed into a traditional hotel until 1982. This building has a lot of history. The old lady who gives tours at this museum is nice, spunky, and very knowledgeable, but does not speak English. The tour is very interesting and tells you a lot of the history of the area, but you will not get as much out of it if you don't understand…

spots.name: Bokusui Park
spots.desc: Bokusui Park is a well-equipped park good for camping, hiking, bbqs, and trying local crafts, but it is out of the way and can be tedious to access. One whole hill is covered in flowers during the spring and summer.

spots.name: Bokusui Wakayama Memorial Museum of Literature
spots.desc: A museum all about Bokusui Wakayama, a famous tanka poet who was active during the start of the 20th century.

spots.name: Mimitsu Historic District
spots.local: 美々津伝統的建造物群保存地区
spots.desc: Mimitsu was a major trade port until partway through the Meiji Period. Many of these Edo and Meiji era buildings are still standing and have been restored. It is designated as an "important preservation district for groups of historic buildings" by the Japanese Government. The traditional atmosphere and cute shops make this a wonderful side trip.

spots.name: Hyuga Historical and Folk Museum
spots.local: 日向市歴史民俗資料館
spots.desc: This museum used to be the home of a wealthy merchant during the Edo Period. It does a good job showing life in the Edo Period, but has little in the way of English explainations.

spots.name: Tobishima Maru
spots.desc: The Tobishima Maru offers boat tours of the Hyuga Coastline. These tours are typically about 30 minutes aboard a converted fishing boat. The route takes you along the cliffs of the Nippo Kaigan Quasi-National Park. Please note, parties must be 3 or more people and there is a slight discount for parties over 10 people.
spots.hours: Tours departing Mon-Fri noon; Sat 11:00, 13:00; Sun and holidays 10:30, noon, 13:30

spots.name: Hyottoko Summer Festival
spots.desc: First Friday and Saturday of August. The Hyottoko Festival is the biggest festival in Hyuga with over 2,000 dancers wearing bright red happi and masks. There are three main characters associated with this dance, hyottoko (the fool), Okame (the beautiful woman), and Kitsune (the mischievous fox). This is an interesting festival with a funny dance (yes, those pelvic thrusts are part of the dance)…

spots.name: Hyuga Jyugoya Festival
spots.desc: September or October, in accordance with the harvest moon. This festival revolves around teams doing traditional folk dancing through streets which are lined with the ever present festival food stalls. It is a nice festival, but much smaller scale than the Hyottoko festival.

spots.name: Hososhima Port Festival
spots.desc: Third Friday, Saturday, and Sunday of July. The Hososhima Port Festival is a small, but high energy local festival. It celebrates the unification of the rival districts (merchants and fishermen). The main attraction of this festival is on Sunday, when the two hand-carried two-ton floats clash on the final day.

spots.name: Aeon Hyuga
spots.desc: Aeon is a chain of shopping malls around Japan. You can find a bit of anything here for a decent price. The first floor is miscellaneous goods and a super market. The second floor is clothes.

spots.name: Trial
spots.desc: Low-priced superstore. If you're familiar with the U.S. Walmart chain, this is similar.

spots.name: Affranchir
spots.desc: Affranchir (pronounced "af-ran-seal" with soft 'a' as in apparel) is one of the more upscale and trendy stores in Hyuga, aimed at younger customers. It is sells a bit of everything, including food, clothing, household goods, and natural personal care products. It is more expensive than many stores in Hyuga, but still reasonably priced.

spots.name: Togo Roadside Station
spots.desc: This is the Togo area's information center, gift shop, and farmer's market all in one place. Practically everything sold here is locally produced.
spots.hours: 08:00-18:00, closed 1st and 3rd Thu of every month and for the New Year Holiday

spots.name: Hyuga Road Side Station
spots.desc: Part rest stop, part souvenir and local product shop. This is a good place to find local products.

spots.name: Comfort Cafe & Bar Buckayro
spots.desc: Depending on what time you go, this is either a cafe, restaurant, or bar. They specialize in pasta, sandwiches, and sweets. The bread used for the sandwiches can break your teeth, but is totally worth it.

spots.name: Shanghai Garden
spots.desc: A standard Chinese restaurant. They offer private rooms for larger parties and all you can drink options as well.

spots.name: Dosanko Ramen
spots.desc: A ramen restaurant near the station. Their specialties are butter ramen and chashuman ramen.

spots.name: Seaside Station Hososhima Restaurant
spots.desc: This restaurant serves sushi right from the fishing boat. The flagship dishes are the tuna bowl and kaisendon (mixed sashimi bowl). Only go here if you can eat raw fish.

spots.name: Uotami
spots.desc: An izakaya (a Japanese-style pub) which carries all varieties of Japanese food and drinks. Private rooms are available, as are timed all-you-can-drink services.

spots.name: Min Cafe and Shop
spots.desc: Located in a repurposed Edo-era house, this two floor cafe and shop sells all sorts of goodies. The cafe has food, drinks, and housemade desserts. The store side is two floors and sells all sorts of fancy but random items from cutlery to clothes to furniture. They also have a rotating selection that changes once a month. This rotating section has local crafts such as pottery, washi (Japanese…

spots.name: Hachiman
spots.desc: Hachiman is one of the main izakaya in Hyuga, dominating two traditional looking buildings in the center of the drinking district. Hachiman features large private rooms and a wide variety of Japanese dishes and drinks. It also has an "all you can drink" option.

spots.name: Bar Peek a boo
spots.desc: A casual American themed bar that usually attracts a younger crowd. This is one of the higher energy bars in town. The owner does not speak much English, but he still tries to crack jokes. It is pretty easy to find, look for a building with an excessive amount of unrelated signs and Christmas lights outside.
spots.price: 2 hours, all you can drink: men ¥2,500 women ¥2,000

spots.name: Ikoma Plateau
spots.desc: This is a flower garden located about 20 minutes from downtown Kobayashi City. It has a variety of flowers that bloom at different times throughout the year. The most spectacular time to visit is in October when there is over one million cosmos flowers. There are a number of events held at this time during the day and night to attract visitors from around Japan. One of Kobayashi City's important…

spots.name: Cape Toi
spots.desc: The cape is famous for its wild Misaki horses, one of just 7 breeds of Japanese horses. The horses live here, so they can be seen year-round. The birthing season goes from March to August with the most births in April and May for those who want to see foals.

spots.name: Cape Toi Lighthouse
spots.desc: It was built in 1929 at the southernmost tip of Miyazaki Prefecture. The lighthouse was originally lit by an oil lamp, but in 1945 it was lit with electricity. At 3 million candelas, it had the highest luminescence of anywhere in Asia at the time. It was rebuilt in concrete after being hit by World War II air raids and by a typhoon later the same year. It's the only lighthouse in Kyushu that can…

spots.name: Shibushiwan Daikoku Dolphin Land
spots.local: 志布志湾大黒イルカランド
spots.desc: An aquarium famous for its multitude of dolphin experiences. They have dolphin shows and a dolphin tank where you can watch the dolphins, but also have opportunities to be kissed by a dolphin, touch dolphins, and even swim with the dolphins. Aside from the dolphins, they also have penguins, turtles, and fish, as well as ponies.

spots.name: Yoshimatsu Residence
spots.desc: This is the former residence of a local politician built in the Taisho era (early 20th century). It has a hina doll display in February.

spots.name: Kojima Island
spots.desc: Kojima is an uninhabited island famous for its Japanese macaque monkeys. it was designated a natural national monument in 1934 as a monkey habitat.

spots.name: Horse-Spotting Guides
spots.desc: For those wanting to ensure that they get to see wild horses during their visit and learn about the horses and the area, there are guides that can take you to places where the horses are known to be during your visit. There are 2 options. The first option is the 90-minute guide (which also offers shorter 60- and 30-minute tours) and the other is a 3-hour walking guide of the cape.
spots.hours: The 90-minute option offers set starting times (09:30, 11:00, 13:00, 15:30). Reservations of at least 2 people are…

spots.name: Maeda Shoten
spots.desc: A small shop near the parking lot of the Cape Toi Lighthouse where visitors can buy local souvenirs and snacks.

spots.name: Takahashi House
spots.desc: The house of Genjiro Takahashi, a former member of the House of Representatives and bank owner.

spots.name: Merchant Museum
spots.desc: The museum displays artifacts from former local merchants. The museum building is the oldest structure in the historic area.

spots.name: Aburatsu Coffee
spots.desc: A relatively new and cozy cafe at the end of the Aburatsu shopping arcade.

spots.name: Atsuyaki Tamago Aratake
spots.local: 厚焼たまご あらたけ
spots.desc: Serves atsuyaki tamago, a local specialty dish of thick eggs.

spots.name: Saitobaru Tombs
spots.desc: This is a Prefectural Natural Park which contains over 300 burial mounds, called kofun, from the 4th to the 7th centuries. This is one of the largest collections of officially recognized burial mounds in Japan.

spots.name: Tenshō Embassy Statues
spots.desc: Statues commemorating the first Japanese emissary to Europe.

spots.name: Shimabara Castle
spots.desc: An unusually striking castle reconstruction due to its regular, tall yet almost pyramidal, design. Furthermore, it is unique in that the town has clearly chosen functionality over form and forgone the usual garden in favour of placing a carpark on the castle plateau. Urgh. You can park 5 metres from the door. Despite this, the thin terraced gardens behind the castle, overlooking the ocean are…

spots.name: Shinozuka Samurai Residence
spots.desc: Home of a vassal of the Matsudaira. The family owned the house for 11 generations.

spots.name: Yamamoto Samurai Residence
spots.desc: The family served 13 successive lords of Shimabara Castle, lasting until the end of the Tokugawa shogunate.

spots.name: Shimei-so
spots.desc: A villa built at the end of the Meiji Period. The garden was built later, including its famous koi pond, which runs under it.

spots.name: Mt Unzen Disaster Memorial Hall
spots.desc: A museum roughly 3 km south of the port. Covers a variety of topics based upon the destruction of southern Shimabara by pyroclastic flows from Mt Unzen's eruption and future disaster prevention.

spots.name: Mizunashi-honjin Fukae
spots.desc: Road Station. Beside 水無川 on Route 251. Roughly 4 km south of the port and walking distance from the Memorial Hall. At first glance, this may just appear to be an ordinary road rest station for long distance drivers (try not to get hung up on the apparent contradiction that this road doesn't lead anywhere further south from here) but beneath this facade it hides easily the most unique tourist…

spots.name: Arima Christian Heritage Museum
spots.desc: Tells the history of Hidden Christians on the Shimabara peninsula. It also aimes to educate visitors about the history of the Shimabara rebellions that took place at nearby Hara Castle. It also hold artifacts unearthed from the Shimabara rebellion.

spots.name: Unzen Hells
spots.desc: While Japanese 'hells' (jigoku) are given these names due to the barren and smelly landscape created by the sulfuric gases they emit, the Unzen Hells have a unique history that makes them truly hellish. From 1627 to 1630, the Unzen Hells were used by the government to torture Christians by lowering them into the boiling waters in an attempt to get them to denounce their faith. Thirty-three of…

spots.name: Sapporo Beer Factory
spots.local: サッポロビール 九州日田工場 ウエルカム館
spots.desc: A must-visit attraction for fans of Japanese beer. Located on a hill offering great views of the city, the factory offers visitors a free guided tour of the facilities followed by a 20-minute free drinking session. Reservations advisable.
spots.hours: Mon Tue Thu Fri 09:45-17:15, and public holidays 08:45-17:15

spots.name: Onta Pottery Village
spots.desc: A small mountain village based around production of distinctive Onta-yaki style pottery. The pottery is still made via the traditional method, introduced to the area by Korean potters in the 16th century. Water driven, see-saw pounders grind down the local clay for moulding into plates, pots, cups and other ceramics. The sound of the see-saws and running water combined with the scenic…

spots.name: Amagase Spa Town
spots.desc: A popular hot-spring resort town about 30 minutes drive from Hita. There are many different types of hot spring overlooking the Mikuma river. These even include a rose petal bath!

spots.name: Attack on Titan Statues
spots.desc: Hajime Isayama, the author of popular manga Attack on Titan (進撃の巨人 shingeki no kyojin) is originally from Hita; the city is capitalizing on this association. There are two statues, one at the Oyama Dam and the other near the Hita station. There's also a smartphone game.
spots.addr: 〒877-0201 大分県日田市大山町西大山2991

spots.name: Ōhara-ya
spots.desc: This very small street-corner cafe type restaurant serving sandwiches, fried chicken and pasta. The owner Luchi and his wife Eriko speak some English and are an excellent resource for further information about Hita. International menu. Not traditional. English menus available.

spots.name: Ichijiku
spots.desc: Traditional Japanese cabbage pancakes - okonomiyaki. Owned by a lovely old woman and her husband. Few English menus available.

spots.name: Takashima
spots.desc: This is one of Hita's best restaurants. Recommended dishes are Chicken Nanban and Tonkatsu, although all are very good. Great value for money. No English menu.

spots.name: Sato
spots.desc: Offers one of a kind "Phnom Penh Ramen", with a tomato and celery base. In addition to ramen, serves a wide range of dishes including Okinawan specialities such as Okinawan ramen and Goya.

spots.name: Bar If
spots.desc: This tiny cocktail bar with under ten seats but over 400 bottles of spirit lining the walls is run by the English-speaking Kohda-san. He is a former cocktail-making champion and he will make you any cocktail you can name, or tailor one to your liking. Intimate and chilled.

spots.name: Xi Amazing Bar
spots.desc: This is a sports bar/flare cocktail bar. The bar staff are very friendly and will put on a show of their cocktail spinning skills if you ask. Great drinks, great fun.

spots.name: Kyūshintei
spots.desc: An old-style tearoom which serves visitors traditional Japanese green tea

spots.name: Banjō Osakana-kan
spots.desc: There is also a store which sells local souvenirs, food, and handicrafts and a public bath that has very nice facilities. Feeding time in the early evening is the best time to go see it, because they have some types of exotic fish which become more excited and active when they realize that they can get some fish heads in their bellies.
spots.hours: 10:00-17:00 (last admission 16:45), closed on the 2nd Tue of the month

spots.name: La Vie Douce
spots.desc: A cute store in the covered walking arcade next to Umaimon-dori. It has a nice selection of handicrafts, natural bath and body products, clothes, and gift items.

spots.name: Kishōka
spots.desc: A new cake and pastry store with both Western and Japanese sweets.

spots.name: Costa Rica
spots.desc: A little coffee shop with good food, such as pizza and Japanified spaghetti. (It's not very Costa Rican, but at least it's different.).

spots.name: Oka Castle
spots.desc: Fortifications were first built here in 1145 and saw some conflict but it was not a full-fledged castle until Hideshige Nakagawa built and expanded it in 1594. The castle survived until the Meiji Period when it was ordered to be torn town. They removed all the structures during that time but the walls were left and remain there today. The ruins are impressive and large, spanning two peaks…

spots.name: Hike to Mount Yufu
spots.desc: You can hike to the top of this volcano (由布岳 Yufudake), see the crater and have a very nice view of the surroundings. Allow two hours to reach the crater (from 800m to 1500m). Then there is a junction, the left path leads to the west peak (由布岳西峰 1583m), the right one to the east peak (由布岳東峰 1580m). The east peak is an easy, although steep, walk but the west peak requires more climbing, there are…

spots.name: Kinshō Korokke
spots.desc: A simple deep-fried snack of minced meat and mashed potato it may be, but this particular "Gold Medal Croquette" was once chosen as the tastiest in all Japan. In addition to the original (¥160), there's a wide range of various flavors and toppings.

spots.name: Yu no Takean
spots.desc: Great variety of Japanese food: Toriten, Grilled beef, sashimi.

spots.name: Shizen Yuudo
spots.local: オーガニックキッチン＆cafe自然食ゆうど
spots.desc: Organic food and vegetables, in the middle of the countryside.

spots.name: Yutoku Inari Shrine
spots.local: 祐徳稲荷神社 Yūtoku Inari jinja
spots.desc: Considered to be one of Japan's top three Inari shrines, it was built in 1687 dedicated to the god Inari. The main shrine, the gohoden, stands atop vermilion wooden beams at an impressive 18 meters high. Its architecture is unique among shrines and it is considered to be among the most visually attractive, as well. It offers a lot of seasonal variation, with cherry blossoms around the shrine in…

spots.name: Kashima Castle Ruins
spots.desc: The castle was constructed in 1807 to replace the former Kashima Domain castle which was built in an area that constantly flooded. There was a palace but never a donjon, so it was spared deconstruction when the One Castle Policy was implemented. Unfortunately, it was burned down in the Saga War, but the gates survived and can be viewed today along with the remains of the moat, which lillies grow…

spots.name: Hizenhama-shuku
spots.desc: A stop along the Old Tara Road, it was successful as a sake brewing town as travelers from Nagasaki would stop to drink before continuing on the long journey to Edo. It was also a port town where trade occurred. Many buildings remain as part of the Hizenhama Preservation District including 3 of the original 12 sake breweries.

spots.name: Shin Aburaya
spots.desc: The makers of the famous Inari Youkan (稲荷ようかん) for over 80 years. It's the most popular local sweet souvenir. Inari Youkan is a red azuki beans in a white bean jelly paste. It comes in a tube with a string on top. To eat it, you push it up from the bottom and use the string to cut off the pieces at whatever thickness you prefer.

spots.name: Nogomi Doll Workshop
spots.desc: Ceramic dolls with bells representing each of the 12 animals of the Chinese zodiac. They are popular souvenirs that can be bought in the Monzen Shopping Arcade in front of Yutoku Inari Shrine.

spots.name: Gran Shario
spots.desc: A restaurant with beef curry, hamburger, and pasta sets. There is also a daily set that, as the name suggests, changes daily.

spots.name: Kiyomizu Falls
spots.desc: A temple area with a stunning waterfall. It is not to be confused with Kiyomizu Temple in Kyoto. Ogi has one other Kiyomizu Temple just 3 kilometers away from the falls, so, be careful to set them apart.

spots.name: Strawberries
spots.desc: Saga Prefecture is where many of Japan's best strawberries come from. You can buy them from farmer's stands in Ogi.

spots.name: Raw Carp
spots.local: 鯉のあらい koi no arai
spots.desc: The other dish, besides yōkan, for which Ogi is known in particular. Strawberries and Marubōro should be tried in Ogi, but because they are from Saga prefecture as a whole, and not just Ogi.

spots.name: Daikichi
spots.desc: A local, family-owned yakitori restaurant and bar. Extremely friendly staff livens up the everyday experience of barbecued meat on skewers.

spots.name: Gyoza Kaikan
spots.desc: Eat with the locals at Gyoza Kaikan, 5 minutes from Takeo Station. The gyoza and ramen here are cheap "B-class gourmet," but they're well-known in the area and the atmosphere is always lively.

spots.name: Saga Hirakawaya
spots.local: 佐嘉平川屋 武雄温泉本店
spots.desc: A modern building across from Takeo Onsen can make it easy to spot. The restaurant serves Onsen Yudofu (温泉湯豆腐), a tofu dish. The tofu is made with local hot springs, the dish therefore tastes different from a normal tofu stew. Every person must order at least one dish. If it looks too much for you, try their ice cream instead. Although the store set the main shop in Takeo, the store started from…

spots.name: Toyotamahime Shrine
spots.desc: A small shrine worships Toyotamahime. There's a white statue called Namasu, which says that you will have beautiful skin if you touch the statue.

spots.name: Aqua Story
spots.desc: The staff may not speak English, but this is a reputable dive shop

spots.name: Shi-Sa Monogatari
spots.desc: Make your own shi-sa. Perfect for a rainy day. If you like what you create you can have it fired and shipped anywhere in Japan.

spots.name: Sabo
spots.desc: A T-shirt shop. Decent designs that usually say Miyako on them.
spots.addr: Across from the A&W on Shimozato O-dori

spots.name: Uminchu Miyako
spots.desc: A T-shirt shop. Catch 22 here: the fact that you are buying an overpriced T-shirt means that you are not 海人, but the stuff inside is cool just the same.
spots.addr: 2 minutes on foot, past A&W and the Sabo shop

spots.name: Miyako Mokkou Gei
spots.desc: A sanshin (Okinawan stringed instrument) and other woodcraft shop.

spots.name: Max Valu
spots.desc: Has a pretty decent selection of stuff to keep you nourished. The food prepared in the market, ranging from fried chicken and sushi to bento "lunch boxes", is all pretty good. The retort packs of curries, pasta sauces and "hashed beef" coupled with the microwavable rice packs are cheap and convenient if nothing more. There are two locations in Hirara, one on Rt. 78 and one on 390. Both are in…

spots.name: Miyako soba
spots.desc: Available everywhere and is a cheap filling meal. Miyako soba is more like pasta or udon than the traditional Japanese buckwheat noodles. It usually has a piece of "rafute" and some "kamaboko" in it for protein. Rafute is a fatty piece of pork that has been simmered in broth. Japanese will tell you that the gelatinous fat is good for you. Kamaboko looks like plastic but it is steamed fish paste…

spots.name: Pani-Pani
spots.desc: Relaxed place run by a nice ossan (middle-aged man). Recommendations: Pizza dog, fruit juices. Stop here on the way to Tako beach or Nagamahama Beach.

spots.name: Copacabana
spots.desc: A standard bar with a reasonable staff and clientele, stays open as long as there is someone standing.

spots.name: New York, New York
spots.desc: Another standard sports bar with a big screen TV, billiards and decent bar food.

spots.name: Iriomote Wildlife Conservation Center
spots.local: 西表野生生物保護センター
spots.desc: This center provides information on Iriomote wildlife, including the Yamaneko wild cat.

spots.name: Pinaisala Falls
spots.desc: Pinaisala Falls is the largest waterfall in Okinawa prefecture, with a height of about 55 m. Pinai means a beard and sala means a waterfall, based on the dialect in Yaeyama islands. You can see this fall like a beard man from a long distance. There are several ways to get close to the waterfall.

spots.name: Ida no Hama beach
spots.desc: A remote pristine beach, can only be reached by ferries from Shirahama port at the west end of the island's road. For lunch, there is a nice small restaurant at the north side of the Funauki village. Just walk straight from the port, stay close to the water and don't turn left onto the path to the Ida beach.

spots.name: Diving Team Unarizaki
spots.desc: One of the largest dive operators on Iriomote. Free pickup from Funaura Port, no English spoken.
spots.price: Two dives from ¥13,650, full gear rental ¥5,250

spots.name: Canoe Tours Kazaguruma
spots.local: 西表島カヌーツアー風車
spots.desc: This well-famed company provide various kinds of canoeing and trekking tours from approximately ¥7,000, Free pick-up and drop-off in west area of Iriomote. Free shoe rental. Tours in English are available.

spots.name: Urauchigawa Kanko
spots.desc: Take a cruise on the Urauchi River (浦内川), the longest river in Okinawa. This river runs deep inland through dense mangroves on the west side of the island and is sometimes likened to a little Amazon. The views can be quite spectacular, especially on a still morning. On your way back, pop into the little museum on the second floor of the cruise pier building, featuring a selection of stuffed and…
spots.price: Cruises ¥1,800, canoe rental ¥800/hour, guided eco tour ¥8,400

spots.name: Iriomote Caffe
spots.desc: Light snacks and cold drinks. Outdoor terrace with river views. 6 windmills will lead your way to the cafe. Before it was named Court Chalet Plaza but now it is called iriomote cafe. This European-bar styled cafe located near the Urauchigawa cruise pier offers a fair selection of local souvenirs, and has a café-restaurant and rental eco-car. 10:30-sunset daily.

spots.name: Hook
spots.desc: Pleasant beachside café offering views out into the bay and a selection of daily set lunches with drink for ¥1000.

spots.name: Shinhachi Shokudo
spots.desc: Good soki soba and other wholesome meals, and packed with locals.

spots.name: Kawanoe Castle
spots.desc: Kawanoe Castle was built in Iyo Province (modern Ehime Prefecture) to protect the province from invasions from Sanuki Province (modern Kagawa). Due to its location at the border with Sanuki Province, Tosa Province (modern Kochi), and Awa Province (modern Tokushima), it was under constant attack during the Warring States Period. All of Shikoku's provinces fought here until it was eventually…

spots.name: Paper Town Museum
spots.desc: Has a handful of exhibits related to local paper production and visitors can make their own paper postcards with reservations.

spots.name: Nora-dokei
spots.desc: A clock built to be visible to farmworkers while they worked the fields. Now it's a popular historic sight and symbol of Aki. Sunflowers and various other flowers bloom in front of it at different times of the year.

spots.name: Samurai Quarters
spots.desc: The historic street is home to samurai residences, one of which can be entered. The road itself maintains the walls and hedges that existed when the samurai roamed the streets.

spots.name: Aki Castle
spots.desc: It was an important castle from which they were able to launch attacks at Awa Province. Today, the moats and some of the castle walls remain.

spots.name: Ryugado Cave
spots.desc: One of Japan's top three caves, visitors can tour this large limestone cavern. At the cave's entrance real Yayoi Period pottery is visible in the walls. The cave is 4 kilometers in length (about 2.5 miles). Visitors are able to explore nearly half (1.5km or 1 mile) of it.
spots.price: ¥1,000 for normal visits, ¥1,500 for the 'adventure course' (must be in high school or older for adventure course)

spots.name: Anpanman Museum
spots.local: アンパンマンミュージアム
spots.desc: Anpanman's creator is from Kochi, so naturally the museum dedicated to the tasty superhero is here, as well.

spots.name: Kagamino Park
spots.desc: One of the most popular places in the prefecture for seeing cherry blossoms, it is on the list of Japan's top 100 places to see cherry blossoms.

spots.name: Hachioji Shrine
spots.desc: Built in the Muromachi Period. The road between the shrine and its torii is lined with cherry trees, making it a nice spot for hanami.

spots.name: Keiki-So
spots.desc: This is the spot where the singer Yoshii Isamu secluded himself. It was used in the Meiji, Taisho, and Showa Periods. It is located next to the Yoshii Isamu Memorial Museum, so if you come to see his museum, stop here to see his former home.

spots.name: Todoro Falls
spots.desc: One of the nation's top 100 falls, it is considered to be a natural monument.

spots.name: Ryuga Onsen
spots.desc: Located in the same area as Ryuga-do Cave, it makes for a nice place to relax after exploring the cave.

spots.name: Nakamura Castle
spots.desc: Also known as Shimanto City Folk Museum (四万十市郷土博物館), it is a reconstructed castle with exhibits related to the city's history.

spots.name: Yasunami Waterwheels
spots.desc: An attractive line of waterwheels that were historically used to help irrigate the rice fields. They are especially beautiful in June when the hydrangea are in bloom.

spots.name: Sada Chinkabashi Bridge
spots.desc: Sada's Chinkabashi is among the most famous and easily recognizable of the submersible bridges that cross the Shimanto River thanks to the bright blue columns that hold it up. It also lies lower than the other bridges, so you are closest to the river when crossing, which is said to give it greater appeal.

spots.name: Yoshida Residence
spots.local: 藍商佐直 吉田家住宅 Aishō Sanao Yoshida-ke Jūtaku
spots.desc: The residence of the Yoshida family. This family traded in indigo, a product for which the region was famous. It was constructed in 1792 by Sagawaya Naoei, who changed his name to Yoshida Naoei. Next to the Yoshida residence is the aigura, a building which was used by the Yoshida family to store indigo. Nowadays the first floor is a gift shop, and the second floor is a cafe.
spots.price: adults ¥500, children ¥250, includes entry to the Wakimachi Theater

spots.name: Wakimachi Theater
spots.desc: Built in 1934, Wakimachi Theater was a playhouse for Kabuki, Rōkyoku (storytelling accompanied with Shamisen music), and other such entertainment. In the post-World War II era, it became a movie theater, and was then closed in 1995. It was scheduled for demolition, but after Shōchiku Films decided to use it as a location in their famous film, The Man Who Catches Rainbows, it was brought back into…
spots.price: adults ¥200; discount for groups of 15 or bigger; prices may differ when there is a performance

spots.name: Former Nagaoka Residence
spots.local: 旧長岡家住宅 Kyū Nagaoka-ke Jūtaku
spots.desc: The former Nagaoka Residence used to be at the foot of the southern slopes of the Sanuki Mountains. In 1976 the residence was awarded the status of 'Important Cultural Property'. In 1979 it was disassembled and reassabled in the Wakimachi area. The house is 12 m long and 6.6 m wide. It has a Yosemune-style thatched roof. The outside walls aren't made from the usual cedar tree bark or wooden…

spots.name: De Rijke Dam
spots.local: デ・レイケ砂防ダム De-Reike Sabō-damu
spots.desc: This anti-erosion dam, the Ōtani River Dam, was built under the supervision of Dutch civil engineer Johannis de Rijke between 1886 and 1887. During the time in which De Rijke was active in Japan (1873-1903), several of these dams were built in the Tokushima region, but this is the only one that has been preserved. In 2002 the dam was awarded the status of Nationally Registered Tangible Cultural…

spots.name: Anmitsukan
spots.desc: Flower exhibit and store. Mima is known for the cymbidium orchid, which blooms late November to March. Free parking.

spots.name: Saimyō Temple
spots.desc: Temple number 3 on the Fudō Myō-ō 36 Temple Route. This temple was constructed during the Tenpyō era (729-748).

spots.name: Anrakuji Temple
spots.desc: This famous temple is the oldest and most influential Jodo sect (Pure Land Buddhism) temple of Shikoku. It is also known for its Noh theatre stage, where every year there are Noh and Kyōgen performances. Its vermillion-laquered, multistoried gate is known as the Red Gate, and is one of the five biggest gates in the prefecture.

spots.name: Ganshōji Temple
spots.desc: This temple was constructed during the Nara period (710-794), and is home to the oldest dry landscape garden in Shikoku, which is believed to be constructed during the Nanbokuchō period (1336-1392). It has been constructed with ishigumi, the same stone arranging technique used in Kyoto's Tenryū-ji.

spots.name: Saikyō Temple
spots.desc: This Jōdo Shinshū temple was of a comparable status with the Anraku Temple during the Hansei period (1603-1867). A notable sight is the more than 200-year-old Hikaku Pine Tree, and one of the temples treasures is the over 750-year-old statue of St. Shinran, the founder of the Jōdo Shinshū sect.

spots.name: Rinshō Temple
spots.desc: This Jōdo Shinshū temple was built at the end of the Muromachi period (1336-1573). Next to the Chinese-style front gate there is a famous, large gingko nut tree, which turns a beautiful golden-yellow in late autumn.

spots.name: Jōnen Temple
spots.desc: This temple, also part of the Jōdo Shinshū sect, has a 1490-m² garden in front of the main entrance, called the Garden of Peace.

spots.name: Izanami Shrine
spots.desc: The Izanami shrine is one of the eleven shrines in the Mima region that were listed in the Engi-shiki. The Engi-shiki was completed in 927, during the Heian period (794-1185), and contained a summary of all the shrines throughout the country. There were seven shrines in the entire list that were named after Izanagi, but this shrine was the only one named after Izanami. It is thought that in many…

spots.name: Ikezuki Park
spots.desc: The park was named for the famous horse Ikezuki, which belonged to Shogun Yoritomo, and was ridden by commander Sasaki Takatsuna, during the Genpei War (1180-1185). The park features the gravesite of Ikezuki’s mother.

spots.name: Aoki Residence
spots.desc: The Aoki residence was constructed in 1915, as a retirement home for the Aoki family. It sits on a 3,590-㎡ plot of land, which is surrounded by a 2-m-high plaster wall. On the premises are the main living building, a shed, and several two storied storage houses, made from both earth and wood. The main building is approximately 20 m long, and 11 m wide, and features a tatami room, a reception, a…

spots.name: Dan Tombs
spots.local: 段の塚穴 Dan no Tsuka-ana
spots.desc: Dan no tsuka-ana, or the Dan tombs, are two ancient burial mounds located on the point of a river terrace near Mima city’s temple town. Both burial mounds were constructed about 1400 years ago, in the late Kofun period (approximately 250-538). They were constructed 25 meters apart. The eastern, large burial mound is known as the Taiko-tsuka, or ‘Drum tomb’, and the smaller one is known as the…

spots.name: Honrakuji Temple
spots.desc: The Honraku-ji was founded in 828 by the monk Sō-Keiun of the Buddhist Shingon sect as a place of meditation, and was initially known as the Rengesan Honraku Temple. In 1131, the restored temple was reopened by the monk Sō-Yūjun. Because of the temple's strategic position, where Mt. Takamaru and the Yoshino River meet, it was used as a fort during the Sengoku period (1467-1568). In the late…

spots.name: Miki Residence
spots.desc: The Miki residence, a traditional wooden house with a thatched roof was built around the start of the Edo period (1603-1867). It shows characteristic elements of old samurai residences. Being the oldest surviving privately owned house in Tokushima prefecture, in 1976 the residence was awarded the status of Important Cultural Property. Furthermore, 45 ancient scrolls dating back to the Kamakura…

spots.name: Kawai Mountain Pass Weeping Cherry Trees
spots.local: 川井峠のシダレザクラ Kawai-tōge no shidarezakura
spots.desc: On the slope of the mountain, there are about 20 weeping sakura (cherry blossom) trees. Sakura blooming season is generally between late March and mid April. The weeping sakura trees bloom about one week after the regular trees (which aren't on a slope).

spots.name: Mt. Tsurugi
spots.desc: With a height of 1955 m, this is the second highest mountain in western Japan. At the top, there are splendid panoramic views of the area, and on clear days one can see as far as the Seto Inland Sea. Mt. Tsurugi opens on May first, as it is closed during winter. From the top of the cable car, it's about a 40-minute climb to the summit. From the Mt. Tsurugi summit, you can also walk to the summits…

spots.name: Mima Motor Land
spots.local: 美馬美馬モーターランド Mima Mōtārando

spots.name: Shirahito shrine o-mato archery festival
spots.local: 白人神社御的祭 Shirahito-jinja o-mato matsuri
spots.desc: According to an old legend, the samurai Minamoto Tametomo (1139-1177) visited emperor Sutoku Jōkō (1119-1156), who had fled to Sanuki in Kagawa prefecture after the Hōgen Revolt of 1156. Tametomo stood on the Aiguri ridge, on the border of Kagawa and Tokushima prefectures, and shot his bow. The arrow flew towards the Anabuki region, and finally landed at the Shirahito shrine. Nowadays, the bow in…
spots.hours: The 14th day of the first month of the old Japanese calendar

spots.name: Sakura viewing
spots.desc: Particularly the cherry blossom at the Yaoyorozu-no-kami-no-goten Shrine, and the shidarezakura (weeping cherry blossoms) of the Kawai Pass.

spots.name: Mt. Ōtaki spring fesitval

spots.desc: Mikagura (ancient Shinto music) at the Nishitera shrine, and a holy fire at the ōtaki temple.

spots.name: Opening of Mt. Tsurugi
spots.desc: Start of the climbing season for Mt. Tsurugi. Due to snow, Mt. Tsurugi can't be climbed during winter. Activities start around 10:30, and include the carrying of a mikoshi portable shrine.

spots.name: Anabuki river homemade rafting tournament
spots.local: 穴吹川筏下り大会 Anabuki-gawa ikada sagari taikai
spots.desc: People from all over participate in homemade rafts on a 5-km or 2.5-km course on the Anabuki river. Teams compete for fastest times and best-looking raft.

spots.name: Summer festival at Shikoku Saburō-no-Sato
spots.local: 四国三郎の郷サマーフェスティバル Shikoku saburō no sato samāfesutibaru
spots.desc: This event is held every year at the Yoshino Riverside Plaza, adjacent to the Shikoku Saburō-no-Sato, and features many events, from concerts to fireworks, canoeing and Awa-odori performances. Many families come here to enjoy the final days of their summer vacation together.

spots.name: Udatsu festival
spots.local: うだつまつり Udatsu matsuri
spots.desc: Events in the Udatsu street area. Some years, the popular television character Mito Kōmon (水戸黄門) participates in parades.

spots.name: Shamisen mochi-tsuki
spots.local: 三味線もちつき Shamisen mochi-tsuki
spots.desc: Pounding steamed rice into the dough that is used for making rice cakes, accompanied by shamisen. During the Edo period (1603-1867), when Wakimachi was a flourishing merchant town, merchants used to hire geisha to play the shamisen, and workers to pound the rice, while singing a mochi song. This was done at the end of the year. It is thought that this is how this tradition started. The current…

spots.name: Jidaiya Village of Bamboo Puppets
spots.desc: This store in the Udatsu street area sells bamboo puppets (竹人形 take-ningyō), that are depicted dancing the Awa-odori dance.

spots.name: Airando Udatsu Rest Area
spots.local: 道の駅藍ランドうだつ Michi no eki airando udatsu
spots.desc: Formerly the indigo warehouse of the Yoshida family, this building has been turned into a cafe and shop. The cafe allows for lunches as well as coffee, while the shop sells all sorts of local products, such as Mima-kara and indigo-dyed clothes and accessories.

spots.name: Matsuri-zushi
spots.local: 祭り寿司 脇町店 Matsuri-zushi wakimachi-ten
spots.desc: A conveyor belt sushi restaurant. Cheap plates are ¥105.

spots.name: Maharajah Spice
spots.desc: A small Indian restaurant. Naan, rice and salad are all-you-can-eat. The main attraction has to be the naan; they serve about 15 kinds, ranging from plain and bacon naan to mentaiko (fish egg) and caramel butter naan.

spots.name: Quench Cafe Premiere
spots.desc: A relatively new cafe, that serves (ice) coffee, tea, cakes, and dinner sets, among others.

spots.name: Cafe Kadoya
spots.desc: A cute little cafe in an old building right on the Udatsu street (across the waterwell). The menu isn't very large, but the atmosphere is nice and laidback.

spots.name: The Children's Ferrite and Science Museum
spots.local: フェライト子ども科学館
spots.desc: This is a small science museum. There are many hands-on exhibits involving magnets, sound, and various other topics. A few exhibits have information in English. Outside, there is a large trampoline and jungle gym.

spots.name: Shirase South Pole Expedition Memorial Hall
spots.local: 白瀬南極探検隊記念館
spots.desc: A memorial for Nobu Shirase, a man from Konoura, who led the first Japanese expedition to the South Pole.

spots.name: Naso no Shirataki
spots.desc: This is a 26-m waterfall. Not far from the waterfall is the Kinpo Shrine.

spots.name: Mototaki Fukuryusui Underflow
spots.desc: This is a 30-m-wide low waterfall. The wide low waterfall creates a mist, which contrasts with the green moss.

spots.name: Shishigahana Wetlands
spots.desc: This wetlands area is a great spot for hiking in the woods. Some of the trees here are centuries old and famous for their age. The hiking trails are mostly tree-covered, and some of the streams naturally have a slightly bluish color. The most popular route is a well-signed 5km loop.

spots.name: Tsuchida Farm
spots.desc: This farm has a restaurant that serves lamb, among other things. It also has soft-serve ice cream, as well as cheese and sausage. In a separate building, there is a small petting zoo. Outdoor benches provide nice views of the plateau and surrounding mountains.

spots.name: Nodoka
spots.desc: The owner makes excellent food, including fresh udon, soba, rice bread, and rice bread pizza.

spots.name: Sasanoi
spots.local: 寿し割烹うなぎ笹乃井
spots.desc: This is a sushi restaurant with good sushi and friendly owners.
spots.price: Lunch and specials for ¥1000-1500; dinner for up to ¥5,000

spots.name: The Jolly Roger Bar
spots.desc: This bar has a mild pirate theme, and is said to have very friendly staff and customers.

spots.name: Nyuto Onsen
spots.desc: A lot of old hot springs. These are famous resorts for Japanese.

spots.name: Tamagawa Hot Springs
spots.desc: This onsen has the highest flow rate in Japan at 150 liters/second.

spots.name: Paper Balloon Festival
spots.desc: In this festival dating back more than a century, large decorated paper balloons are lit and float off in the evening sky. The evening can get cold, so warm clothing is recommended.

spots.name: Five-Colored Ponds
spots.desc: Crystal-clear springwater ponds in various colours formed by Bandai-san's eruption. Well worth checking out if you are in the area. A one hour walk links all the ponds. Take a bus from Inowashira station to Goshikinuma Iriguchi (五色沼入り口) bus stop. The walk finishes at Bandaikogen Eki (磐梯高原駅) where the bus can take you back again.

spots.name: Hibara-ko lake
spots.desc: Formed in 1888 by the eruption and resulting landslide across the valley, Hibara-ko is a clear mountain lake well-stocked with Black Bass fish. Lake sightseeing cruises depart from Bandaikogen Eki.

spots.name: Hanabusa
spots.desc: Various kinds of ramen and gyoza (dumplings) are served here
spots.price: Large bowls of ramen start from about 700

spots.name: Rire bros.

spots.name: Shirakawa Beer Station
spots.local: 白河ビアステーション
spots.desc: Sells snacks and large pitchers of beer for about 1100. Beer Station has a friendly atmosphere complete with photo-phobic dog Rabuchan. It is only open during summer, from about 5pm, but can vary randomly according to the owner's whim.

spots.name: Cariboo
spots.desc: Nakamachi 42, Basement of the Shirai Building (中町４２白井ビル地下), is a Jamaican bar with occasional live DJs playing reggae music. The owner's wife is Jamaican, and makes a good range of light meals, including Jerk Chicken and Pepper Shrimp. Red stripe beer is available (¥680), as are a variety of rums (from ¥500). Downstairs opposite the Joyo Bank in by Shirakawa station. Look for the English sign.

spots.name: Irimizu Cave
spots.desc: Another cave, 6km away from Abukumado Cave. This undeveloped cave is for the hard-core adventurer. Its 3 interconnected courses follow a 10°C stream as its snakes its way through darkness. The water height is rarely higher than your ankles and not swift. Water drips from the ceiling so raincoats may be a good idea. A hard hat with light is highly recommended.

spots.name: Nobezawa Silver Mines
spots.desc: These are the former silver mines for which Ginzan Onsen's name is derived. The mines were active during the Edo Period prior to the existence of the onsen town. It is said that it was the miners who discovered the onsen waters that the town was then built around.

spots.name: Shirogane Falls
spots.desc: Waterfalls just north of Ginzan Onsen. In the summer, they light up the waterfall at night.

spots.name: Izu Kokeshi Workshop
spots.desc: This is where you can buy Izu Kokeshi. It is also where they make them.

spots.name: Takahashi Nittō Shoten
spots.desc: This liquor store is one of the only places in the region that has a decent selection of Belgian beer. It also has a lot of Japanese liquor and sake.

spots.name: Tendo Shogi Museum
spots.desc: A compact but comprehensive museum about the history of shogi, with impressive displays on how pieces are made, some gorgeous sets, and reams of information on grandmasters through the years. Displays are only in Japanese, but the front desk can provide an excellent English booklet, and the exhibits are easy to follow. Next door is a small shogi parlor; if you arrive on a day the museum is…
spots.addr: JR Tendo Station, first floor (east exit)

spots.name: Hiroshige Museum of Art
spots.desc: This museum has a small collection of prints and artifacts related to the ukiyo-e master, Hiroshige. It is not intended to cover his entire career, focusing mostly on lesser-known work that he did for the Tendo samurai clan. Descriptive materials are only in Japanese. Upstairs are a decent-sized library and another gallery for temporary (non-Hiroshige) exhibits.

spots.name: Eishundo
spots.desc: There are a few shogi shops in town, but this one is easy to find and readily open to visitors. Don't expect much more than a grunt from the resident craftsman, but you can see bit of the process, and there are a few shelves of affordable shogi pieces and Tohoku's native kokeshi dolls for sale in the next room.

spots.name: Maruza Chikuan
spots.desc: An izakaya with private rooms.

spots.name: Hamanasu Onsen
spots.desc: An onsen, rotemburo, and sauna.
spots.addr: 日本 秋田県にかほ市金浦中谷地２０−１

spots.name: Hoshi no Mura Observatory in Takine
Mushi-Mushi Land in Tokiwa
spots.desc: A rhinoceros beetle theme park.

spots.name: Shirogane Yu
spots.desc: A public hot spring in Ginzan Onsen.

spots.name: Taisho Roman-kan
spots.desc: A souvenir shop that also has a few eating options.

spots.name: Kurumaya Ramen
spots.desc: This shop has tasty miso ramen.

spots.name: Olive
spots.desc: An Italian pizza and pasta restaurant.

spots.name: Sultan
spots.desc: An Indian restaurant.

spots.name: Site of Reversible Destiny
spots.desc: Fall on your arse. No, seriously. Although part of a broader, unfinished vision for Yōrō, this site is for all intents and purposes a theme park where the theme is you, yes you, falling on your butt. Its sloped surfaces and utterly bizarre design is intended to disorient visitors. Try not to miss the pitch-black tunnel system on the northwest side, but don't worry, there's no creepy crawlies…

spots.name: Fujifilm Square
spots.desc: Fujifilm's exhibition space for the latest and greatest in photography. Exhibits are usually free and well worth a visit.

spots.name: Ninja Akasaka
spots.desc: The entrance is a little difficult to find, but what do you expect from a restaurant designed like a hidden ninja fortress? Navigate through dark corridors, over bridges and trap doors to your hidden room, where ninja waiters attend to your needs while performing tricks and illusions. The food is delicious as well as being presented in unique ways that are sure to entertain. Pre-set menus…

spots.name: Rokuhara
spots.desc: Specializes in kushiage, counter in a very Japanese cozy atmosphere.

spots.name: Ichiryu Bekkan
spots.desc: Their speciality (and only dish) is the Seolleongtang soup, a white broth with beef, served with many side dishes including kimchi. Add salt and pepper yourself to the soup at your convenience.

spots.name: Arita Porcelain Park
spots.local: 有田ポーセリンパーク
spots.desc: A considerably large replica of a wannabe German village, located in the outskirts of Arita on the road to Hasami. Most stunning is probably the copy of the “Zwinger” a famous German castle in the city of Dresden. Inside the castle is a permanent exhibition of European porcelain held in one track and Arita porcelain in the other. Both are pretty impressive. Behind the castle lies a European style…

spots.name: Mihama American Village
spots.desc: An Americanized shopping and dining complex made to resemble an American beach such as Venice Beach, Santa Monica, etc. Popular among U.S. military members due to its close proximity to many U.S. Marine bases. The area has a Ferris wheel, a few hotels, many clothing and souvenir stores and restaurants of various cuisine, and Sunset Beach. Plus there is live entertainment almost nightly.

spots.name: Cape Zanpa
spots.desc: Peninsula on the western side of the island near Yomitan Village. Has a lighthouse and a beautiful beach. Also is where the famous sweet potato-flavored cookies are made.

spots.name: Hamahiga Island
spots.desc: East of Okinawa Island accessible by the Sea Road (a sight in itself). Hamahiga Island has many rock formations, many shaped like mushrooms.

spots.name: Busena Marine Park
spots.desc: Peninsula with an underwater observation tower, and a glass-bottom boat that leaves every 20 minutes. Free shuttle bus that looks like a tram.
spots.price: Boat & tower combo tickets ¥2100/1050 adult/child. Tickets for just the deck or just the boat are available too.

spots.name: Kihōin
spots.desc: Japan's southernmost temple, but it's not much to look at. It houses about 3,000 historical artifacts and local handicrafts gathered from around the island. With no English explanations, visitors may find it to be of limited interest; however, it is essentially the island's history and culture museum.

spots.name: Nagomi-no-tō
spots.desc: A purpose-built concrete tower that offers views over the entire island. The steps up are very steep.

spots.name: Folkcraft Museum
spots.desc: Has local artisans weaving traditional Yaeyaman minsā cloth.

spots.name: West Pier
spots.desc: This disused pier is where Taketomi's villagers used to set off by canoe to tend their rice fields on Iriomote. Today, it's Taketomi's best sunset-watching spot, but you'll have to stay overnight to catch this nightly event.

spots.name: Kondoi Beach
spots.desc: A spectacular expanse of white sand and turquoise water, and the only beach where swimming is allowed.
spots.price: Free toilets and showers; expensive beach gear rentals

spots.name: Kaiji Beach
spots.desc: Taketomi is one of only two islands in Japan (the other is Iriomote) that accumulate this 'sand' formed from the shells of thousands of tiny crustaceans. While Star Sand Beach (星砂の浜 Hoshizuna-no-hama) usually refers to the more accessible Kaiji, you can also find the stuff at the rarely visited Aiyaruhama (アイヤル浜) near the Hoshinoya resort. People are not allowed to take the sand — you must…

spots.name: Shidame-kan
spots.desc: Lovely little cafe-restaurant-bar right below the Nagomi-no-to tower, serving up a wide variety of Okinawan and Japanese staples. Best known for their rafti-don (ラフティ丼, ¥1,000), a rice bowl dripping with porky goodness, and their home-made sata-andagi donuts (2 for ¥100). Stays open late, with customers hanging out after dinner drinking awamori and sampling snacks.

spots.name: Takenoko
spots.desc: A well-known island eatery, Takenoko is justly famous for their rendition of Yaeyama soba, which they've been serving since 1975. Order the soki variant with melt-in-your-mouth pork ribs, spice it up with a dash of their homegrown piyashii pepper or a careful slug of kuchu chilli-infused awamori, then cool down with a bowl of shaved ice (kakigōri).

spots.name: Minamidera
spots.local: 家プロジェクト 南寺 ジェームズ・タレル
spots.desc: “Backside of the Moon” by James Turrell. Architecture by Tadao Ando. Walk into a building in complete darkness and feel the sensation after the lights are eventually slowly turned on.

spots.name: Kadoya
spots.local: 家プロジェクト 角屋
spots.desc: “Sea of Time '98”, “Naoshima’s Counter Window”, “Changing Landscape” by Tatsuo Miyajima. Watch a "sea" of LED numbers counting up and down.

spots.name: Go'o Shrine
spots.local: 家プロジェクト 護王神社
spots.desc: “Appropriate Proportion” by Hiroshi Sugimoto. You can get into the shrine by taking the little path to the right, i.e. the seaside. It's quite simply incredible so don't miss it.

spots.name: Ishibashi
spots.desc: “The Falls” and “The Garden of Kū” by Hiroshi Senju. The former large expansive home of the Ishibashi family, a successful salt producer during the Meiji Period.

spots.name: Haisha
spots.local: 家プロジェクト はいしゃ
spots.desc: “Dreaming Tongue/Bokkon-Nozoki” by Shinro Ohtake. Haisha means "dentist" and this was once the house of a dentist.

spots.name: Gokaisho
spots.local: 家プロジェクト 碁会所
spots.desc: “Gokaisho” by Yoshihiro Suda. Gokaisho means "place to play go" and this was a gathering place for people to play the game of Go

spots.name: Zuigan-ji Temple
spots.desc: Matsushima's top Zen temple with over a thousand years of history, but not a top choice for relaxation: tickets are sold from vending machines and guides shouting into megaphones herd tour groups through the temple, which has been turning into a museum with everything of interest partitioned off and/or packaged in glass cases. The approach with its moss-covered Kannon statues is atmospheric…

spots.name: Fukuura Island
spots.desc: Connected to the mainland by a long bridge, the island is crisscrossed in all directions by paths small and large, paved and muddy, well-trod and overgrown. A circuit of the island won't take more than an hour and there are some very sparsely beautiful spots to be seen. An interesting anecdote, there is a local superstition that crossing the bridge with a girlfriend/boyfriend will cause a breakup.

spots.name: Ōtakamori
spots.desc: One of the 4 Famous Places to view Matsushima Bay and a good place to catch the sunset over the island. The start of the 1-km trail to the top is some 3 km from the Pila Youth Hostel in Oku-Matsushima.

spots.name: Eiheiji Temple
spots.local: 大本山永平寺 Daihonzan Eiheiji
spots.desc: An extremely impressive structure totally constructed from wood, with intricate frescoes decorating the inner walls. The atmosphere of tranquility is further enhanced by a stream that flows through the inner court yards. The temple is a true testament to the ability of the ancient Japanese to fuse architecture and nature in a seamless and timeless endeavor. Eiheiji is the head temple of the Soto…

spots.name: Meditate at Eiheiji Monastery
spots.desc: Visitors can apply to attend a two-day (参籠 sanrō) or three-day (参禅, sanzen) meditation training program at Eiheiji Monastery. Since the 3-day program is quite strenuous, applicants must have long Zazen (meditation) experience to gain admittance. While the program is advertised as 2 or 3 days, it is in fact less as the first day activities start 16:00 with those on the final day ending at 10:00.…

spots.name: Dansuke Goma Dofu
spots.desc: A traditional food chosen by Eiheiji temple to keep its abstemious monks vital. Made of ground sesame and kuzu (葛) powder. Smooth and chewy. Enjoy the rich flavor of sesame with miso paste. There is a cafe in the shop where you can enjoy fresh goma dofu.

spots.name: Ikeda Onsen Honkan
spots.desc: The original Ikeda Onsen, open exclusively for day visitors. It has indoor baths, a small sauna, and nice outdoor onsen. Some of the outdoor baths are under a roof, but hats are provided for use in the open outdoor onsen if it rains.

spots.name: Ikeda Onsen Shinkan
spots.desc: A newer and larger onsen than the honkan that mainly serves day visitors but also has overnight accommodations.

spots.name: Gifu Sekigahara Battlefield Memorial Museum
spots.local: 岐阜関ケ原古戦場記念館, Gifu Sekigahara Kosenjō Kinenkan
spots.desc: This new museum (built 2020) offers a good introduction to the battle itself. It is especially helpful because the first two exhibits (both visual media - a bird's eye view of the battle and an anime-like 4D theater movie depicting what it was like in the fray) provide the necessary background to understand how the 6-hour battle went and why Tokugawa won. The upper floors contain mainly replicas…
spots.price: ¥500 for adults, ¥400 for students, and ¥300 for kids

spots.name: Battlefield Commencement Marker
spots.local: 国指定史跡 関ヶ原古戦場 開戦地
spots.desc: A marker dedicated to where the first shots of the battle were fired. It also has benches and information boards that detail the order of battle and positions.

spots.name: Eastern and Western Head Mounds
spots.desc: On opposite sides of the train tracks, two shrines commemorate the sites where two large mounds of the severed heads of fallen soldiers were buried. As per traditional Japanese concepts of reverence for the dead, these shrines are dedicated to all who fell in the battle, not solely forces of one side.

spots.name: Field Camp Ground
spots.desc: Also called "Tokugawa's Final Encampment", this is the spot where Tokugawa Ieyasu held a council meeting after the end of the battle and was presented with the decapitated heads of the enemy's leaders. A small shrine marks the spot.

spots.name: Grave of Okudaira Sadaharu
spots.desc: A leader who fought under the traitor Kobayakawa. He died while attacking Otani Yoshitsugu's army. The grave was built here by one of his descendants.

spots.name: Ishida Mitsunari's Encampment
spots.desc: To the north of the town on a small hill that offers a commanding view of both the town and the battlefield. This is where Ishida Mitsunari, Tokugawa Ieyasu's main opponent and leader of the Western Alliance at the battle, based his camp. Two rows of wooden palisades flank the base of the hill, and a stairpath allows visitors to walk up to the memorial at the top. Can easily be seen from the…

spots.name: Kobayakawa Hideaki's Encampment Site
spots.desc: Infamous traitor to the Western Army, Kobayakawa Hideaki is considered by many historians to have tipped the battle in the Tokugawa (Eastern army's) favor. He defeated Otani Yoshitsugu and then attacked Ukita Hideie's army, throwing them into dissarray and eventual defeat. After the battle, he was made leader of Bizen Province, the province previously lead by Ukita Hideie who he betrayed and…

spots.name: Okayama Signaling Hill
spots.desc: To the northeast of the town, this was from where the flare was fired that signaled that the Western Alliance needed reinforcements. The signal sent a message to Tokugawa that enabled him to move his camp closer to the battlefield, boosting troop morale among the Eastern Alliance forces. Like Ishida's Encampment, this can easily be seen from most of the town.

spots.name: Ōtani Yoshitsugu's Grave
spots.local: 大谷吉継の墓 Ōtaniyoshitsugu no haka
spots.desc: One of the westernmost memorial markers in the town, this spot marks both the encampment and final burial site of Ōtani Yoshitsugu, one of the Western Alliance's main commanders. When he realized the defections of Kobayakawa Hideaki and others and the increasingly small likelihood of Western victory, he committed seppuku, or ritual suicide. Best reached by bicycle (although it is within walking…

spots.name: Site of Sekigahara Battleground
spots.local: 関ケ原古戦場 Sekigahara kosenjō
spots.desc: This marks the site of the bloodiest clash between the Eastern and Western armies in the Battle of Sekigahara. The monument here is flanked by the flags of the leaders of both armies, Ishida and Tokugawa.

spots.name: Ukita Hideie's Encampment Site
spots.desc: Ukita Hideie from Bizen Province (present-day Okayama), served as Vice Commander of the Western army, and brought the largest army on the Western Front, consisting of over 17,000 soldiers. Hideie was able to escape the battle and travel all the way to Satsuma Province (Kagoshima) before eventually being apprehended. He was spared a death sentence but was exiled to Hachijojima where he spent the…

spots.name: Other Memorial Markers
spots.desc: There are plenty of other markers and memorials scattered throughout the town, too numerous to list. The maps on the bridge over the train tracks list them with their relevant commanders.

spots.name: Fuwanoseki Museum (Sekigahara Town History and Folklore Museum)
spots.desc: Local history covering 6 eras from prehistoric to contemporary.

spots.name: Imasu-juku's Toiyaba
spots.desc: Toiyaba were places in post towns where Daimyo and officials went to get or exchange horses, personnel, and perform various administrative tasks. They existed in every post town, however very few Toiyaba exist today. The Imasu-juku's Toiyaba is Gifu's sole remainder.

spots.name: Mino and Omi Province Border Marker
spots.local: 美濃国と近江国との国境
spots.desc: A stone monument marks the border between the former Omi Province and Mino Province. On either side of the border, there are also markers that give the modern borders of Shiga Prefecture and Gifu Prefecture.

spots.name: Sekigahara-juku's Honjin
spots.local: 関ケ原宿本陣跡 Sekigahara-juku Honjin-ato
spots.desc: Sekigahara was one of the post towns along the Nakasendo. The honjin was a designated inn where passing daimyo and other important officials would stay. Like most of the honjin, the building no longer exists. On its former site there is a marker and a tree that stood in the front garden. The rest of the former honjin now contains Hachiman Shrine. The gate of Sekigahara's honjin is preserved in…

spots.name: Sekigahara-juku's Wakihonjin
spots.desc: Every post town had a wakihonjin which was an inn used for daimyo when the honjin could not be used, when more than one daimyo were staying, or for lower-level vassals who could not stay in the honjin. Wakihonjin were also available for the public to stay in when daimyo were not here. The wakihonjin no longer exists, but a replica of the gate was built here with a signpost. There is an additional…

spots.name: Eco Museum Sekigahara
spots.local: エコミュージアム関ケ原
spots.desc: A small museum featuring exhibits about the flora and fauna found in western Gifu Prefecture. The exhibits are interactive and fun for children.

spots.name: Sekigahara Limestone Cave
spots.desc: A 518-meter-long cave that maintains a temperature of 15 °C (59 °F) all year round. The cave has many stalagtites and stalagmites, some of which have been noted and named for their unique appearances, such as "The Giant's Foot" (巨人の足) which really does look like a giant leg and foot. It also contains fossils and there are trout in the river that runs through it. The pathway is flat and has no…
spots.hours: Hours vary by month. Closed Wed, except on holidays and open everyday in August

spots.name: Sekigahara Town History and Folklore Museum
spots.local: 歴史民俗学習館 Rekishi minzoku gakushukan
spots.desc: Renewed in 2020, this museum focuses on topics other than the famous battle, from archaeological times to today.

spots.name: Sekigahara War Land
spots.desc: While it's not a historic site, War Land is an open-air recreation of the Battle of Sekigahara. It includes encampments with the famous leaders marked so you can take pictures with your favorites. They also have samurai armor rentals for an additional fee so you can take pictures in the battlefield as a fighter. Armor rentals are not available in the summer due to the high risk of heat stroke.…

spots.name: Sekigahara Memorial Museum Bekkan
spots.local: 岐阜関ケ原古戦場記念館 別館
spots.desc: This is the museum's souvenir shop, located in a separate annex (bekkan) across from the museum. Here you can find a variety of items from clothing to stationary to pottery with the emblems of the Eastern and Western armies, as well as the emblems of some of the domains involved. There are also books and maps about the battle, as well as edible souvenirs.

spots.name: Hanaibuki Restaurant Sekigahara
spots.desc: A restaurant and general store located near War Land and the Iketera Pond.

spots.name: Ibukian
spots.desc: Small cafeteria-style cafe with good and relatively cheap food.

spots.name: Omatsu Sushi
spots.desc: A sushi restaurant near Uoshige restaurant on the south side of town.
spots.hours: Fri-Wed 11:30-14:00, 16:00-22:00; Sat Sun and holidays until 21:00

spots.name: Restaurant Mirai
spots.desc: A restaurant near the Battle Commencement Marker, with views of the surrounding mountains.

spots.name: Uoshige
spots.desc: A restaurant specializing in eel dishes, located in the heart of the southern side of town.
spots.hours: Thu-Tue 11:00-14:00, 17:00-20:00; closed the first and third Tuesdays of each month

spots.name: Takenaka Jinya
spots.desc: Built by Takenaka Shigekado, the Takenaka Jinya was the residence of the Takenaka family who were the lords of the area. The jinya itself no longer remains however, the gate has survived along with part of the moat. The statue in front of the jinya is Takenaka Hanbei, father of Shigekado.

spots.name: Nangu Shrine
spots.desc: The top shrine of Mino Province, it enshrines Kanayamahiko no Mikoto. There is a large torii gate leading up to the shrine.

spots.name: Tarui no Izumi
spots.desc: Gifu Prefecture has many springs that are known for their pure water. Tarui's water is among them and has been well-known for centuries. It was featured in one of the poems in the Shika Wakashu, an imperial anthology of waka poems, in 1070. Matsuo Basho also stopped here and wrote a poem after drinking the water. Today there is a small, attractive area where the spring water flows and visitors…

spots.name: Honryūji Temple
spots.desc: The temple's mountain gate and the entrance of its shoin (study hall) are said to have been relocated from the Nakasendo waki-honjin in Sekigahara. In 1691, the famous haiku poet Matsuo Basho visited the chief priest Kigai here, spending the winter and composing several poems. A monument related to this garden, the Tsukuriki-zuka, was later built on the grounds in 1809, and a hermitage called…

spots.name: Yaoya Dining Uedaya
spots.desc: A restaurant serving a variety of seafood and vegetable dishes.

spots.name: Jindonooka Park
spots.desc: Park outside of memorial hall with monuments to the Holocaust, Sugihara and to Japanese-Lithuanian relations.

spots.name: Gohou Waterfall
spots.desc: Gotou is a scenic spot nicknamed the Five Treasure Waterfalls of Yaotsu. The falls lie in the centre of a forest and are busiest during autumn. It is said that Musashi Miyamoto trained here.

spots.name: Inaba-jo Park
spots.desc: Ruins of a castle from 1590, all that remains is a reconstructed watch tower providing views of the surrounding area.

spots.name: Daisenji
spots.desc: Musashi Miyamoto, one of Japan's most famous swordsmen, is said to have meditated at this temple. In front of the temple lies the stone he meditated on. There is also a garden.

spots.name: Senbei Hall
spots.desc: Senbei has always been a popular snack in Yaotsu, at its peak there were over 150 senbei factories in Yaotsu, senbei line the walls of this shop and are one of Yaotsu's most popular souvenirs.

spots.name: Hinomaru Confectionary
spots.local: 日の丸製菓（やおつのおやつ屋）
spots.desc: Founded in 1954, this is one of the few senbei shops that offers guided tours. They have a variety of senbei products ranging from burdock root to Ginger sugar.

spots.name: Sankatsuya
spots.desc: Founded in 1933 this is the busiest and oldest restaurant in Yaotsu, the three most famous dishes are the Katsudon, Chinese style soba, and Paigu, crispy fried pork back-ribs.

spots.name: Midoriya Roho
spots.desc: Yaotsu's most famous sweet shop, the most popular dish is Kuri Kinton, a sweet invented in Yaotsu made from chestnut. Various types of mochi are also produced, and sweets must be purchased in sets of 10.

spots.name: Kuramoto Yamada
spots.desc: Founded in 1886, Kuramoto Yamada is a sake brewery famous around Japan for its Tamakashiwa, a sake that has won many awards.

spots.name: Hanamori Sake Brewery
spots.desc: Sake brewery with both raw and standard sake, along with free samples. Their most popular sake is the Hanazakari Junmai Daiginjo 39.
spots.price: ¥4000-7000 for 1,800 ml bottle, ¥2,000-3,500 for 720 ml bottle

spots.name: Yoro Falls
spots.desc: A picturesque waterfall recognized as one of Japan's top 100 waterfalls. There is a legend that long ago a young man who was supporting his elderly father but was very poor. He lamented that he couldn't even buy sake for his father until one day he smelled sake and went to the waterfall. When he tried the water, he realized it was sake. He took it home to his father and when his father drank the…

spots.name: YORO Land
spots.desc: Classic amusement park since 1974 with inside and outside rides for young kids.

spots.name: Jigokudani Yaen-koen
spots.desc: Snow monkeys! See the wild, but not too shy, Japanese Macaques in a hot spring.

spots.name: Shiga Kogen
spots.desc: Japan's largest ski resort, host of 1998 Nagano Winter Olympic Giant Slalom. With 21 interlinked ski fields and over 70 lifts, it takes days to explore all the runs the area has to offer.

spots.name: Hakuba 47 Winter Sports Park
spots.local: Hakuba 47 ウインタースポーツパーク
spots.desc: With an annual snowfall of over 10 m, Hakuba 47 offers 23 name runs, from beginner to advanced, as well as snowshoe and snowmobile tours. Private lessons for skiers or snowboarders are available in English and they rent basic equipment too.

spots.name: Hakuba Happo-one
spots.local: 白馬八方尾根スキー場
spots.desc: Hakuba Happo-one is an extremely popular ski resort, with ski runs varying from beginner level to Olympic challenging long course and downhill runs (Nagano Olympic 1998). 13 courses and 23 lifts with the longest run 8000 m. Incidentally, the name is pronounce "oh-neh", not "1".

spots.name: Juro No Yu
