spots.desc: Enjoy the piping hot mineral waters in the inside and outside baths while looking out over the snow capped mountains. When your skin starts shrivelling up, dry off and head to the lounge to kick back on the tatami and watch TV or dig into a steaming bowl of tempura soba. Sauna, lockers provided.
spots.hours: Dec-Mar 24 hr, Apr-Nov 10:00-22:00, closed 2nd Tue each month

spots.name: Tenjin No Yu
spots.desc: Recommended by locals for its healing waters, Tenjin No-Yu offers great views of the mountains from both indoor and outdoor baths. Lockers available.

spots.name: The Boarding Co
spots.desc: Hakuba's largest Burton dealer. The owner has snowboarded in Hakuba for 17 seasons.

spots.name: Burton Pro Snowboard Shop and Rentals
spots.desc: Huge range of rental boards. Brand new boots, boards and bindings. Try a Prior Powderstik or Burton Fish next time it dumps. Boots in all sizes—up to size 15 for men and size 10 for ladies. Staff speak English. Door to door deliveries and fitting service available.
spots.addr: Turn off Route 147 towards Goryu Ski Field

spots.name: Spicy Rentals
spots.desc: Largest ski & snowboard rental shop with the best selection in the Hakuba valley and over 25 years of experience in Hakuba and Whistler. Free helmet with all kids rentals.

spots.name: Eclipse Bar & Restaurant
spots.desc: Located in the Hakuba Luna Hotel (see below) at the base of the Sakka Quad Chair, Eclipse has the best pizza in Hakuba, together with excellent fresh pastas, salads and great desserts. Serves a range of international wines, local beers, sake, spirits and cocktails. Espresso coffee available. Open for dinner. Occasionally closed. Very reasonably priced (e.g. regular pizzas approx. ¥900; large…

spots.name: Gravity Worx Cafe
spots.desc: This warm and inviting cafe has English menus and homemade apple pie. A wide range of pizza and pasta dishes are available, or you can settle in with a few drinks and watch a movie on the bar tv. The large hot chocolate, served rich and steaming in a huge beer stein, is the best medicine for the icy winter days. Service is excellent and there is local produce and baked goods for sale.

spots.name: Hindi Momo
spots.desc: Some of the best Indian dishes in Japan. The menu is constantly refreshed, offering the best "in season" vegetables. The tandoori prawns are a favourite dish.

spots.name: Uncle Steven's
spots.desc: Just across the bridge up the hill from Happo Village. Some of the best Mexican food in Japan. Don't miss the baked banana. It usually runs a family of four about 8,000 including beer and bananas. Free Wi-Fi.

spots.name: White Horse Restaurant
spots.desc: Offers a great range of hearty western style meals including steaks, burgers, and pizzas. They have a large international wine list and English speaking staff. Friday night is the famous BBQ night. Expresso coffee available.

spots.name: Yamano Hotel Restaurant
spots.desc: Offers delicious French style and traditional Japanese style meals (Chanko Nabe - famed sumo wrestlers one-pot meal) and also a wide range of drinks: wine, beer, sake, etc., to enjoy with. Service is excellent with friendly English speaking staff. A reservation is required in advance.

spots.name: Nonjae
spots.desc: A modern day izakaya, with a cheerful atmosphere, and decently priced drinks - beers, sakes. Excellent Genghis Khan mutton BBQ, and grilled squid, also assorted yakitori sticks. Also offers pizzas. In a quiet location, but worth the effort.

spots.name: Hie
spots.desc: Designed for foreigners to enjoy a traditional Japanese izakaya, this place has great food! An English menu is available as well as private Japanese style rooms.

spots.name: Mt Hakuba Bar
spots.desc: New in Echoland, Mt Hakuba has cheap meals all ¥500, happy hour every day from 18:00, billiard table and free wireless internet.

spots.name: Off Piste
spots.desc: A cute pub showing snowboarding and skiing videos, darts and great drinks. The staff is very friendly and it's always warm inside! Check for special events. +81 261 727274 for more information.

spots.name: Tomatito
spots.desc: New in Echoland, Tomatito has everything, from pizza to sake. There is a pool table, darts and fussball. The spring rolls are a must try.

spots.name: Tracks Bar
spots.desc: One of Hakuba's most happening nightspots. "Temporarily" closed from 2020.

spots.name: White Horse Bar
spots.desc: A cool atmosphere for apres drinks with a great selection of local and international beers, wines and spirits and some smooth tunes. Situated in Echoland.

spots.name: Yamano Hotel Bar
spots.desc: Called "Noroc" in Happo - One, in front of the Ski Jumping Stadium. Good music, wide range of drinks and friendly staff. Opening hours: 22:00 - 01:00

spots.name: Fire Festival
spots.desc: The event of the year, held every January 15. Families with boys born in the last year build elaborate umbrella-like totem polems called hatsuakarikago, while all 40- to 42-year-old men in the village built a wooden shrine called shaden, both nearly 10 m tall. On the night of the festival, a ritual battle ensues after a torch procession, and the shrine and the poles are ceremonially burned amid…

spots.name: San-Poo-Loh Restaurant and Terrace
spots.desc: Temporarily Closed for COVID19. An elegant restaurant and coffee shop in the heart of Obuse. Italian food and fresh bread. Excellent service, delicious coffee, and delightful decor.
spots.price: Coffee ¥400; cappuccino ¥450; coffee and cake sets from ¥600

spots.name: Jigokudani Monkey Park
spots.local: 地獄谷野猿公苑 Jigokudani Yaenkōen
spots.desc: Famous for its population of wild Japanese Macaques (Macaca fuscata), odds are you've already seen this place on TV. The best time for a visit is winter, when snow covers the ground and the monkeys come to bathe in the hot spring at the valley bottom — a unique sight.

spots.name: Gala Yuzawa Snow Resort
spots.desc: Gala Yuwaza is a ski resort with 15 runs and nine lifts.Gala Yuwaza has a respectable dining area and a spa (Onsen & unisex swimming pool, so take your bathing suit) for soaking after skiing. One-day lift ticket, ¥4300 adults/¥2100 children; one-day rental of skis, poles and boots, ¥4800 adults/¥1500 children.

spots.name: NASPA Ski Garden
spots.local: ナスパスキーガーデン
spots.desc: The resorts courses range from very easy gentle slopes - suitable for small children and beginners - to the very steep and difficult, complete with three steep mogul courses.
spots.price: One-day lift ticket and lunch, ¥4300 Adults (over 12)/¥3300 children/¥14400 Family (2 Adults and 2 Children)

spots.name: Sake Museum Ponshu-kan
spots.desc: Ponshu-kan, enjoy different varieties of sake tasting. In the storeroom more than 100 varieties of sake are on display at a temperature of 15 degrees. You can also take a dip in a sake-flavored bath next-door. Has branches at Niigata and Nagaoka stations.

spots.name: Mini Super Shiodaya Honke
spots.local: ミニスーパー 塩田屋本家
spots.desc: This blink-and-you'll-miss-it grocery store is famous for an unusual dish: fruit sandwiches (フルーツサンド furuutsu sando) prepared by placing generous portions of sliced seasonal fruit -- strawberries, grapes, persimmons! -- between slices of white bread and sealing them in with copious amounts of whipped cream. From ¥500 each.

spots.name: Okuni Shrine
spots.desc: Construction on this beautiful shrine began in 555. The shrine is dedicated to the god Okuninushi no Mikoto, a benevolent god involved in the mythical creation of the archipelago, and a key figure in the famous story of the White Rabbit of Inaba (see Tottori). Very popular with Ieyasu Tokugawa and other members of his clan, this is still the most popular shrine in the ancient Totomi region. It is…

spots.name: History and Folk Museum
spots.desc: Located in a building that dates back to 1885, it mostly features items used in daily life from past eras.

spots.name: Gokurakuji
spots.desc: A temple surrounded by hydrangeas which typically bloom in June.

spots.name: Acty Mori
spots.desc: This hand-on center offers visitors a chance to try their hands at several traditional Japanese crafts, including Tōgei pottery, roof-tile making, paper-making, and traditional cloth-dyeing using local plants. The center also provides for some outdoor activities like cycling and canoeing.

spots.name: Kakitagawa Park
spots.desc: Famous for one of Japan's largest volumes of spring water. The crystal-clear river is the town’s main natural attraction.

spots.name: Honjoyama Park
spots.desc: Small hilltop park with an observation deck overlooking the town. Cherry blossoms bloom in spring.

spots.name: Comprehensive Sports Park
spots.desc: Multi-purpose sports park with shaded areas suitable for summer visits.

spots.name: Sun to Moon Kakita River
spots.desc: Large regional shopping centre with a wide variety of shops.

spots.name: Numazu Wholesale Market Food and Travel Market
spots.desc: Wholesale-style food market known for good prices and quality products.

spots.name: Kameya Main Store
spots.desc: Specialises in wasabi and traditional pickles using local ingredients.

spots.name: Miso Ramen Kakita River Hibari
spots.desc: Popular ramen shop known for rich miso broth. Limited parking available.

spots.name: Soba Restaurant Shoan (Shimizu Branch)
spots.desc: Well-known for soba and excellent tempura. Sakura shrimp dishes are recommended.

spots.name: Senryu Park
spots.desc: If you’re after breathtaking views of the countryside, there’s no better place to go. This park is frequented by townspeople, visitors, and students who run to the park for P.E. classes. It’s no Fuji, but to get to the top of Senryuu, you must climb a steep, very long flight of stone steps winding uphill through a dense, dark forest of trees and foliage. Once you reach the top, you are rewarded…

spots.name: Kumenan Library & Culture Center
spots.desc: A modern building built in 2002. The two-story structure is a dazzling sight of glass and brick. The first floor is a cozy yet massive library that is impeccably clean and welcoming. Several of the librarians speak some English and are more than happy to assist you. The selection of English books at the library is sizable for a town where there are practically no English speakers. Books about…

spots.name: Coffee House Village
spots.desc: A small family-run restaurant serving Japanized Western food. It's a popular hangout with locals, but people passing through often stop at the restaurant as well. The food there is affordable and served in heaping portions. Recommended dishes include the fried chicken, the mixed plate, spaghetti with meat sauce, and chicken katsu. Curry dishes and a variety of others are also available, including…

spots.name: Nagi MOCA
spots.desc: The Nagi Museum of Contemporary Art (Nagi MOCA) is a world-class museum of modern art in which the entire museum was constructed for and around the art within.

spots.name: Bodai-ji
spots.desc: Bodaiji Temple is most known for its gigantic 900 year old gingko tree. Its circumference is 12 meters. It's the kind of site that can really make a person feel small. It's especially beautiful in the fall when the leaves turn yellow. The actual temple building is rather small and nondescript, but those with an appreciation of nature should be quite at peace here.

spots.name: Nagi Vicarya Museum
spots.local: なぎビカリアミュージアム
spots.desc: A museum that features 16 million year old Vicarya fossils excavated from Nagi. It also has information about other fossils and archaeology.

spots.name: Yokozen Kabuki
spots.desc: A local form of kabuki theater meaning "On the side of the mountain" (山の横 yama no yoko), it has existed continuously for hundreds of years.

spots.name: PIZZERIA La Gita
spots.desc: A popular pizzeria with the approval of the Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana, an organization based in Naples, that promotes pizzerias that serve authentic Neapolitan pizza. In addition to their pizzas, they also have a variety of pasta dishes and salads.

spots.name: Wakasugi Primeval Forest
spots.desc: A protected forest that outlines Okayama's border with Tottori. It's home to around 200 different species of trees, including large beech trees and maple trees that make it a popular autumn leaf destination. Moss-covered rocks, numerous waterfalls, and the coolness of the mountains also make a great place to enjoy nature and beat the heat in the summertime. There are three hiking courses through…
spots.hours: Spring-Autumn (toilets and parking lot are closed in winter)

spots.name: Kagekiyo Shrine
spots.desc: This shrine was built on the spot where Taira no Kagekiyo was born. Kagekiyo was featured in The Tales of the Heike (Heike Monogatari). He was present at the famous Battle of Yashima and it is said that he was captured at the Battle of Dan-no-Ura and taken to Kamakura, the capital at the time, where he starved himself to death. He has been featured in ukiyoe and video games. The shrine features a…

spots.name: Ogaya Shibazakura Park
spots.desc: A popular place to enjoy shibazakura (moss phlox/pink moss) annually around Golden Week (late April to mid-May).

spots.name: Awakura Stone Circles
spots.desc: These stone circles stand on a steep slope, with many fallen stones below. It is unknown who built them or why. There is a sign from the road pointing down a path that leads by the spires. The stones are located on the slope, a bit off the path, and the path continues past them, so you need to look for them. The fallen stones are the best indicator to stop walking and look up the hill. You can…

spots.name: Mount Komano
spots.desc: From the trailhead by the road, it takes about an hour to reach the summit. In May, you can see the Japanese Enkianthus perulatis (ドウダンツツジ) along the trail. From the summit, on a clear day, you can see Mount Daisen to the west and the Seto Inland Sea to the south.

spots.name: Iwakura Temple
spots.desc: Hosts the Iwakura Eyo, a local "Naked Festival" like the larger one at Saidaiji Temple in Okayama.

spots.name: Awakura Shrine
spots.desc: The shrine was built at the behest of Nakayama Shrine, the top shrine (Ichinomiya) of Mimasaka Province. The large cypress tree standing in the shrine precincts is over 800 years old and at 6.2 meters in diameter and 35 meters tall, it is said to be the largest tree in the prefecture.

spots.name: Do Yashiki
spots.desc: A preserved Edo Period house built in the 18th century with a traditional thatched roof and well. Inside there are artifacts and documents on display.
spots.hours: 10:00-17:00, Opening days are irregular. It's best to call in advance.

spots.name: Nishiawakura Dandan Berry Farm
spots.local: にしあわくらだんだんベリー畑
spots.desc: A berry farm where visitors can come to pick blueberries, Juneberries, raspberries, and more from June to July. They also sell berry jams and other goods.

spots.name: Yu~topia Ogonsen
spots.desc: A hot spring for day visitors. There is an indoor onsen with a sauna, as well as an open-air onsen with nice views of the forest and river.

spots.name: Awakura Onsen Motoyu
spots.desc: This onsen is said to be where the tanuki bathed and where the first onsen site was established. It features a small indoor onsen with pieces of local Japanese cypress that help scent the water. If it pleases you, you can buy your own wood in the front restaurant area. See "Ikoi no Ie Motoyu" listing in "Sleep" for the location and information about staying overnight.

spots.name: Awakurando
spots.desc: Awakurando (a combination of Awakura and Land) is a rest stop where you can buy local souvenirs, such as products made from Awakura's Japanese cypress, Hinoki Beer, and foodstuffs. They also sell souvenirs from Tottori. There is a restaurant inside, as well, serving curries, donburi (meat over rice), tenpura, and other dishes. Many of their meals feature Daisen chicken from Daisen.

spots.name: Former Kageishi Elementary School
spots.desc: A schoolhouse-turned-multipurpose building, it houses Hat Shop UKIYO (帽子屋UKIYO), selling trendy and cute locally-made hats, Sake Urara (酒うらら) selling local nihonshu, and the Fureru Shokudo restaurant (see "Eat"), which also sells souvenirs, such as local wood products and the local Someya Suzuki organic cotton bags, as well as goods from Tottori and Shimane.
spots.hours: Each shop has its own days and hours. Sake Urara is typically open on Saturdays and some Sundays

spots.name: Aru no Mori Kominka Cafe
spots.local: あるの森古民家カフェ
spots.desc: An authentic Thai restaurant in a traditional Japanese farmhouse. See Aru no Mori (Sleep) for location.

spots.name: Motoyu Cafe and Restaurant
spots.local: 元湯カフェ＆レストラン
spots.desc: Located in the front of the Motoyu, the restaurant open to the public serving a variety of dishes with locally harvested mushrooms and vegetables. They're most known for their meals containing local venison, a rarity in Japan. In addition, they have an alcohol menu and desserts.

spots.name: Awakura Shun no Sato
spots.desc: A buffet restaurant with a variety of options, such as beef curry, croquettes, fried chicken, pork cutlets, basil chicken, and goya champloo to name a few. They also have desserts, such as ice cream, lemon and honey pound cake, and puddings.
spots.price: ¥1200 middle school and up, ¥800 elementary school, ¥500 age 4-elementary, 3 and under free

spots.name: Fureru Shokudo
spots.desc: A restaurant with lunch sets, sandwiches, and desserts that change daily. Some typical sets include curry and donburi (meat over rice). Sandwiches typically feature some meat, such as bacon or venison, with lettuce and some kind of complimentary condiments. There is not much seating available, so they recommend making a reservation if you wish to dine in with a group.

spots.name: Kunchiden
spots.desc: A small cafe offering a brunch set (pizza toast or a hot sandwich) from 09:00-11:00 and lunch sets (pad thai udon, green curry, or "food plate") from 11:00-14:00.
spots.price: All brunch and lunch sets cost ¥500

spots.name: Hugo et Léo
spots.desc: An "organic, vegetarian, vegan" French bakery selling various breads, whole quiches, and carmelized onion pizza, along with sweets, such as muffins, brioche, custards, etc.

spots.name: Yakage Museum
spots.desc: A museum featuring works by Yakage natives Issho Sato and Kaido Tanaka along with exhibits of modern local artists. Visitors can also ascend the tower for a view of the town.

spots.name: Yakage Honjin
spots.desc: Also known as the Ishii Residence (石井家住宅), the honjin was the principal inn of the Yakage-juku where daimyo and high-ranking officials stayed.

spots.name: Yakage Wakihonjin
spots.desc: Also known as the Takakusa Residence (髙草家住宅), the wakihonjin served as the secondary inn where lower-ranking officials stayed when traveling along the Yakage-juku.

spots.name: Kibi no Makibi Park
spots.desc: A park dedicated to Kibi no Makibi (695-775CE) where he was born. Kibi no Makibi went as an envoy to China and is credited with introducing Go to Japan upon his return. The park was built over the spot of his former residence.

spots.name: Tonomachi
spots.desc: This is the main site seeing road with numerous shops and some old samurai houses. One the side of the main Tonomachi streets are canals lined with large carp. There are also numerous food and product stands.

spots.name: Tsuwano Castle
spots.desc: This castle was built around 1295 and demolished during the Meiji Restoration, almost 600 years later. The stone foundations are pretty much all that remain, but the summit offers spectacular views over the valley and town. It can be reached via chair lift near Taikodani Inari Jinja. Alternatively, from Taikodani, walk down to the parking lot and follow the road approximately 50 meters, then…
spots.hours: Chair lift Mar-Nov 09:00-16:30 daily, Dec-Feb weekends only

spots.name: Tsuwano Catholic Church
spots.local: 津和野カトリック教会
spots.desc: A nice church with tatami mat floors and if you go on a fine day the sunshine shines through the stained glass windows; very good for photos. You can also pick up a copy, for a small fee, of the story of the Otome-Toge Martyrs. Carp food is also available to buy.

spots.name: Chapel of Saint Maria
spots.desc: In the area known as Otome-toge (Otome Pass) behind the station. 36 Japanese Christians were tortured and killed here during the Meiji Period. When Japan "opened" to the West, many Japanese Christians mistakenly thought that meant it was okay to come out and admit their faith but Christianity was still illegal, so those found to be Christian were taken here (and to other special places) and…

spots.name: Taikodani Inari Jinja
spots.desc: One of the Five Great Inari Shrines. It was built in 1773 by Tsuwano's seventh generation feudal lord Kamei Norisada to enshrine a share of the rice spirit Inari worshipped at Fushimi Inari in Kyoto. The walk up the mountain-side, through over a thousand bright red torii (gates), leads to a great view over the town.

spots.name: Yomei-ji Temple
spots.desc: Built in 1420, it is one of the 2 great Soto sect temples. It was the family temple for many of the Tsuwano feudal lords and has the Mori Ogai's grave.

spots.name: Washibara Hachiman-gu Shrine
spots.desc: A small shrine on the edge of town. It has archery contests on the 2nd of April. It is a pleasant walk through the garden.

spots.name: Tsuwano Japan Heritage Center
spots.local: 津和野町日本遺産センター
spots.desc: A small museum and tourism information center. The visitors can learn about the history of Tsuwano through "100 views of Tsuwano Then and Now", which is a collection of drawings showing Tsuwano's townscape as it was 150 years ago. Many places, the scenery remained, so one can compare the old and the new. A full-size costume of the Heron dance (Sagimai) is exhibited on the 1st floor. The staff…

spots.name: Anno Mitsumasa Art Museum
spots.desc: Art museum that specialises in Mitsumasa Anno, who was born in Tsuwano. There is also a planetarium, a reproduction of Anno's home studio space and a 1930s-style elementary school classroom.

spots.name: Hori Gardens
spots.desc: While not near the center of town, this is a great place to visit. The residence of the Hori family, the estate consists of a main building, a very beautiful garden, and guest house.

spots.name: SL Train
spots.desc: Two authentic early 1900s steam locomotives run once daily (only 1 train a day) on weekends and on national holidays (except in the winter) from Shin Yamaguchi Station to Tsuwano and back. It only stops for about three hours in Tsuwano before returning to Shin Yamaguchi Station.

spots.name: Yabusame
spots.desc: In the spring, when the cherry blossoms are in bloom, men in bright outfits take part in a horseback archery festival.

spots.name: Otome-toge Festival
spots.desc: A procession from Tsuwano Catholic Church in Tono-machi to Maria Cathedral at Otome-toge Pass is followed by a mass at the square in front of the cathedral.

spots.name: Gion Festival
spots.desc: Men in white bird outfits perform graceful dances to the music of bells, flutes and drums. This festival is held to worship the gods at Yasaka Shrine. At the same time, another group made up of young children in costumes proceed along Tonomachi, the station vicinity, and the city outskirts.

spots.name: Bon Odori
spots.desc: A black scarf, white head band, white short kimono, and black tights are worn by Tsuwano Odori dancers. This dance began in the Muromachi period (1336 - 1573) in memory of the dead and is now recognized as an intangible cultural asset of Shimane Prefecture.

spots.name: Pino Rosso
spots.desc: An Italian restaurant with delicious and authentic Italian appetizers, pizzas, pasta, and pastries, as well as a large collection of international liquors. This is one of the few restaurants open past 18:00.

spots.name: Furusato Shokudo
spots.desc: A small restaurant with western style and Japanese tables. At this restaurant you can order a locally specialty of uzume-meshi, which is a soupy rice dish served with wasabi, small pieces of mountain vegetables and tofu.

spots.name: Tsurube
spots.desc: A small udon-only restaurant, clustered with other small noodle and okonomiyaki shops. The owner is a former horse-back archer, and the shop is littered with his old photographs and shattered wood targets. Top class udon of all kinds can be found here.

spots.name: Naniwa
spots.desc: An Osaka-style restaurant specializing in okonomiyaki. It is owned and operated by the brother of the neighboring Tsurube Udon-ya, and aside from having table-side griddle-cooked okonomiyaki, also serves a variety of soba/udon/noodle dishes. A large back room can seat parties of seven or more.

spots.name: Daisen Museum of Nature and History
spots.local: 鳥取県立大山自然歴史館
spots.desc: A museum detailing the flora and fauna found in the area, as well as local history.

spots.name: Daisen White Resort
spots.local: だいせんホワイトリゾート
spots.desc: Mount Daisen is a highly popular winter destination for skiers, particularly in the Chugoku area.
spots.price: Rental prices: carving ski set costs ¥4000, snowboard sets cost ¥4000, and sportswear costs ¥3500

spots.name: Gosho Aoyama Manga Factory
spots.desc: A cute little museum dedicated to Detective Conan and Aoyama Gosho, the author of this famous manga.
spots.price: Adults ¥700, middle and high school students ¥500, elementary school students ¥300

spots.name: Sanbutsu-ji
spots.desc: Sanbutsu-ji is a mountain temple complex that's famous building, Nageiredo (投入堂, literally "thown-in chapel"), is built into the side of a cliff. The building is a National Treasure and a unique site in Japan. Visitors wishing to make the trek to the Nageiredo (or to visit any part of the complex) should be aware that you must travel in a group of 3. Single visitors are not permitted to ascend.…

spots.name: Statue of Marie Curie
spots.desc: Misasa's hot springs contain radium - so the city has her statue, Curie Park and Curie Festival (4th Sunday of July).

spots.name: Enchoen Chinese Garden
spots.desc: One of the largest Chinese gardens in Japan. It was first assembled in China, disassembled, and then rebuilt here with Lake Togo as its backdrop. Chinese acrobatic performances are held here daily. The gift shop just outside the garden contains a lot of Chinese souvenirs and sweets, as well.

spots.name: Ueshi Castle
spots.desc: The original was destroyed by the Tokugawa army. It was rebuilt in 1990.

spots.name: Shitori Shrine
spots.desc: The main hall of the shrine was rebuilt in 1818, but many of the artifacts from the shrine are National Treasures and exhibited in the Tokyo National Museum.

spots.name: Hawai Onsen
spots.desc: Promoting itself as "Hawaii of Japan", planting some palm trees (which don't look like growing well). Yurihama Town and Hawaii County have been sister cities since 1996.

spots.name: Moss Canyon
spots.local: 苔の洞門 Koke no dōmon
spots.desc: On the south side of the lake, these are in fact two canyons, both several hundred meters long, densely carpeted with thick, green moss. Free entry and well worth a visit.

spots.name: Kyūkamura Shikotsuko
spots.desc: A somewhat clinical hot spring resort across the Chitose River from Shikotsuko Onsen.

spots.name: Hot Spring Hotel Marukoma
spots.desc: This is a lakeside hotel and onsen. There are indoor and outdoor baths, and also saunas.

spots.name: Pō River Nature Park
spots.desc: The spacious park within Shibetsu wetland, provided wooden walkway.

spots.name: Yumechiyokan Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the 1985 television show The Diary of Yumechiyo which took place and was filmed in Yumura Onsen. It features a variety of costumes and props from the show and episodes are shown on a retro television.

spots.name: Pioneer Memorial Home of Hamasaka
spots.local: 浜坂先人記念館 以命亭
spots.desc: Also known as the Imeitei, it was built as a retirement home for a member of the Mori family. It features a brewery, a plum garden, and information about the poet Mori Aio.

spots.name: Refresh Park Yumura
spots.local: リフレッシュパークゆむら
spots.desc: A unique family-friendly pool and hot spring for daytrippers. Unlike other hot springs, when you enter, you are required to bring or rent swimwear. Once inside, go to the locker rooms. From the locker rooms, you can enter a traditional onsen where you must be naked to enter however, if you change into your swimsuit, you can exit the locker rooms and enjoy the swimming pool or head on down a…

spots.name: Yakushi-yu
spots.desc: An old daytripper hot spring in Yumura Onsen that is popular among locals. It has an indoor and outdoor bath, as well as a sauna.

spots.name: Shichikama Onsen Yuraku-kan
spots.local: 七釜温泉 ゆ〜らく館
spots.desc: A daytripper hot spring in Shichikama Onsen, it offers multiple indoor and outdoor baths.

spots.name: Ebisuya
spots.desc: An izakaya serving ramen, katsudon, yakisoba, and other hearty dishes.

spots.name: Kamigamo Shrine
spots.desc: Collectively, Kamigamo Shrine and Shimogamo Shrine are known as the Kamo Shrines, and they were highly favored by the Imperial Court during the Heian Period. The shrine is most famous for the tatesuna, the two large sand cones. Their origins and original purpose are unknown, but it has been speculated that they represent nearby mountains. Kamigamo Shrine is one of Kyoto's World Heritage Sites.

spots.name: Kyoto Botanical Garden
spots.desc: Japan's first botanical garden since 1924, the Kyoto Prefectural Botanical Garden is quite large and houses a wide variety of plants. It is a popular place for plum blossom viewing in February and early March and cherry blossoms, which typically bloom in early April. The indoor garden has a wide variety of tropical plants, desert cactuses, and other plants. The entrance fee only covers the…
spots.price: ¥200 to see the outdoor flowers and gardens and an additional ¥200 to see the indoor botanical garden

spots.name: Shūgakuin Imperial Villa
spots.desc: A beautiful villa commissioned by Emperor Gomizuno-o in 1655 and completed four years later. The area is separated into three separate villas. In the lower villa, you'll find a lovely garden with a stream running through it and the Jugetsukan, where the emperor relaxed before making his way to the upper villa. The middle villa is home to the Rakushi-ken, princess Akinomiya's home, and the…

spots.name: Amida-ji
spots.desc: A temple where followers are trained to recite the Nyoho Nenbutsu chants. The statue kept within the shrine was originally adorned with the hair of the temple's founding priest.

spots.name: Zen Meditation at Shunkō-in
spots.desc: The temple's American-educated vice abbot, Rev. Taka Kawakami, offers a detailed English tour of temple and leads Zen meditation lessons. The temple hosts many important artistic and cultural properties related to Zen Buddhism and also connected to Shinto and Christianity, and also offers accommodation for ¥5000/night.
spots.price: Accommodations: ¥4000-5000; Tour: ¥2000, including matcha green tea and sweet

spots.name: Zen Meditation at Taizō-in
spots.desc: Much more than simply a Zen meditation session, after one hour of meditation, participants will also get to experience a brief tea ceremony, calligraphy lessons, and an English tour of the temple's garden. It is a rare opportunity for tourists, but be aware that you will need to devote half of a day for the entire session. Reservations are required, but you can make your reservation in English at…
spots.hours: Session occurs from 09:00 to 13:00 only one day per week

spots.name: Kurama Onsen
spots.desc: Well known hot spring in the small village of Kurama (see #See). There are both inside and outside baths, but if the weather permits do take the outside bath (rotenburo). Lying in the hot water, while admiring the green and hilly scenery is wonderfully relaxing. There are separate pools for men and women. There's also a free shuttle bus going every now and then, but you're recommended to take the…
spots.price: Day entry ¥1400-2700 depending on chosen plan and date

spots.name: Kitano Tenmangu Shrine Flea Market
spots.desc: On the 25th of each month Kitano Tenmangu hosts a flea market, with vendors lining both sides of the pathway leading up to the honden and then extends around each side. Pottery, porcelain, traditional dolls, and clothing are among the items sold, along with food. If you can manage to get here on the 25th, it's a great place to find unique souvenirs for great prices.

spots.name: Kurazushi
spots.desc: A cheap and fun way to dine. For every five plates you finish, put the down the shoot to play a game on the screen above the sushi. Each game is different, but you'll typically be asked to choose one of three options and then watch the animation to see if you win. If you win, you get a prize. It's entertaining, and the sushi tastes good.

spots.name: Falafel Garden
spots.desc: An Israeli restaurant serving a variety of falafel pockets, as well as meal sets.
spots.hours: 11:30-21:30, closed Wed in April and May
spots.price: Medium-sized falafels range in price from ¥860-1100, large sizes available

spots.name: Bistro Cerisier
spots.local: ビストロ スリージェ bisutoro suriije
spots.desc: A French restaurant decorated with a variety of French posters. They claim to have the approval of the French themselves.

spots.name: Bar Moonwalk
spots.desc: Offers a large selection of drinks at a great cost. Finger food is also available.
spots.price: Drinks sell for about ¥200 each, though expect smaller quantities of alcohol than the average bar.

spots.name: Ringo
spots.desc: A bar dedicated to the Beatles' singer Ringo Star, with Beatles memorabilia decorating the walls and even a cover band that plays here live. The fresh pizza is quite good.

spots.name: The Flying Keg
spots.desc: A great place for anyone wanting to sample beers from around the world or missing beer from home, The Flying Keg offers beers from the U.S., Kenya, Germany, Ireland, Israel, China, Mexico, Australia, India, Brazil, Indonesia, Thailand, Belgium, New Zealand, the Caribbean, Italy, and the UK.
spots.price: Most drinks sell for ¥600-900, wines for ¥2000-3000

spots.name: Kyoto Kamigamo Mankawa
spots.desc: A cocktail bar along with a restaurant serving various health food dishes.
spots.hours: Open from 5PM to midnight. Closed Tuesdays and holidays
spots.price: Original cocktails sell for ¥730-840, umeshu ¥630, detox drinks from ¥630-730

spots.name: Tortoise Stone
spots.desc: Kameishi (Tortoise Stone) is one of the unusual carved stones scattered across the Asuka countryside. The large, roughly turtle-shaped stone is thought to date from the Asuka period, although its original purpose and meaning remain uncertain. Local tradition says that the stone faces toward the direction of Nara and that, should it ever turn completely around, the surrounding region would be…

spots.name: Monkey Stones
spots.desc: Saruishi (Monkey Stones) are a group of unusual carved stones near the village of Asuka. The four stone figures have roughly human or animal-like faces and are thought to date from the Asuka period, although their original purpose is unknown. Their distinctive expressions have led to various interpretations, including connections with guardian figures or influences from the Korean Peninsula.

spots.name: Sakafune-ishi
spots.desc: Sakafune-ishi is a large, unusually shaped stone on a hillside in Asuka, carved with a series of channels, grooves and shallow depressions. Its purpose is unknown, although various theories have suggested that it was used for ritual activities, the preparation of liquids, or some form of ancient water system. The stone is generally dated to the Asuka period and is one of several mysterious carved…

spots.name: Spa World
spots.desc: Gender-separated European and Asian-themed spas and saunas as well as a pool for the family with slides and fun (don't forget your swimming trunks). Open 24 hr so it is handy if you're stuck for accommodation or locked out of your hotel after a night on the town, just pay up, change into their cotton overalls and pass out on one of their comfy leather recliners with as many blankets as you like.…
spots.price: ¥1500 for all day (¥500 extra if using the pool); extra charge ¥1450 for entering, staying, or leaving between…

spots.name: Jan-Jan Yokocho Street
spots.desc: Jan-Jan Yokocho is a famous shopping street along a narrow lane. There are still many establishments running in the same shops they built immediately after World War II. The entire area is squashed with small, cheap eating houses.

spots.name: Kushikatsu Daruma Shinsekai Main Shop
spots.local: 串かつだるま 新世界総本家
spots.desc: The original Shinsekai shop of Osaka's most famous kushikatsu institution, with its trademark grumpy uncle statue admonishing diners not to double-dip their skewers into the shared sauce pots. Order a 13-piece Shinsekai set for an easy sampler of this Osakan classic and wash it down with draft beer or a whiskey highball. If there's a queue at the original outlet (and there usually is), there are…

spots.name: Hollywood Dream
spots.desc: A long and wild rollercoaster, where you set the soundtrack of your choice to listen while you ride from the speakers pumping next to your seat. For an extra adrenaline kick, pick the Backdrop version, which sends you hurtling through the same ride backwards! Hollywood Dream is very popular with multi-hour waits on busy days so it's better to come here early or during the night.

spots.name: Space Fantasy - The Ride
spots.desc: An indoor family-friendly rollercoaster where you board a spaceship and travel through the solar system to the sun and back. The vehicles can also spin! The attraction gets a lot of temporary overlays so you may not experience it in its original version.

spots.name: Cinema 4D Theater
spots.desc: A rotating selection of 4D movies, like Shrek 4D Adventure and Sesame Street 4D Movie Magic and My Hero Academia, mostly in Japanese.

spots.name: SING on Tour
spots.desc: A musical based on the movie Sing with mix of live actors and animatronics in the Illumination Theater.

spots.name: Playing with Curious George
spots.desc: A small stage show set in a cartoon studio with the famous monkey, Curious George as the protagonist.

spots.name: Universal Monsters Live: Rock and Roll Show
spots.desc: A live show where classic Universal monsters like Dracula and Frankenstein sing and dance to hits from the '80s and '90s.

spots.name: Despicable Me Minion Mayhem
spots.desc: On this 3D motion simulator, you're invited into Gru's mansion as you prepare to be turned into one of his Minions by Dr. Nefario. However, things go wrong and a madcap adventure throughout his lab ensues with Gru, Margo, Edith, and Agnes at your side. As an only-in-Japan twist, Gru speaks pitch-perfect Osaka dialect! The ride can get crowded during the afternoon.

spots.name: Freeze Ray Sliders
spots.desc: A children's spinner ride with ice-making vehicles that glide across a (fake) frozen pool.

spots.name: Jurassic Park: The Ride
spots.desc: A water-based ride that takes guests on a scenic boat tour through the dinosaur habitats of Jurassic Park. The journey turns thrilling as riders encounter a menacing T-Rex, culminating in an 85-foot plunge. For those who don't want to get wet, there are free ponchos available.

spots.name: The Flying Dinosaur
spots.desc: Another very popular attraction, a thrilling suspended rollercoaster where a Pteranodon sends the vehicles soaring through the sky. The ride offers some very unique views of the park. Keep in mind that the ride is fast with big drops and large inversions, so it may be rough for people with motion sickness or fear of heights.

spots.name: JAWS
spots.desc: Step into the boat for a charming and peaceful ride around Amity Village from the movie Jaws before it takes a turn for the worse as a huge shark attacks you. This is the only original Universal attraction remaining in any of the parks.

spots.name: Waterworld
spots.desc: The movie may not have been a success, but this frenetic live-action show full of jet ski acrobatics, explosions, and water is worth attending. You can sit in the blue-seated Splash Zone if you fancy getting wet!

spots.name: Mario Kart: Koopa's Challenge
spots.desc: Ever wanted to play Mario Kart in real life? Here's your chance! Inside Bowser's Castle (Koopa in Japanese) is an interactive dark ride combining physical sets and augmented reality where guests race through iconic tracks from the game. Riders join Team Mario, with their goal being to defeat Bowser and his minions by hitting them with shells and collecting power-ups and coins.

spots.name: Mine Cart Madness
spots.desc: The signature attraction in Donkey Kong Country and the newest in the park, opening in 2024. It is a rollercoaster that whizzes you through the jungle and the Golden Temple on board a mine cart. The ride uses a unique system to make it seem as if the mine carts are flying above broken sections of track!

spots.name: Yoshi's Adventure
spots.desc: A kid-friendly ride where small Yoshis take you for a relaxing tour around the Mushroom Kingdom.

spots.name: Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey
spots.desc: This "robocoaster" combines a robotic arm with a rollercoaster track while also mixing physical sets and effects with huge screens. Go on a thrilling journey with Harry, Ron, and Hermione around the Wizarding World, whilst encountering many of its creatures like dragons and spiders along the way. The queue is set within Hogwarts and passes through places like Dumbledore's office and the…

spots.name: Flight of the Hippogriff
spots.desc: A short family-friendly rollercoaster where you fly around on a hippogriff, an eagle-like horse. An animatronic hippogriff and Hagrid's Hut are next to the queue.

spots.name: Ollivanders Experience
spots.desc: A small show where a wand chooses a wizard. Even if you are not chosen, you can still purchase a wand in the shop. The wands are interactive and can be used at select places around Hogsmeade.

spots.name: Snoopy’s Great Race
spots.desc: A mini roller coaster where riders zoom around in Snoopy-themed cars.

spots.name: Hello Kitty’s Cupcake Dream
spots.desc: A spinning ride with colorful cupcake-shaped vehicles inspired by Hello Kitty’s love for sweets.

spots.name: Hello Kitty’s Ribbon Collection
spots.desc: An interactive walkthrough where guests can take cute photos with Hello Kitty.

spots.name: Moppy’s Balloon Trip
spots.desc: A gentle aerial carousel offering great views of the Wonderland area.

spots.name: Big Bird’s Big Nest
spots.desc: A fun indoor playground with soft play equipment and a carrousel.

spots.name: Gladrags Wizardwear
spots.desc: Souvenir stores that sell Harry Potter-themed clothing, wands. It is right next to the Owl Post and Owlery which carries stationery products.

spots.name: Happiness Cafe
spots.desc: This Minions-themed cafe serves up only three dishes, namely burgers, fried chicken and curry, but at least you get a filling and reasonably tasty set meal for your ¥2000-2200.

spots.name: Hashigui-Iwa Rock Formations
spots.desc: A legendary set of rock formations that stretch out sea for about 850 meters, and is pretty much ingrained into the town's identity to both locals and visitors.

spots.name: Turkish Memorial and Museum
spots.desc: As the signs outside Kushimoto JR Station proclaim, Kushimoto is the official "Town of Japanese-Turkish Friendship." This proud history began in 1890, when the Turkish frigate Ertugrul crashed on the rocks off O-shima Island during a typhoon, after visiting Yokohama to conduct talks between the rising Empire of Japan and the declining Ottoman Empire. The museum is small and its information is…

spots.name: Japan-US Friendship Hall
spots.local: 日米修交記念館 Nichibei Shūkō Kinenkan
spots.desc: A museum commemorating the first actual arrival of an American ship in Japan—the USS Lady Washington in 1791—taking place decades before Commander Perry's more famed 19th-century landing. Also houses a small collection of memorabilia of the town's American Sister City (Hemet, California). Exhibits have English-language recordings and materials.

spots.name: Kashinozaki Lighthouse
spots.desc: Japan's oldest stone lighthouse and is still in use. Also known for being the home of an Englishman who tended to the area, planting daffodils that continue to bloom to this day.

spots.name: Koza
spots.desc: This town was independent until 2005 and continues to maintain its own identity. The scenery along the waterway that bisects the town, the Koza River, is quite picturesque.

spots.name: Kushimoto Big Bridge Park
spots.local: 串本大橋公園 Kushimoto Ōhashi Kōen
spots.desc: Small park with a wooden overlook structure allowing for views of Kushimoto Harbor and the channel between Cape Shiono-Misaki and Oshima.

spots.name: Kushimoto Marine Park
spots.local: 串本海中公園 Kushimoto Kaichū Kōen
spots.desc: See the local sea life through its underwater exhibit built underwater and through a glass bottomed boat ride.

spots.name: Mt. Kasane
spots.desc: A high peak. The park at the summit has a playground and has a breathtaking overlook of Kushimoto Harbor, the Kushimoto Big Bridge, Oshima Island and more. A popular destination for day-hikers and BBQ parties.

spots.name: Okyo Rosetsu Art Museum
spots.local: 串本応挙芦雪館 Kushimoto Ōkyo Rosetsu kan
spots.desc: This art museum prides itself as being Japan's smallest. Houses a fine collection of "India-ink" paintings by Ōkyo Maruyama and his disciple Rosetsu Nagasawa.

spots.name: Oshima Port
spots.desc: The site of the annual Boat Race Festival is not much to look at, but it offers an amazing view of Kushimoto Harbor and the rest of the mainland, and the mountains that background everything else. The road to get here is semi-treacherous.

spots.name: Shiono-Misaki Southernmost Point Park
spots.local: 本州最南端の地 Honshū Sainantan no Chi
spots.desc: A grassy area that denotes the southernmost point of Honshu and serves as the festival grounds for the annual Fire Festival. Nearby watchtower offers views of the area.

spots.name: Shiono-Misaki Lighthouse
spots.local: 潮岬灯台 Shiono Misaki Tōdai
spots.desc: Built in 1873 and at 19.55 meters, this Meiji-era lighthouse served as an important marker for ships entering Osaka Bay.

spots.name: Shichikawa Dam
spots.desc: Recreational area popular during the cherry blossom viewing season with spectacular views.

spots.name: Umikongo Rock Formations
spots.desc: Rock formations taking on strangely recognizable shapes, such as pyramids and lion masks. Declared in 1983 by Asahi Shimbun newspaper as one of Japan's 100 Most Important Natural Treasures for the 21st Century.

spots.name: Oheji Trail
spots.desc: Oheji is a coastal branch of the bigger Kumano Kodo pilgrimage (熊野古道), a Heian-era pilgrimage road linking the 3 Grand Shrines of Kumano (熊野三山): Nachi Taisha (那智大社), Hongu Taisha (本宮大社), and Hayatama Taisha (速玉大社).

spots.name: Koza Sightseeing Association Canoe Rental
spots.local: 古座観光協会カヌーレンタル Koza Kankō Kyōkai Kanu Rentaru
spots.desc: Offers kayak + gear rentals for use on the Koza River. Be sure to plan ahead in the warmer months as reservations fill up quickly. Courses available: 5 km/hr (¥1500), 8 km/2 hr (¥2000), 12 km/3 hr (¥3000), 16 km/4 hr (¥4000). Taxi fare to starting area not included. Seasonal. Reservations Tel. 0735-72-0645 (Japanese only). Reservation window located inside Koza Station, rental pickup located…

spots.name: Kumano Nachi Taisha
spots.desc: A Shinto shrine that's been designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site.

spots.name: Katsuura Seafood Market
spots.desc: After Tokyo, this is the largest tuna market in Japan. Tuna auctions start from 07:00, although they use a silent bid system and are thus quite subdued. View from 2nd floor observation platform is free, or pay ¥1000 for auction floor access including a tuna sample. The main market is wholesale only but there are plenty of retailers and tuna restaurants around.

spots.name: Three Step Cliff
spots.desc: A beautiful view from cliffs on the ocean edge that are 50 meters high. There is also a guided tour into to the caverns inside the cliffs. It is said that pirates (kumano suigun)used to inhabit the caverns and the remains of their dwellings can be seen. A good tour for young children and dads trying to avoid shopping. Admission charged.

spots.name: Senjojiki
spots.desc: A beautiful rocky point near Shirahama beach. The view is best late in the afternoon. Admission is free.

spots.name: Kishu Museum
spots.desc: Temporarily Closed as of May 2024. A small but interesting museum housing Ukiyo-e prints of all "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji" by Andō Hiroshige among some quality pottery and screens.

spots.name: Engetsu Island
spots.desc: A small island in Shirahama bay (20 minutes walk from the mean beach to get in front of it). A rock formation with a hole in the middle allows in some days to see the Sun set through it. An enjoyable view and stroll in any (not too hot or humid) day.

spots.name: Shirahama Sakinoyu Onsen
spots.desc: This spectacular hot spring is celebrated as one of Japan's Top 3 hot springs and cited in old texts. As it lies just at the waterfront bigger waves from ocean cool down the pool's hot water and splash the bathers which adds to the fun and pleasure.
spots.price: ¥420 entrance fee, ¥200 for a towel, ¥100 for using a locker

spots.name: Shirohama Flower Park
spots.desc: Lots of flowers, and a big greenhouse where firebugs can be seen at night.

spots.name: Sand hill
spots.desc: A surprising mountain flanked on each side by huge sand slopes. Local kids have fun sledging or sand skiing from the top. Climbing it is a fun 5-minutes hike and offers a nice view.

spots.name: Motona Beach Club
spots.desc: Upmarket beach club with live DJ promising "laidback luxury" that quite frankly looks out of place on the rather drab Motona Beach. The bar/restaurant serves up fruity cocktails and Hawaiian fare. Daybeds from ¥10,000 (fits 4).

spots.name: Kataoka Tsurutaro Art Museum
spots.desc: An art museum of Japanese actor and artist Tsurutarō Kataoka. The concept is to be a place which people can stop by with yukata (浴衣) that is Japanese traditional clothes. There is a shop for souvenir.

spots.name: Kusatsu Bälz Memorial Hall
spots.desc: Small exhibit in memory of Erwin von Bälz, who discovered the good effects of Kusatsu hot spring.

spots.name: Sainokawara Park
spots.desc: A small valley with a river fed by the natural hot springs surrounded by forest. An open air onsen is present within the park for a fee. There is also the Kusatsu visitor centre in the park detailing the flora and fauna of the region (descriptions are all in Japanese).

spots.name: Kusatsu visitor center
spots.local: 草津ビジターセンター
spots.desc: To learn the relationship between Kusatsu hot spring and volcano and nature and plants of Kusatsu.
spots.hours: 09:00-16:00, closed on Thu, the 2nd Tue of the month and for New Year

spots.name: Netsu-no-yu
spots.desc: A bath house converted into a performance centre adjacent to the upper level of the yubatake. Watch performances of the Yumomi ceremony where residents in the past used to cool down the hot spring waters using wooden boards. During the performance, you can take photos and videos of the performance and singing.

spots.name: Sainokawara Open-air Bath
spots.local: 西の河原露天風呂 (Sainokawara Rotenburo)
spots.desc: This is the biggest outdoor bath in Kusatsu located within Sainokawara Park.

spots.name: Otaki Hot Spring
spots.desc: There are different kinds of hot springs and it's known as the department store of hot springs. There is a restaurant to eat and also people are able to use massage service by appointment in front office.

spots.name: Goza Hot Spring
spots.desc: Built in the style combining Edo and Meiji era bath houses, this onsen overlooks the Yubatake field. It has two bath halls which alternate between males and females.
spots.hours: Daily 07:00–21:00; hours may change depending on season

spots.name: Therme Therme
spots.desc: Therme Therme is in the Kusatsu Hotel Village complex, which also has a golf course and ski area. The concept of this facility is German hot spring plus Japanese traditional taste of hot spring. There is a swimming pool, water slides, and hot spring facilities.

spots.name: Kusatsu Hot Spring Hall
spots.desc: This hall is one of the facilities in Kusatsu Highland Hotel (草津ハイランドホテル).

spots.name: Craft and folk craft
spots.desc: In the city, one of the activities is to experience making Kusatsu craft.

spots.name: Yamagataya souvenir shop
spots.desc: This shop is famous for beckoning cat (招き猫) and there are thousands of beckoning cats in this shop.

spots.name: Aoyama
spots.desc: Hand-made buckwheat noodles restaurant which is located on Sainogawara Street. There are varieties of hot soba, cool soba, and rice.

spots.name: Matsumoto
spots.desc: Udon noodle shop known for its himokowa wide udon noodles using local flour, a Gunma prefecture specialty. Also serves a variety of tempura with the set meals.

spots.name: Donguri
spots.desc: It is a famous European restaurant. they have been taken up with television and magazine. a famous item is acorn hamburg for ¥1050.

spots.name: Tsuki-ya
spots.desc: It is a famous Shabu-shabu restaurant which was opened in 2006. It's taken up with TV and key item in this restaurant is "pork shabu-shabu set' for ¥1700.

spots.name: Makoto Sushi
spots.desc: It is in center of Kusatsu and local people often go this place. They provide variety kinds of sushi and each season, they have special menu. This place is often used as party place.

spots.name: Kusatsu Plateau Beer
spots.desc: Beer which is good for health is the feature and a target. Water is from Czech republic.

spots.name: Koarai-seika
spots.desc: Their “dorayaki” (kind of Japanese pancakes) are a famous sweet sold in Minakami. They are also a favorite treat of the Japanese animated character "Doraemon". The red azuki beans used in these Dorayaki are carefully selected and roasted, then blended until smooth with fresh cream. Besides red bean paste, there are a wide variety of other fillings to choose from, including Tirumisu, Custard…

spots.name: Kunio Yanagida Memorial Park
spots.desc: The house of Japanese folklorist "Yanagida Kunio" is preserved. Materials related to Kunio are on display there.

spots.name: Kōmō Shrine
spots.desc: Very old shrine. According to oral heritage, it was founded in 288BC lore and there are written records dating back to 698AD.

spots.name: Donto-Yaki
spots.desc: In mid-January, New Year offerings are burned around the town.

spots.name: Soba Restaurant Yamamoto
spots.desc: Soba. This place is listed in Bib Gourmand Restaurant in the Michelin Guide Shonan.

spots.name: Kōunkaku
spots.desc: The restaurant on the ground floor of the shrine ryokan offers basic meals of noodles, curry rice and such.

spots.name: Shōkyōin
spots.desc: Built in 1739, the Small Teaching Hall on the grounds of Mitsumine Shrine now offers tea, coffee and snacks in the ¥500 range. Try the local shiso (parilla) juice if you feel daring.

spots.name: Mashiko Sankokan Museum
spots.desc: Shoji Hamada's workshop and home turned museum, showcasing about 30 of his works as well as his private collection. Near Hamada's thatched-roof home is a huge climbing kiln. Admission ¥800, Tu-Su 09:30 to 16:00; closed in February.

spots.name: Tōgei Messe Mashiko
spots.desc: A museum of ceramic arts, displaying works by Shoji Hamada and other potters, not only from Mashiko but around Japan. Admission ¥600, open Tu-Su 09:30 to 16:00.

spots.name: Zen no Rōka
spots.desc: An indoor and outdoor museum of statues and artpieces, displaying works by Nandor Wagner a Hungarian sculptor who lived for three decades in Mashiko. There are a spring and an autumn exhibition check for details at .

spots.name: Yoshimura Strawberry Park
spots.desc: Yoshimura Strawberry Park is a family run Strawberry farm in Mashiko, Tochigi ken. You can enjoy all-you-can-eat strawberry picking from as little as ¥1,000. This area has the largest harvest of strawberries in all of Japan and the local brand 'Tochiotome' which is available to pick is the most popular strawberry brand in Tokyo and exported as a luxury brand abroad.
spots.price: Low season ¥1,000, mid season ¥1,300, high season ¥1,500

spots.name: Mashikoyaki Kamamoto Kyōhan Center
spots.local: 益子焼窯元共販センター
spots.desc: A cooperative sales center that sells works by most kilns in town at reasonable prices.

spots.name: Harvey Young Pottery
spots.local: ハービー ヤング 陶房
spots.desc: A small handmade pottery workshop operated since 1984 by an American who first went to Mashiko in 1969 to study pottery making. Tableware, Kitchenware, Flower Arrangement ware. Visitors are welcome, by appointment.

spots.name: Lake Rindo Family Farm
spots.local: りんどう湖ファミリー牧場
spots.desc: Tourist farm, amusement park and zoo combined in Nasu, including dozens of alpacas imported from Chile.

spots.name: Asian Old Bazaar
spots.local: アジアンオールドバザール
spots.desc: Southeast Asia themed shopping area with three shops and two restaurants: Ubud for Balinese cuisine and Mekong for Thai/Vietnamese cuisine. The Balinese style restaurant has a terrace with excellent views of the surrounding area.

spots.name: Trekkling
spots.desc: Rent-a-bike and bike tours, including a wasabi farm tour guided by David, Australian ex-reporter. Its website is bilingual.

spots.name: Lake Okutama
spots.desc: Located behind a large dam on the Tama River is the largest lake in Tokyo. The western end of the lake extends into Yamanashi. Regular buses are available from Okutama Station (20 min). There's also a mostly gentle 9-km hiking trail called the "Mukashi-michi" (昔道, "old road") that can get you there in about 4 hours.

spots.name: Mount Mitake
spots.desc: This 929 m mountain is famous for the mountaintop Mitake Shrine. If you don't want to hike up the mountain, a ropeway and bus service cover most of the distance between the shrine and Mitake Station on the Ome Line. On a clear day you can see all of Tokyo as well as Nikko's peaks to the northeast. From the mountaintop there are trails, some quite strenuous, that can make for a good half-day of…

spots.name: Aman
spots.desc: Run by a warm and helpful couple, this is an Italian restaurant open at lunchtime for the half the week (it is closed on Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday). The husband (Toshi-san) speaks English and Italian and spent time as a sculptor in Tuscany. The pasta with tomato sauce and prawns is particularly delicious.This is freshly prepared and well-cooked food by people keen to share the best of Yoron…
spots.price: Soups are ¥700 and pasta risotto dishes start at ¥1000. Coffee and tea are ¥300

spots.name: Yoron Seaside Garden
spots.desc: A delightful garden café with beautiful sea views and friendly service. English spoken. Limited menu but the emphasis is on the environment, not the fare.
spots.addr: 2019 Furusato 〒891-9307 鹿児島 県 大島 郡 与論 町 古里 2019

spots.name: Nakanoshima Observatory
spots.desc: The largest telescope in Kyushu, with a 60-cm mirror. Open most evenings, but reservations required.

spots.name: Tokara Museum
spots.desc: The only museum in the islands. A modest affair, and the exhibits are only in Japanese.

spots.name: Boze Matsuri
spots.desc: A local variant of Japan's Bon festival, held yearly on the 16th of July in the old calendar; meaning sometime between August and September. The island's men dress up in bizarre, spectacular costumes made of palm leaves and husk, representing the Masked God Boze, and dance to scare away the devils and bring in a new year.

spots.name: Chiho no Ie Restaurant
spots.desc: This establishment serves Nagashi Somen, thin wheat noodles streaming through bamboo chutes. The takachiho beef grill or rice bowl is also a must try here. Known for its sweetness, Japan-famous Miyazaki cattle here are fed with squeezed beer curd and once won national best wagyu awards.

spots.name: Arita Kan
spots.desc: Has an exhibition of modern art porcelain, 400 different cups for coffee or tea and a theater with mechanical computerized puppets made of porcelain.

spots.name: China On The Park
spots.local: 深川製磁 チャイナ･オン･ザ･パーク
spots.desc: Experience pottery and porcelain design. The establishment dates back to the end of the last century when the Fukugawa factory was chosen to provide the Imperial household with porcelain. This large and modern style facility contains a factory, galleries, shops and a restaurant.

spots.name: Rokuroza
spots.desc: If you are really interested in pottery but only have a half day you can spare, then Rokuroza is the place for you. Here you can learn how to make your own pottery.

spots.name: RanRanRan
spots.desc: Specializes in fried curry and blueberry parfaits. Temporarily closed as of April 2024.

spots.name: Hateno Beach
spots.desc: Sandbar located 15 mins off of Kumejima. Accessible by tour boats, jet ski, or kayaks. Great for snorkeling. Kumejima's finest white sand beach and crystal clear blue waters.

spots.name: Iifu (Eef) Beach
spots.desc: Fine white sand beach named one of the 100 Best Beaches in Japan.

spots.name: Spiral Reggae Bar
spots.desc: Small hole-in-the-wall bar/restaurant, also offering delicious Indonesian/Thai cuisines

spots.name: Zakimi Castle
spots.desc: Built 1416–1422, the ruins of this castle and partially restored walls offer a visitor center, a museum covering its history and architecture and views (¥500), along with a good architectural education in castle design and defence. Next to the castle is a local cafe selling ices in the summer at good value. The nearest bus stop to this castle is over 1km away on highway 58. Limited free…

spots.name: Araha Beach
spots.desc: This beautiful sandy beach and park covers much of Chatan's coastline. Epic pirate ship climbing gym, basketball courts, BBQ pits. Free parking.

spots.name: Reef Encounters
spots.desc: All instructors are fluent in both English and Japanese. Ask to drift dive Ugan or get lost with the sharks in the Kamiyama labyrinth. PADI and NAUI courses are available, with a discount for combined open water/advanced open water courses. For the experienced or adventurous ask about technical courses or diving Yonaguni.

spots.name: Koza Music Town
spots.local: コザ・ミュージックタウン
spots.desc: Music Town is home to dozens of restaurants, music halls, recording and editing studios, entertainment halls, money exchanges and retail businesses. Located only a short drive from Kadena Air Base Gate 2.

spots.name: Yachimun no Sato
spots.desc: Yachimun is Okinawan for pottery (yakimono in Japanese), and this village has no less than 19 Okinawan pottery workshops. Many are run by family and disciples of pottery master Jirō Kinjō (金城次郎, 1918-2004), who was Okinawa's first Living National Treasure and did much to popularize Okinawan pottery. Faithful imitations of Jirō's work, many of which feature fish or crustacean themes, can be picked…

spots.name: CoCo's
spots.desc: A family restaurant. This place is especially popular with United States Marines stationed on the island.

spots.name: Yoshihachi
spots.desc: A famous sushi place also known as Yoshi's, geared towards American tastes. Try the Yoshi Roll.

spots.name: Jirocho Zushi
spots.desc: Recognizable with the Iron Horse in front, this is probably the best restaurant on Okinawa. Jirocho's sushi, sashimi, tempura and sake are world-class. They also serve some excellent Okinawan dishes, often as specials. The seafood is as fresh as you will find on Okinawa--what truly distinguishes this restaurant is the emphasis on fresh and seasonal ingredients. All of this is served in an elegant…

spots.name: Kasthamandap
spots.desc: The best curry on Okinawa and maybe anywhere else outside of London or Bombay. The owner takes great care to make authenic Nepalese curry from scratch and the results are well worth it. Kastamandap is small and no-frills but the delicious curry and ice cold beer make it one of the most satisfying dining experiences around. Although it is just a shack, the homey but exotic atmosphere and friendly…

spots.name: Nago Pineapple Park
spots.local: ナゴパイナップルパーク
spots.desc: Kitschy pineapple-themed park. A short but entertaining ride on an automated golf cart gives you some history about pineapple cultivation, dropping you off in a shopping center where all the products are either pineapple-themed or contain pineapple (or both!) Worth a stop if you're in the area and you like pineapple.
spots.price: Adult (16 years old) ¥850, junior high school (13-15 years old) ¥600, elementary school students ¥450, pre-school…

spots.name: Cape Hedo
spots.desc: Northern-most point of Okinawa Island, beautiful views from high cliffs.

spots.name: Haneji Inland Sea
spots.desc: Enclosed by Yayagi Island and the western peninsula. Beautiful especially at sunset.

spots.name: Hiji Falls
spots.desc: In the northern part of the island, a 45-minute hike from the visitors center taking you by a river dam, over a suspension bridge, and finally to the falls itself.

spots.name: Diamond Beach
spots.desc: The beach itself is nothing special, but the snorkeling here is some of the best on the island, with plenty of fish and vibrant coral. There's a staircase down at the right side of the Okashi Goten shop, but it closes at 18:00 sharp.

spots.name: Nabee Beach
spots.desc: Public beach nestled between the private hotel beaches. Kayaks, banana boats, snorkeling gear etc for rent.

spots.name: Okashi Goten
spots.desc: The local franchise of the "Snack Palace" is hard to miss, since there are lurid purple billboards for miles around and it's housed in an extravagant ersatz Okinawan palace. Drop in for purple sweet potato tarts, pastries, cakes, ice cream and more. There's also a restaurant on the second floor with nice views of the bay.

spots.name: Nougeichaya Shikinoaya
spots.local: 農芸茶屋 四季の彩
spots.desc: Delightful cafe is surrounded by nature. While you eat your meal you may choose to sit at a counter overlooking lush mountains. Many handmade shisa decorate the cafe and are for sale.

spots.name: Kinokawa
spots.desc: Unpretentious Japanese food in a very unpretentious building. The only real reason to climb there is to eat their peanuts tofu, it looks like ice cream and is probably the most delicious form of tofu you'll ever eat.

spots.name: Big Blue Dining
spots.desc: Bar with Okinawan food in the evenings, but the real standout here is the lunchtime taco menu that wouldn't be out of place in LA, serving up 5 types daily on proper handmade tortillas. The fish tacos are particularly tasty, and there's a good selection of hot sauces as well.

spots.name: Hanamura Soba
spots.desc: Don't be put off by the daggy exterior, this little noodle shop is lovely on the inside, with some fine specimens of local ceramics, and has great Okinawan noodles to boot. Their special, Hanamura soba, has both melt-in-your-mouth pork belly and ribs (sōki).

spots.name: Paanilani
spots.desc: A reasonable facsimile of an Hawaiian diner, serving up both sweet and savory pancakes: whipped cream and pineapple jam, bacon and Spam, even fried chicken. If you're really hungry, try the 16-pancake "Diamond Head" stack.

spots.name: Yambaru
spots.desc: Perennially packed Okinawan eatery specializing in local pork (あぐー agū) dishes, popular with tourists and locals alike. Try their speciality "lard rice" (ラード飯), where you mix a spoonful of pure homemade pig fat into a bowl of piping hot rice with a half-cooked egg, garlic and sauce: sinful but oh so good.

spots.name: Taco Rice Cafe Kijimuna
spots.desc: Fast food eatery specializing in taco rice and their own spin on it, "omu taco", which plops a fluffy omelette on top. 5 basic toppings including a vegetarian bean option, then add on extras like avocado or jalapenos.

spots.name: Yukino
spots.desc: The locals come here for the generous tonkatsu pork cutlet sets, but this maze-like local eatery also serves up fresh sushi/sashimi and all your Okinawan favorites. Try the fu champuru.

spots.name: Helios Brewery Factory Tour
spots.local: ヘリオス酒造工場見学 heriosu shuzō
spots.desc: All kinds of Awamori (Rice made Shōchū), you can taste several. Reservation required phone or web.

spots.name: Orion Happy Park
spots.desc: The brewery where Okinawa's most popular beer is made, open to tours and tastings. Temporarily closed for renovation as of November 2024.

spots.name: Astronomical Observatory
spots.desc: Temporarily closed from 2022. Minimal planetarium presentations in the evening. The Southern Cross is visible from mid December to June. Many local inns provide shuttle service (free or ¥500) to and from the observatory.

spots.name: Nishihama
spots.desc: The turquoise waters on this beach are among the most beautiful in all of the islands.

spots.name: Ayafufami
spots.desc: A charming cafe/restaurant with a library and musical instruments to play.

spots.name: Iriomote Wildlife Center
spots.desc: A wildlife center dedicated to preserving and educating visitors about the Iriomote cat, which can only be found on island of Iriomote.

spots.name: Yugafukan
spots.desc: An informative museum run by the national parks authority, but all the information is in Japanese. On the plus side, the 15-minute film and the audio sets of Yaeyaman stories and songs are interesting to everyone.

spots.name: Bar Take-To-Me
spots.desc: Forget marble countertops and tuxedoed waiters: this is an open-air wooden platform piled with plastic lawn chairs and surrounded by hibiscus flowers. Order an awamori straight or turned into a cocktail, kick back, watch the starry skies and enjoy the quiet of Taketomi at night. Open only during high season.

spots.name: Seto Wind Hill Park
spots.desc: This park is on top of a mountain in the Seto area. From it you can see many of Ikata's numerous windmills, spinning above the Inland Sea to the north and the Pacific Ocean to the south. Haikus about the windmills, submitted for Ikata's Windmill Festival, are on display in the park.

spots.name: Ikata Visitors Center
spots.desc: This hands-on science museum teaches all about nuclear power with beautiful interactive displays and fun activities for all ages. The building is connected to the Kirara-kan, which houses an aquarium and sells souvenirs and local agricultural products.

spots.name: Red Wing Park
spots.desc: Named after Ikata's sister city, this park is home to Adventure Hill—a playground full of climbing nets, roller slides, and other exciting children's play equipment.

spots.name: Kamegaike Onsen
spots.desc: A hot spring bathing facility and park. According to legend, a giant crab lives in the adjacent Kamegaike Pond. There is also a simple accommodation facility on the premises: ¥5,000 for 2 people (1 room).

spots.name: Uchiko-za Theater
spots.desc: Built in 1916 to commemorate the ascension of Emperor Taisho, it is a 2-story theater still in use today. The theater can be toured by visitors when there are no events going on.

spots.name: Kamihaga Residence
spots.desc: The Kamihaga Family was one of the city's most prosperous wax producing families. The residence is preserved and furnished and includes information about the family as well as Uchiko's wax production.

spots.name: Omura Residence
spots.desc: Home of a former indigo-dying merchant. It is one of the oldest buildings in the town with its business predating the start of wax-making in the town.
spots.hours: Not open, except for special openings

spots.name: Machiya Museum
spots.desc: Built in 1783, it is now a small folk museum with old daily living objects and farming tools.

spots.name: Zum schwarzen Keiler
spots.local: ツム・シュバルツェン・カイラー
spots.desc: A German restaurant with a German chef. The Keiler family also serves their own Keiler beer.

spots.name: Great Gate
spots.desc: The Great Gate, halfway up the hill, marks your entry into the shrine complex.

spots.name: Asahi Shrine
spots.desc: This shrine, which dates back to 1837, is the largest, oldest, and most impressive of Kompira's many shrine halls, in ornately decorated unpainted wood.

spots.name: Main Shrine
spots.desc: The centerpiece of the shrine complex, with a large square in front and many buildings packed in a cluster.

spots.name: Izutama Shrine
spots.desc: Far fewer visitors make it all the way up here, and you'll be rewarded with nice views over the city. Also known as the Inner Shrine.

spots.name: Kinryo Sake Museum
spots.desc: This museum describes the various stages in sake production. The exhibits are mostly in Japanese, but there are leaflets in other languages at the entrance to explain the process.
spots.price: Admission ¥310. At the end, generous shots of sake are available for ¥100

spots.name: Kotohira Maritime Museum
spots.local: 琴平海洋博物館（海の科学館）
spots.desc: Highlights include a restored vessel from the Edo period along with all sorts of radio-controlled boats, bridges, and musings about man's relationship with the sea.

spots.name: Museum of History
spots.desc: A good match with a visit to Kanamaru-za (see below), this museum showcases local folkcraft, including plenty of kabuki costumes and props.

spots.name: Konpira Onsen Kotosankaku
spots.local: こんぴら温泉郷 琴参閣
spots.desc: Stop in if you need a soak after the walk up to Kompira-san — or, if you're really sore, switch your accommodation to one of the several hotels that comprise this hot spring "village".

spots.name: Naniwado Rice Cake Shop
spots.desc: Established in 1866 and run by five generations of the same family, Naniwa bakes fresh sweets daily. Bean cakes and rice cakes are specialties, but there are several varieties to try.

spots.name: Ando Museum
spots.desc: A small museum featuring the works of architect Tadao Ando, designer of most of the museums on Naoshima Island. Ando was born in 1941 in Osaka. Ando has received many international awards.

spots.name: Art House Project
spots.desc: The Art House Project began in 1998 with Tatsuo Miyajima's Kadoya, and comprises 7 vacant houses, which were converted into works of art, weaving in the history and memories of the period when the houses were homes.
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00–16:30; closed on the following day of a public holiday
spots.price: ¥410 for entry to a single house. ¥1,030 for a ticket good for entry to six of the art houses. Kinza has its own…

spots.name: Kinza
spots.local: 家プロジェクト・きんざ
spots.desc: “Being Given” by Rei Naito. Reservations must be made in advance online.
spots.hours: Thu-Sun and holidays 11:00–13:00, 14:00–16:30; closed on Thu Fri from Dec 1 to end of Feb
spots.price: ¥510, not included in the Art House Project combined ticket

spots.name: Mitsubishi Materials Smelter and Refinery
spots.desc: Mitsubishi Materials is the major employer on the island. Most of the north side of the island is taken up with material processing facilities. A tour of these facilities can be organized if reservations are made at least a week in advance. Tours must be booked in and are conducted in Japanese only. Security procedures are strict.

spots.name: Aisunao
spots.desc: Literally "Brown Rice Hearty Eatery". Vegetarian restaurant.

spots.name: Café Ougiya
spots.desc: Japanese food railway-style, one of tenants in the ferry terminal. Standard udon, curry & rice, etc. Bicycle rental is available.

spots.name: Nagomi (in the Fukushi Center)
spots.local: なごみ（福祉センター内）
spots.desc: Table d'hote (set meal), has udon etc. There's a public pool and fitness center in this complex as well.

spots.name: Café Saya
spots.desc: This charming place is attached to the rear of a house. Café Saya serves excellent green tea lattes and sweets. They also serve tsukune-don (a ground-chicken patty on top of rice), Saya men (beef on top of noodles), etc.
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, may open Sat Sun at 08:00

spots.name: Little Plum Naoshima
spots.desc: Cafe and bar with a good local beer selection. Bicycle rental and accommodation are available.

spots.name: Mino
spots.desc: Rice ball take-out, packed 3 rice balls, curry & rice, ice-cream cone

spots.name: Naoshima Tsuri Koen
spots.desc: Sashimi of sea bream and a bowl of rice, curry and rice served on weekend, National holidays during May to September

spots.name: New Olympia
spots.desc: The best quality seafood you'll get outside of Benesse House. Try the Tempura, and don't worry about language barriers just point and smile and you'll be treated royally. The chef has a cheat sheet of English translations of his dishes behind the counter.

spots.name: Terrace Restaurant @ Benesse House "Park"
spots.desc: Terrace restaurant of the Bennesse House. French food with a great view of the water.

spots.name: Shodoshima Great Kannon
spots.desc: A 50-m-high statue with a temple inside depicting Kannon, the Buddhist goddess of mercy. The statue was built in 1993. Visitors can walk or take an elevator to the top to see a display of the tooth of Buddha. The statue also offers spectacular views of the island. The temple also has hundreds of miniature statues of Kannon on display and a worship hall.

spots.name: Nijushi no Hitomi Movie Village
spots.desc: Nijushi no Hitomi (literally 'Twenty-Four Eyes') is a 1954 Japanese movie that follows the lives of a family in the years leading up to World War II. The movie was remade in color in 1987. The movie set consists of an entire reconstructed village.
spots.price: ¥830 to see the movie village and the school house

spots.name: Ruins of Osaka Castle Stone Cutting Workshop
spots.desc: After the destruction of Osaka Castle in 1615, many stones were harvested from Shidoshima to rebuild the castle.

spots.name: Osaka Castle Stones Michi no Eki
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to tools and stones harvested from Shidoshima to rebuild Osaka Castle in the early 1600s.

spots.name: Marukin Soy Sauce Factory & Museum
spots.desc: Soy sauce has been produced on Shidoshima for over 400 years. The Marukin factory is open for tours and has English displays.

spots.name: Kankakei Gorge
spots.desc: Considered to be one of the most beautiful gorges in Japan. As much as 812 m deep. Celebrated for its maple trees. The gorge can be traversed by cable car (¥750 one way, ¥1,350 return) or by a steep hike.

spots.name: Choshikei Monkey Park
spots.desc: There are 500 Japanese macaques roaming around the park. There are monkey shows twice per day as well as a feeding area. Near the park is an observation deck with a great view of the island.

spots.name: Angel Road
spots.desc: A sandbar that connects 3 small islands to Shodoshima. It gets its name from how the road mysteriously appears and then disappears. Make sure to visit during low tide since at that time you can walk along the sandbar. It is said that if you walk across hand-in-hand with your lover, you'll have happiness together.

spots.name: Nakayama Senmaida Rice Terraces
spots.desc: Hundreds of rice terraces are carved into the hills. There is a stage that has hosted outdoor kabuki plays since the Edo period.

spots.name: Olive Park
spots.desc: The site of the first olive cultivation in Japan in 1908, it is a park full of olive trees and an olive museum. It also has the Sun Olive Bath House, which has 8 pools separated by gender. The bath house costs ¥700 and is open from 12:00 to 21:00.

spots.name: Misato Lavendar Fields
spots.desc: A field of 20,000 lavendar stocks blooming, including the Misato Sekka, a local variety of white lavendar, that bloom from mid-June to early July.

spots.name: Takeuchi Festival
spots.desc: A part of the weeklong "Rokugo no Kamakura" festival, this evening features people hitting each other in the head with bamboo poles. Participants are given helmets for safety, though people have sustained injuries in the past. This very interesting festival is not known for being particularly safe.

spots.name: Tatsuko Statue
